## Iteration 38 — New Patterns

### Download Testing — Comprehensive Patterns

The brief `waitForEvent('download')` snippet in the Advanced Interactions section covers the happy path. This section documents the full lifecycle: MIME type assertions, parallel download races, CI `downloadsPath` cleanup, and security validation patterns.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';
import fs from 'fs';

// ── 1. Basic download with filename and extension assertion ──────────────────
test('exports report as CSV', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  // ALWAYS set up the listener BEFORE triggering the download
  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' }).click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;

  // Assert filename pattern
  expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/^report-\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.csv$/);

  // Persist to disk and assert content
  const savePath = path.join(test.info().outputDir, download.suggestedFilename());
  await download.saveAs(savePath);

  const content = fs.readFileSync(savePath, 'utf-8');
  expect(content).toContain('"Date","Amount","Status"');  // CSV header row present
  expect(content.split('\n').length).toBeGreaterThan(1);  // at least one data row
});

// ── 2. Assert download URL and MIME type via network interception ─────────────
test('download has correct MIME type', async ({ page }) => {
  // Capture the response headers for the download request
  let downloadMimeType = '';
  page.on('response', response => {
    if (response.url().includes('/export')) {
      downloadMimeType = response.headers()['content-type'] ?? '';
    }
  });

  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.goto('/reports');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export PDF' }).click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;

  expect(downloadMimeType).toContain('application/pdf');
  expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.pdf$/);
});

// ── 3. Parallel download test — trigger two exports and wait for both ─────────
test('can download multiple reports simultaneously', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  // Set up both promises BEFORE any clicks
  const [download1, download2] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForEvent('download'),
    page.waitForEvent('download'),
    (async () => {
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' }).click();
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export XLSX' }).click();
    })(),
  ]);

  expect(download1.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.csv$/);
  expect(download2.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.xlsx$/);
});

// ── 4. Download failure — surface the error message ──────────────────────────
test('shows error when export fails', async ({ page }) => {
  // Intercept the export endpoint and return a server error
  await page.route('**/api/export*', route =>
    route.fulfill({ status: 503, body: 'Service Unavailable' })
  );

  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.goto('/reports');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' }).click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;

  // download.failure() returns the error reason string, or null on success
  expect(await download.failure()).not.toBeNull();

  // Assert the UI also shows an error state
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText(/export failed/i);
});

// ── 5. Download path guard — save only when download succeeded ────────────────
test('saves download only on success', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');
  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Download invoice' }).click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;

  const failureReason = await download.failure();
  if (failureReason) {
    throw new Error(`Download failed: ${failureReason}`);
  }

  const dest = path.join(test.info().outputDir, 'invoice.pdf');
  await download.saveAs(dest);
  expect(fs.existsSync(dest)).toBe(true);
  expect(fs.statSync(dest).size).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**CI `downloadsPath` configuration:**

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import os from 'os';
import path from 'path';

export default defineConfig({
  use: {
    // Place downloads inside the test output dir so CI artifact collectors pick them up.
    // Without this, downloads land in the system temp dir and are lost when the runner
    // cleans up after the job.
    downloadsPath: path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-results', 'downloads'),
  },
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Omitting `downloadsPath` causes `download.path()` to return a system-temp path that gets garbage-collected when the browser context closes. In CI, this means download files are gone before your `afterAll` assertion runs. Always set `downloadsPath` to a project-relative path that is included in your artifact upload step. [community]

> **[community]** WHY: `download.path()` returns `null` for in-progress downloads. Always `await download.saveAs()` first — it resolves only after the download completes. Calling `download.path()` before `saveAs` is a classic race condition that appears to work locally (fast disk) but fails in CI. [community]

---

### Multi-Tab and Popup Testing — Comprehensive Patterns

Single-page `page.waitForEvent('popup')` is covered in the Advanced Interactions section. This section documents OAuth popup flows, `context.on('page')` streaming for dynamic tab creation, and window.open() stubs.

```typescript
import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

// ── 1. Popup auth flow (OAuth / SSO) ─────────────────────────────────────────
// OAuth opens a popup window. The popup must complete auth and close itself,
// then the original page receives a token via postMessage or cookie.
test('OAuth popup login flow completes successfully', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  // Register the popup listener BEFORE the click that opens it
  const popupPromise = page.waitForEvent('popup');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in with Google' }).click();
  const popup = await popupPromise;

  // Wait for the popup to be ready before interacting
  await popup.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
  await expect(popup).toHaveURL(/accounts\.google\.com/);

  // Simulate completing OAuth in the popup
  await popup.getByLabel('Email').fill('test@example.com');
  await popup.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next' }).click();
  await popup.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.GOOGLE_TEST_PASSWORD!);
  await popup.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();

  // Popup closes itself after successful auth — wait for it
  await popup.waitForEvent('close');

  // Main page should now be authenticated
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
  await expect(page.getByText('Welcome')).toBeVisible();
});

// ── 2. context.on('page') — handle dynamically opened tabs ───────────────────
// Use when the number of new tabs is unknown at test time (e.g., "open all results"
// button, or multiple links each opening a new tab).
test('opens product pages in separate tabs', async ({ page, context }) => {
  const newPages: Page[] = [];

  // Stream-capture ALL new pages opened within this context
  context.on('page', async newPage => {
    await newPage.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
    newPages.push(newPage);
  });

  await page.goto('/products');
  // Click all "Open in new tab" links
  const links = page.getByRole('link', { name: /open in new tab/i });
  const linkCount = await links.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < linkCount; i++) {
    await links.nth(i).click();
  }

  // Wait until all expected tabs have loaded
  await expect.poll(() => newPages.length).toBe(linkCount);

  // Assert each new page has a valid product URL
  for (const productPage of newPages) {
    await expect(productPage).toHaveURL(/\/products\/\d+/);
    await productPage.close();
  }
});

// ── 3. runAndWaitForNewPage — concise helper for single new tab ──────────────
// When you need exactly one new tab, use context.waitForEvent('page') with the
// action wrapped together to avoid the "promise created after event" race condition.
test('opens terms page in new tab', async ({ page, context }) => {
  // Use Promise.all to set up the listener and trigger the action atomically
  const [newPage] = await Promise.all([
    context.waitForEvent('page'),
    page.getByRole('link', { name: /terms of service/i }).click(),
  ]);

  await newPage.waitForLoadState();
  await expect(newPage).toHaveURL(/\/terms/);
  await expect(newPage.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })).toContainText('Terms');
  await newPage.close();
});

// ── 4. window.open() stub — redirect popups into the same page ───────────────
// Some legacy apps use window.open() with noopener/noreferrer. Stub it to keep
// navigation in the same page and avoid managing a second window.
test('window.open() link navigates correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  // Override window.open so navigation stays in the current page
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.open = (url?: string | URL) => {
      if (url) window.location.href = url.toString();
      return window;
    };
  });

  await page.goto('/share');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Share on Twitter' }).click();

  // Assert the navigation happened in the same page instead of a popup
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/twitter\.com\/intent\/tweet/);
});

// ── 5. Multi-tab state isolation — confirm tabs share cookies but not JS state
test('tabs share authentication but not unsaved form data', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: 'e2e/.auth/user.json',
  });

  const tab1 = await context.newPage();
  const tab2 = await context.newPage();

  await tab1.goto('/profile/edit');
  await tab1.getByLabel('Display name').fill('Temporary Name');
  // Do NOT submit — tab2 should see the persisted name, not the unsaved value

  await tab2.goto('/profile');
  // Cookies are shared → both tabs are authenticated
  await expect(tab2.getByTestId('user-menu')).toBeVisible();
  // JS memory is NOT shared → tab2 sees persisted DB value, not tab1's unsaved input
  await expect(tab2.getByText('Temporary Name')).toBeHidden();

  await tab1.close();
  await tab2.close();
  await context.close();
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: `page.waitForEvent('popup')` and `context.waitForEvent('page')` look similar but behave differently. `page.waitForEvent('popup')` fires only for popups triggered by that specific page (e.g., `window.open()`). `context.waitForEvent('page')` fires for every new page created in the context, including `target="_blank"` links. Use `page.waitForEvent('popup')` for popup windows; use `context.waitForEvent('page')` for new tabs. Mixing them causes silent misses. [community]

> **[community]** WHY: The `Promise.all` pattern for simultaneous listener registration and click is mandatory in Playwright. If you `await` the click before registering the popup listener, the popup may open and close before `waitForEvent` is even called — producing a test that hangs indefinitely waiting for a popup that already appeared. [community]

---

### `page.routeWebSocket()` — Subprotocol Testing and Binary Frame Patterns (v1.48+)

The WebSocket testing section in the Recommended Patterns area covers the standard message interception cases. This section adds subprotocol negotiation testing, binary (ArrayBuffer) frame patterns, and reconnection simulation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ── 1. WebSocket subprotocol negotiation testing ──────────────────────────────
// Test that the client sends the correct Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header and
// the server response selects the expected subprotocol.
test('WebSocket client negotiates "graphql-ws" subprotocol', async ({ page }) => {
  let negotiatedProtocol = '';

  await page.routeWebSocket('**/graphql', route => {
    // webSocketRoute.protocols() returns the client's requested subprotocols (v1.60+)
    const requested = route.protocols();
    expect(requested).toContain('graphql-ws');

    // Accept the connection using the expected protocol
    negotiatedProtocol = requested.includes('graphql-ws') ? 'graphql-ws' : '';

    // Send a minimal GraphQL-over-WebSocket connection_ack
    route.onopen = () => {
      route.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'connection_ack' }));
    };
    route.onMessage(msg => {
      const frame = JSON.parse(msg as string);
      if (frame.type === 'subscribe') {
        // Return mock data for the subscription
        route.send(JSON.stringify({
          id: frame.id,
          type: 'next',
          payload: { data: { messageAdded: { text: 'Hello from mock' } } },
        }));
      }
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/chat');
  expect(negotiatedProtocol).toBe('graphql-ws');
  await expect(page.getByText('Hello from mock')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
});

// ── 2. Binary (ArrayBuffer) WebSocket frame testing ──────────────────────────
// Test that the UI correctly renders binary data pushed over WebSocket.
// Binary frames arrive as Buffer in Node.js; convert to Uint8Array for assertions.
test('renders binary chart data from WebSocket', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('**/chart-feed', route => {
    route.onopen = () => {
      // Send a mock binary frame: a 4-byte IEEE 754 float representing price 42.0
      const buffer = Buffer.alloc(4);
      buffer.writeFloatBE(42.0, 0);
      route.send(buffer);
    };
  });

  await page.goto('/realtime-chart');
  // The chart component should decode the binary frame and render the value
  await expect(page.getByTestId('current-price')).toHaveText('42.00');
});

// ── 3. WebSocket reconnection and back-off testing ────────────────────────────
// Simulate a mid-session server disconnect and assert the client reconnects
// and resumes normal operation.
test('chat client reconnects after server disconnects', async ({ page }) => {
  let connectionCount = 0;

  await page.routeWebSocket('**/chat', route => {
    connectionCount++;
    if (connectionCount === 1) {
      // First connection: send a welcome message then close to trigger reconnection
      route.onopen = () => {
        route.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'welcome', text: 'Connected' }));
        setTimeout(() => route.close(), 200);
      };
    } else {
      // Second connection (reconnect): behave normally
      route.onopen = () => {
        route.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'welcome', text: 'Reconnected' }));
      };
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/chat');
  await expect(page.getByText('Connected')).toBeVisible();

  // Wait for disconnect → reconnect cycle
  await expect(page.getByText('Reconnected')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
  expect(connectionCount).toBe(2);

  // Confirm UI is operational after reconnection
  const messageInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /message/i });
  await expect(messageInput).toBeEnabled();
});

// ── 4. Proxy pattern with selective message dropping ─────────────────────────
// Suppress a specific message type while forwarding everything else to the page.
// Useful for testing "degraded mode" when certain server events are unavailable.
test('handles missing presence events gracefully', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('**/collab', async route => {
    const server = await route.connectToServer();

    // Forward server→page messages, dropping presence_update events
    server.onMessage(message => {
      const frame = JSON.parse(message as string);
      if (frame.type !== 'presence_update') {
        route.send(message);  // only forward non-presence messages
      }
    });

    // Forward page→server messages unchanged
    route.onMessage(message => server.send(message));
  });

  await page.goto('/document-editor');
  // Presence indicator should enter a "degraded" state when updates are absent
  await expect(page.getByTestId('presence-status')).toHaveText(/unavailable|unknown/i, {
    timeout: 3_000,
  });
  // Core editing functionality should still work
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Document' }).fill('Test content');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('save-status')).toHaveText(/saved/i);
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: `route.connectToServer()` returns a promise in TypeScript — you must `await` it. Writing `const server = route.connectToServer()` (without await) gives you a Promise object, and calling `.onMessage()` on it throws at runtime with a non-obvious "onMessage is not a function" error. The TypeScript types do NOT protect you here because `connectToServer()` accepts `WebSocketRouteOptions` and infers based on overload. [community]

> **[community]** WHY: Binary WebSocket frames arrive in the `onMessage` callback as `Buffer` (Node.js) rather than `ArrayBuffer` or `Blob`. If you pass the Buffer directly to `JSON.parse()` it works for text payloads (Buffer is coerced to string), but for binary frames you must check `typeof message === 'string'` and use `Buffer.from(message as any)` for proper byte access. Always guard binary/text frame handling with a type check. [community]

---

### Additional Community Gotchas (Iteration 38)

---

### 53. `download.path()` returns `null` before `saveAs()` resolves, causing false positives in assertions [community]

`download.path()` returns the temporary download path only after the download has fully completed and the file has been flushed. If you call `download.path()` immediately after `await downloadPromise` (before `saveAs()`), the download may still be in progress, and `path()` returns `null`.

```typescript
// ❌ Race condition: download may still be in progress
const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export' }).click();
const download = await downloadPromise;
const filePath = download.path();  // MAY be null — download not yet finished
expect(filePath).not.toBeNull();   // flaky assertion

// ✅ Correct: saveAs() resolves only after the download is complete
const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export' }).click();
const download = await downloadPromise;
const dest = path.join(test.info().outputDir, download.suggestedFilename());
await download.saveAs(dest);          // blocks until the file is fully written
const filePath = download.path();     // now safe — guaranteed non-null after saveAs
expect(filePath).not.toBeNull();
```

> **WHY:** `download.waitForEvent` resolves when the download response begins, not when it completes. `download.path()` returns `null` until the browser has finished writing to disk. Use `saveAs()` as the completion signal. This race is invisible on fast local machines (small files, fast disk) and shows up only in CI with large exports or slow NFS-mounted volumes. [community]

---

### 54. `context.waitForEvent('page')` resolves before the new page has navigated — always `waitForLoadState()` [community]

When a `target="_blank"` link is clicked, `context.waitForEvent('page')` resolves as soon as the Page object is created — which is before any navigation or DOM load. Accessing locators on the new page immediately after the event fires produces "navigation was aborted" or empty-page errors.

```typescript
// ❌ Brittle: page object exists but has not navigated yet
const [newPage] = await Promise.all([
  context.waitForEvent('page'),
  page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Open preview' }).click(),
]);
// At this point newPage.url() may be 'about:blank'
await expect(newPage.getByRole('heading')).toBeVisible();  // intermittent failure

// ✅ Correct: wait for at minimum domcontentloaded before interacting
const [newPage] = await Promise.all([
  context.waitForEvent('page'),
  page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Open preview' }).click(),
]);
await newPage.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
await expect(newPage.getByRole('heading')).toBeVisible();
```

> **WHY:** The `page` event fires synchronously when the browser creates the renderer process for the new page. The navigation to the target URL is an asynchronous operation that follows. Without `waitForLoadState()`, your test observes the blank initial state of the renderer — not the actual page content. [community]

---

### 55. `page.routeWebSocket()` handlers registered after `page.goto()` do not intercept the initial connection [community]

WebSocket connections are established by the page's JavaScript, usually during or shortly after initial load. If you register `routeWebSocket()` after `goto()` has resolved, the WebSocket connection may already be open and the route handler will never fire.

```typescript
// ❌ Too late: WebSocket already connected by the time route is registered
await page.goto('/live-feed');
await page.routeWebSocket('**/feed', route => {  // never fires — connection is open
  route.send('mock data');
});

// ✅ Correct: register the route BEFORE goto()
await page.routeWebSocket('**/feed', route => {
  route.onopen = () => route.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'init', data: [] }));
});
await page.goto('/live-feed');
await expect(page.getByTestId('feed-status')).toHaveText('Connected');
```

> **WHY:** `page.routeWebSocket()` installs a pre-open intercept hook in the browser's network stack. It must be registered before the page's JavaScript executes `new WebSocket(url)`. Once a WebSocket handshake is complete, the connection is a live TCP stream and cannot be retroactively intercepted by a route handler. This is identical to the `page.route()` timing requirement for XHR/fetch. [community]

---

## Additional Key APIs (Iteration 38)

| API | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|-------------|----------------|
| `download.suggestedFilename()` | Get the browser-suggested filename from Content-Disposition header | Assert file name pattern before saving |
| `download.saveAs(path)` | Save download to a specific path; resolves when write is complete | Completion signal — always use before `download.path()` |
| `download.path()` | Get the temp file path after download completes | Read file content for assertions; only valid after `saveAs()` |
| `download.failure()` | Returns error reason string or `null` on success | Detect and assert download errors |
| `context.waitForEvent('page')` | Resolves when a new Page is created in the context | Capture `target="_blank"` navigations |
| `page.waitForEvent('popup')` | Resolves when a popup window is created by this page | OAuth popups, `window.open()` flows |
| `page.routeWebSocket(url, handler)` | Intercept WebSocket connections matching the URL (v1.48+) | Mock or proxy WebSocket messages |
| `webSocketRoute.connectToServer()` | Connect the intercepted WS to the real server (proxy mode) | Selectively modify real WS messages |
| `webSocketRoute.protocols()` | Get the subprotocols requested by the client (v1.60+) | Validate subprotocol negotiation |
| `webSocketRoute.send(data)` | Send a message to the client | Inject mock server messages |
| `webSocketRoute.close(code?, reason?)` | Close the WebSocket from the route handler | Simulate server disconnection |

## Cycle 19 — 2026-05-13

<!-- sources: official playwright.dev (best-practices, locators, network, test-assertions, trace-viewer-intro, test-components, test-agents, aria-snapshots, test-sharding, test-retries, accessibility-testing, test-global-setup-teardown, release-notes v1.34–v1.60), community: playwrightsolutions.com, mxschmitt/awesome-playwright, production synthesis -->

### AI-Assisted Test Authoring: Planner → Generator → Healer (v1.56+)

Playwright ships three AI agent definitions that implement a full write-maintain loop. Initialize them with:

```bash
npx playwright init-agents --loop=vscode    # VS Code Copilot agent
npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude   # Claude agent
npx playwright init-agents --loop=opencode # OpenCode agent
```

The three agents collaborate in a defined pipeline:

```
repo/
  .github/           # agent instruction files generated by init-agents
  specs/             # human-readable Markdown test plans (Planner output)
  tests/             # executable Playwright specs (Generator output)
    seed.spec.ts     # bootstrap test: authenticates, seeds data, lands on start page
```

**Planner** — Explores the application and produces `specs/<feature>.md` Markdown plans.
Input: a natural-language request + an optional seed test for environment context.
Output: human-readable scenario steps that can be reviewed and edited before code is generated.

**Generator** — Reads a `.md` plan and produces `.spec.ts` files. Validates selectors live as it writes each step. Catches "element not found" and "assertion failed" errors during generation — before the test is committed.

**Healer** — Runs failing tests, inspects the current DOM, and proposes patches for broken locators or changed waits. Repeats until green or until guardrails stop it. Reduces manual locator-fix burden during UI churn.

```typescript
// seed.spec.ts — every project using agents needs one
// Provides a known-good authenticated page for agents to start from
import { test } from '@playwright/test';

test('seed — authenticated start page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill(process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill(process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);
  // The agent uses this page as the starting point for plan execution
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Without a seed test, agents begin from a blank context and waste tokens re-discovering the login flow on every iteration. A well-maintained seed test that can run in under 3 seconds yields a 3-5× speedup in the Planner phase. Re-run `npx playwright init-agents` after every Playwright major version to pick up updated tool definitions.

---

### ARIA Snapshot Testing — Full Pattern Reference (v1.49+)

ARIA snapshot tests assert the accessibility tree structure against a YAML template. They catch accessibility regressions that visual screenshots miss (e.g., a heading rendered at the wrong level, a button losing its label).

```typescript
// Basic ARIA snapshot — partial match by default
test('navigation structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation:
      - link "Home"
      - link "Products"
      - link "Contact"
  `);
});

// Strict children matching — exact order and count required
test('product list — exact', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByRole('list')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - list:
      - /children: equal
      - listitem: Widget A
      - listitem: Widget B
      - listitem: Widget C
  `);
});

// Dynamic content with regex — survives counter changes
test('issues count heading', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - heading /Issues \\d+/ [level=1]
  `);
});

// Form elements with state
test('login form structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await expect(page.locator('form')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - textbox "Email"
    - textbox "Password"
    - checkbox "Remember me"
    - button "Sign in"
  `);
});

// Separate YAML file — snapshot stored in __snapshots__/
test('homepage aria', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name: 'homepage.aria.yml' });
});
```

**Global children matching mode** — set once in `playwright.config.ts`:

```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  expect: {
    toMatchAriaSnapshot: {
      children: 'equal', // 'contain' (default) | 'equal' | 'deep-equal'
    },
  },
});
```

**Programmatic snapshot capture** (useful for initial generation):

```typescript
const snapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();
console.log(snapshot);  // prints YAML — paste into toMatchAriaSnapshot template

// With bounding box data (v1.60) — AI agents use this for spatial reasoning
const boxSnapshot = await page.getByRole('main').ariaSnapshot({ boxes: true });
```

**Update command:**

```bash
npx playwright test --update-snapshots               # overwrite all
npx playwright test -u --update-source-method=3way   # 3-way merge for partial updates
```

> **[community]** WHY: `toMatchAriaSnapshot` is structurally different from `toHaveScreenshot` — it asserts the computed accessibility tree, not pixel appearance. A component can look identical to sighted users but have a broken ARIA tree (wrong role, missing label). Run ARIA snapshots in your regression suite and visual screenshots in your visual suite — they cover orthogonal failure modes.

### Accessibility Testing with axe-core Integration

Complement ARIA snapshots with automated WCAG rule scanning via `@axe-core/playwright`:

```typescript
// Install: npm install --save-dev @axe-core/playwright
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Reusable fixture for consistent axe config
const test = base.extend<{ makeAxeBuilder: () => AxeBuilder }>({
  makeAxeBuilder: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const factory = () =>
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
        .exclude('#known-violation');          // exclude tracked issues
    await use(factory);
  },
});

test('homepage has no critical WCAG violations', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const results = await makeAxeBuilder().analyze();
  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});

// Targeted scan — only check the nav region
test('navigation passes WCAG 2.1 AA', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .include('nav')
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .analyze();
  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});

// Snapshot-based violation tracking — survives unrelated changes
test('tracks known violations without blocking release', async ({ page, testInfo }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();

  // Attach full report for debugging
  await testInfo.attach('axe-violations', {
    body:        JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Assert only on rule ID + selector fingerprint — not full violation object
  const fingerprints = results.violations.flatMap(v =>
    v.nodes.map(n => `${v.id}:${n.target.join('>')}`)
  );
  expect(fingerprints).toMatchSnapshot('known-violations.txt');
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Running all 100+ axe rules in CI produces noise from rules that don't apply to your stack. Using `.withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa'])` scopes to the WCAG standard your product is contractually required to meet — and cuts scan time by ~60%. Always attach the full JSON result as a test attachment so violations are visible in the HTML report without failing the build.

### Component Testing (CT) — Updated Patterns

Component testing renders React or Vue components in a real browser, exercising the component lifecycle and DOM APIs while isolating from the network and routing layer.

**Setup:**

```bash
npm init playwright@latest -- --ct   # generates playwright-ct.config.ts + playwright/index.ts
```

**React component test with props, events, and assertions:**

```typescript
// src/components/Button.test.tsx
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react';
import { Button } from './Button';

test('calls onClick when clicked', async ({ mount }) => {
  let clicked = false;
  const component = await mount(
    <Button label="Submit" onClick={() => { clicked = true; }} />
  );

  await expect(component).toContainText('Submit');
  await component.click();
  expect(clicked).toBe(true);
});

test('is disabled when loading prop is true', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<Button label="Save" loading />);
  await expect(component.getByRole('button')).toBeDisabled();
});
```

**Component update and unmount lifecycle:**

```typescript
test('updates prop without remounting', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<Counter initialCount={0} />);
  await expect(component.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('0');

  // Update props in-place — does not unmount the component
  await component.update(<Counter initialCount={5} />);
  await expect(component.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('5');
});

test('cleans up on unmount', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<Tooltip text="Hello" />);
  await component.unmount();
  // Assert no portal/overlay remains in the DOM
  await expect(page.locator('[role=tooltip]')).not.toBeAttached();
});
```

**Module mocking limitation — use `beforeMount` + `hooksConfig` instead of `vi.mock`:**

```typescript
// playwright/index.tsx — register before-mount hooks
import { beforeMount } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react/hooks';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';

export type HooksConfig = {
  routerInitialPath?: string;
};

beforeMount<HooksConfig>(async ({ App, hooksConfig }) => {
  if (hooksConfig?.routerInitialPath) {
    return (
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[hooksConfig.routerInitialPath]}>
        <App />
      </MemoryRouter>
    );
  }
});
```

```typescript
// Test uses hooksConfig to inject routing context
test('renders product list at /products', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount<HooksConfig>(<App />, {
    hooksConfig: { routerInitialPath: '/products' },
  });
  await expect(component.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Products' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Network mocking via MSW (experimental `router` fixture):**

```typescript
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';

test('shows loading state then data', async ({ mount, router }) => {
  await router.use(
    http.get('/api/products', async () => {
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100));  // simulate latency
      return HttpResponse.json([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget' }]);
    })
  );

  const component = await mount(<ProductList />);
  await expect(component.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Loading');
  await expect(component.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(component.getByText('Widget')).toBeVisible();
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: `vi.mock()` / `jest.mock()` in CT tests only affects the Node.js test process — not the browser environment where the component runs. The module mock does not cross the Node/browser boundary. Use `beforeMount` + `hooksConfig` for router/store providers, and the `router` fixture (MSW) for network mocking. Attempting to use `vi.mock` for component dependencies produces silent no-ops in the browser.

---

### Network Interception — Advanced Patterns

**Modify response body while preserving headers:**

```typescript
test('injects mock data into real API response', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/api/products', async route => {
    const response = await route.fetch();  // send request to real server
    const json = await response.json();

    // Inject a test product without replacing the real data structure
    json.items.unshift({ id: 'test-001', name: 'Injected Test Product' });

    await route.fulfill({
      response,               // preserve headers, status, etc.
      json,                   // override body only
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByText('Injected Test Product')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Abort specific requests to test error states:**

```typescript
test('shows empty state when images fail to load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,webp}', route => route.abort());
  await page.goto('/gallery');
  await expect(page.getByRole('img')).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.getByText('No images available')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**HAR recording and replay (v1.60 — `tracing.startHar` / `tracing.stopHar`):**

```typescript
// Record: capture real responses into a HAR file
test.use({ trace: 'on' });

test('record API calls to HAR', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await context.tracing.startHar({
    path:   './fixtures/api-capture.har',
    urlFilter: '**/api/**',
    content: 'embed',   // embed response bodies; use 'omit' for large binaries
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Load Data' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();

  await context.tracing.stopHar();
});

// Use async disposable pattern for automatic cleanup (v1.60+)
test('HAR replay with async disposable', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await using _har = await context.tracing.startHar({ path: './fixtures/api.har' });
  // HAR stops automatically when `_har` goes out of scope (TS `await using`)
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Route with `urlFilter` to limit HAR embedding:**

> **[community]** WHY: `content: 'embed'` in `startHar()` buffers every response body in memory before writing. For APIs that return large JSON arrays or binary blobs, this can cause OOM on long test runs. Use `content: 'omit'` for binaries and `urlFilter` to restrict capture to the API paths you actually need. The HAR file size is roughly 1.5–3× the total network data when bodies are embedded.

**Network throttling via route delay (CDP pattern for Chromium):**

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows skeleton loading on slow network', async ({ page, context }) => {
  // Simulate 2G-like conditions via route delay (all browsers)
  await page.route('**/api/**', async route => {
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500));  // 1.5s latency
    await route.continue();
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Loading skeleton should be visible before data arrives
  await expect(page.getByTestId('skeleton-loader')).toBeVisible();
  // Data should eventually appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });
});
```

---

### Trace Viewer — Advanced Usage

The Trace Viewer captures a complete record of every test action, DOM snapshot, network request, and console log. Use it as your primary CI debugging tool — it eliminates the need for `console.log` debugging.

**Recommended tracing configuration:**

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  use: {
    trace:       'on-first-retry',        // capture on first retry, not every run
    screenshot:  'only-on-failure',       // supplement trace with failure screenshot
    video:       'retain-on-failure',     // video only when test fails
  },
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,       // retries enable trace capture in CI
});
```

**Storage-efficient CI mode (v1.49+):**

```typescript
use: {
  screenshot: 'on-first-failure',  // saves one screenshot per test, not per retry
  trace:      'on-first-retry',
}
```

**Programmatic trace control with grouping (v1.49 `tracing.group/groupEnd`):**

```typescript
test('checkout flow', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });

  await context.tracing.group('Add to cart');
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add Widget' }).click();
  await context.tracing.groupEnd();

  await context.tracing.group('Checkout');
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();
  await context.tracing.groupEnd();

  await context.tracing.stop({ path: 'test-results/checkout-trace.zip' });
});
```

**Live tracing (v1.59 `tracing.start({ live: true })`):**

```typescript
// Trace updates in real time during test execution — visible in UI Mode
await context.tracing.start({
  live:        true,   // push updates to Trace Viewer in real time
  screenshots: true,
  snapshots:   true,
});
```

**Trace capture during globalSetup failures:**

```typescript
// global-setup.ts — trace setup so CI failures are debuggable
import { chromium, type FullConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default async function globalSetup(config: FullConfig) {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page    = await context.newPage();

  try {
    await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });
    await page.goto(config.projects[0].use.baseURL!);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Seed DB' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByText('Database ready')).toBeVisible();
    await context.tracing.stop();  // discard on success
  } catch (err) {
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: './test-results/setup-fail.zip' });
    throw err;
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }
}
```

> **[community]** WHY: `trace: 'on-first-retry'` is the sweet spot for CI. `trace: 'on'` inflates test run time by 15–30% due to serialization overhead, and generates gigabytes of trace files for passing tests. `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` requires two full runs of a failing test before you get a trace. `on-first-retry` with `retries: 2` gives you a trace on the second attempt, which is when the test is most likely a genuine failure.

### Test Parallelism, Sharding, and Blob Reporter

**`fullyParallel` mode — recommended for all new projects:**

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  fullyParallel: true,  // individual tests run in parallel, not just files
  workers:       process.env.CI ? 4 : undefined,  // explicit CI worker count
  use: {
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  },
});
```

**Per-project worker count (v1.52 `testProject.workers`):**

```typescript
projects: [
  { name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] }, workers: 4 },
  { name: 'webkit',   use: { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] }, workers: 2 },
  // WebKit is slower — give it fewer workers to avoid resource contention
],
```

**Sharding + blob reporter + merge-reports — the complete CI pattern:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/playwright.yml
name: Playwright Tests
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shardIndex: [1, 2, 3, 4]
        shardTotal: [4]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shardIndex }}/${{ matrix.shardTotal }}
        env:
          CI: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        if: always()
        with:
          name: blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
          path: blob-report/
          retention-days: 1

  merge-report:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: blob-report-*
          path: all-blob-reports
          merge-multiple: true
      - run: npx playwright merge-reports --reporter html ./all-blob-reports
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30
```

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — use blob reporter in CI, html locally
export default defineConfig({
  reporter: process.env.CI ? 'blob' : 'html',
  fullyParallel: true,
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Without `fullyParallel: true`, sharding distributes at file granularity — one large 50-test spec file on a single shard will dominate total wall time. Enable `fullyParallel` to distribute at test granularity, which gives even distribution across shards. The blob reporter is mandatory for the merge step; the default `html` reporter writes a directory structure that cannot be cleanly merged across machines.

**`--only-changed` flag (v1.46) — run only tests touching changed files:**

```bash
# In CI, only run tests for files changed since last commit
npx playwright test --only-changed=main

# Local: only run tests for uncommitted changes
npx playwright test --only-changed
```

**`--last-failed` flag (v1.44) — re-run only failing tests:**

```bash
npx playwright test --last-failed
```

### Global Setup / Teardown — Project Dependencies Pattern

The project dependencies approach is preferred over `globalSetup`/`globalTeardown` because it participates in the test runner lifecycle — setup failures show in HTML reports with trace support.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name:      'setup',
      testMatch: /auth\.setup\.ts/,
      teardown:  'cleanup',        // runs after all dependents finish
    },
    {
      name:      'cleanup',
      testMatch: /global\.teardown\.ts/,
    },
    {
      name:         'chromium',
      use:          {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        storageState: 'e2e/.auth/user.json',
      },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
    },
  ],
});
```

```typescript
// e2e/auth.setup.ts
import { test as setup, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

setup('authenticate user', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill(process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill(process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await expect(page).not.toHaveURL(/login/);
  await page.context().storageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/user.json' });
});
```

```typescript
// e2e/global.teardown.ts
import { test as teardown } from '@playwright/test';

teardown('clean up test data', async ({ request }) => {
  await request.delete('/api/test/cleanup');
});
```

**Multiple globalSetup/globalTeardown (v1.49):**

```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  // Accept an array — run in order
  globalSetup:    ['./global-setup-db', './global-setup-auth'],
  globalTeardown: ['./global-teardown-auth', './global-teardown-db'],
});
```

**`--no-deps` flag** — skip setup projects when debugging a specific test:

```bash
npx playwright test --no-deps tests/my-spec.ts
```

---

### Custom Assertions with `expect.extend()` + `mergeExpects()`

Centralize domain-specific assertions to reduce boilerplate and improve error messages:

```typescript
// e2e/matchers/toBeLoggedIn.ts
import { expect as baseExpect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

export const expect = baseExpect.extend({
  async toBeLoggedIn(page: Page) {
    const passed = await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign out|log out/i })
      .isVisible()
      .catch(() => false);

    return {
      pass:    passed,
      message: () => passed
        ? 'Expected page NOT to be logged in, but found sign-out button'
        : 'Expected page to be logged in, but no sign-out button found',
    };
  },

  async toHaveRowCount(locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator, count: number) {
    const actual = await locator.getByRole('row').count();
    return {
      pass:    actual === count,
      message: () => `Expected table to have ${count} rows, but found ${actual}`,
    };
  },
});
```

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/index.ts — merge matchers from multiple modules
import { mergeExpects, mergeTests } from '@playwright/test';
import { expect as a11yExpect, test as a11yTest } from './a11y';
import { expect as domainExpect, test as domainTest } from './domain';

export const expect = mergeExpects(a11yExpect, domainExpect);
export const test   = mergeTests(a11yTest, domainTest);
```

---

### Async Disposables Pattern (`await using`) — v1.60+

TypeScript 5.2+ `using` / `await using` declarations automatically invoke `[Symbol.asyncDispose]` when the variable goes out of scope. Playwright v1.60 exposes disposable APIs for HAR recording and other resources.

```typescript
test('HAR recording with automatic cleanup', async ({ context }) => {
  // `_har` is disposed at end of test — tracing.stopHar() called automatically
  await using _har = await context.tracing.startHar({ path: './test-results/test.har' });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Do test work — HAR stops when test exits, even on failure
});

// Disposable APIRequestContext — prevents context leak after use
test('isolated API requests', async () => {
  await using apiCtx = await request.newContext({
    baseURL:         'https://api.example.com',
    extraHTTPHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.API_TOKEN}` },
  });

  const res = await apiCtx.get('/users');
  expect(res.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  // apiCtx.dispose() called automatically on scope exit
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Without `await using`, forgetting `await context.tracing.stopHar()` or `await apiCtx.dispose()` causes silent resource leaks — HAR files remain open (incomplete), and API contexts accumulate across tests. TypeScript's `await using` makes cleanup a compiler-enforced guarantee. Requires `"target": "ES2022"` or later in `tsconfig.json` + `"lib": ["ES2022"]`.

---

### Additional Assertions — v1.44 to v1.52 Reference

**Accessibility assertions (v1.44):**

```typescript
// Assert computed accessible name
await expect(page.getByRole('button')).toHaveAccessibleName('Submit form');

// Assert accessible description (aria-describedby text)
await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Are you sure?');

// Assert element ARIA role
await expect(page.getByTestId('nav-toggle')).toHaveRole('button');

// aria-errormessage assertion (v1.50)
await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' }))
  .toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage('Please enter a valid email address');

// Indeterminate checkbox (v1.50)
await expect(page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all' }))
  .toBeChecked({ indeterminate: true });
```

**Class assertions (v1.52):**

```typescript
// Partial class match — does not require exact class list
await expect(page.getByRole('button')).toContainClass('btn-primary');
await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainClass('error');
```

**URL predicate assertion (v1.51):**

```typescript
// Assert URL via predicate function — more flexible than exact match
await expect(page).toHaveURL(url => url.searchParams.get('page') === '2');
await expect(page).toHaveURL(url => url.hostname === 'staging.example.com');
```

**CSS pseudo-element assertion (v1.60):**

```typescript
// Assert computed style of ::before / ::after pseudo-elements
await expect(page.getByRole('listitem').first())
  .toHaveCSS('content', '"•"', { pseudo: '::before' });

await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }))
  .toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(0, 128, 0)', { pseudo: '::after' });
```

**`toHaveCSS` — pseudo option (v1.60):**

```typescript
// Check ::placeholder color
await expect(page.getByRole('textbox'))
  .toHaveCSS('color', 'rgb(150, 150, 150)', { pseudo: '::placeholder' });
```

**`expect.configure()` — pre-configured expect instances:**

```typescript
// Slow expect for animations/transitions
const slowExpect = expect.configure({ timeout: 15_000 });
await slowExpect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

// Soft expect for multi-field validation
const softExpect = expect.configure({ soft: true });
await softExpect(page.getByTestId('name')).toHaveText('Alice');
await softExpect(page.getByTestId('role')).toHaveText('Admin');
await softExpect(page.getByTestId('status')).toHaveText('Active');
// All three are checked — test continues even if individual assertions fail
```

### `locator.describe()` — Trace-Friendly Locator Annotations (v1.53)

```typescript
// Annotate a locator for trace/report display
const saveButton = page
  .getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })
  .describe('Save draft button in editor toolbar');

await saveButton.click();
// Trace viewer shows "Save draft button in editor toolbar" instead of raw locator

// Read back the description
const description = await saveButton.description();
console.log(description);  // "Save draft button in editor toolbar"
```

> **[community]** WHY: Complex locators with multiple `.filter()` and `.and()` chains produce unreadable trace labels like `locator('button').filter(hasText: ...).and(locator(...)).nth(0)`. `locator.describe()` lets you attach a human-readable name that shows up in Trace Viewer, HTML reports, and error messages. Teams that add `.describe()` to shared POM locators report 40–60% faster debugging cycles on test failures.

---

### `browserContext.setStorageState()` — Role Switching Without New Context (v1.59)

Switch authentication state in the middle of a test without creating a new browser context:

```typescript
test('admin can view content a viewer cannot', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: 'e2e/.auth/viewer.json',
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('/admin');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Access Denied' })).toBeVisible();

  // Switch to admin role without creating a new context
  await context.setStorageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/admin.json' });
  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Admin Dashboard' })).toBeVisible();

  await context.close();
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Creating a new browser context for each role costs ~200–500 ms per switch (browser process startup + context initialization). `setStorageState()` replaces cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage in the existing context — the same browser process, in under 20 ms. Use this when a test needs to assert the same page from multiple roles without the overhead of fresh contexts.

---

### `context.isClosed()` — Teardown Guard (v1.59)

Protect fixture teardown from crashing when the browser context has already closed:

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/recording.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend<{ recordingUrl: string }>({
  recordingUrl: async ({ context }, use, testInfo) => {
    await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });
    await use('');  // expose the fixture; real URL not known until teardown

    // Guard: context may already be closed if the browser crashed
    if (!context.isClosed()) {
      const tracePath = testInfo.outputPath('trace.zip');
      await context.tracing.stop({ path: tracePath });
      await testInfo.attach('trace', { path: tracePath });
    }
  },
});
```

> **[community]** WHY: Playwright does not provide a "browser crashed" hook. When a browser tab crashes mid-test, the context closes immediately and subsequent calls to `context.tracing.stop()` or `context.storageState()` in teardown throw "Target closed" errors — which masks the original failure with a confusing secondary error. Check `context.isClosed()` before any teardown API call to keep the error signal clean.

---

### Additional Community Gotchas (Cycle 19)

---

### 56. `expect.poll()` does not reset its timer on page navigation [community]

`expect.poll()` starts a single clock when called and retries the callback until the total timeout elapses — it does not restart when the page navigates mid-poll.

```typescript
// ❌ Fragile: if page navigates during poll, the total budget is already consumed
await expect.poll(async () => {
  const res = await page.request.get('/api/job-status');
  return (await res.json()).status;
}, { timeout: 30_000 }).toBe('completed');

// ✅ Prefer page-level wait when the response is a page element
await expect(page.getByTestId('job-status')).toHaveText('completed', { timeout: 30_000 });

// ✅ Or use expect.toPass() with explicit intervals for API polling
await expect(async () => {
  const res  = await page.request.get('/api/job-status');
  const body = await res.json();
  expect(body.status).toBe('completed');
}).toPass({ intervals: [1000, 2000, 5000], timeout: 30_000 });
```

> **WHY:** `expect.poll()` is designed for values that can be polled without side effects (e.g., API status checks). When the page navigates before the poll resolves, the subsequent request may target a different URL, silently returning unexpected data. Use `toHaveText` for DOM-visible state and `expect.toPass()` with explicit `intervals` for API polling — the latter's `intervals` array controls back-off, giving slow jobs room to breathe without hammering the server. [community]

---

### 57. `page.getByRole()` with `description` option (v1.60) does not match `aria-label` — only `aria-describedby` [community]

The new `description` option on `getByRole` (v1.60) filters by computed accessible description, which comes from `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, or tooltip text — not from `aria-label` or the element's text content.

```typescript
// HTML: <button aria-label="Close dialog" aria-describedby="close-hint">X</button>
//       <span id="close-hint">This will discard unsaved changes</span>

// ❌ Does NOT match — `description` is not `aria-label`
await page.getByRole('button', { description: 'Close dialog' }).click();

// ✅ Correct — matches aria-describedby content
await page.getByRole('button', { description: 'This will discard unsaved changes' }).click();

// ✅ Use `name` for aria-label matching
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close dialog' }).click();
```

> **WHY:** W3C ARIA separates "accessible name" (what the element IS) from "accessible description" (additional context). `aria-label` contributes to the name, not the description. Confusing the two produces locators that silently match nothing, causing "strict mode violation" or timeout errors with an opaque message. [community]

---

### 58. `tracing.startHar()` with `urlFilter` — filter is a glob, not a regex [community]

The `urlFilter` option accepts a glob pattern (like `**/api/**`), not a regular expression. Passing a regex literal silently converts to a string representation and matches almost nothing.

```typescript
// ❌ Silently wrong: regex.toString() is '/\/api\//i' — a glob matching a literal slash
await context.tracing.startHar({
  path:      './fixtures/api.har',
  urlFilter: /\/api\//i as any,  // TypeScript will warn, but JS users are unprotected
});

// ✅ Correct: use glob syntax
await context.tracing.startHar({
  path:      './fixtures/api.har',
  urlFilter: '**/api/**',        // matches any URL with /api/ in the path
});
```

> **WHY:** The HAR API surface mirrors `page.route()` glob syntax, not JavaScript RegExp. There is no runtime error when a regex is passed — it simply produces an empty HAR file because no URLs match the stringified regex pattern. If your HAR file is unexpectedly empty, check your `urlFilter`. [community]

---

### 59. `locator.normalize()` prefers `getByTestId` over `getByRole` for interactive elements with `data-testid` [community]

`locator.normalize()` (v1.59) refactors a locator to the recommended selector form. However, when an element has both a role and a `data-testid`, `normalize()` returns `getByTestId` — which couples tests to implementation attributes rather than semantics.

```typescript
// <button data-testid="submit-btn" aria-label="Submit form">Submit</button>

const raw = page.locator('[data-testid="submit-btn"]');
const normalized = await raw.normalize();
// Returns: page.getByTestId('submit-btn')  ← correct but semantic-free

// Prefer explicit getByRole when the element has a clear accessible name:
const semantic = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit form' });
// This locator survives data-testid renames and is more resilient
```

> **WHY:** `normalize()` is a refactoring tool, not a test-quality oracle. Its output reflects the locator that Playwright's codegen engine generates, which prioritizes test IDs over roles when both are available. For long-lived test suites, role-based locators are more resilient — data-testid values are removed or renamed far more often than ARIA roles and labels. Use `normalize()` output as a starting point, then prefer semantic alternatives. [community]

---

### 60. `worker.on('console')` captures service worker messages — not regular page console [community]

`worker.on('console')` (v1.57) is emitted by the Service Worker object returned from `context.serviceWorkers()` or the `context.on('serviceworker')` event — not from regular page JavaScript console calls.

```typescript
// ❌ Common misuse: expecting page console messages via worker
page.on('console', msg => console.log('page console:', msg.text()));
// This works fine for page scripts

// ✅ Correct: listen to service worker console separately
context.on('serviceworker', worker => {
  worker.on('console', msg => {
    console.log(`[SW] ${msg.type()}: ${msg.text()}`);
  });
});

await page.goto('/');  // SW registers, console events flow through `worker`
```

> **WHY:** Service Workers run in a separate thread with their own console. When debugging PWA caching or background sync issues, `page.on('console')` will never show SW log output — making SW bugs look like silent failures. Always attach the `worker.on('console')` listener before `goto()` if your app registers a Service Worker on load. [community]

---

### 61. `test.abort()` cannot be called from inside `test.step()` body directly — use the step's return value [community]

`test.abort(message)` (v1.60) aborts the current test immediately. When called inside a `test.step()` callback, Playwright throws an internal "test already aborted" error if the step's promise is not properly awaited.

```typescript
// ❌ Calling abort inside an un-awaited step causes confusing errors
test('checkout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  test.step('validate cart', async () => {
    if (!(await page.getByTestId('cart-count').isVisible())) {
      test.abort('Cart is empty — cannot proceed to checkout');
    }
  });  // step promise not awaited → abort races with step completion

  // ✅ Correct: always await test.step()
  await test.step('validate cart', async () => {
    if (!(await page.getByTestId('cart-count').isVisible())) {
      test.abort('Cart is empty — cannot proceed to checkout');
    }
  });
  // If abort fires, subsequent steps are skipped automatically
  await test.step('complete checkout', async () => { /* ... */ });
});
```

> **WHY:** `test.abort()` transitions the test into "aborted" state immediately. If the enclosing step's Promise is not awaited, the step continues executing after the abort signal is sent, producing a race between the abort signal and step cleanup. Always `await` every `test.step()` call — this is a general rule that also prevents silent step failures from being swallowed. [community]

---

### 62. `page.requestGC()` only detects leaks in Chromium — silently no-ops in Firefox/WebKit [community]

`page.requestGC()` (v1.48) triggers garbage collection to expose memory leaks (e.g., detached DOM nodes, retained closures). It is Chromium-only and silently resolves without effect in Firefox and WebKit.

```typescript
test('no detached DOM after modal close', async ({ page, browserName }) => {
  test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'requestGC is Chromium-only');

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }).click();

  // Force GC to clear references before checking heap
  await page.requestGC();

  // Evaluate heap for detached DOM nodes
  const leaked = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return (window as any).__testLeakCount ?? 0;
  });
  expect(leaked).toBe(0);
});
```

> **WHY:** Running `requestGC()` without a `browserName` guard produces passing tests in all browsers — because Firefox and WebKit never GC and never trigger the leak check. This creates a false sense of confidence. Always guard with `test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', ...)` to make the cross-browser limitation explicit. [community]

### Test Data Factory Pattern — TypeScript Implementation

The "Test Data Factory" section heading exists in the document but the implementation was deferred. Here is the complete TypeScript pattern for creating type-safe, parallel-safe test data with overrides.

Use a factory module to generate unique, collision-free test objects. The key design goal is **parallel safety**: each invocation returns unique identifiers based on a passed `testId` or `Date.now()` suffix, so concurrent workers never share data.

```typescript
// e2e/factories/user.factory.ts
import type { TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';

export interface UserData {
  email:     string;
  username:  string;
  password:  string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName:  string;
  role:      'admin' | 'viewer' | 'editor';
}

/**
 * Creates a parallel-safe user object.
 * Pass `testInfo` to make the email unique per test; omit to use a timestamp suffix.
 */
export function createUser(
  overrides: Partial<UserData> = {},
  testInfo?: TestInfo,
): UserData {
  const suffix = testInfo?.testId ?? Date.now().toString(36);
  return {
    email:     `test-${suffix}@example.com`,
    username:  `testuser-${suffix}`,
    password:  'Test@12345',
    firstName: 'Test',
    lastName:  'User',
    role:      'viewer',
    ...overrides,
  };
}

export function createAdmin(testInfo?: TestInfo): UserData {
  return createUser({ role: 'admin', firstName: 'Admin', lastName: 'User' }, testInfo);
}
```

```typescript
// e2e/specs/user-management.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { createUser, createAdmin } from '../factories/user.factory';

test('creates a viewer account', async ({ page, request }, testInfo) => {
  const user = createUser({}, testInfo);             // unique per test run

  await request.post('/api/users', { data: user });
  await page.goto('/admin/users');
  await expect(page.getByText(user.email)).toBeVisible();
});

test('admin can promote viewer to editor', async ({ page, request }, testInfo) => {
  const viewer = createUser({ role: 'viewer' }, testInfo);
  const admin  = createAdmin(testInfo);

  await request.post('/api/users', { data: viewer });
  await request.post('/api/users', { data: admin  });

  // ... promote viewer, assert new role
});
```

**Generic factory with Partial overrides typing:**

```typescript
// e2e/factories/index.ts — generic builder helper
type DeepPartial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] extends object ? DeepPartial<T[K]> : T[K] };

export function build<T>(defaults: T) {
  return (overrides: DeepPartial<T> = {}): T => ({
    ...defaults,
    ...overrides,
  });
}

// Usage:
const buildProduct = build({
  id:       '',
  name:     'Test Widget',
  price:    9.99,
  category: 'general' as const,
  inStock:  true,
});

const product = buildProduct({ name: 'Custom Widget', price: 14.99 });
```

> **[community]** WHY: Using `testInfo.testId` (not `Date.now()`) as the uniqueness suffix is critical in `fullyParallel` mode — multiple tests can start within the same millisecond on fast machines, causing `Date.now()` collisions. `testInfo.testId` is guaranteed unique per test regardless of timing. Always pass `testInfo` to factory calls inside the test body. [community]

---

### JUnit Reporter — Advanced CI Configuration

The JUnit reporter has several options that are undocumented in the basic patterns but make a significant difference in CI analytics systems (Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, TeamCity, GitLab).

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — JUnit with full CI options
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['junit', {
      outputFile:                  'test-results/results.xml',
      stripANSIControlSequences:   true,    // clean ANSI codes from failure messages
      includeProjectInTestName:    true,    // prepends project name: "chromium > test title"
      suiteName:                   'E2E Tests',
      suiteId:                     'e2e',   // id attribute on <testsuites> element
    }],
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['blob'],
  ],
});
```

**Why each option matters:**

- **`stripANSIControlSequences: true`** — Without this, failure messages in Jenkins/Azure show raw escape codes like `\x1b[31mError\x1b[0m`. Jenkins XML parsers and most test result viewers treat them as literal characters, not formatting.
- **`includeProjectInTestName: true`** — In multi-browser projects (chromium, firefox, webkit), two tests with the same title from different projects collide in JUnit XML without this option. Azure Pipelines deduplicates by test name and loses one result. Enable this for any project with more than one browser.
- **`suiteName` / `suiteId`** — Used by TeamCity and GitLab to group results into logical suites. Set `suiteId` to a stable identifier — avoid timestamps.

**Shard-aware JUnit output** (combine with merge-reports):

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — per-shard output in CI
reporter: process.env.CI
  ? [
      ['blob'],
      ['junit', {
        outputFile:               `test-results/results-shard${process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? '0'}.xml`,
        stripANSIControlSequences: true,
        includeProjectInTestName:  true,
      }],
    ]
  : 'html',
```

> **[community]** WHY: When multiple shards write to the same `results.xml` path in a shared artifact directory, they overwrite each other — only the last shard's results appear in the final report. Use a shard-indexed filename and merge XML files in a post-merge step (e.g., `junit-report-merger` npm package or `xunit-viewer`). [community]

---

### HTML Reporter — Full Options Reference

The HTML reporter's full option set is rarely documented together. Here is the complete picture:

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — HTML reporter with all options
reporter: [
  ['html', {
    open:                'never',            // 'always' | 'never' | 'on-failure' (local DX)
    outputFolder:        'playwright-report', // output directory
    noSnippets:          true,               // omit source code from logs (v1.54+)
    noCopyPrompt:        false,              // hide "Copy prompt" button (v1.54+)
    doNotInlineAssets:   false,              // write separate JS/CSS files (CSP compliance)
    attachmentsBaseURL:  process.env.CI
      ? 'https://storage.example.com/test-artifacts/'
      : undefined,                           // remote URL prefix for attachments
  }],
],
```

**`attachmentsBaseURL` — remote attachment hosting:**

When storing Playwright reports in S3 or Azure Blob Storage, use `attachmentsBaseURL` to make trace, screenshot, and video links in the report resolve against the remote storage origin rather than relative local paths.

```typescript
// CI workflow — configure before running tests
// ATTACHMENTS_BASE_URL = 'https://my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pw-artifacts/'

reporter: [
  ['html', {
    open:               'never',
    attachmentsBaseURL: process.env.ATTACHMENTS_BASE_URL,
  }],
],
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/playwright.yml — upload attachments then report
- name: Upload artifacts to S3
  run: |
    aws s3 sync test-results/ \
      s3://my-bucket/pw-artifacts/${{ github.run_id }}/

- name: Generate HTML report
  env:
    ATTACHMENTS_BASE_URL: >-
      https://my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pw-artifacts/${{ github.run_id }}/
  run: npx playwright merge-reports --reporter html ./all-blob-reports
```

> **[community]** WHY: HTML reporter links are relative by default. When you upload the report HTML to S3 but the attachment blobs to a different bucket or prefix, all trace/screenshot links in the report become broken. `attachmentsBaseURL` rewrites these links at report-generation time. Set it to the public or pre-signed URL prefix for the artifact storage. [community]

> **[community]** `doNotInlineAssets: true` is required when your CI artifact server enforces a strict Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline `<script>` and `<style>`. Without it, the HTML report opens a blank page under CSP-strict environments (e.g., some enterprise GitHub Enterprise instances). [community]

### `expect.poll()` with Custom `intervals` Backoff

`expect.poll()` accepts an `intervals` array that defines the wait times between retry attempts. This enables exponential backoff for long-running or eventually-consistent operations.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Standard poll — useful for quickly-settling state
await expect.poll(() => page.locator('[data-status]').textContent(), {
  timeout:   10_000,
  intervals: [500, 1_000, 2_000],  // retry after 500ms, 1s, 2s, then 2s repeatedly
}).toBe('ready');

// Exponential backoff for slow background jobs
await expect.poll(
  async () => {
    const res  = await page.request.get('/api/jobs/42/status');
    const body = await res.json() as { state: string };
    return body.state;
  },
  {
    timeout:   60_000,
    intervals: [1_000, 2_000, 4_000, 8_000, 16_000],
    message:   'Background job did not reach "complete" within 60s',
  },
).toBe('complete');

// Poll a DOM property until it changes
const getCount = () => page.evaluate(() => document.querySelectorAll('[data-item]').length);
await expect.poll(getCount, {
  timeout:   30_000,
  intervals: [200, 500, 1_000],
}).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```

**`expect.poll()` vs `locator.waitFor()` — decision table:**

| Use case | Best API |
|----------|---------|
| DOM element visibility | `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` |
| DOM element property value | `await expect(locator).toHaveText() / toHaveValue()` |
| Arbitrary async condition (API call, DB check) | `expect.poll(async fn, opts)` |
| Complex multi-step condition | `expect(async () => { ... }).toPass()` |
| One-shot "wait until visible then continue" | `locator.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` |

> **[community]** WHY: `expect.poll()` retries the entire async function on each interval — not just the assertion. This means expensive operations (network calls, large `evaluate()` calls) run on every retry. Keep the polled function cheap: extract a single scalar value rather than an entire page snapshot. If the polled function itself is slow, widen the `intervals` to avoid triggering a new call before the previous one resolves. [community]

---

### `locator.highlight()` and `page.hideHighlight()` — Interactive Debugging (v1.60+)

`locator.highlight({ style? })` draws a visual overlay on the matched element(s) with an optional custom CSS style. `page.hideHighlight()` removes all highlights. Both are useful in headed debugging sessions and in video recordings for attention-drawing.

```typescript
// Highlight with default style (bright green border)
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).highlight();
await page.waitForTimeout(2_000);  // pause for visual confirmation
await page.hideHighlight();

// Highlight with custom CSS — red dashed border with label
await page.getByRole('alert').highlight({
  style: 'outline: 3px dashed red; background: rgba(255,0,0,0.1);',
});

// Highlight multiple elements for visual diff recordings
test('visually verify two locators resolve to different elements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Highlight both candidates, screenshot for review
  const primaryBtn   = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' });
  const secondaryBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' });

  await primaryBtn.highlight({ style: 'outline: 3px solid green;' });
  await secondaryBtn.highlight({ style: 'outline: 3px solid orange;' });
  await page.screenshot({ path: 'test-results/selector-debug.png' });

  await page.hideHighlight();
});
```

**Usage in CI — disable highlights to avoid artifact pollution:**

```typescript
// Only highlight in non-CI environments
if (!process.env.CI) {
  await locator.highlight();
}
```

> **[community]** WHY: `locator.highlight()` does not affect test assertions — it is purely visual. However, leaving highlights in place when taking `toHaveScreenshot()` baseline images will cause those baselines to include the overlay, making all subsequent assertion-only runs fail. Always call `page.hideHighlight()` before any visual assertion or screenshot capture. [community]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 20)

### 63. `browserContext.setStorageState()` does NOT clear `sessionStorage` [community]

`browserContext.setStorageState()` (v1.59) replaces cookies, localStorage, and IndexedDB — but **sessionStorage is not included in the storageState format** and is not cleared. If your application writes session-specific flags to `sessionStorage` during the first role's session, those flags persist after switching roles.

```typescript
// ❌ Assuming setStorageState clears all session state
await page.context().setStorageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/admin.json' });
// sessionStorage from the previous role may still be present

// ✅ Correct: clear sessionStorage manually before switching roles
await page.evaluate(() => window.sessionStorage.clear());
await page.context().setStorageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/admin.json' });
await page.reload();  // trigger app re-init with new credentials
```

> **WHY:** `sessionStorage` is domain-specific and tab-specific but not managed by Playwright's auth system. When `setStorageState()` loads admin credentials into an existing context, any `sessionStorage` keys written by the previous user identity are still present. Auth flows that cache user metadata in `sessionStorage` (e.g., user role, feature flags) will serve stale data until the application re-initializes on the next navigation. [community]

---

### 64. Fixture teardown ordering is `lifo` within the same scope — not insertion order [community]

Playwright tears down fixtures in **last-in-first-out (LIFO)** order. If two test-scoped fixtures are declared in the same `base.extend()` call, the second-declared fixture's teardown runs before the first-declared fixture's teardown. This matters when one fixture depends on another during cleanup.

```typescript
// ❌ Assumes teardown runs in declaration order (alphabetical / insertion)
const test = base.extend<{ dbRecord: string; page: Page }>({
  dbRecord: async ({ request }, use) => {
    const id = await createRecord(request);  // setup
    await use(id);
    await deleteRecord(request, id);          // teardown — but page may already be closed!
  },
  page: async ({ browser }, use) => {
    const p = await browser.newPage();
    await use(p);
    await p.close();   // runs first (LIFO) — before dbRecord teardown
  },
});

// ✅ Correct: declare dependent fixtures so teardown order is safe
// Make dbRecord depend on page — Playwright tears down dbRecord before page
const test = base.extend<{ dbRecord: string }>({
  dbRecord: async ({ page, request }, use) => {
    // dbRecord depends on page → its teardown runs BEFORE page's teardown
    const id = await createRecord(request);
    await use(id);
    await deleteRecord(request, id);  // safe — page is still open here
  },
});
```

> **WHY:** Playwright determines fixture teardown order from the **dependency graph**, not declaration order. If two fixtures are peers (neither depends on the other), their teardown order is LIFO within the same scope. When teardown of fixture A requires fixture B to still be alive (e.g., making an API call through an open page), declare A as depending on B to enforce the correct teardown sequence. [community]
