### 65. `noCopyPrompt: false` on `html` reporter leaks source code in screenshots if reporter is included in artifacts [community]

The HTML reporter's "Copy prompt" button (enabled by default when `noCopyPrompt` is not set to `true`) includes a full AI-prompt payload containing the failing test's source code, test title, and error message. When the reporter HTML is included in public CI artifacts (GitHub Actions public repos), anyone can read the source code via the copy prompt.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — suppress copy prompts in public repos
reporter: [
  ['html', {
    open:          'never',
    noCopyPrompt:  true,   // removes the "Copy prompt" button from all failure entries
  }],
],
```

> **WHY:** The "Copy prompt" feature formats failure context for AI assistants. In private CI, this is a productivity win. In public repositories (open-source projects, contractor work), it exposes test implementation details and application logic to anyone who downloads the HTML report artifact. Set `noCopyPrompt: true` in any project where the Playwright HTML report is accessible outside the team. [community]

### `page.clock.pauseAt()` + `resume()` — Pause-and-Inspect Pattern (v1.45+)

`pauseAt()` jumps to a specific future time and freezes the clock there. Timers that were due during the jump fire **at most once** and then stop. `resume()` restarts real-time progression from that frozen moment. This is the correct pattern for testing "snapshot-at-a-moment" scenarios (session expiry warnings, countdown displays, scheduled job previews) where you want to land at a precise moment and then run assertions before time moves again.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/session-expiry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows session expiry warning at T-60 seconds', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install clock BEFORE goto — see Gotcha #31
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Jump to 60 seconds before session expiry (session = 30 minutes)
  // pauseAt fires timers due during the jump once each, then freezes
  await page.clock.pauseAt(new Date('2026-01-01T10:29:00Z'));

  // Clock is now frozen at 10:29:00 — the expiry warning should appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText('1 minute')).toBeVisible();

  // Advance 30 more seconds with runFor() to test the countdown update
  await page.clock.runFor(30_000);
  await expect(page.getByText('30 seconds')).toBeVisible();

  // Resume real time — let the app finish its own cleanup
  await page.clock.resume();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session expired/i })).toBeVisible({
    timeout: 70_000,  // real time resumes; give it generous budget
  });
});
```

**`pauseAt()` vs `runFor()` decision table:**

| Goal | Use | Why |
|------|-----|-----|
| Land at a specific future moment and freeze | `pauseAt(targetTime)` | Fires each due timer once; page state reflects that exact moment |
| Simulate continuous time passing (e.g., polling, chained `setTimeout`) | `runFor(ms)` or `tick(ms)` | Invokes each timer callback in sequence as time progresses |
| Freeze `Date.now()` without touching timers at all | `setFixedTime(time)` | Only affects date-reading code; timers still run on real schedule |
| Shift system clock without re-running due timers | `setSystemTime(time)` | Timezone/DST testing; safe after `page.goto()` |

> **[community]** Teams that use `pauseAt()` to test countdown timers often find that `runFor()` fires the countdown callback multiple times — once per tick interval — producing the correct countdown sequence but at 0-ms speed. If your countdown has debounce logic (fires only once per second), `pauseAt()` lands more accurately at a single snapshot without triggering multiple callbacks. Reserve `runFor()` for timer chains where you need every intermediate state.

### Comprehensive `route.fetch()` Modify-Response Pattern

The `route.fetch()` → modify → `route.fulfill({ response, json })` pipeline intercepts real API calls and surgically patches their response. This is more powerful than `route.fulfill()` alone (which fully mocks the response) because it preserves real response headers, cookies, and status codes while injecting test-specific data overrides.

```typescript
// e2e/utils/routeModifiers.ts — reusable response patch utility
import { type Page, type Route, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

type Patcher<T> = (data: T) => T;

/**
 * Intercept a URL and patch the JSON response body before it reaches the app.
 * All other fields (headers, status, cookies) are preserved from the real server.
 */
export async function patchJsonResponse<T>(
  page: Page,
  urlGlob: string,
  patcher: Patcher<T>,
): Promise<void> {
  await page.route(urlGlob, async (route: Route) => {
    // Fetch the real response from the upstream server
    const real: APIResponse = await route.fetch();
    const body = await real.json() as T;

    // Apply the patch — caller controls what changes
    const patched = patcher(body);

    // Fulfill with the real response + patched body
    // Playwright merges: status/headers from `response`, body from `json`
    await route.fulfill({ response: real, json: patched });
  });
}
```

```typescript
// e2e/specs/feature-flags.spec.ts — inject a feature flag into a real API response
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/pages';
import { patchJsonResponse } from '../utils/routeModifiers';

test('shows beta banner when feature flag is enabled', async ({ page }) => {
  // Enable a feature flag that is OFF in the test environment
  await patchJsonResponse<{ flags: Record<string, boolean> }>(
    page,
    '**/api/v1/config',
    (config) => ({
      ...config,
      flags: { ...config.flags, betaBanner: true },
    }),
  );

  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('banner', { name: /beta/i })).toBeVisible();
});

test('injects extra item into paginated list without changing pagination metadata', async ({ page }) => {
  await patchJsonResponse<{ items: Array<{ id: number; name: string }>; total: number }>(
    page,
    '**/api/v1/products?page=1*',
    (body) => ({
      ...body,
      items: [{ id: 9999, name: 'Test Product' }, ...body.items],
    }),
  );

  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByText('Test Product')).toBeVisible();
  // Pagination metadata unchanged — total still reflects real server value
});
```

**Conditional pass-through (only patch matching records):**

```typescript
await page.route('**/api/orders/**', async (route) => {
  const response = await route.fetch();
  const order = await response.json() as { id: string; status: string };

  // Only patch orders with a specific ID — pass all others through unchanged
  if (order.id !== 'ORDER-007') {
    await route.fulfill({ response });
    return;
  }

  await route.fulfill({
    response,
    json: { ...order, status: 'pending_approval' },
  });
});
```

> **[community]** `route.fetch()` is safe to call multiple times in the same handler for retries, but do NOT chain it — a second `route.fetch()` after the first one resolved creates a second live request to the server. If you need the body twice (e.g., for logging and patching), store it in a variable:
> ```typescript
> const real = await route.fetch();
> const body = await real.json();
> console.log('original:', body);
> await route.fulfill({ response: real, json: { ...body, patched: true } });
> ```

### `reporter.onError(error, workerInfo)` — Worker-Attributed Error Handling (v1.60+)

Before v1.60, `reporter.onError()` received only an error object. It was impossible to tell which worker crashed. v1.60 added `workerInfo` as the second argument, enabling per-worker error attribution — critical for diagnosing which parallel worker caused a fixture teardown failure.

```typescript
// e2e/reporters/worker-error-reporter.ts
import type { Reporter, TestError, WorkerInfo } from '@playwright/test/reporter';

class WorkerErrorReporter implements Reporter {
  private workerErrors: Map<number, TestError[]> = new Map();

  onError(error: TestError, workerInfo?: WorkerInfo): void {
    if (!workerInfo) {
      // Pre-v1.60 or non-worker error (e.g., global setup)
      console.error('[global] Test error:', error.message);
      return;
    }

    const { workerIndex, parallelIndex } = workerInfo;
    const bucket = this.workerErrors.get(workerIndex) ?? [];
    bucket.push(error);
    this.workerErrors.set(workerIndex, bucket);

    console.error(
      `[worker-${workerIndex} (parallel-${parallelIndex})] Error:`,
      error.message,
      error.stack?.split('\n').slice(0, 3).join('\n'),
    );
  }

  onEnd(): void {
    const totalErrors = [...this.workerErrors.values()].reduce((sum, arr) => sum + arr.length, 0);
    if (totalErrors > 0) {
      console.error(`\nWorker error summary: ${totalErrors} errors across ${this.workerErrors.size} workers`);
      for (const [workerIndex, errors] of this.workerErrors) {
        console.error(`  Worker ${workerIndex}: ${errors.length} error(s)`);
      }
    }
  }
}

export default WorkerErrorReporter;
```

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — register alongside built-in reporters
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['html'],
    ['./e2e/reporters/worker-error-reporter.ts'],
  ],
});
```

**`WorkerInfo` interface reference (v1.60+):**

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `workerIndex` | `number` | Unique worker index (0-based, stable per run) |
| `parallelIndex` | `number` | Index within the parallel group |
| `project` | `FullProject` | The project this worker belongs to |

> **[community]** `workerInfo` is `undefined` for errors thrown in `globalSetup`/`globalTeardown` because those don't run in a worker context. Always guard with a null check before accessing `workerInfo.workerIndex` to avoid crashes in your reporter when global setup fails. [community]

### `apiRequestContext.fetch()` with `maxRetries` — Resilient API Assertions (v1.46+)

Test environments are inherently less stable than production — internal APIs occasionally return transient 5xx errors. `maxRetries` retries the request up to N times before failing, eliminating flaky API tests caused by transient upstream errors.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/api/health.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('health endpoint returns 200 after retries', async ({ request }) => {
  // Retry up to 3 times on network errors or non-2xx responses
  // Default behavior: retries on ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, 5xx status codes
  const response = await request.get('/api/health', {
    maxRetries: 3,
  });
  expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  const body = await response.json();
  expect(body.status).toBe('healthy');
});

// Use in fixtures for the full suite
// e2e/fixtures/api.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend<{ resilientRequest: typeof base.prototype.request }>({
  resilientRequest: async ({ playwright }, use) => {
    const context = await playwright.request.newContext({
      baseURL: process.env.API_BASE_URL,
      // maxRetries on context level applies to all requests in this context
    });
    await use(context);
    await context.dispose();
  },
});

// Per-request override
const response = await request.post('/api/users', {
  data: { email: 'test@example.com' },
  maxRetries: 2,
  timeout: 10_000,
});
```

> **[community]** `maxRetries` retries on network-level errors (`ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, timeouts) AND on 408/429/500/502/503/504 status codes — but NOT on 4xx client errors (400, 401, 403, 404). A retry on a 404 would silently mask a broken API contract. If you need to retry on specific status codes beyond the default set, use `expect.poll()` or a manual retry loop with `request.get()`. [community]

### `locator.contentFrame()` and `frameLocator.owner()` — Frame/Locator Round-Trip (v1.43+)

`locator.contentFrame()` converts a `<iframe>` Locator into a `FrameLocator`, enabling you to operate on its content. `frameLocator.owner()` reverses the conversion — getting the `<iframe>` Locator back from a `FrameLocator`. This is essential when you need to assert on the frame element itself (e.g., visibility, size, attributes) while also interacting with its content.

```typescript
// Pattern: interact with iframe content AND assert on the frame element itself
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('payment iframe is loaded and accepts card number', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Locate the frame element first
  const iframeLocator = page.frameLocator('#payment-frame').owner();

  // Assert on the frame element (size, visibility, data attributes)
  await expect(iframeLocator).toBeVisible();
  await expect(iframeLocator).toHaveAttribute('data-loaded', 'true');

  // Now get the FrameLocator to interact with frame content
  const frame = iframeLocator.contentFrame();
  await frame.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242 4242 4242 4242');
  await frame.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/30');
  await frame.getByLabel('CVC').fill('123');

  // Verify a value inside the frame
  await expect(frame.getByLabel('Card number')).toHaveValue('4242 4242 4242 4242');
});

test('dynamically loaded iframe becomes visible before interaction', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/embed');

  const iframeEl = page.locator('iframe[data-testid="embed-frame"]');

  // Wait for the frame element to load before entering
  await expect(iframeEl).toBeAttached();

  // Convert Locator → FrameLocator using contentFrame()
  const frameLocator = iframeEl.contentFrame();

  await expect(frameLocator.getByRole('heading')).toBeVisible();
});
```

> **[community]** Before v1.43, teams had to use `page.frame({ name: '...' })` or `page.frames().find(...)` to get a frame reference, and then manually correlate it with the DOM element via `frame.frameElement()`. The `contentFrame()`/`owner()` round-trip is cleaner and locator-chain compatible — the `FrameLocator` propagates selector re-evaluation correctly across navigation events. [community]

## Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 22 Additions

### 66. `clock.pauseAt()` fires each due timer once — `runFor()` fires them on every interval [community]

**What:** Tests using `page.clock.pauseAt()` to advance time by 5 minutes find that a `setInterval(fn, 60_000)` callback fires only once (at the 1-minute mark), not five times (once per minute). The same test using `page.clock.runFor(300_000)` correctly fires the callback five times.

```typescript
// ❌ If you need all 5 interval ticks, pauseAt() is wrong
await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z') });
await page.goto('/live-feed');
await page.clock.pauseAt(new Date('2026-01-01T10:05:00Z'));
// live-feed refresh fires only ONCE — the app thinks 5 minutes passed instantly
// and fires the timer once at the boundary, not once per minute

// ✅ Use runFor() to fire the timer once per interval
await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z') });
await page.goto('/live-feed');
await page.clock.runFor(300_000); // fires interval callback 5 times (1m, 2m, 3m, 4m, 5m)
await expect(page.getByText('Refreshed 5 times')).toBeVisible();
```

> **WHY:** `pauseAt()` is modeled after "skipping to a point in time" semantics — each timer fires **at most once** during the jump regardless of how many intervals fit in the elapsed duration. `runFor()` advances the clock in the smallest increment of pending timer deadlines, invoking each callback before moving forward, which replicates the real-time behavior of multiple interval ticks. Choose `pauseAt()` for snapshot-at-moment tests (e.g., session expiry at exactly T=29min); choose `runFor()` for timer-sequence tests (e.g., polling refreshed N times in M minutes). [community]

---

### 67. Route URL glob patterns lost `?` and `[]` support in v1.52 — query strings in globs break silently [community]

**What:** Glob patterns in `page.route()` and `context.route()` that used `?` (match any single character) or `[...]` (character class) to match URL query parameters now match those characters **literally** as of Playwright v1.52. A route like `'**/api/users?active=true'` no longer matches requests to `/api/users?active=true` — it only matches a URL where the query part is literally the string `?active=true` including the `?`.

```typescript
// ❌ Broken in v1.52+: ? is now a literal match
await page.route('**/api/users?role=admin', route => route.fulfill({ json: [] }));
// This route NEVER matches — requests to /api/users?role=admin are not intercepted

// ✅ Use a wildcard that matches the query separator
await page.route('**/api/users*', async route => {
  const url = new URL(route.request().url());
  if (url.searchParams.get('role') === 'admin') {
    await route.fulfill({ json: [] });
  } else {
    await route.continue();
  }
});

// ✅ Or use a regex pattern instead of a glob
await page.route(/\/api\/users\?role=admin/, route => route.fulfill({ json: [] }));
```

> **WHY:** Playwright v1.52 tightened glob semantics so `?` and `[]` no longer act as regex-style wildcards in URL globs. This prevents accidental over-matching where `?` in a query parameter was interpreted as "any character" and inadvertently matched unrelated URLs. Teams that relied on the old behavior will find their route handlers silently stop matching after upgrading — no error is thrown, requests just pass through to the real server. [community]

---

### 68. `expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` captures the full page tree — includes off-screen and hidden-but-attached content [community]

**What:** `expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` (page-level, v1.60+) generates an aria snapshot from the **entire accessibility tree** of the page, not just what is visible in the viewport. An element with `visibility: hidden` or `display: none` is excluded, but elements that are merely out of the scroll viewport — or elements in a `<details>` element that is closed — are still included in the snapshot.

```typescript
// ❌ Assumes page snapshot matches only visible viewport
await expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
  - heading "Active Products" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem: "Product A"
`);
// FAILS: snapshot also includes archived products from the same page
// that are below the fold inside a collapsed <details> section

// ✅ Use locator-based snapshot to scope to a specific region
await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
  - heading "Active Products" [level=2]
`);

// ✅ Or assert the full tree with the full snapshot (update baseline)
// npx playwright test --update-snapshots
await expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot();
```

> **WHY:** The accessibility tree is a DOM-level construct and does not respect scroll position. `<details>` sections render their closed children as hidden in the ARIA tree only when they are explicitly `hidden` — a `<details closed>` element's `<summary>` IS included in the snapshot. Teams upgrading from locator-based `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` to page-level assertions frequently see baseline mismatches because the page tree is much wider than the locator subtree they were previously testing. [community]

---

### 69. `apiRequestContext.fetch()` `maxRetries` does not retry on 4xx status codes — only on network errors and 5xx [community]

**What:** Tests that expect `maxRetries: 3` to handle transient auth token expiry (401) or resource-not-found races (404) find that `maxRetries` does NOT retry on those status codes — the first response is returned immediately.

```typescript
// ❌ Assumes maxRetries handles 401 token refresh race
const response = await request.get('/api/protected', { maxRetries: 3 });
// Returns 401 immediately if token is expired — does not retry

// ✅ For 401 retry (token refresh), use expect.poll() with a refresh action
let response: import('@playwright/test').APIResponse;
await expect.poll(async () => {
  response = await request.get('/api/protected');
  if (response.status() === 401) {
    // Refresh token between retries
    await request.post('/api/auth/refresh');
  }
  return response.status();
}, { intervals: [500, 1000, 2000] }).toBe(200);
```

> **WHY:** `maxRetries` is designed for transient network failures and server-side errors (5xx) where retrying the exact same request is safe. Retrying on 4xx would mask contract errors (broken API, wrong URL, missing permissions) and could cause side effects (e.g., retrying a 403 on a write operation). For cases that require application-level logic between retries (token refresh, waiting for a record to be created), use `expect.poll()` with explicit retry actions. [community]

### ARIA Snapshot Children Matching Modes — `contain`, `equal`, `deep-equal` (v1.52+)

Aria snapshots default to `contain` mode where the snapshot template is a *subset* — the page may have additional children not listed. Use `equal` to enforce exact child count at one level, and `deep-equal` to enforce exact matching of the full subtree. Set `children` globally in `playwright.config.ts` to raise the default strictness.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/navigation.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('nav menu has exactly the expected items (equal)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // 'equal' mode: no undocumented items allowed at this level
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation:
      - /children: equal
      - link "Home"
      - link "Products"
      - link "About"
      - link "Contact"
  `);
});

test('cart badge matches full subtree (deep-equal)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();

  // 'deep-equal' mode: all descendants must match precisely — no extra icons or spans
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'cart' })).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - status "cart":
      - /children: deep-equal
      - img "cart icon"
      - text: 1 item
  `);
});
```

Configure the default globally to prevent snapshot drift across the suite:

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  expect: {
    toMatchAriaSnapshot: {
      children: 'equal',  // Enforce exact child count by default
    },
  },
});
```

> **[community]** Upgrading from `contain` (the default) to a global `equal` config often reveals undocumented elements — hidden alerts, skip-navigation links, invisible tooltips — that have been silently attached to the DOM for years. Run `npx playwright test --update-snapshots` after changing the default to generate a fresh baseline before comparing.

### ARIA Accessibility Assertion Trio — `toHaveAccessibleName`, `toHaveRole`, `toHaveAccessibleDescription` (v1.44+)

Use these three assertions together to verify that interactive elements are correctly described for assistive technologies. They check the *computed* accessible name and description — not the raw HTML — so they catch misconfigurations like a `<button>` that has an `aria-label` pointing to a non-existent `id` via `aria-labelledby`.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/a11y-button.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('submit button is fully accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  const submitBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit order/i });

  // 1. Role: Playwright computes the ARIA role from the element type + ARIA overrides
  await expect(submitBtn).toHaveRole('button');

  // 2. Accessible name: computed from aria-label / aria-labelledby / text content
  await expect(submitBtn).toHaveAccessibleName('Submit order');

  // 3. Accessible description: computed from aria-describedby / aria-description
  await expect(submitBtn).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/review before confirming/i);
});

test('form group has correct accessible structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  const emailGroup = page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Email address' });

  await expect(emailGroup).toHaveRole('group');
  await expect(emailGroup).toHaveAccessibleName('Email address');

  // The nested input's description comes from the help text below
  const emailInput = emailGroup.getByRole('textbox');
  await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/we will never share/i);
});
```

> **[community]** `toHaveAccessibleName()` uses the W3C *Accessible Name and Description Computation* algorithm, not a simple text match. A `<button aria-labelledby="missing-id">` will have an empty accessible name, not the button's text content — a common auth form bug where the label element was later given a new `id`. Running this assertion on every primary CTA after each release has proven to catch regressions invisible to visual review.

### `locator.filter({ visible: true })` — Isolating Live DOM Copies

When a page renders multiple copies of a component (e.g., a list with skeleton loaders, a modal that lingers during close animation, or a tabs panel with multiple panels kept in the DOM), `locator.filter({ visible: true })` narrows the match to only the currently visible instance. This is preferable to `.nth(0)` because it is position-independent and survives reordering.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/tabs.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('only active tab panel is visible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // THREE tab panels are in the DOM simultaneously — only one is display:block
  const activePanel = page.getByRole('tabpanel').filter({ visible: true });

  // Assertions run only against the visible panel
  await expect(activePanel).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(activePanel).toContainText('Revenue Overview');
});

test('modal does not leave stale overlay in DOM', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete account' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }).click();

  // During close animation both new and old modal may coexist briefly
  const visibleDialogs = page.getByRole('dialog').filter({ visible: true });
  await expect(visibleDialogs).toHaveCount(0);  // None visible after cancel
});
```

> **[community]** `filter({ visible: true })` uses the same visibility algorithm as `toBeVisible()` — the element must have non-zero dimensions and not be hidden via CSS. It does *not* check if the element is inside the viewport. For viewport-intersection tests, use `expect(locator).toBeInViewport()` separately. Teams migrating from jQuery-style `:visible` selector found this distinction caused unexpected test gaps. [community]

### Fixture `{ box: true }` and `{ box: 'self' }` — Hiding Internal Steps from Reports (v1.46+)

"Boxing" a fixture collapses its internal steps in the HTML report and Trace Viewer, reducing noise when the fixture contains a long sequence of setup actions. `{ box: true }` hides the fixture body and all sub-steps. `{ box: 'self' }` hides only the fixture's own step but still shows sub-steps called from within it — useful for fixtures that themselves call `test.step()`.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { LoginPage } from '../pages/LoginPage';

type AuthFixtures = { loggedInPage: import('@playwright/test').Page };

export const test = base.extend<AuthFixtures>({
  loggedInPage: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      // All login steps are hidden in the report — they're implementation details
      const login = new LoginPage(page);
      await login.goto();
      await login.fillEmail('test@example.com');
      await login.fillPassword(process.env.TEST_PASSWORD!);
      await login.submit();
      await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
      await use(page);
    },
    { box: true },  // Collapses entire fixture body in Trace Viewer
  ],
});

// For a fixture that contains test.step() calls you want to keep visible:
export const testWithVisibleSteps = base.extend<AuthFixtures>({
  loggedInPage: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      await test.step('Login via API', async () => {
        // This step IS still visible in the report
        await page.request.post('/api/auth/login', { data: { /* ... */ } });
      });
      await use(page);
    },
    { box: 'self' },  // Only hides the fixture frame; 'Login via API' step remains
  ],
});
```

> **WHY:** Teams with extensive authentication fixtures often find their Trace Viewer overwhelmed with 30+ "fill email / click submit / wait for nav" steps per test. Boxing the auth fixture reduces report noise to zero while keeping the test's own assertion steps readable. Use `{ box: 'self' }` when the fixture contains meaningful named `test.step()` calls that should remain visible for post-failure debugging.

### Worker-Based Parallel Auth — One Account Per Worker

When tests mutate shared server-side state (e.g., create/modify database records), sharing one storage state file across all parallel workers causes inter-test pollution. Use a `workerStorageState` worker-scoped fixture to provision a unique account per worker, then wire it to `storageState` so all tests in that worker use it automatically.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/workerAuth.ts
import path from 'path';
import fs   from 'fs';
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';

/** Account provisioning — implement for your own backend */
async function acquireAccount(parallelIndex: number) {
  return {
    username: `ci-worker-${parallelIndex}@example.com`,
    password: process.env.WORKER_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD!,
  };
}

export const test = base.extend<{}, { workerStorageState: string }>({
  /**
   * Worker-scoped: runs once per parallel worker, not once per test.
   * The JSON file is reused across all tests in the same worker process.
   */
  workerStorageState: [
    async ({ browser }, use) => {
      const idx      = test.info().parallelIndex;
      const authFile = path.resolve(
        test.info().project.outputDir,
        `.auth/worker-${idx}.json`,
      );

      if (fs.existsSync(authFile)) {
        // Reuse cached state from a previous run (same worker index)
        await use(authFile);
        return;
      }

      const account = await acquireAccount(idx);
      const page    = await browser.newPage({ storageState: undefined });

      await page.goto('/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(account.username);
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(account.password);
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
      await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
      await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
      await page.close();

      await use(authFile);
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],

  // Wire the worker auth file into every test's page context automatically
  storageState: ({ workerStorageState }, use) => use(workerStorageState),
});
```

> **[community]** `test.info().parallelIndex` is always in range `0..workers-1`, making it stable as an array index for a pre-provisioned account pool. `workerIndex` can exceed `workers-1` across retries on different workers, so prefer `parallelIndex` when mapping to a fixed account pool. Teams that switched from shared auth found their test isolation and failure diagnosis improved dramatically — a failing test no longer contaminates the other 15 tests that touched the same user record. [community]

### `routeFromHAR()` — Record-Replay Network Workflow

`page.routeFromHAR()` enables a two-phase workflow: **record** once against the real API (with `update: true`), then **replay** in CI without network access. This is the correct approach for mocking APIs that are expensive, slow, or unavailable in CI.

```typescript
// Phase 1 — record: run once locally to generate the HAR file
// npx playwright test --project=record-mode
// playwright.config.ts projects entry:
// { name: 'record-mode', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } }

// e2e/specs/product-catalog.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const HAR_PATH = './e2e/fixtures/hars/product-catalog.har';

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  // update: true  → writes to HAR file on each run (recording phase)
  // update: false → serves from HAR file (replay phase, the default)
  await page.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, {
    url: '*/**/api/products**',
    update: !!process.env.UPDATE_HAR,   // Toggle via env var
    updateContent: 'embed',             // Embed response bodies in the HAR file
    updateMode: 'minimal',             // Only record urls that match
  });
});

test('shows first 20 products on load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop');
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(20);
});

test('search filters products by name', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop');
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('laptop');
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem').first()).toContainText('laptop', {
    ignoreCase: true,
  });
});
```

Run with `UPDATE_HAR=true npx playwright test` to refresh the HAR, then commit it and run normally in CI.

> **[community]** HAR files embed full response bodies and headers — including `Set-Cookie` and auth tokens. Commit them only if your repository is private, or use `updateContent: 'attach'` (stores bodies as separate files alongside the HAR) and add both to `.gitignore`. [community]

### `page.emulateMedia()` — Full Emulation Reference

`page.emulateMedia()` overrides CSS media features at runtime without re-launching the browser. Call it mid-test to simulate state transitions (e.g., user switches to dark mode, prints the page, prefers reduced motion) or to reset to system defaults.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/media-emulation.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dark mode renders correct background', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  // 1. Override to dark — affects prefers-color-scheme media query
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(18, 18, 18)');

  // 2. Override to light — reset
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(255, 255, 255)');
});

test('reduced motion disables carousel animation', async ({ page }) => {
  // prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/home');

  const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'featured products' });
  // Carousel should auto-pause when reduced motion is preferred
  await expect(carousel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pause' })).not.toBeVisible();
  await expect(carousel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play' })).not.toBeVisible();
  // All items rendered statically
  await expect(carousel.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(5);
});

test('print media renders print-only footer', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/invoice');

  // Switch to print media — @media print rules apply
  await page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' });
  await expect(page.getByTestId('print-footer')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('nav-bar')).not.toBeVisible();
});

test('prefers-contrast: more — high-contrast mode', async ({ page }) => {
  // v1.51+ — test forced colors / high-contrast accessibility
  await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
  await page.goto('/form');
  // Inputs should have visible borders even under forced colors
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox').first()).toBeVisible();
});
```

| Option | Values | What it tests |
|--------|--------|---------------|
| `colorScheme` | `'light'` \| `'dark'` \| `'no-preference'` \| `null` (reset) | `prefers-color-scheme` media query |
| `media` | `'screen'` \| `'print'` \| `null` | CSS `@media print` rules |
| `reducedMotion` | `'reduce'` \| `'no-preference'` \| `null` | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query |
| `forcedColors` | `'active'` \| `'none'` \| `null` | `forced-colors` media query (Windows high-contrast) |

> **[community]** `emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` only affects CSS media queries — it does NOT set `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` or any JavaScript-driven theme. Applications that read `window.matchMedia` on load and then cache the result in state will not respond to mid-test media changes. For those apps, set `colorScheme` *before* `page.goto()` or use `page.addInitScript()` to stub `matchMedia`. [community]

### `locator.or()` — Conditional Element Handling

`locator.or()` matches elements that satisfy *either* locator. It is the idiomatic pattern for handling two possible UI states (e.g., a "cookie banner" that may or may not appear, or a new user wizard shown only on first visit).

```typescript
// e2e/specs/onboarding.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dismisses cookie banner or skips if already dismissed', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const cookieBanner = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookies/i });
  const mainContent  = page.getByRole('main');

  // Wait until either the banner is visible OR main content is loaded
  await expect(cookieBanner.or(mainContent).first()).toBeVisible();

  // Dismiss banner only if it appeared
  if (await cookieBanner.isVisible()) {
    await cookieBanner.getByRole('button', { name: 'Accept all' }).click();
  }

  await expect(mainContent).toBeVisible();
});

test('handles first-visit wizard or dashboard', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/app');

  const wizard    = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Welcome wizard' });
  const dashboard = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Dashboard' });

  // One or the other must appear within the default assertion timeout
  await expect(wizard.or(dashboard).first()).toBeVisible();

  if (await wizard.isVisible()) {
    await wizard.getByRole('button', { name: 'Skip' }).click();
  }

  await expect(dashboard).toBeVisible();
});
```

> **[community]** `locator.or()` returns *the first matching element* when both locators match simultaneously — add `.first()` explicitly rather than relying on implicit ordering. In practice, the two locators rarely both match at the same time, but during a transition animation (banner fading out while main content fades in) both can be briefly visible and `.or()` without `.first()` will select whichever is earlier in the DOM. [community]

### `axe-core` Fixture Pattern — Reusable Accessibility Scanning

Wrapping `AxeBuilder` in a Playwright fixture ensures every accessibility scan is identically configured (WCAG tags, exclusions, attachment). The fixture adds the full scan result as a JSON attachment so failures are diagnosable in the HTML report without re-running.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/axe.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

type A11yFixtures = {
  makeAxeBuilder: () => AxeBuilder;
};

export const test = base.extend<A11yFixtures>({
  makeAxeBuilder: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const factory = () =>
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
        .exclude('#known-violation');   // Suppress pre-existing issues

    await use(factory);
  },
});

// e2e/specs/checkout-a11y.spec.ts
import { test } from '../fixtures/axe';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout page has no WCAG 2.1 AA violations', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Run axe and attach the full results for debugging
  const axeBuilder = makeAxeBuilder();
  const results    = await axeBuilder.analyze();

  await test.info().attach('axe-results', {
    body:        JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});

test('checkout page step 2 passes after user interaction', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to shipping' }).click();

  // Re-run axe after state change — dynamic content may introduce new violations
  const results = await makeAxeBuilder().analyze();
  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});
```

> **[community]** Always run `analyze()` *after* the page has reached the target state — axe scans a snapshot of the current DOM. Scanning immediately after `page.goto()` before loading spinners resolve will include hidden/loading elements in the accessibility tree. Add a `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` or assert a key element visible before calling `analyze()`. [community]

### `toHaveValues()` — Multi-Select Assertion

`expect(locator).toHaveValues()` asserts the set of selected values in a `<select multiple>` element. Unlike `toHaveValue()` (single selection), it checks an array and requires all provided values to be selected.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/filters.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('multi-select filter shows correct pre-selected options', async ({ page }) => {
  // URL pre-selects "europe" and "asia"
  await page.goto('/reports?regions=europe,asia');

  const regionSelect = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: 'Regions' });

  // Assert all pre-selected values — order must match the DOM option order
  await expect(regionSelect).toHaveValues(['europe', 'asia']);
});

test('selecting all regions works correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  const select = page.locator('select[name="regions"]');
  await select.selectOption(['europe', 'asia', 'americas']);

  await expect(select).toHaveValues(['europe', 'asia', 'americas']);
});
```

> **[community]** `toHaveValues()` requires the values to be in the **same order** as the HTML `<option>` elements — even if the user selected them in a different order. A test asserting `['asia', 'europe']` will fail if the DOM order is `['europe', 'asia']`. Always match DOM option order, not selection order. [community]

### `toBeInViewport({ ratio })` — Partial Visibility Assertion

`expect(locator).toBeInViewport({ ratio: N })` asserts that at least `N` (0–1) fraction of the element's bounding box is within the viewport. The default `ratio: 0` means any overlap counts. Use `ratio: 1` for fully-in-viewport assertions.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/infinite-scroll.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('sticky CTA bar is at least 80% visible when scrolled mid-page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/product/1234');

  // Scroll past the fold
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);  // Allow scroll animation

  const ctaBar = page.getByRole('complementary', { name: 'purchase options' });

  // At least 80% of the CTA must be in the viewport
  await expect(ctaBar).toBeInViewport({ ratio: 0.8 });
});

test('lazy-loaded image enters viewport after scroll', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/gallery');

  const lazyImage = page.getByRole('img', { name: /gallery photo 10/i });

  // Initially off-screen
  await expect(lazyImage).not.toBeInViewport();

  // Scroll the image into view
  await lazyImage.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

  // Now fully visible
  await expect(lazyImage).toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1 });
});
```

> **[community]** `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` does not guarantee the element is fully in the viewport — it scrolls the element into view using the browser's built-in behavior, which may only partially expose the element if the scroll container has padding or the element is larger than the viewport. Assert `toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1 })` explicitly after scrolling if full visibility is required. [community]

---

### `toContainClass()` — Partial CSS Class Assertion

`expect(locator).toContainClass('active')` asserts that the element's `class` attribute contains the given class name(s). Unlike `toHaveClass()` (full match), `toContainClass()` passes as long as the listed classes are present alongside others.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/active-states.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('active nav item has correct CSS class', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const dashboardLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Dashboard' });

  // ✅ toContainClass: passes if 'active' is present even with other classes
  // The element might have class="nav-link active text-bold"
  await expect(dashboardLink).toContainClass('active');

  // ❌ toHaveClass would fail: expects EXACT class string
  // await expect(dashboardLink).toHaveClass('active');
  // → fails because the full class is "nav-link active text-bold"
});

test('error input has validation class', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/signup');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();
  const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });

  // Assert both validation classes are present
  await expect(emailInput).toContainClass('is-invalid error-highlight');
});
```

> **[community]** Many CSS-in-JS frameworks (Tailwind, styled-components, CSS Modules) generate hashed or utility class names that change on every build. Asserting on these with `toHaveClass()` creates fragile tests. `toContainClass()` with semantic state classes (`active`, `selected`, `is-invalid`) that your team controls is far more stable. If there are no stable semantic classes, add `data-state` attributes and assert with `toHaveAttribute('data-state', 'active')` instead. [community]

### `playwright.devices` Spread Pattern — Multi-Device Project Config

`devices` from `@playwright/test` provides pre-configured emulation settings for 40+ real devices. Spread them into a project's `use` block alongside custom overrides. This avoids maintaining separate `userAgent`, `viewport`, and `isMobile` values manually.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './e2e',
  projects: [
    // Desktop browsers
    { name: 'chromium',      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
    { name: 'firefox',       use: { ...devices['Desktop Firefox'] } },
    { name: 'webkit',        use: { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] } },

    // Mobile — touch events, correct viewport, isMobile: true
    { name: 'mobile-chrome', use: { ...devices['Pixel 7'] } },
    { name: 'mobile-safari', use: { ...devices['iPhone 15'] } },

    // Tablet
    { name: 'ipad',          use: { ...devices['iPad Pro'] } },

    // Override specific properties after spread — e.g., custom viewport
    {
      name: 'chromium-4k',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        viewport: { width: 3840, height: 2160 },
        deviceScaleFactor: 2,
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

Check available device names at runtime:

```bash
npx playwright --list-devices
```

> **[community]** Always spread `devices['…']` *before* your overrides — spreading after will silently overwrite the device's `viewport` or `userAgent`. Teams that put overrides first find the device defaults win and their customizations are ignored. The spread operator's last-write-wins rule is easy to get backwards. [community]

---

### `eslint-plugin-playwright` with ESLint Flat Config (v1.6+)

`eslint-plugin-playwright` enforces Playwright-specific rules (no `.waitForTimeout()`, no `page.pause()` in CI, proper `expect` async). ESLint v9 requires the **flat config** format (`eslint.config.js` or `.mjs`). Version 1.6+ of the plugin exports a `configs` object compatible with flat config.

```typescript
// eslint.config.mjs
import playwright from 'eslint-plugin-playwright';

export default [
  // Apply Playwright rules only to test files
  {
    ...playwright.configs['flat/recommended'],
    files: ['e2e/**/*.spec.ts', 'e2e/**/*.test.ts'],
    rules: {
      ...playwright.configs['flat/recommended'].rules,

      // Strictly disallow arbitrary waits — the most common flakiness cause
      'playwright/no-wait-for-timeout': 'error',

      // Require await before every assertion
      'playwright/valid-expect': ['error', { alwaysAwait: true }],

      // Disallow page.pause() — it hangs CI
      'playwright/no-page-pause': 'error',

      // Warn on skipped tests left in — common review oversight
      'playwright/no-skipped-test': 'warn',

      // Require descriptive test names
      'playwright/valid-title': 'error',
    },
  },
];
```

Install:

```bash
npm install -D eslint eslint-plugin-playwright
# Ensure eslint >= 9.0 for flat config support
```

> **[community]** The legacy `.eslintrc.*` format is **unsupported** in ESLint v9. If your project has both an old `.eslintrc.json` and a new `eslint.config.js`, ESLint v9 silently ignores the `.eslintrc` file. Teams that kept both files intact found their Playwright-specific rules stopped applying after upgrading ESLint, with no warning. Delete `.eslintrc.*` after migrating to flat config. [community]

### Additional Community Gotchas (Cycle 23)

---

#### 70. Fixture `{ box: true }` hides ALL steps including assertions — use `{ box: 'self' }` to preserve sub-steps [community]

**What:** When a fixture is declared with `{ box: true }`, the Trace Viewer and HTML report collapse the *entire fixture body* — including any `test.step()` calls, `expect()` assertions, and nested fixtures invoked from within it. If the fixture contains meaningful diagnostic steps, none of them appear in the report on failure.

```typescript
// ❌ Box: true hides the login steps AND the assertion inside
auth: [async ({ page }, use) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');  // ← This step is hidden!
  await use(page);
}, { box: true }]

// ✅ Box: 'self' hides the fixture's own wrapper but shows its named steps
auth: [async ({ page }, use) => {
  await test.step('Login', async () => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  });
  await test.step('Verify redirect', async () => {
    await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');  // ← Visible in report!
  });
  await use(page);
}, { box: 'self' }]
```

> **WHY:** `{ box: true }` is designed for infrastructure fixtures where *no* internal step is relevant to the test author. `{ box: 'self' }` is the correct choice for fixtures that perform meaningful actions that should be visible in failure reports. The distinction is documented but easy to miss in the fixture options table. [community]

---

#### 71. `locator.or()` returns the first DOM match, not the first visible match — add `.filter({ visible: true })` for conditional-display patterns [community]

**What:** `locator.or()` combines two locators and returns the first matching element in document order. If both locators match simultaneously (e.g., a dialog fading out while a banner fades in), `or()` returns whichever is earlier in the DOM — not whichever is currently visible.

```typescript
// ❌ May return the hidden/fading-out element
const target = cookieBanner.or(mainContent).first();
await expect(target).toBeVisible();  // Can match the fading banner

// ✅ Filter to visible elements first, then take the first
const target = cookieBanner.or(mainContent).filter({ visible: true }).first();
await expect(target).toBeVisible();
```

> **WHY:** During CSS transitions, elements that are `display:block` but `opacity:0` or `visibility:hidden` are NOT considered visible by Playwright. However, `locator.or()` does not filter by visibility — it returns all matching elements. The `.filter({ visible: true })` step ensures you get the element the user actually sees. [community]

---

#### 72. `routeFromHAR()` silently serves stale 401 responses when session tokens embedded in the HAR file expire [community]

**What:** HAR files record auth tokens in `Cookie` request headers and `Set-Cookie` response headers. When the HAR is replayed, the response bodies are served verbatim — including 401 responses recorded when the token was already expired during the initial recording.

```typescript
// ❌ Recorded with an expired token — silently replays 401 to every test
await page.routeFromHAR('./hars/api.har', { url: '*/**/api/**' });
await page.goto('/dashboard');
// Tests see "Unauthorized" because the HAR captured a 401 session

// ✅ Re-record periodically in CI using UPDATE_HAR=true
// Or override specific broken routes after routeFromHAR:
await page.routeFromHAR('./hars/api.har', { url: '*/**/api/**' });
await page.route('*/**/api/session', route =>
  route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { user: 'ci-user' } })
);
```

> **WHY:** `routeFromHAR()` is a pure replay mechanism — it does not evaluate whether the recorded responses are still valid. Teams that record HAR files manually on developer machines often commit them with dev-environment session cookies that expire within hours. Set up a CI job to re-record HARs on a schedule (weekly or after auth changes) to keep them fresh. [community]

---

#### 73. `AxeBuilder.analyze()` blocks indefinitely on pages with cross-origin iframes — add an explicit timeout [community]

**What:** `@axe-core/playwright`'s `analyze()` attempts to scan all frames on the page, including cross-origin iframes (ads, embedded payment forms, third-party widgets). Cross-origin iframes raise CORS errors that cause axe's frame scanning to hang without a timeout.

```typescript
// ❌ Hangs if the page embeds a cross-origin iframe (Stripe, Adyen, etc.)
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();

// ✅ Option 1: Exclude the cross-origin iframe element
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
  .exclude('iframe[src*="stripe.com"]')
  .analyze();

// ✅ Option 2: Scope the scan to the main document
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
  .include('body > *:not(iframe)')
  .analyze();

// ✅ Option 3: Set a timeout on the page before calling analyze
page.setDefaultTimeout(30_000);
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
```

> **WHY:** axe-core tries to inject a script into every iframe to compute its accessibility tree. For cross-origin iframes the browser blocks the injection via the same-origin policy, but axe does not always time out gracefully — it can wait indefinitely for a response from a sandboxed frame. The most defensive pattern is to explicitly exclude known third-party embeds before scanning. [community]

---

#### 74. `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` does not affect JavaScript-driven theming — only CSS media queries [community]

**What:** Applications that read `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches` on load and store the result in React state, Zustand, or localStorage will not respond to `emulateMedia()` called after `page.goto()`. The media override takes effect immediately for CSS but the JavaScript query already ran and cached the result.

```typescript
// ❌ Application reads matchMedia on mount — override arrives too late
await page.goto('/dashboard');
await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });  // Too late for React state
await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(18, 18, 18)');
// Fails: body background is still light because React cached the value

// ✅ Set colorScheme BEFORE goto — media is emulated before scripts run
await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
await page.goto('/dashboard');
await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(18, 18, 18)');

// ✅ Alternative: stub matchMedia via addInitScript for apps that call it on load
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  Object.defineProperty(window, 'matchMedia', {
    value: (query: string) => ({
      matches: query.includes('dark'),
      media: query,
      addListener: () => {},
      removeListener: () => {},
      addEventListener: () => {},
      removeEventListener: () => {},
    }),
  });
});
await page.goto('/dashboard');
```

> **WHY:** `emulateMedia()` is a browser-level override of the CSS media environment. CSS rules re-evaluate immediately. JavaScript code that read `matchMedia` before the override was applied has already computed and cached the value — no new event fires to notify it. This is a fundamental browser behavior, not a Playwright limitation. [community]

---

#### 75. `toHaveValues()` on `<select multiple>` requires values in DOM option order, not selection order [community]

**What:** `expect(locator).toHaveValues(['b', 'a'])` fails when the HTML `<option>` order is `a` then `b`, even though the user selected `b` before `a`. The assertion compares against the list of selected options in DOM order, not in selection/click order.

```typescript
// HTML: <option value="europe">Europe</option>
//        <option value="asia">Asia</option>
//        <option value="americas">Americas</option>

// ❌ Fails — assertion order does not match DOM order
await expect(select).toHaveValues(['asia', 'europe']);

// ✅ Passes — matches DOM option element order
await expect(select).toHaveValues(['europe', 'asia']);

// For dynamic multi-selects where order is unknown, sort both arrays:
const actual   = await select.evaluate((el: HTMLSelectElement) =>
  Array.from(el.selectedOptions, o => o.value).sort()
);
expect(actual).toEqual(['asia', 'europe'].sort());
```

> **WHY:** `toHaveValues()` is implemented by reading `element.selectedOptions` as a `HTMLOptionsCollection`, which follows DOM insertion order. The browser does not reorder selected options to match the user's click sequence. This is consistent with the HTML spec but trips up teams that write assertions in the order they click the options rather than in the order options appear in the source. [community]

| API | Version | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `toMatchAriaSnapshot({ children: 'equal'\|'deep-equal' })` | v1.52+ | Control how strictly aria snapshot children are matched | Use `equal` to catch undocumented sibling elements; `deep-equal` for full subtree regression |
| `expect.configure({ expect: { toMatchAriaSnapshot: { children } } })` | v1.52+ | Set global default children matching mode for all aria snapshots | Suite-wide strictness enforcement without per-assertion options |
| `expect(locator).toHaveRole(role)` | v1.44+ | Assert computed ARIA role | Verify that role overrides (`role="button"`) and semantic elements have the expected role |
| `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleName(name)` | v1.44+ | Assert computed accessible name (W3C algorithm) | Catch broken `aria-labelledby` references, missing alt text, empty labels |
| `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleDescription(desc)` | v1.44+ | Assert computed accessible description | Verify `aria-describedby` wiring for help text, error messages, tooltips |
| `locator.filter({ visible: true })` | all | Narrow locator to only currently visible elements | Exclude off-screen, transitioning, or skeleton-loading duplicates |
| `{ box: true }` fixture option | v1.46+ | Collapse entire fixture in Trace Viewer/report | Infrastructure fixtures with no per-test diagnostic value |
| `{ box: 'self' }` fixture option | v1.46+ | Collapse fixture frame but keep named `test.step()` sub-steps visible | Fixtures that contain meaningful named steps |
| `page.routeFromHAR(path, { update: true })` | v1.23+ | Record network to HAR file | One-time recording phase; commit the HAR then replay with `update: false` |
| `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion\|forcedColors\|colorScheme\|media })` | v1.11+ | Override CSS media features at runtime | Test dark mode, print layout, reduced motion, high-contrast accessibility |
| `locator.or(other)` | v1.33+ | Match elements satisfying either locator | Handle conditional UI (cookie banners, onboarding wizards, optional modals) |
| `expect(locator).toHaveValues([…])` | v1.23+ | Assert all selected values in a `<select multiple>` | Multi-select filter components, settings panels with multi-choice options |
| `expect(locator).toBeInViewport({ ratio })` | v1.31+ | Assert element is N% inside the viewport | Sticky headers, lazy-loaded images, infinite scroll triggers |
| `expect(locator).toContainClass(className)` | v1.52+ | Assert element's class attribute contains the given class(es) | State classes (`active`, `selected`, `is-invalid`) alongside dynamic utility classes |
| `createUser(overrides, testInfo)` (factory) | TypeScript pattern | Generate parallel-safe test data objects | Any test that creates user or domain entities via API or UI |

### `page.routeWebSocket()` — Message Interception and Server Passthrough (v1.48+)

`page.routeWebSocket()` intercepts the WebSocket handshake before the connection is established, giving you full control over every frame in both directions. The `ws.connectToServer()` method upgrades the interceptor to a transparent proxy so you can selectively rewrite only the frames you care about while passing the rest to the real server unchanged.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/chat.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('injects a system message into the live WebSocket stream', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register the route BEFORE the page loads — registration after connection is too late
  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://chat.example.com/ws', ws => {
    // Connect to the real server transparently
    const server = ws.connectToServer();

    // Intercept messages from the BROWSER → rewrite a specific command
    ws.onMessage(message => {
      if (typeof message === 'string' && message.startsWith('{"type":"ping"')) {
        server.send('{"type":"ping","source":"playwright-intercepted"}');
      } else {
        server.send(message);          // pass all other frames unchanged
      }
    });

    // Intercept messages from the SERVER → inject an extra system message
    server.onMessage(message => {
      ws.send(message);               // forward the original frame first
      if (typeof message === 'string' && message.includes('"connected":true')) {
        ws.send('{"type":"system","text":"[QA] Connection hijacked by Playwright"}');
      }
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/chat');
  await expect(page.getByText('[QA] Connection hijacked by Playwright')).toBeVisible();
});

test('mocks entire WebSocket — no real server needed', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://prices.example.com/feed', ws => {
    // No connectToServer() call → fully offline mock
    ws.onMessage(message => {
      const req = JSON.parse(String(message));
      if (req.subscribe === 'BTC/USD') {
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ symbol: 'BTC/USD', price: 65_000, ts: Date.now() }));
      }
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/prices');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Subscribe BTC/USD' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('btc-price')).toHaveText('$65,000');
});
```

> **[community]** Register `routeWebSocket()` before `page.goto()`. If the page opens the WebSocket during script execution (e.g., in a React `useEffect`) and your route is registered after `goto` returns, the handshake has already completed and the route handler is never invoked. The route must be in place before the browser initiates the connection. [community]

---

### `storageState({ indexedDB: true })` — Capturing IndexedDB Across Test Sessions (v1.51+)

By default `context.storageState()` serializes cookies and `localStorage` only. Pass `indexedDB: true` to also capture IndexedDB stores, which many modern SPAs use for offline caching, tokens, or large structured data. This is critical when `localStorage` alone does not fully restore an authenticated session.

```typescript
// e2e/auth/indexeddb.setup.ts
import { test as setup, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

const authFile = path.join(__dirname, '../.auth/user-with-idb.json');

setup('capture IndexedDB auth token', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.E2E_USER!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.E2E_PASS!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');

  // Wait for the IndexedDB write to complete — apps often write async on 'visibilitychange'
  await page.waitForFunction(() => {
    return new Promise<boolean>(resolve => {
      const req = indexedDB.open('auth-db');
      req.onsuccess = e => {
        const db = (e.target as IDBOpenDBRequest).result;
        if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('tokens')) { resolve(false); return; }
        const tx = db.transaction('tokens', 'readonly');
        tx.objectStore('tokens').get('access').onsuccess = r =>
          resolve(!!(r.target as IDBRequest).result);
      };
    });
  });

  // v1.51+: include IndexedDB in the saved state file
  await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile, indexedDB: true });
});
```

Configure the auth file as the default storageState for the project that needs IndexedDB:

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
projects: [
  { name: 'setup-idb', testMatch: /auth\/indexeddb\.setup\.ts/ },
  {
    name: 'spa-with-idb',
    use: { storageState: 'e2e/.auth/user-with-idb.json' },
    dependencies: ['setup-idb'],
  },
]
```

> **[community]** `storageState({ indexedDB: true })` only serializes primitive-valued entries (strings, numbers, booleans, plain objects). `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, `File`, `CryptoKey`, and class instances are silently dropped from the snapshot. Apps that store raw `ArrayBuffer` tokens (e.g., Web Crypto derived keys) need to convert to Base64 before writing to IDB, otherwise the restored state will be missing the key and authentication will silently fail. [community]
