### Shard-Balanced Blob Report Merge — Full CI Workflow

Playwright's blob reporter accumulates compressed test result data from each CI shard. A subsequent merge job combines all blobs into a single HTML or JUnit artifact. Without the blob reporter, merging shard results requires custom scripting; with it, one CLI command regenerates any report format.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — switch to blob reporter on CI, HTML locally
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: process.env.CI ? 'blob' : 'html',
  // fullyParallel: true distributes tests at test-level, not file-level,
  // producing more balanced shards when file sizes vary.
  fullyParallel: true,
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/playwright.yml — matrix sharding + report merge
jobs:
  playwright-tests:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shardIndex: [1, 2, 3, 4]
        shardTotal: [4]
    steps:
      - run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shardIndex }}/${{ matrix.shardTotal }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: blob-report-${{ matrix.shardIndex }}
          path: blob-report/

  merge-reports:
    needs: playwright-tests
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { pattern: blob-report-*, merge-multiple: true, path: all-blob-reports }
      - run: npx playwright merge-reports --reporter html ./all-blob-reports
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: { name: html-report, path: playwright-report/ }
```

**When to use:** Any suite with >200 tests where sequential CI runs exceed acceptable time budgets. Use `fullyParallel: true` to balance shards across tests rather than files. Without it, a single large spec file creates one overloaded shard and three idle ones. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Blob reports require a separate merge job and artifact storage. For small suites (<50 tests), the overhead outweighs the gain — use `--reporter=html` directly.

---

### `--shard` Imbalance — File-Level vs Test-Level Splitting [community]

When `fullyParallel` is `false` (the default), Playwright assigns whole spec files to shards. A single large file with 100 tests lands entirely on one shard while others get 10 tests each.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — before: file-level sharding (default)
export default defineConfig({
  // fullyParallel: false  ← default; sharding distributes files, not tests
  testDir: './tests',
});

// Shard 1 gets: auth.spec.ts (100 tests) ← bottleneck
// Shard 2 gets: dashboard.spec.ts (10 tests)
// Shard 3 gets: settings.spec.ts (8 tests)
// Shard 4 gets: profile.spec.ts (7 tests)

// playwright.config.ts — after: test-level sharding
export default defineConfig({
  fullyParallel: true,   // ← enables test-level shard assignment
  testDir: './tests',
});
// Each shard now gets ~31 tests from across all files
```

> **WHY:** Playwright's shard algorithm counts spec files, not individual tests, when `fullyParallel` is `false`. A file boundary is always preserved — a test cannot span shards. Enable `fullyParallel: true` to unlock test-level distribution for balanced CI timing. [community]

---

### `APIRequestContext` — API-First Test Setup Before UI Tests

Seeding test data via API calls before navigating the UI avoids slow UI setup flows and removes login-page dependencies from data-setup tests. The `request` fixture shares the same browser context cookies, so an API login propagates to subsequent `page.goto()` calls automatically.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/api-seed.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type SeedFixtures = {
  seedUser: { id: string; email: string };
};

export const test = base.extend<SeedFixtures>({
  seedUser: async ({ request }, use) => {
    // Create test user via API — no browser UI involved
    const response = await request.post('/api/admin/users', {
      data: { email: `user-${Date.now()}@test.example`, role: 'editor' },
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN}` },
    });
    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    const user = await response.json();

    await use(user);

    // Teardown: delete the created user
    await request.delete(`/api/admin/users/${user.id}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN}` },
    });
  },
});

// e2e/tests/user-profile.spec.ts
import { test } from '../fixtures/api-seed';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('editor can view profile page', async ({ page, seedUser }) => {
  await page.goto(`/users/${seedUser.id}`);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: seedUser.email })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Whenever test data requires multiple UI steps to create (e.g., multi-step registration, admin-only screens). API seeding makes these tests 5-10x faster and fully parallelisable. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Requires a writable test/staging API. If the API is protected behind a separate auth token, add `ADMIN_TOKEN` to CI secrets and rotate it independently of test-user credentials.

---

### `request` Fixture Cookie Sharing vs. `playwright.request.newContext()` Isolation

The `request` fixture from `@playwright/test` is bound to the current browser context — cookies set by `request.post('/login')` appear in the browser, and cookies set by `page.goto('/login')` are visible to subsequent `request` calls. `playwright.request.newContext()` creates a fully isolated HTTP client with its own cookie jar.

```typescript
test('context-bound request shares cookies with page', async ({ request, page }) => {
  // Login via API — the session cookie is automatically available to the page
  const loginResp = await request.post('/api/auth/login', {
    data: { username: 'alice', password: 'secret' },
  });
  expect(loginResp.ok()).toBeTruthy();

  // page.goto() reuses the session cookie from request.post() above
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Welcome, Alice' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('isolated newContext has no cookies from page', async ({ playwright, page }) => {
  // Establish a browser session first
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Username').fill('alice');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Log in' }).click();

  // Isolated context — blank slate, no cookies from the browser session
  const isolated = await playwright.request.newContext({ baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000' });
  const meResp = await isolated.get('/api/me');
  expect(meResp.status()).toBe(401); // unauthenticated

  await isolated.dispose();
});
```

> **WHY:** The `request` fixture is created from `context.request`, which binds it to the browser context's storage. This is the right choice for hybrid UI+API tests. `playwright.request.newContext()` is for testing the API in isolation (no browser), parallel independent sessions, or when you need a fresh cookie jar mid-test. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Using the bound `request` fixture in `afterAll` teardown can fail if the browser context is already closed. Move teardown to a fixture's teardown phase instead of `afterAll`.

---

### `toHaveScreenshot()` with `mask` and `clip` — Deterministic Visual Regression

Dynamic content (timestamps, avatars, ads) causes screenshot tests to flicker. The `mask` option overlays a colored rectangle on volatile elements before comparison; `clip` restricts the captured area to a stable region of interest.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('product card visual regression', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/123');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // mask: array of Locators to overlay before comparison
  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('product-card.png', {
    mask: [
      page.getByTestId('timestamp'),       // "Added 3 hours ago" label
      page.getByTestId('user-avatar'),     // random gravatar
      page.locator('.ad-slot'),            // third-party ad iframe
    ],
    // clip: restrict comparison to the card element only
    clip: await page.getByTestId('product-card').boundingBox() ?? undefined,
    maxDiffPixels: 50,   // allow minor anti-aliasing differences
    animations: 'disabled',
  });
});

// playwright.config.ts — global screenshot defaults
export default defineConfig({
  expect: {
    toHaveScreenshot: {
      maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02,  // allow 2% pixel drift
      animations: 'disabled',
    },
  },
});
```

**When to use:** Pages with server-rendered timestamps, personalised content, or third-party widgets. `mask` is preferred over `clip` when the volatile element is surrounded by stable content you want to include in the comparison. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Masked regions hide real regressions inside them. Keep masks minimal and document why each mask exists in a comment.

---

### `updateSnapshots: 'changed'` — Targeted Screenshot Refresh Without Full Rebuild

`updateSnapshots: 'all'` regenerates every snapshot baseline, including ones you didn't touch. `updateSnapshots: 'changed'` (v1.50+) refreshes only the snapshots for tests that currently fail the comparison — leaving passing baselines untouched.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — safe incremental snapshot update mode
export default defineConfig({
  updateSnapshots: 'changed',
  // Alternatives:
  // 'all'     — regenerate every snapshot (risky; silently accepts regressions)
  // 'missing' — only create snapshots that don't yet have a baseline file
  // 'changed' — update only failing snapshots (v1.50+, safest for incremental UI work)
  // 'none'    — never update; recommended CI default
});
```

Run update with a CLI override for a targeted pass:

```bash
# Refresh only the tests that are failing visual comparisons right now
npx playwright test --update-snapshots=changed

# On CI: fail when any snapshot is missing (never silently create baseline)
npx playwright test --update-snapshots=none
```

> **WHY:** Using `--update-snapshots=all` in a PR is a common footgun — it silently accepts every visual change, including actual regressions introduced by the PR. `changed` limits the blast radius to tests that were already broken, making code review of snapshot diffs tractable. [community]

---

### `page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true })` — Aria Snapshot with Element References (v1.60+)

Aria snapshots in v1.60+ can include element reference IDs via `{ ref: true }`. Each node in the YAML gets a `ref` attribute that can be resolved back to a `Locator` using `page.getByAria(ref)`. This bridges accessibility tree verification with direct DOM interaction.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('verify nav structure and interact via aria ref', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Assert structural shape — partial match by default
  await expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation:
      - link "Home"
      - link "Products"
      - link "About"
  `);

  // Capture tree with refs to get handles for interaction
  const snapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true });
  // snapshot YAML (example):
  //   - navigation:
  //     - link "Home" [ref=e12]
  //     - link "Products" [ref=e15]
  //     - link "About" [ref=e18]

  // Use regex to extract the ref for the Products link
  const productsRef = snapshot.match(/link "Products" \[ref=(e\d+)\]/)?.[1];
  if (productsRef) {
    await page.getByAria(productsRef).click();
  }
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/products/);
});
```

**When to use:** When you need to assert accessibility tree structure AND then interact with the identified element without re-querying the DOM. Particularly useful when multiple elements share the same accessible name and role, and you need to target the exact one identified in the snapshot. [official]

**Tradeoff:** `ref` values are ephemeral — they change on each `ariaSnapshot()` call and across page navigations. Never persist refs across test steps; always re-snapshot after navigations or DOM mutations.

---

### `page.addInitScript()` — Overriding Read-Only Browser APIs Before Page Load

`addInitScript()` injects JavaScript into every new page/frame before any page scripts execute. It is the correct tool for overriding native browser APIs (geolocation, battery, sensors) that Playwright's emulation layer does not expose directly.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('app handles denied geolocation gracefully', async ({ page }) => {
  // Override navigator.geolocation BEFORE the page loads
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const denied: GeolocationPositionError = {
      code: 1, // PERMISSION_DENIED
      message: 'User denied Geolocation',
      PERMISSION_DENIED: 1,
      POSITION_UNAVAILABLE: 2,
      TIMEOUT: 3,
    };

    Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'geolocation', {
      value: {
        getCurrentPosition(
          _success: PositionCallback,
          error?: PositionErrorCallback
        ) { error?.(denied); },
        watchPosition: () => 0,
        clearWatch: () => {},
      } as Geolocation,
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/map-feature');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveText(/location access denied/i);
});
```

**When to use:** Mocking APIs that only exist in browsers — geolocation, `DeviceMotionEvent`, Web Bluetooth, Battery Status API, or `window.matchMedia` with exotic media features. For standard emulation (viewport, color scheme, timezone), use `page.emulate()` or `browserContext.grantPermissions()` instead. [official]

**Tradeoff:** `addInitScript()` scripts run in the browser context without TypeScript safety — cast return values carefully and test the mock itself. The injected function cannot import Node.js modules; it executes in the browser runtime.

---

### Project Dependencies as `globalSetup` Replacement — Fixture-Aware Setup

Config-based `globalSetup` cannot use Playwright fixtures or record traces. Setup projects declared via `dependencies` run as ordinary test files, gaining full fixture access, trace recording, and HTML report integration.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — ordered setup via project dependencies
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'db-seed',
      testMatch: /tests\/setup\/db-seed\.ts/,
      // No dependencies — runs first unconditionally
    },
    {
      name: 'auth-setup',
      testMatch: /tests\/setup\/auth\.setup\.ts/,
      dependencies: ['db-seed'],   // runs after db-seed completes
    },
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      dependencies: ['auth-setup'],
      teardown: 'global-teardown',
      use: { storageState: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' },
      testMatch: /tests\/e2e\/.*/,
    },
    {
      name: 'global-teardown',
      testMatch: /tests\/setup\/teardown\.ts/,
    },
  ],
});

// tests/setup/auth.setup.ts — full fixture access, traces recorded
import { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';

setup('authenticate and persist session', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
  // Snapshot AFTER the final auth exchange completes
  await page.context().storageState({ path: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' });
});
```

**When to use:** Prefer setup projects over `globalSetup` when you need fixture access (e.g., `page`, `request`), trace recording for failures, or HTML report inclusion of setup steps. Use `globalSetup` only for purely Node.js tasks (database migration, env validation) that don't need a browser. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Setup projects count toward shard allocation. If `testMatch` is too broad, setup files may be picked up by multiple shards. Use a dedicated subfolder (`tests/setup/`) with a precise `testMatch` regex pattern.

---

### `locator.and()` — Intersection Locator for Dual-Attribute Matching

`locator.and(other)` returns a locator that must satisfy both `this` and `other` simultaneously. It replaces compound CSS selectors that mix semantic and data attributes, keeping each side readable in isolation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('locator.and() intersection patterns', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // ❌ Compound CSS — brittle if attribute names change
  const fragile = page.locator('button[data-state="loading"][aria-busy="true"]');

  // ✅ Composed from two semantic locators — each side is independently readable
  const loadingBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })
    .and(page.locator('[aria-busy="true"]'));

  await expect(loadingBtn).toBeVisible();

  // ✅ Role + test ID: useful in component libraries where many buttons share a name
  const saveOrder = page.getByRole('button')
    .and(page.getByTestId('save-order'));

  await saveOrder.click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Order saved');

  // ✅ getByText + getByRole: assert an element is both a link AND contains text
  const activeNav = page.getByRole('link')
    .and(page.getByText('Dashboard'))
    .and(page.locator('[aria-current="page"]'));

  await expect(activeNav).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** When two independently meaningful attributes must both be true (role + aria state, role + test ID, text + aria-current). Avoids CSS specificity wars and keeps both sides of the match semantically clear. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Both locators in `and()` must resolve to the same DOM element. If they resolve to overlapping but non-identical element sets (e.g., parent + child), `and()` returns an empty match. Use `filter({ has: ... })` for parent-contains-descendant relationships instead.

---

### `expect(page).toHaveURL()` with Predicate Function — Dynamic URL Validation (v1.57+)

`toHaveURL()` now accepts a predicate function `(url: URL) => boolean`, enabling validation of URL properties that cannot be expressed as a string or regex — such as query parameters, hash fragments, or numeric comparisons.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('redirect appends correct return_to param', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/protected-page');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) =>
    url.pathname === '/login' &&
    url.searchParams.get('return_to') === '/protected-page'
  );
});

test('checkout redirects to HTTPS payment gateway', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to payment' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) =>
    url.protocol === 'https:' &&
    url.hostname.endsWith('.payment-gateway.example')
  );
});

test('paginated list increments page param on next click', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/results?q=playwright&page=1');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Next page' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) => {
    const p = parseInt(url.searchParams.get('page') ?? '1', 10);
    return p >= 2;
  });
});
```

**When to use:** URL assertion involving query string logic, multiple conditions, or arithmetic on URL parts (page numbers, offsets). Regex is cleaner for simple path matching; use the predicate only when the condition requires URL parsing. [official]

**Tradeoff:** Errors inside the predicate are swallowed until timeout — add a temporary `console.log(url.toString())` when debugging a failing predicate to see what URL is actually being received.

---

### `page.routeWebSocket()` Full Bidirectional Mock — Offline and Passthrough Patterns

`page.routeWebSocket()` (v1.48+) intercepts the WebSocket connection before it reaches the server. By not calling `connectToServer()`, the mock operates entirely offline. With `connectToServer()`, messages can be inspected or transformed in both directions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('real-time dashboard renders mock price feed (offline)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://prices.example.com/stream', ws => {
    // Offline mock — never calls connectToServer()
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'snapshot', BTC: 62000, ETH: 3400 }));

    let tickCount = 0;
    const interval = setInterval(() => {
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'tick', BTC: 62000 + tickCount++ * 10 }));
      if (tickCount >= 3) clearInterval(interval);
    }, 100);

    ws.onClose(() => clearInterval(interval));
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('btc-price')).toHaveText(/62[,.]?\d{3}/);
});

test('partial intercept: force ETH price in passthrough mode', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://prices.example.com/stream', async ws => {
    const server = await ws.connectToServer();

    // Transform server messages before forwarding to the page
    server.onMessage(rawMsg => {
      const data = JSON.parse(rawMsg as string);
      if (data.type === 'tick') data.ETH = 9999; // force known value
      ws.send(JSON.stringify(data));
    });

    // Forward client messages to server unchanged
    ws.onMessage(msg => server.send(msg));
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('eth-price')).toHaveText('9,999');
});
```

**When to use:** Testing real-time UIs (chat, trading, live dashboards) without a running WebSocket server. Use the offline pattern for unit-style UI tests; use `connectToServer()` with message transformation for integration tests against a real server where you need to control specific message payloads. [official]

**Tradeoff:** `routeWebSocket()` must be registered before `page.goto()` — calling it after the WebSocket connection is established has no effect on the existing connection. [community]

---

### Component Testing `beforeMount` Hook — Router and Store Provider Injection

Playwright CT's `beforeMount` hook lets you wrap the component under test in providers (router, Redux store, theme, i18n) without modifying the component source. The `hooksConfig` parameter carries per-test options from the test file to the browser context.

```typescript
// playwright/index.tsx — CT entry point for React
import { beforeMount } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react/hooks';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Provider } from 'react-redux';
import { createTestStore } from '../src/store/test-store';

interface HooksConfig {
  initialPath?: string;
  initialState?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

beforeMount<HooksConfig>(async ({ App, hooksConfig }) => {
  const store = createTestStore(hooksConfig?.initialState ?? {});
  return (
    <Provider store={store}>
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[hooksConfig?.initialPath ?? '/']}>
        <App />
      </MemoryRouter>
    </Provider>
  );
});
```

```typescript
// tests/ct/UserProfile.spec.tsx
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react';
import UserProfile from '../../src/components/UserProfile';

test('shows admin badge for admin role', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<UserProfile userId="u42" />, {
    hooksConfig: {
      initialPath: '/profile/u42',
      initialState: { user: { id: 'u42', role: 'admin', name: 'Alice' } },
    },
  });
  await expect(component.getByRole('img', { name: 'Admin badge' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('unmount triggers subscription cleanup', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount(<UserProfile userId="u42" />);
  await expect(component.getByText('Alice')).toBeVisible();
  await component.unmount();
  // Verify no residual DOM or error after unmount
});
```

**When to use:** When the component requires routing context, global state, or a theme provider that cannot be passed as props. Centralising provider setup in `beforeMount` keeps test files declarative. [official]

**Tradeoff:** `hooksConfig` crosses the Node-to-browser serialization boundary — only plain JSON-serializable values are supported. Functions, class instances, and Symbols cannot be passed through `hooksConfig`.

---

### Additional Community Gotchas (Cycle 27)

#### 89. `test.step()` error propagation is not isolated — it is a reporting construct, not a try-catch boundary [community]

**What:** A common misconception is that `test.step()` isolates failures. An unhandled error inside a step fails the entire test immediately, regardless of `{ box: true }` settings. `test.step()` affects the trace viewer display and reporter output only.

```typescript
// ❌ Misconception: step failure is catchable and non-fatal
test('multi-step form', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  await test.step('fill step 1', async () => {
    await page.getByLabel('Name').fill('Alice');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'NONEXISTENT' }).click(); // throws
    // ↑ Entire test fails here; lines below never execute
  });

  await test.step('fill step 2', async () => { /* never runs */ });
});

// ✅ For non-fatal multi-step checking, use expect.soft() inside steps
test('multi-step form with soft assertions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  await test.step('validate step 1 fields', async () => {
    await expect.soft(page.getByLabel('Name')).toBeVisible();
    await expect.soft(page.getByLabel('Email')).toBeVisible();
  });

  // Soft assertion failures accumulate — subsequent steps still run
  await test.step('validate step 2 fields', async () => {
    await expect.soft(page.getByLabel('Phone')).toBeVisible();
  });
  // All soft assertion failures surface together at test end
});
```

> **WHY:** `test.step()` is a scoping and labelling construct that groups actions in traces and contributes to `testStepInfo.titlePath` in reporters. Error propagation is unchanged from code outside a step. For tests that must continue after partial assertion failures, use `expect.soft()`. [community]

---

#### 90. `context.storageState()` snapshots cookies at call time — token refreshes after the call are silently missed [community]

**What:** Calling `context.storageState({ path: 'auth.json' })` snapshots the current cookie jar at that instant. If `page.goto()` triggers a silent token refresh (Set-Cookie response header) after the snapshot, the refreshed token is absent from `auth.json`. Tests that load this file subsequently start with an expired token.

```typescript
// ❌ storageState captured before token-refresh response arrives
await page.goto('/login');
await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('alice@example.com');
await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
// ← /login may redirect to /dashboard and trigger a refresh token exchange
await page.context().storageState({ path: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' });
// If the new refresh-token Set-Cookie header arrived after this line, it's missing

// ✅ Wait for the final auth network exchange before snapshotting
await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
// OR explicitly wait for the token endpoint if the app has one
await page.waitForResponse(
  resp => resp.url().includes('/api/token') && resp.status() === 200
);
await page.context().storageState({ path: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' });
```

> **WHY:** `storageState()` is synchronous with respect to the current in-memory cookie jar. Any network activity that sets new cookies after the snapshot point (token refresh, silent renew, SSO callback) is missed. Always snapshot *after* the final network exchange of the auth flow completes. [community]

---

#### 91. `routeFromHAR()` URL matching is case-sensitive — hostname case mismatches cause silent cache misses [community]

**What:** When recording a HAR and later replaying it, any URL that differs in case (e.g., `https://API.example.com/` recorded vs `https://api.example.com/` replayed) produces a cache miss. Playwright's HAR matcher performs an exact string comparison on the URL, not a case-insensitive hostname comparison as RFC 7230 permits.

```typescript
// ❌ HAR recorded against https://API.EXAMPLE.COM/graphql
// App under test requests https://api.example.com/graphql → cache miss → request falls through

// ✅ Option 1: use a case-insensitive regex URL filter
await context.routeFromHAR('./fixtures/api.har', {
  url: /api\.example\.com\/graphql/i,  // case-insensitive flag
  update: false,
});

// ✅ Option 2: post-process the HAR file to normalise URL casing
// (run a script lowercasing all .request.url and .response.redirectURL fields)

// ✅ Option 3: configure the app's API client to always use lowercase hostnames
// in the test environment, eliminating the mismatch at the source
```

> **WHY:** RFC 7230 section 2.7.3 specifies that the host component of HTTP URIs is case-insensitive. Playwright's HAR matching operates at the string level and does not apply RFC semantics. Any case variation between the recorded and replayed URL causes a miss. Set `notFound: 'abort'` on `routeFromHAR()` to surface cache misses as request failures rather than silently falling through to the network. [community]

---

#### 92. `page.waitForResponse()` resolves on the first match — background polling triggers premature resolution [community]

**What:** `page.waitForResponse()` resolves as soon as *any* response matching the predicate is received. If the page fires two requests to the same endpoint (initial load + background refresh poller), the wait resolves on the first one — which may be a 304 Not Modified with an empty body, causing `response.json()` to throw.

```typescript
// ❌ Resolves on first /api/items response (may be a cached 304)
const response = await page.waitForResponse('**/api/items');
const data = await response.json(); // throws: body is empty on 304

// ✅ Add a status-code predicate to require a full 200 response
const response = await page.waitForResponse(
  resp => resp.url().includes('/api/items') && resp.status() === 200
);
const data = await response.json();

// ✅ Use Promise.all to eliminate the race between setup and the triggering action
const [response] = await Promise.all([
  page.waitForResponse(
    resp => resp.url().includes('/api/items') && resp.status() === 200
  ),
  page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh' }).click(),
]);
const data = await response.json();
```

> **WHY:** `page.waitForResponse()` is a single-use promise that resolves on the first event matching the predicate. A background polling interval or browser prefetch can satisfy the predicate before the user-triggered request completes. Always include a status code check in the predicate, and use `Promise.all` to avoid the setup-before-action race condition. [community]

---

#### 93. `--grep` and `--shard` are independent — grep-filtered test counts alter shard distribution unpredictably [community]

**What:** When using `--grep` alongside `--shard`, Playwright computes shard boundaries based on the *filtered* test count, not the full suite. Using `--shard=1/4 --grep=@smoke` runs only the first 25% of smoke tests, not all smoke tests on one shard. You cannot combine tag-based filtering with sharding to mean "all matching tests on this machine."

```bash
# ❌ Intent: run ALL @smoke tests on shard 1
# Actual: runs only the first 25% of @smoke tests
npx playwright test --grep=@smoke --shard=1/4

# ✅ Run all @smoke tests without sharding — they're fast enough for one machine
npx playwright test --grep=@smoke

# ✅ Use a dedicated project for tag isolation instead of CLI grep+shard combo
# playwright.config.ts:
#   { name: 'smoke', grep: /@smoke/, testMatch: /tests\/e2e\/.*/ }
# Then: npx playwright test --project=smoke
```

> **WHY:** Sharding and grep filtering operate as independent pipeline stages. The shard index is computed *after* grep filtering is applied — there is no "assign all matching tests to shard 1" mode. Combine `--grep` with a named project configuration for predictable isolation of test subsets in CI. [community]

## Key APIs Added / Updated — Cycle 27 Summary

| API | Version | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `--shard=x/y` + `fullyParallel: true` | v1.0+ / v1.7+ | Distribute individual tests (not files) across CI shards for balanced timing | Suites with unevenly-sized spec files; always pair with `fullyParallel: true` |
| `reporter: 'blob'` + `merge-reports` | v1.37+ | Accumulate per-shard results and merge into any report format in a post-job | Multi-shard CI pipelines needing a single consolidated HTML or JUnit report |
| `request` fixture (context-bound) | v1.0+ | Shares cookies with the browser context for hybrid API+UI tests | API-first data seeding where the seeded state must be visible to browser navigations |
| `playwright.request.newContext()` | v1.0+ | Creates an isolated HTTP client with its own cookie jar | Parallel API sessions, unauthenticated API verification, mid-test cookie isolation |
| `toHaveScreenshot({ mask, clip })` | v1.23+ | Black out volatile elements and restrict capture region for stable visual diffs | Pages with timestamps, avatars, or third-party ad slots |
| `updateSnapshots: 'changed'` | v1.50+ | Regenerate only baselines for currently-failing screenshot tests | Incremental UI work — avoids silently accepting unrelated regressions in PRs |
| `page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true })` | v1.60+ | Include element refs in YAML snapshot enabling DOM interaction after a11y assertion | Tests that verify accessibility tree structure then interact with identified nodes |
| `page.addInitScript(fn)` | v1.0+ | Inject JS before any page script to override native browser APIs | Mocking geolocation, battery, Device Motion, or exotic `window.matchMedia` values |
| `projects[].dependencies + teardown` | v1.31+ | Declare ordered setup/teardown projects with full fixture and trace support | Auth setup, DB seeding — replaces config-based `globalSetup` when fixture access needed |
| `locator.and(other)` | v1.27+ | Intersection locator: element must satisfy both locators simultaneously | Dual-attribute matching (role + aria state, role + test ID) without compound CSS |
| `expect(page).toHaveURL(predicate)` | v1.57+ | Assert URL properties with a function `(url: URL) => boolean` | Query parameter logic, multi-condition URL checks, arithmetic on page number params |
| `page.routeWebSocket(url, handler)` | v1.48+ | Full offline WebSocket mock or server passthrough with message transformation | Real-time UIs (chat, trading, live dashboards) without a running WebSocket server |
| CT `beforeMount` / `afterMount` hooks | experimental-ct | Wrap components in router/store/theme providers without modifying component source | React/Vue/Svelte CT tests requiring context providers or global state initialization |

## Cycle 28 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 1: `expect(page).toHaveURL()` with Predicate Function (v1.57+) [official]

`toHaveURL()` accepts a function `(url: URL) => boolean` in addition to strings and regexes. Use the predicate form when assertions require URL logic — multi-param checks, numeric comparisons, or decoding encoded values — that a regex cannot express clearly.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/pagination.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('pagination increments page param correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products?page=1&size=20');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }).click();

  // Predicate: check both params simultaneously — impossible with a single regex
  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) =>
    url.searchParams.get('page') === '2' &&
    url.searchParams.get('size') === '20'
  );
});

test('filter resets page to 1 when applied', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products?page=5&category=electronics');
  await page.getByLabel('Category').selectOption('books');

  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) => {
    const pageParam = Number(url.searchParams.get('page'));
    return pageParam === 1;  // arithmetic check not possible with plain regex
  });
});

test('sort order is reflected in URL canonically', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search?q=laptop');
  await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Sort by' }).selectOption('price-asc');

  // Verify sort param exists and is one of the valid values
  await expect(page).toHaveURL((url: URL) =>
    ['price-asc', 'price-desc', 'relevance'].includes(url.searchParams.get('sort') ?? '')
  );
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use the predicate form for multi-condition or arithmetic URL checks. Use a string/regex for simple path or single-param assertions — predicates have no retry-debugging message without a custom `message` option. When NOT to use: single-condition URL assertions (prefer `toHaveURL(/pattern/)` for readability). Alternative: `page.waitForURL((url) => ...)` for imperative waiting before assertions.

---

### Pattern 2: `page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true })` — Interact After ARIA Assertion (v1.60+) [official]

The `ref: true` option on `ariaSnapshot()` / `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` appends short stable element references (`[ref=e1]`) to each node. You can then use these refs as locator arguments immediately after the assertion, combining structural accessibility verification with element interaction.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/aria-interact.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('navigates via aria-identified links', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/nav');

  // Snapshot with ref=true: each ARIA node gets a [ref=eN] token
  const snapshot = await page.getByRole('navigation').ariaSnapshot({ ref: true });

  // Assert structure — same as toMatchAriaSnapshot
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation:
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Home" [ref=e1]
        - listitem:
          - link "Products" [ref=e2]
        - listitem:
          - link "About" [ref=e3]
  `);

  // Use the ref to locate the Products link by its verified ARIA identity
  // page.getByAria(ref) is the idiomatic way to resolve refs
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Products' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/products/);
});

test('identifies and dismisses the correct dialog button', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();

  // Verify the dialog has exactly the expected action buttons before acting
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - dialog "Settings":
      - button "Cancel"
      - button "Save changes"
  `);

  // Now click "Save changes" with full confidence the structure was verified
  await page.getByRole('dialog').getByRole('button', { name: 'Save changes' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeAttached();
});

test('full-page aria snapshot for AI-assisted diagnostics', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // ref:true + mode:'ai' for compact format suitable for LLM prompts
  const aiTree = await page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai', ref: true });
  // Feed to LLM: "Here is the page tree. Which element matches the Delete User action?"
  console.log(aiTree);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when you need to verify ARIA structure AND interact with a specific identified node in one step. The snapshot assertion + ref-based interaction is most valuable for complex UIs where similar buttons exist at different depths. Do NOT use `ref: true` when you only need the structural assertion — it adds ref metadata to the snapshot YAML, making diffs noisier on updates. Alternative: scope with `getByRole` + `filter` for most interactions without needing refs.

---

### Pattern 3: `request` Fixture vs. `playwright.request.newContext()` — When to Use Each [community]

The `request` fixture shares cookie state with the browser context. `playwright.request.newContext()` creates a completely isolated HTTP client. Using the wrong one causes silent auth failures or cookie leaks between parallel sessions.

```typescript
// ✅ CORRECT — request fixture: shares cookies with the page (use for hybrid API+UI tests)
test('API-seeded data appears in UI', async ({ page, request }) => {
  // request shares the same storageState as page — cookies and localStorage included
  const res = await request.post('/api/items', {
    data: { name: 'Widget', ownerId: 'test-user-1' },
  });
  expect(res.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  const { id } = await res.json();

  // Navigation picks up the same auth cookies seeded by storageState
  await page.goto(`/items/${id}`);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Widget' })).toBeVisible();
});

// ✅ CORRECT — newContext(): isolated session (use for unauthenticated or alternate-role calls)
test('unauthenticated request returns 401', async ({ playwright }) => {
  // Completely fresh context — no cookies from storageState
  const unauthRequest = await playwright.request.newContext({
    baseURL: process.env.WEB_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  });

  const res = await unauthRequest.get('/api/admin/users');
  expect(res.status()).toBe(401);
  await unauthRequest.dispose();  // always dispose to release resources
});

// ✅ CORRECT — newContext() for concurrent parallel sessions with different auth
test('admin and viewer see different data', async ({ playwright, page }) => {
  const viewerRequest = await playwright.request.newContext({
    storageState: 'e2e/.auth/viewer.json',
    baseURL: process.env.WEB_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  });

  // page uses admin auth; viewerRequest uses viewer auth — completely independent
  const [adminRes, viewerRes] = await Promise.all([
    page.request.get('/api/settings'),      // admin — from fixture (shared cookies)
    viewerRequest.get('/api/settings'),     // viewer — isolated context
  ]);

  expect(adminRes.status()).toBe(200);
  expect(viewerRes.status()).toBe(403);
  await viewerRequest.dispose();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Always use the `request` fixture when the API call must share auth state with the browser (seeding, reading state the UI depends on). Use `playwright.request.newContext()` when you need a completely isolated session (parallel role tests, unauthenticated assertions). Do NOT call `playwright.request.newContext()` when you need cookies set by `storageState` without passing `{ storageState: ... }` explicitly — those cookies are not loaded automatically. Alternative: `page.request` is an alias for the context-bound request client when inside a test body.

---

### Pattern 4: Region-Scoped Visual Regression with `toHaveScreenshot({ clip })` [official]

Capture only a specific rectangular region of the page for visual regression rather than the whole page. Reduces noise from layout shifts outside the component under test and speeds up snapshot comparison.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/visual-clip.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('hero section visual regression — isolated clip region', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  // Clip to only the hero section — eliminates noise from dynamic navbar/footer
  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('hero-section.png', {
    clip:           { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 600 },
    maxDiffPixels:  30,
  });
});

test('data table visual regression — clip to element bounds', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/admin/users');
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();

  // Compute table bounding box at runtime and clip to it
  const table       = page.getByRole('table');
  const boundingBox = await table.boundingBox();
  expect(boundingBox, 'table must have a layout box').not.toBeNull();

  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('user-table.png', {
    clip: {
      x:      boundingBox!.x - 8,   // 8px padding around table
      y:      boundingBox!.y - 8,
      width:  boundingBox!.width  + 16,
      height: boundingBox!.height + 16,
    },
    maxDiffPixels: 20,
  });
});

// Simpler alternative: take screenshot of the locator directly (auto-clips to element bounds)
test('badge component visual regression', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/design-system/badges');
  const badge = page.getByTestId('status-badge-active');
  await expect(badge).toBeVisible();
  // locator.toHaveScreenshot() auto-clips to the element's bounding box
  await expect(badge).toHaveScreenshot('status-badge-active.png');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `clip` gives deterministic bounds independent of page layout. Use when the component position on the page is stable but surrounding content is dynamic. Do NOT use `clip` with hardcoded pixel coordinates if the component position changes between viewports or OS font-rendering differences shift layout — use `locator.toHaveScreenshot()` instead, which auto-clips to the element. Alternative: `mask` hides specific elements while keeping the full page screenshot; `clip` restricts the capture region entirely.

---

### Pattern 5: `testProject.grep` — Project-Level Tag Routing Without CLI Flags [official]

Configure per-project `grep` patterns in `playwright.config.ts` to route tests by tag automatically. Eliminates the need to remember complex `--grep` invocations in CI commands and makes tag routing explicit in code review.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './e2e',
  projects: [
    {
      name:  'setup',
      testMatch: /auth\.setup\.ts/,
    },
    {
      // Smoke project: only tests tagged @smoke, runs on every PR
      name:         'smoke-chromium',
      grep:         /@smoke/,
      use:          { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], storageState: 'e2e/.auth/user.json' },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
    },
    {
      // Regression project: all tests except @wip, runs nightly
      name:         'regression-chromium',
      grepInvert:   /@wip/,
      use:          { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], storageState: 'e2e/.auth/user.json' },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
    },
    {
      // Accessibility project: only @a11y-tagged tests with reduced parallelism
      name:         'accessibility',
      grep:         /@a11y/,
      workers:      2,
      use:          { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
    },
  ],
});
```

```bash
# PR gate: only smoke project
npx playwright test --project=smoke-chromium

# Nightly a11y gate
npx playwright test --project=accessibility

# Full nightly regression
npx playwright test --project=regression-chromium
```

```typescript
// e2e/specs/checkout.spec.ts — tests declare their own tags
test('checkout completes end-to-end', { tag: ['@smoke', '@critical'] }, async ({ page }) => {
  // Included in smoke-chromium AND regression-chromium
});

test('order history paginates correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  // No @smoke tag — only in regression-chromium
});

test('checkout form is accessible', { tag: '@a11y' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // Only in accessibility project
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Project-level `grep` encodes test routing decisions in code, making them reviewable and discoverable. Use when you have stable, long-lived tag categories (smoke, regression, a11y). Do NOT use when tag sets change frequently — each grep config change requires a `playwright.config.ts` PR. Alternative: CLI `--grep` is more flexible for ad-hoc runs; project-based grep is for CI permanence.

---

### Pattern 6: Fixture-Based Dynamic Test Skip via Feature Flag API [community]

Skip tests at fixture level by checking feature flags from the API before the test body runs. This avoids test bodies that start, do partial work, then skip mid-way — a common source of confusing partial failures.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/feature-flags.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

type FeatureFlagFixtures = {
  featureFlags: Record<string, boolean>;
  requireFlag: (flag: string) => void;
};

export const test = base.extend<FeatureFlagFixtures>({
  // Worker-scoped: fetch once per worker, not per test
  featureFlags: [async ({ request }, use) => {
    const res   = await request.get('/api/feature-flags');
    const flags: Record<string, boolean> = res.ok() ? await res.json() : {};
    await use(flags);
  }, { scope: 'worker' }],

  requireFlag: async ({ featureFlags }, use) => {
    // Returns a function that skips the test if the named flag is off
    await use((flag: string) => {
      if (!featureFlags[flag]) {
        test.skip(true, `Feature flag "${flag}" is disabled — skipping test`);
      }
    });
  },
});

// e2e/specs/new-checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/feature-flags';

test('new checkout flow completes', async ({ page, requireFlag }) => {
  requireFlag('new-checkout-v2');  // skips entire test if flag is off
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('checkout-v2-header')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout\/payment/);
});

test('legacy checkout still works', async ({ page }) => {
  // No flag guard — always runs regardless of feature flags
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Checkout' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Worker-scoped flag fetching costs one network call per worker (not per test). Do NOT use this pattern for flags that change during a test run — fetch once at worker start and cache. Alternative: environment variable flags (`process.env.FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT === 'true'`) are faster but require separate CI configuration per environment; API-based flags work identically across all environments.

---

### Pattern 7: Network Cache Header Regression Testing [community]

Test that API responses include correct `Cache-Control`, `ETag`, and related HTTP caching headers. These regressions are invisible to functional tests but cause performance and security issues in production.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/caching.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('static assets have long-lived Cache-Control headers', async ({ page }) => {
  const assetCacheHeaders: Array<{ url: string; cacheControl: string }> = [];

  page.on('response', response => {
    const url = response.url();
    if (url.match(/\.(js|css|woff2|png|svg)(\?|$)/)) {
      const cc = response.headers()['cache-control'] ?? '';
      assetCacheHeaders.push({ url, cacheControl: cc });
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  // Every static asset should have long-lived immutable caching
  for (const { url, cacheControl } of assetCacheHeaders) {
    expect(cacheControl, `Missing caching on: ${url}`)
      .toMatch(/max-age=\d{5,}/);  // at least 10000 seconds
  }
});

test('API responses carry ETag for conditional requests', async ({ request }) => {
  const first = await request.get('/api/products?page=1');
  expect(first.status()).toBe(200);
  const etag = first.headers()['etag'];
  expect(etag, 'ETag header must be present on list API responses').toBeTruthy();

  // Conditional request using received ETag — should get 304
  const second = await request.get('/api/products?page=1', {
    headers: { 'If-None-Match': etag! },
  });
  expect(second.status()).toBe(304);
});

test('sensitive endpoints are never cached', async ({ request }) => {
  const sensitiveEndpoints = [
    '/api/user/profile',
    '/api/payment/methods',
  ];

  for (const endpoint of sensitiveEndpoints) {
    const res = await request.get(endpoint);
    const cc  = res.headers()['cache-control'] ?? '';
    expect(cc, `${endpoint} must have no-store`).toContain('no-store');
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Cache header testing catches a class of regression that functional tests never surface. Run in a dedicated spec file; do not mix with functional test files. Do NOT assert on specific `max-age` values for API responses where TTL is configured externally — assert on the presence of the directive, not its exact value. Alternative: HAR recording (`tracing.startHar`) captures all response headers offline for bulk auditing without writing per-endpoint assertions.

---

### Pattern 8: `addInitScript` for Exotic Browser API Mocking [community]

Use `page.addInitScript()` to replace browser APIs that Playwright cannot configure natively — `matchMedia` with custom queries, `navigator.connection`, `BatteryManager`, and `DeviceMotionEvent`. The script runs before any page JavaScript, so the app sees the mocked API from first render.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/device-apis.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('app detects narrow viewport via matchMedia override', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const originalMatchMedia = window.matchMedia.bind(window);
    window.matchMedia = (query: string): MediaQueryList => {
      if (query === '(max-width: 768px)') {
        return {
          ...originalMatchMedia(query),
          matches: true,
          addEventListener:    () => {},
          removeEventListener: () => {},
        } as MediaQueryList;
      }
      return originalMatchMedia(query);
    };
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Hamburger menu visible because matchMedia thinks we're on a narrow display
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Open menu')).toBeVisible();
});

test('battery saver mode disables animations', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (navigator as any).getBattery = async () => ({
      level:              0.06,   // 6% — triggers battery saver UI
      charging:           false,
      chargingTime:       Infinity,
      dischargingTime:    540,
      addEventListener:   () => {},
      removeEventListener: () => {},
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  const animDuration = await page.evaluate(() =>
    getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--animation-duration').trim()
  );
  expect(animDuration).toBe('0ms');
});

test('network-aware component shows slow connection warning', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'connection', {
      get: () => ({
        effectiveType:  '2g',
        downlink:        0.3,
        rtt:             600,
        saveData:        true,
        addEventListener: () => {},
      }),
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /slow connection|data saver/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `addInitScript` runs once per navigation — re-navigation refreshes the page context and the init script runs again automatically (no re-registration needed). Use `page.context().addInitScript()` when the mock must persist identically across ALL new pages opened in the same context (e.g., popups). Do NOT use for APIs that Playwright already controls natively (`navigator.geolocation`, color scheme, locale) — Playwright's built-in emulation options are more reliable and interop correctly with headless mode. Alternative: `page.route()` for network-level mocking; `addInitScript` is for in-page JavaScript API surface.

---

### Pattern 9: Retry-Safe Cleanup with `testInfo.errors` in `afterEach` [community]

Check `testInfo.errors.length` in `afterEach` to run cleanup conditionally — skipping cleanup on pass (for speed) but always cleaning up on failure. Combined with `testInfo.retry`, this prevents stale data from causing retry failures.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/admin.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Track created resource IDs for teardown
let createdUserId: number | null = null;

test.afterEach(async ({ request }, testInfo) => {
  // Clean up if the test failed OR was a retry (retries leave data from previous attempt)
  if ((testInfo.errors.length > 0 || testInfo.retry > 0) && createdUserId !== null) {
    await request.delete(`/api/users/${createdUserId}`).catch(() => {
      // Deletion may 404 if the test never created the user — suppress the error
    });
    createdUserId = null;
  }
});

test('admin can create and delete a user', async ({ page, request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/users', {
    data: { email: `test-${crypto.randomUUID()}@example.com`, role: 'viewer' },
  });
  expect(res.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  createdUserId = (await res.json()).id;

  await page.goto(`/admin/users/${createdUserId}`);
  await expect(page.getByText('viewer')).toBeVisible();

  // Delete via UI
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete user' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/admin\/users$/);

  createdUserId = null;  // deletion succeeded — afterEach skip flag set
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Conditional cleanup avoids unnecessary API calls on passing tests, improving suite speed by skipping teardown in the common path. Use when cleanup is slow (database teardown, file deletion) and tests pass reliably. Do NOT skip cleanup for destructive operations (sending emails, charging payments, provisioning cloud resources) — always clean those up unconditionally. Alternative: `test.step` with try/finally for in-test cleanup; project `teardown` for suite-level cleanup that must survive CI failures.

---

### Pattern 10: `getByRole` with `exact: false` for Substring Accessible Name Matching [official]

`getByRole()` defaults to exact name matching. Pass `exact: false` to match accessible names that contain the target string as a substring — useful for dynamic names that include data (e.g., "Order #12345", "Hello, Alice").

```typescript
// e2e/specs/dynamic-names.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('any order notification is dismissible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/orders');

  // Order number is dynamic — exact match requires knowing it in advance
  // exact: false matches any alert whose accessible name contains "Order"
  const orderAlert = page.getByRole('alert').filter({
    has: page.getByText(/Order #\d+/),
  });
  await expect(orderAlert).toBeVisible();
  await orderAlert.getByRole('button', { name: 'Dismiss' }).click();
  await expect(orderAlert).not.toBeAttached();
});

test('personalised greeting shows correct username', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Heading is "Hello, Alice Smith" — exact would require knowing the name
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Hello', exact: false })
  ).toBeVisible();
});

test('status badge for any running state is visible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/jobs');

  // Badge text is "Running: 3 of 12 complete" — match on stable fragment
  const badge = page.getByRole('status', { name: 'Running', exact: false });
  await expect(badge).toBeVisible();
  await expect(badge).toContainText(/\d+ of \d+/);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `exact: false` makes locators more resilient to dynamic content but also less precise — a page with multiple elements containing the same substring will still throw a strict-mode error. Use sparingly on genuinely dynamic names that include data. Do NOT use `exact: false` when element names are stable — it masks future regressions where element names change unexpectedly. Alternative: `locator.filter({ hasText: /pattern/ })` for regex substring matching on any element type.

---

### Pattern 11: Parallel-Safe Worker-Scoped Mock HTTP Server [community]

Start a real HTTP test-double server once per Playwright worker using a worker-scoped fixture. Assign port `0` so the OS picks a free port — no conflicts between parallel workers.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/mock-server.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import http             from 'node:http';
import { AddressInfo }  from 'node:net';

type MockHandler = (req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse) => void;

type MockServerFixtures = {
  mockServerUrl: string;
  addRoute: (path: string, handler: MockHandler) => void;
};

export const test = base.extend<MockServerFixtures, { _server: http.Server }>({
  _server: [async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
    const routes = new Map<string, MockHandler>();
    const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
      const handler = routes.get(req.url ?? '');
      if (handler) {
        handler(req, res);
      } else {
        res.writeHead(404).end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Not found' }));
      }
    });

    // Port 0: OS assigns a free port — eliminates worker port collisions
    await new Promise<void>(resolve => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve()));
    const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;
    console.log(`[worker ${workerInfo.workerIndex}] Mock server started on :${port}`);

    // Attach routes map so fixtures can add to it
    (server as any)._routes = routes;
    await use(server);

    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) =>
      server.close(err => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()))
    );
  }, { scope: 'worker' }],

  mockServerUrl: async ({ _server }, use) => {
    const { port } = _server.address() as AddressInfo;
    await use(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}`);
  },

  addRoute: async ({ _server }, use) => {
    const routes: Map<string, MockHandler> = (_server as any)._routes;
    await use((path, handler) => routes.set(path, handler));
  },
});

// e2e/specs/email-preview.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/mock-server';

test('email preview iframe renders template', async ({ page, mockServerUrl, addRoute }) => {
  addRoute('/templates/welcome', (_req, res) => {
    res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/html' });
    res.end('<h1>Welcome to our service!</h1>');
  });

  // Point the app's iframe at the worker-specific mock server
  await page.route('**/api/email-template**', route =>
    route.fulfill({ status: 302, headers: { Location: `${mockServerUrl}/templates/welcome` } })
  );

  await page.goto('/campaigns/create');
  await page.getByLabel('Template').selectOption('welcome');
  const frame = page.frameLocator('[data-testid="email-preview"]');
  await expect(frame.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Welcome' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Worker-scoped HTTP servers amortize startup cost across all tests in the worker. Use for test doubles serving binary content, streaming responses, or chunked encoding that `page.route()` cannot replicate. Do NOT use this pattern when all you need is JSON mocking — `page.route()` is simpler and has no port management overhead. Alternative: `page.routeFromHAR()` for replay-based mocking; MSW for React component testing with realistic fetch behavior.

---

### Pattern 12: `toMatchAriaSnapshot` with `children: 'contain'` for Partial Tree Assertions [official]

Use `children: 'contain'` to assert that the ARIA tree contains expected nodes without requiring an exact match of the full tree. This makes snapshots resilient to design-system additions while still verifying critical structural elements.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/nav-partial.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('navigation always includes key routes regardless of additions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // children: 'contain' — asserts these items exist, ignores extra items
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation:
      - list:
        - /listitem/:
          - link "Home"
        - /listitem/:
          - link "Products"
  `, { children: 'contain' });
  // If nav has 5 items, test still passes — only the 2 listed are verified
});

test('modal dialog always has a close mechanism', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();

  // Only assert critical elements — ignore implementation-detail elements
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - dialog:
      - /heading/:
          /Settings/
      - button "Save changes"
  `, { children: 'contain' });
});

test('form has required fields (partial check ignores optional extras)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/signup');

  await expect(page.getByRole('form')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - form:
      - textbox "Email" [required]
      - textbox "Password" [required]
  `, { children: 'contain' });
  // Optional fields (name, phone, referral code) are ignored
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `contain` mode is resilient to additions (new nav items, extra buttons, optional fields) but does not catch removals of unlisted nodes. Use for "safety net" checks that verify critical navigation and interaction points exist across releases. Do NOT use `contain` for structural regression tests where you want to catch accidental removals — use the default `equal` or `deep-equal` mode. Alternative: scoping `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` to a sub-locator already limits blast radius without needing `contain` mode.

---

### Pattern 13: Accessibility Violation Fingerprinting Fixture [community]

Store accessibility violation fingerprints (rule ID + CSS target paths) rather than raw HTML-coupled violation objects. This decouples a11y regression tests from cosmetic HTML changes while still catching new rule violations.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/a11y.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder       from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { NodeResult } from 'axe-core';

export type ViolationFingerprint = { ruleId: string; targets: string[] };

type A11yFixtures = {
  checkA11y: (selector?: string) => Promise<ViolationFingerprint[]>;
};

export const test = base.extend<A11yFixtures>({
  checkA11y: async ({ page }, use, testInfo) => {
    const checkA11y = async (selector?: string): Promise<ViolationFingerprint[]> => {
      const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa']);

      if (selector) builder.include(selector);

      const results = await builder.analyze();

      // Fingerprint: rule ID + CSS target paths — immune to HTML text changes
      const fingerprints: ViolationFingerprint[] = results.violations.map(v => ({
        ruleId:  v.id,
        targets: v.nodes.flatMap((n: NodeResult) => n.target as string[]),
      }));

      // Attach full axe results as artifact for debugging (not part of assertion)
      await testInfo.attach(`axe-full-${selector ?? 'page'}`, {
        contentType: 'application/json',
        body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
      });

      return fingerprints;
    };

    await use(checkA11y);
  },
});

// e2e/specs/a11y.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/a11y';

test('login page — zero WCAG violations', async ({ page, checkA11y }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  const violations = await checkA11y();
  // Snapshot the fingerprints — run --update-snapshots when intentionally fixing violations
  expect(violations).toMatchSnapshot('login-a11y-fingerprints.json');
});

test('settings modal has no a11y violations when opened', async ({ page, checkA11y }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

  // Scope scan to dialog only — ignore background content violations
  const violations = await checkA11y('[role="dialog"]');
  expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Fingerprinting is resilient to cosmetic HTML changes (text rewrites, class name refactors) while still catching rule-level violations. Use in teams where known pre-existing violations exist and you want to track progress without snapshot noise. Do NOT fingerprint without also reviewing the attached full violations JSON — fingerprints can mask the severity of a violation. Alternative: `expect(violations).toHaveLength(0)` for zero-violation enforcement on greenfield projects; `.disableRules(['known-rule'])` for targeted suppression.

---

### Pattern 14: `page.clock.install()` with Timer Cascade Testing [official]

Install the Playwright clock to control `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `performance.now()` simultaneously. Unlike `setFixedTime()` (which only freezes `Date`), `clock.install()` intercepts the entire timer infrastructure — enabling multi-step timer cascade tests.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/clock-cascade.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session expiry warns then logs out automatically', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install full clock BEFORE page load — timers registered at init are captured
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2025-06-15T09:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  // App registers a 15-minute inactivity timer on mount
  // Advance to just before the warning (14 min 59 s)
  await page.clock.fastForward(14 * 60 * 1000 + 59 * 1000);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: /session expiring/i })).not.toBeVisible();

  // Cross the 15-minute threshold — triggers warning
  await page.clock.fastForward(1_000);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Advance past the 60-second countdown — auto-logout fires
  await page.clock.fastForward(61_000);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  await expect(page.getByText('Your session has expired')).toBeVisible();
});

test('scheduler retries with exponential backoff', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.clock.install();

  let callCount = 0;
  await page.route('**/api/jobs/process', async route => {
    callCount++;
    if (callCount < 3) {
      await route.fulfill({ status: 503, body: 'Service unavailable' });
    } else {
      await route.fulfill({ status: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ status: 'done' }) });
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/scheduler');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Run job' }).click();

  // First attempt fails immediately
  await expect(page.getByTestId('job-status')).toHaveText('Failed (retry in 5s)');

  // Jump past 5s backoff — retry 1
  await page.clock.fastForward(5_000);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('job-status')).toHaveText('Failed (retry in 10s)');

  // Jump past 10s backoff — retry 2 succeeds
  await page.clock.fastForward(10_000);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('job-status')).toHaveText('Completed');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `clock.install()` intercepts ALL timers including third-party library timers (React Query, Axios retry, analytics heartbeats). This can cause unexpected UI behaviour when libraries rely on `setTimeout` for internal scheduling. Use `clock.install({ toFake: ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval'] })` to limit which APIs are faked. Do NOT use `clock.install()` without advancing the clock — the clock is paused after install and any timer-dependent code will hang indefinitely. Alternative: `page.clock.setFixedTime()` when you only need to freeze `Date` without intercepting timers; `page.clock.fastForward()` vs `runFor()` differ — fastForward jumps in one step, runFor fires each intermediate callback.

---

### Pattern 15: `context.waitForEvent('page')` vs `page.waitForEvent('popup')` — Disambiguation [community]

`context.waitForEvent('page')` captures ALL new page creations in the context. `page.waitForEvent('popup')` only captures popups that originated via the current page's `window.open()` or `target=_blank`. Using the wrong one causes missed events or premature resolution on an unrelated tab.

```typescript
// e2e/specs/new-tab.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ✅ page.waitForEvent('popup') — opened by this page's window.open() or target=_blank link
test('external link opens in new tab', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/blog/post-123');

  const [popup] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForEvent('popup'),  // only fires for popups from THIS page
    page.getByRole('link', { name: 'View source on GitHub' }).click(),
  ]);

  await popup.waitForLoadState();
  await expect(popup).toHaveURL(/github\.com/);
});

// ✅ context.waitForEvent('page') — use for programmatic navigation and OAuth popups
test('OAuth sign-in popup completes', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  const [oauthPopup] = await Promise.all([
    context.waitForEvent('page'),  // catches all new pages in context
    page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in with Google' }).click(),
  ]);

  await oauthPopup.getByLabel('Email').fill('test@googletest.example.com');
  await oauthPopup.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next' }).click();
  await oauthPopup.waitForEvent('close', { timeout: 15_000 });

  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
});

// ✅ context.on('page') — for tests where multiple tabs open at unpredictable times
test('report generator opens multiple preview tabs', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const openedTabs: import('@playwright/test').Page[] = [];
  context.on('page', newPage => openedTabs.push(newPage));

  await page.goto('/reports');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Preview all' }).click();

  // Wait for all preview tabs to open (app opens one per report)
  await expect.poll(() => openedTabs.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);

  // All tabs should show the report viewer
  for (const tab of openedTabs) {
    await tab.waitForLoadState();
    await expect(tab.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `page.waitForEvent('popup')` is scoped and safer for controlled window.open() flows. `context.waitForEvent('page')` catches everything — including background navigations from service workers or browser-initiated prefetch that can resolve the promise prematurely. Scope to `page.waitForEvent('popup')` whenever possible. Do NOT use `context.waitForEvent('page')` if the app opens multiple new pages simultaneously — only the first is captured; use `context.on('page', handler)` for multi-tab scenarios. Alternative: `page.waitForEvent('popup')` + `page.runAndWaitForPopup()` for single-popup flows; `context.on('page', ...)` for unlimited multi-tab flows.
