## Cycle 28 — Community Gotchas

### 94. `page.clock.install()` captures only timers registered AFTER installation — module-level intervals are missed [community]

**What:** If an app registers a `setInterval` during module initialization (before `page.goto()`), `page.clock.install()` called after `page.goto()` does not control that interval. Advancing the clock does not fire the callback.

**WHY:** `clock.install()` replaces the global timer functions with fakes. Timers registered before installation hold a reference to the original `setTimeout`/`setInterval` functions and are not transferred to the fake clock implementation.

**Fix:** Always call `page.clock.install()` BEFORE `page.goto()`. This ensures the page's script environment sees the fake clock from the very first script execution.

```typescript
// ❌ Too late — app's setInterval registered at module load uses real timers
test('broken clock install order', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');  // app registers setInterval during boot
  await page.clock.install();     // misses already-registered intervals
  await page.clock.fastForward(5_000);
  // setInterval callback never fires — assertion times out
});

// ✅ Install clock before navigation so all timers use the fake clock
test('correct clock install order', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install();     // fake timers in place before any scripts run
  await page.goto('/dashboard');  // app's setInterval now uses fake clock
  await page.clock.fastForward(5_000);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('auto-refresh-count')).toHaveText('1');
});
```

---

### 95. `locator.boundingBox()` returns `null` for hidden elements — crashing `clip` usage in `toHaveScreenshot()` [community]

**What:** `await locator.boundingBox()` returns `null` for elements that are in the DOM but are not rendered (`display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or zero-area). Passing `null` to `clip` in `toHaveScreenshot()` causes a runtime TypeError.

**WHY:** `boundingBox()` returns `null` rather than throwing when an element has no layout box. This is by design — elements with `display: none` have no position or dimensions.

**Fix:** Assert `toBeVisible()` before calling `boundingBox()`, then add a non-null assertion before using the result in `clip`.

```typescript
// ❌ Crashes with TypeError if element is hidden or detached
const box = await page.getByTestId('chart').boundingBox();
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot({ clip: box! }); // TypeError if box is null

// ✅ Guard before use
const chart = page.getByTestId('chart');
await expect(chart).toBeVisible();                    // ensures element is rendered
const box   = await chart.boundingBox();
expect(box,   'chart must have a layout box').not.toBeNull();
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot({ clip: box! });
```

---

### 96. `request.storageState()` in setup only saves cookies set BY that API request — browser-set CSRF cookies are excluded [community]

**What:** When authenticating via `page.request.post()` (API-only, no browser navigation), calling `request.storageState({ path })` captures only cookies set by that `APIRequestContext`. Cookies set by the browser during `page.goto()` redirects (CSRF tokens, device fingerprinting) are not included.

**WHY:** `APIRequestContext` and the browser's cookie jar are separate subsystems. The `request` fixture in a test shares cookies with the page only when both are in the same context. Setup-file `request` objects created without a `page` context do not share the browser cookie jar.

**Fix:** In setup files, authenticate via full browser navigation (`page.goto()`), then call `page.context().storageState({ path })` to capture ALL cookies including browser-set ones.

```typescript
// ❌ Misses browser-set CSRF cookies — tests get 403 Forbidden
setup('authenticate via API only', async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/auth/login', { data: { email: '...', password: '...' } });
  await request.storageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/user.json' });  // missing CSRF token
});

// ✅ Full browser navigation captures every cookie
setup('authenticate via browser', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await expect(page).not.toHaveURL(/login/);
  await page.context().storageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/user.json' }); // all cookies captured
});
```

---

### 97. `testProject.grep` regex matches the full title string including `describe` block names [community]

**What:** When using `grep: /@smoke/` in a project config, `test.describe('Cart @smoke group', ...)` causes ALL tests inside that describe block to match — including tests that do not have the `@smoke` tag in their own title.

**WHY:** Playwright's grep filter matches against the full title: `"{describe title} > {test title}"`. A `@smoke` substring in a `describe` name makes every test in that block match `/@smoke/`.

**Fix:** Avoid tag strings in `describe` block names. Use the `{ tag: [...] }` option on individual test cases for precise control.

```typescript
// ❌ All tests in 'Cart @smoke group' match /@smoke/ — unintended
test.describe('Cart @smoke group', () => {
  test('adds item to cart',  async ({ page }) => { /* unintentionally @smoke */ });
  test('updates quantity',   async ({ page }) => { /* also unintentionally @smoke */ });
});

// ✅ Only explicitly tagged tests match
test.describe('Cart', () => {
  test('checkout completes', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ page }) => {
    // Only this test matches project grep: /@smoke/
  });
  test('quantity updates correctly', async ({ page }) => {
    // Not @smoke — excluded from smoke project
  });
});
```

---

### 98. `expect(fn).toPass()` swallows intermediate errors — final failure message loses context [community]

**What:** When `expect(async () => { ... }).toPass()` retries a block with multiple assertions, and the final retry also fails, only the last assertion's error is surfaced. Earlier failures within the retry window (which may point to the real root cause) are discarded.

**WHY:** `toPass()` retries the entire function until it passes or times out. Only the final attempt's error is propagated; intermediate errors are silently discarded on successful retries and lost on final failure.

**Fix:** Use `test.step()` labels inside the `toPass()` callback so each assertion appears in traces regardless of retry behaviour. For simple eventual-consistency checks, prefer `expect.poll()` with a single assertion — it surfaces the polled value directly in the failure message.

```typescript
// ❌ Opaque failure: "Expected 'pending' to equal 'completed'" — which step failed?
await expect(async () => {
  const res  = await request.get(`/api/jobs/${jobId}`);
  const data = await res.json();
  expect(data.status).toBe('completed');
  expect(data.completedAt).toBeTruthy();
}).toPass({ timeout: 15_000 });

// ✅ Labeled steps survive into trace even when retried
await expect(async () => {
  const res  = await request.get(`/api/jobs/${jobId}`);
  const data = await res.json();
  await test.step('check job status', async () => {
    expect(data.status).toBe('completed');
  });
  await test.step('check completedAt timestamp', async () => {
    expect(data.completedAt).toBeTruthy();
  });
}).toPass({ timeout: 15_000 });

// ✅ Even simpler: expect.poll() for single-value eventual consistency
await expect.poll(
  async () => {
    const res = await request.get(`/api/jobs/${jobId}`);
    return (await res.json()).status;
  },
  { timeout: 15_000, message: `Job ${jobId} did not complete` }
).toBe('completed');
```

## Key APIs Added / Updated — Cycle 28 Summary

| API | Version | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `expect(page).toHaveURL(predicate)` | v1.57+ | Assert URL with `(url: URL) => boolean` for multi-param or arithmetic checks | Pagination, query string multi-condition assertions |
| `page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true })` | v1.60+ | ARIA tree with `[ref=eN]` tokens; refs usable as locator selectors | Verify structure then interact with specific identified nodes |
| `playwright.request.newContext()` | v1.0+ | Isolated HTTP client independent of browser cookie jar | Unauthenticated requests, parallel multi-session role tests |
| `toHaveScreenshot({ clip: BoundingBox })` | v1.23+ | Restrict capture to a pixel rectangle for focused visual diffs | Component regression without full-page layout noise |
| `testProject.grep` / `grepInvert` | v1.0+ | Project-level regex routing — encode tag routing in config not CLI | Stable smoke/regression/a11y project separation in CI |
| `getByRole(role, { exact: false })` | v1.0+ | Substring accessible name match for dynamic element names | Order numbers, user names, status messages with variable text |
| `toMatchAriaSnapshot({ children: 'contain' })` | v1.52+ | Partial ARIA tree assertion — listed nodes must exist, extras ignored | Safety net checks for critical nav and dialog elements |
| `page.addInitScript(fn)` | v1.0+ | Inject JS before any page script to override browser APIs | `matchMedia`, `navigator.connection`, Battery API, DeviceMotion |
| `page.clock.install({ toFake: [...] })` | v1.45+ | Selectively intercept only specified timer APIs | Avoid side effects on third-party timers while controlling app timers |
| `testInfo.errors` in `afterEach` | v1.0+ | Array of errors collected during the test | Conditional teardown: skip cleanup on pass, always clean up on failure |
| `context.storageState({ path })` | v1.0+ | Snapshot cookies + localStorage to JSON for reuse across test files | Auth persistence — call after the final token-exchange response, not before navigation |

### Pattern 1: `page.addLocatorHandler()` — Automatic Overlay Dismissal (v1.42+) [official]

Cookie banners, GDPR consent dialogs, newsletter pop-ups, and chat widgets appear unpredictably over UI elements and break locator chains. `addLocatorHandler()` registers a function that Playwright calls whenever a specified overlay is detected before performing any action — the handler dismisses the overlay, then Playwright retries the original action automatically.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/overlay-handler.ts
import { test as base, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function installOverlayHandlers(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  // Dismiss cookie consent banner if it appears
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie|consent/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      const acceptBtn = dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /accept|agree/i });
      if (await acceptBtn.isVisible()) {
        await acceptBtn.click();
      }
    },
    { times: 1 }, // banner should only appear once per session
  );

  // Dismiss "subscribe to newsletter" modal
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /newsletter|subscribe/i }),
    async () => {
      await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    },
  );
}

export const test = base.extend<{ withOverlayHandlers: void }>({
  withOverlayHandlers: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      await installOverlayHandlers(page);
      await use();
    },
    { auto: true }, // auto-installs for all tests that import this fixture
  ],
});
```

**When to use:** Any suite testing real-world pages with consent banners, chat widgets, or promotional modals that randomly appear over interactive elements. Essential for maintaining test stability on marketing pages.

**When NOT to use:** For deterministic single-page apps under full test control — handler overhead adds latency. Also avoid when the overlay itself is what you want to assert on; the handler would dismiss it before your assertion runs.

**Alternatives:** `page.route()` to intercept the endpoint that triggers the overlay; manual `beforeEach` dismissal (brittle — fires even when overlay is absent). [official]

---

### Pattern 2: `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` — Isolated Per-Test Log Capture (v1.56+) [official]

`page.on('console')` accumulates all messages for the page's lifetime and shares the buffer across tests in the same context. The v1.56 APIs `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` return only messages captured since the last navigation, enabling precise per-test log assertions without cross-test pollution.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout page emits no console errors', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Interact with the page to trigger any lazy-loaded error paths
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Review order' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order summary' })).toBeVisible();

  // Collect only messages from this navigation — prior pages not included
  const errors = page.consoleMessages().filter(m => m.type() === 'error');
  const pageErrors = page.pageErrors();

  // Attach full logs to report for debugging even on pass
  await test.info().attach('console-errors', {
    body: JSON.stringify(errors.map(e => e.text()), null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  expect(errors, 'unexpected console errors on checkout page').toHaveLength(0);
  expect(pageErrors, 'uncaught JS exceptions on checkout page').toHaveLength(0);
});

test('can also clear log buffer between interactions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Perform first action
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Load data' }).click();
  const firstBatchErrors = page.consoleMessages().filter(m => m.type() === 'error');

  // Clear buffer before second action to isolate its log output
  page.clearConsoleMessages();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' }).click();
  const exportErrors = page.consoleMessages().filter(m => m.type() === 'error');
  // exportErrors contains ONLY messages from after clearConsoleMessages()
  expect(exportErrors).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**When to use:** Regression tests where console errors indicate broken API calls, missing translations, or React hydration failures. Smoke tests that assert a page loads clean. Use `clearConsoleMessages()` to isolate sub-interactions within a single test.

**When NOT to use:** Do not replace functional assertions with log assertions — a page can render correctly while emitting warnings. Use log checks as a secondary signal, not the primary assertion.

**Alternatives:** `page.on('console', handler)` for streaming real-time processing; `page.on('pageerror', handler)` for uncaught exception streaming. [official]

---

### Pattern 3: `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveRole()` — Semantic UI Assertions (v1.44+) [official]

CSS or text changes can break semantic markup silently — a button may visually say "Submit" but its accessible name or ARIA role may have regressed. `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveRole()` assert the computed accessibility properties of elements, catching regressions that visual or text assertions miss.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form controls have correct accessible semantics', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/signup');

  const emailField = page.locator('#email-input');
  const submitBtn  = page.locator('[data-testid="submit"]');
  const statusMsg  = page.locator('.status-banner');

  // Assert computed accessible name (derived from label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
  await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleName('Email address');

  // Assert ARIA role — catches if a <div role="button"> loses its role attribute
  await expect(submitBtn).toHaveRole('button');

  // After a failed submission, assert error banner role
  await submitBtn.click();
  await expect(statusMsg).toHaveRole('alert');
  await expect(statusMsg).toHaveAccessibleName(/please fill in/i);

  // toHaveAccessibleDescription() checks aria-describedby content
  await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/we will send a confirmation/i);
});
```

**When to use:** Any page with form elements, interactive widgets, or status banners where accessibility regression is a concern. Include in smoke tests for WCAG compliance. Pair with `toHaveRole('alert')` for dynamic status regions.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use instead of `getByRole()` locators — these are assertions on existing locators, not locator strategies. They do not wait for the accessible name to appear; pair with `waitFor()` if the name is set asynchronously.

**Alternatives:** `@axe-core/playwright` for broader WCAG scanning; `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for full subtree structure validation. [official]

---

### Pattern 4: Per-Worker Authentication Fixture — Parallel-Safe Multi-Account Strategy [official]

When tests modify server-side state (orders, notifications, user prefs), a shared auth file causes cross-test contamination: worker A's actions pollute worker B's assertions. Worker-scoped fixtures assign each parallel worker its own account, eliminating contention.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts
import { test as base, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';

// Pool of pre-created test accounts — one per worker
const ACCOUNTS = [
  { email: 'worker0@test.example', password: process.env.TEST_PASS! },
  { email: 'worker1@test.example', password: process.env.TEST_PASS! },
  { email: 'worker2@test.example', password: process.env.TEST_PASS! },
  { email: 'worker3@test.example', password: process.env.TEST_PASS! },
];

export const test = base.extend<object, { authedContext: BrowserContext }>({
  authedContext: [
    async ({ browser }, use, workerInfo) => {
      const account  = ACCOUNTS[workerInfo.parallelIndex % ACCOUNTS.length];
      const authFile = `playwright/.auth/worker-${workerInfo.parallelIndex}.json`;

      // Authenticate once per worker, reuse for all tests on that worker
      const page = await browser.newPage();
      await page.goto('/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(account.email);
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(account.password);
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
      await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);
      await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
      await page.close();

      const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: authFile });
      await use(context);
      await context.close();
    },
    { scope: 'worker' }, // created once per worker, not per test
  ],
});
```

**When to use:** Any suite where tests create, modify, or delete server-side records that would affect other parallel tests if sharing one account. E-commerce checkouts, messaging apps, document editing.

**When NOT to use:** Read-only test suites — shared auth state is faster and simpler. Also avoid if your test environment cannot provision multiple accounts.

**Alternatives:** Single shared `storageState` file (sufficient for read-only tests); API-level setup per test with request fixtures (more isolated but slower). [official]

---

### Pattern 5: Multi-Role Simultaneous Context — Testing Role Interactions in One Test [official]

Collaboration features (shared documents, real-time comments, dual-role approval workflows) require two authenticated actors in the same test. Each role uses its own `BrowserContext` loaded from a separate `storageState` file.

```typescript
import { test, expect, chromium } from '@playwright/test';

test('admin can see editor comments in real time', async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();

  // Load two separate authentication states
  const adminContext  = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'playwright/.auth/admin.json' });
  const editorContext = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'playwright/.auth/editor.json' });

  const adminPage  = await adminContext.newPage();
  const editorPage = await editorContext.newPage();

  // Both actors navigate to the shared document
  await Promise.all([
    adminPage.goto('/docs/shared-doc-123'),
    editorPage.goto('/docs/shared-doc-123'),
  ]);

  // Editor adds a comment
  await editorPage.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Add comment' }).fill('Needs revision here');
  await editorPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Post comment' }).click();

  // Admin sees the comment appear in real time without reload
  await expect(
    adminPage.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Needs revision here' }),
  ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });

  await adminContext.close();
  await editorContext.close();
  await browser.close();
});
```

**When to use:** Real-time collaboration features, dual-approval workflows, admin + user interaction testing, WebSocket-driven shared state.

**When NOT to use:** For simple role-based access control (reading different pages) — a single context with `storageState` swap per test is sufficient and faster. Avoid in parallelized CI without resource limits — each multi-context test consumes two browser processes.

**Alternatives:** Two separate test files with a single role each, communicating via API state; mock WebSocket with `routeWebSocket()` to simulate the other actor's messages. [official]

---

### Pattern 6: `expect.configure()` — Pre-Setting Global Soft Assertion Defaults [official]

When an entire test section should use soft assertions (collect all failures rather than stopping at the first), decorating every `expect` call with `.soft()` is verbose and error-prone. `expect.configure({ soft: true })` creates a pre-configured expect instance scoped to that block.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('product details page has all required metadata', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/widget-pro');

  // Create a soft-assertion expect — all failures collected, test continues
  const softExpect = expect.configure({ soft: true });

  // Assert all metadata fields — test collects every failure before stopping
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('product-title')).toBeVisible();
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('product-price')).toContainText('$');
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('product-sku')).toBeVisible();
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('product-description')).not.toBeEmpty();
  await softExpect(page.getByRole('img', { name: /product image/i })).toBeVisible();
  await softExpect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' })).toBeEnabled();

  // Hard assertion for the critical action path — stops immediately if broken
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' })).toBeEnabled();
});

test('expect.configure() also accepts timeout override', async ({ page }) => {
  // Useful for API polling assertions where default 5s timeout is too short
  const slowExpect = expect.configure({ timeout: 30_000 });
  await page.goto('/reports/generate');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Generate' }).click();
  await slowExpect(page.getByTestId('report-download-link')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Comprehensive "health check" tests that should report ALL broken fields at once. Also useful for wrapping assertions in slow async scenarios where a longer timeout is always needed.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use soft assertions for control-flow-critical assertions (e.g., navigation completed before proceeding). A soft assertion failure does not stop execution — subsequent steps may throw cryptic errors if the prior step silently failed.

**Alternatives:** Individual `expect.soft()` calls; grouped assertions in a `test.step()` block that surfaces all failures through trace steps. [official]

---

### Pattern 7: `test.abort()` — Immediate Failure on Unrecoverable State [official]

When a prerequisite assertion fails (server is down, auth is broken, test environment is wrong), continuing the test produces dozens of misleading failures that obscure the real cause. `test.abort()` stops execution immediately with a clear message, unlike a thrown error which triggers retries.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('user can submit support ticket', async ({ page, request }) => {
  // Pre-flight: verify the support API is reachable before running UI test
  const health = await request.get('/api/health', { timeout: 3_000 }).catch(() => null);
  if (!health || !health.ok()) {
    await test.abort('Support API is not reachable — environment not ready');
    // test.abort() throws internally; code below never runs
  }

  await page.goto('/support');
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Subject' }).fill('Cannot login');
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Message' }).fill('I forgot my password');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Ticket submitted');
});
```

**When to use:** Tests that have hard environmental preconditions (external API availability, required seeds, feature flags). Use in `beforeAll` to abort an entire describe group.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use as a substitute for proper assertions — `test.abort()` skips retries, masking intermittent failures. Reserve for deterministic precondition checks.

**Alternatives:** `test.skip()` with a condition (marks as skipped, not failed); throwing an error (triggers retries); `expect(health.ok()).toBeTruthy()` as a hard assertion (counts as a test failure, retried). [official]

---

### Pattern 8: Geolocation and Timezone Emulation — Location-Sensitive Feature Testing [official]

Features like delivery availability, store finder, currency display, and date formatting depend on geolocation and timezone. Playwright's `context.setGeolocation()` and `timezoneId` option let you emulate these conditions without physical relocation or system clock changes.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — define geo-targeted test projects
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'US-East',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        geolocation: { latitude: 40.7128, longitude: -74.0060 }, // New York
        timezoneId: 'America/New_York',
        permissions: ['geolocation'],
        locale: 'en-US',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'UK',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        geolocation: { latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 }, // London
        timezoneId: 'Europe/London',
        permissions: ['geolocation'],
        locale: 'en-GB',
      },
    },
  ],
});

// e2e/specs/delivery-zones.spec.ts
test('shows same-day delivery for NYC users', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  // Geolocation already emulated via project config
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Detect location' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('delivery-option-same-day')).toBeVisible();
});

test('shows localized date format', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/orders/12345');
  // UK locale produces DD/MM/YYYY; US locale produces MM/DD/YYYY
  const dateEl = page.getByTestId('order-date');
  await expect(dateEl).toHaveText(/\d{2}\/\d{2}\/\d{4}/);
});
```

**When to use:** E-commerce delivery zones, location-based content gating, date/currency formatting regressions, GDPR/CCPA compliance pages that differ by region.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use geolocation emulation to test server-side geofencing — the browser's `navigator.geolocation` does not affect server IP detection. Test server-side geo logic at the API level with `X-Forwarded-For` headers.

**Alternatives:** `page.addInitScript()` to override `navigator.geolocation` with a stub (more granular but not officially emulated). [official]

---

### Pattern 9: `locator.pressSequentially()` — One-Key-At-a-Time Input for Special Characters [official]

`locator.fill()` sets the input value directly without simulating individual keystrokes, which bypasses `keydown`/`keypress`/`keyup` event handlers. Autocomplete components, rich text editors, and masked inputs that depend on individual keystroke events require `pressSequentially()`.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('credit card number mask formats on input', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/payment');
  const cardInput = page.getByLabel('Card number');

  // fill() sets value atomically — mask's keydown handler never fires
  // await cardInput.fill('4111111111111111');  // would bypass the mask

  // pressSequentially types each character individually
  await cardInput.pressSequentially('4111111111111111', { delay: 30 });

  // Mask should have formatted the raw digits as groups
  await expect(cardInput).toHaveValue('4111 1111 1111 1111');
});

test('autocomplete dropdown triggers on typing', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const searchInput = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search products' });

  // Type slowly to trigger debounced search API
  await searchInput.pressSequentially('blue wid', { delay: 50 });

  // Wait for autocomplete suggestions to appear
  const suggestions = page.getByRole('listbox');
  await expect(suggestions).toBeVisible();
  await expect(suggestions.getByRole('option').first()).toContainText(/blue/i);
});
```

**When to use:** Masked inputs (phone, credit card, date), rich text editors (Slate, Tiptap, Quill), autocomplete/combobox components that debounce on keypress, any component with `onKeyDown` business logic.

**When NOT to use:** Simple `<input type="text">` or `<textarea>` elements with no keystroke handlers — `fill()` is faster, more reliable, and recommended by Playwright for standard inputs.

**Alternatives:** `locator.type()` (deprecated in Playwright v1.30+ — use `pressSequentially`); `page.keyboard.type()` for global keyboard input not scoped to a locator. [official]

---

### Pattern 10: Dark Mode and Color Scheme Emulation — Appearance Regression Testing [official]

Rendering regressions in dark mode are invisible in light-mode CI snapshots. Playwright's `colorScheme` option emulates `prefers-color-scheme: dark` at the browser level, enabling visual snapshot diffs across themes without requiring a theme toggle UI.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — dual-theme visual regression projects
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'light-theme',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], colorScheme: 'light' },
      testMatch: /.*visual.spec.ts/,
    },
    {
      name: 'dark-theme',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], colorScheme: 'dark' },
      testMatch: /.*visual.spec.ts/,
    },
  ],
});

// e2e/visual/dashboard.visual.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dashboard header matches theme snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('banner')).toHaveScreenshot('dashboard-header.png', {
    // Mask dynamic content — timestamps, user avatars
    mask: [
      page.getByTestId('current-time'),
      page.getByRole('img', { name: 'User avatar' }),
    ],
  });
});

// Per-test override when config-level is not sufficient
test('modal renders correctly in dark mode', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
  await page.goto('/settings');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open theme preview' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toHaveScreenshot('theme-preview-dark.png');
});
```

**When to use:** Any application with `prefers-color-scheme` CSS, manual dark mode toggle, or system theme detection. Visual regression suites for design system components.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use `colorScheme` emulation to test application-level theme state toggled via JavaScript (class on `<html>`, CSS custom properties) — emulation only sets the media query, not the JS state. Use the actual toggle UI or `addInitScript` to set the theme class.

**Alternatives:** `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` per test; `page.addInitScript()` to force a CSS class. [official]

---

### Pattern 11: `axe-core` WCAG Tag Filtering with Fixture — Targeted Accessibility CI [official]

Running all axe rules on every page is slow and surfaces known/accepted violations. Scoping scans to specific WCAG tags (e.g., `wcag2aa`) and sharing configuration via a fixture makes accessibility testing maintainable and CI-friendly.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/a11y.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

type A11yFixtures = {
  makeAxeBuilder: () => AxeBuilder;
};

export const test = base.extend<A11yFixtures>({
  makeAxeBuilder: async ({ page }, use) => {
    // Factory function so tests can customize (include/exclude/tag)
    const factory = () =>
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
        .exclude('#legacy-widget') // known third-party violation
        .disableRules(['color-contrast']); // managed separately in design system

    await use(factory);
  },
});

// e2e/specs/a11y.spec.ts
import { test } from '../fixtures/a11y';
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

for (const route of ['/home', '/products', '/checkout', '/account']) {
  test(`${route} has no WCAG 2.1 AA violations`, async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
    await page.goto(route);
    // Wait for dynamic content before scanning
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await makeAxeBuilder().analyze();

    // Attach full scan results as JSON for CI artifact inspection
    await test.info().attach('axe-results', {
      body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
}
```

**When to use:** WCAG compliance requirements, accessibility CI gates, design system component libraries. Use `withTags()` to align with your project's compliance target (AA, AAA).

**When NOT to use:** Automated axe scanning cannot detect all accessibility issues — do not use alone as a compliance guarantee. Manual screen reader testing is still required for keyboard navigation and ARIA live region correctness.

**Alternatives:** `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for structural accessibility assertions; `toHaveRole()` and `toHaveAccessibleName()` for individual element assertions. [official]

---

### Pattern 12: `mergeTests()` — Composing Fixtures from Multiple Modules [official]

Large test suites accumulate fixture files per domain (auth, database seeds, page objects, mock servers). Importing and re-extending `test` in a long chain becomes unmaintainable. `mergeTests()` composes independent fixture modules without nesting.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ authedPage: void }>({
  authedPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.E2E_EMAIL!);
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.E2E_PASS!);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);
    await use();
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/seeds.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ testProduct: { id: string; name: string } }>({
  testProduct: async ({ request }, use) => {
    const res = await request.post('/api/products', {
      data: { name: `Test Product ${Date.now()}`, price: 9.99 },
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN}` },
    });
    const product = await res.json();
    await use(product);
    await request.delete(`/api/products/${product.id}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN}` },
    });
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/index.ts — merge all fixture modules
import { mergeTests } from '@playwright/test';
import { test as authTest } from './auth';
import { test as seedTest } from './seeds';

export const test = mergeTests(authTest, seedTest);
export { expect } from '@playwright/test';

// e2e/specs/product-editing.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures';

// Both authedPage and testProduct fixtures available without chained extends
test('editor can update product price', async ({ page, authedPage, testProduct }) => {
  await page.goto(`/products/${testProduct.id}/edit`);
  await page.getByLabel('Price').fill('19.99');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('price-display')).toContainText('$19.99');
});
```

**When to use:** Projects with 3+ fixture modules that multiple test files need in combination. Eliminates `base.extend(auth.extend(seed.extend(...)))` pyramid hell.

**When NOT to use:** Simple projects with one or two fixture files — the extra indirection is not worth it. Also requires all merged modules to import from the same base `test` to avoid fixture name collisions.

**Alternatives:** Re-exporting a single extended `test` object from a shared `fixtures/index.ts` using chained `.extend()` (works fine up to ~3 modules). [official]

---

### Pattern 13: `page.requests()` — Recent Network Traffic Assertion Without Event Listeners (v1.56+) [official]

Setting up `page.on('request')` listeners before every navigation for traffic inspection adds boilerplate and can miss requests that fire before the listener is attached. `page.requests()` returns up to 100 recent requests post-navigation, enabling retrospective traffic assertions without listeners.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('analytics events are fired on product view', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/widget-pro');

  // Trigger the product view event by scrolling
  await page.mouse.wheel(0, 500);
  await page.waitForTimeout(500); // allow debounced analytics flush

  // Inspect recent requests — no pre-navigation listener needed
  const analyticsRequests = page.requests().filter(r =>
    r.url().includes('/collect') && r.method() === 'POST',
  );

  expect(analyticsRequests.length, 'analytics POST fired').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

  // Assert payload contains product ID
  const body = analyticsRequests[0].postData() ?? '';
  expect(body).toContain('widget-pro');
});

test('no requests made to third-party trackers', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const externalRequests = page.requests().filter(r =>
    !r.url().startsWith('https://our-domain.example'),
  );
  // Log all external requests for visibility
  for (const req of externalRequests) {
    console.log('External request:', req.url());
  }
  // Assert privacy policy compliance
  const trackerRequests = externalRequests.filter(r =>
    /facebook|doubleclick|hotjar/.test(r.url()),
  );
  expect(trackerRequests).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**When to use:** Post-hoc traffic verification, analytics event assertions, privacy compliance tests. Simpler than `page.on('request')` for retrospective checks.

**When NOT to use:** `page.requests()` only stores the last 100 requests. For high-traffic pages or tests checking every single network call, use `page.on('request')` to stream and accumulate all requests. Also, `requests()` does not give you response bodies — use `route.fulfill()` or `page.on('response')` for that.

**Alternatives:** `page.waitForRequest(url)` for waiting on a specific URL; `page.on('request')` for streaming all requests; `page.route()` to intercept and inspect. [official]

---

### Pattern 14: Session Storage Persistence via `addInitScript` — Bridging the Auth Gap [official]

`page.context().storageState()` persists cookies and `localStorage` but silently drops `sessionStorage`. Apps that store tokens or user state in `sessionStorage` require a manual bridge: serialize the session storage in the setup file, then restore it via `addInitScript()` before navigation.

```typescript
// e2e/auth.setup.ts
import { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

const authFile    = 'playwright/.auth/user.json';
const sessionFile = 'playwright/.auth/session-storage.json';

setup('authenticate and capture session storage', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.E2E_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.E2E_PASS!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);

  // Capture sessionStorage — storageState() misses this
  const sessionStorage = await page.evaluate(() =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      Object.keys(window.sessionStorage).map(k => [k, window.sessionStorage.getItem(k)]),
    ),
  );
  fs.writeFileSync(sessionFile, JSON.stringify(sessionStorage));
  await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
});

// e2e/fixtures/session-auth.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

export const test = base.extend({
  page: async ({ page }, use) => {
    // Restore sessionStorage before every navigation
    const sessionData: Record<string, string> = JSON.parse(
      fs.readFileSync('playwright/.auth/session-storage.json', 'utf8'),
    );
    await page.addInitScript((data) => {
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(data)) {
        window.sessionStorage.setItem(key, value);
      }
    }, sessionData);
    await use(page);
  },
});
```

**When to use:** SPAs that store access tokens, cart state, or user preferences in `sessionStorage`. Required when `storageState` alone results in redirect-to-login after a successfully saved auth file.

**When NOT to use:** If you can convince the app to use `localStorage` or cookies for auth tokens, do that instead — it is simpler and avoids this workaround entirely.

**Alternatives:** Modify the application to use `localStorage` for auth state; authenticate via API in `beforeEach` and receive a `localStorage`-stored token. [official]

---

### Pattern 15: Runtime Test Annotations via `test.info()` — Dynamic Metadata for CI Reports [official]

Hard-coded annotations in `test()` signatures are fixed at definition time. `test.info().annotations.push()` lets tests add metadata discovered at runtime — browser versions, feature flag states, API response codes — directly into HTML reports without modifying test declarations.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout works for current pricing tier', async ({ page, request, browserName }) => {
  // Discover runtime environment info
  const config = await (await request.get('/api/config')).json();

  // Attach runtime context as annotations visible in HTML report
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'pricing-tier',
    description: config.pricingTier,
  });
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'feature-flags',
    description: JSON.stringify(config.featureFlags),
  });
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'browser',
    description: browserName,
  });

  // Conditionally annotate known limitations without skipping
  if (config.maintenanceWindow) {
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: '_maintenance',  // underscore prefix: hidden from HTML report
      description: 'maintenance window active during this run',
    });
  }

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('pricing-display')).toContainText(config.pricingTier);
});
```

**When to use:** Tests that interact with dynamic environments (feature flags, A/B variants, staging configs), multi-tenant apps where test behavior differs per tenant. Annotations surface in the HTML report without adding to the test title.

**When NOT to use:** Do not use as a substitute for assertions — annotations are metadata, not pass/fail signals. Use `type` values starting with `_` for annotations you want to keep private from HTML report display (they appear in JSON but not the UI).

**Alternatives:** `test.info().attach()` to embed full JSON payloads as downloadable artifacts; `console.log()` for ephemeral debugging (not persisted to report). [official]

---

## Cycle 29 — Community Gotchas

### 99. `page.addLocatorHandler()` with `times: 1` still fires if the overlay re-opens [community]

**What:** `times: 1` limits how many times the handler is invoked, not how many times the overlay can appear. If your application re-opens the cookie banner (e.g., after a soft-navigation or route change in a SPA), the handler is already exhausted and the overlay blocks the next action, causing a timeout.

**WHY:** `times: 1` is a call-count guard, not a guard against re-appearance. Once the handler fires once, Playwright removes it from the registry. Subsequent appearances of the matching locator are not handled — they block Playwright's pre-action overlay check and cause the test to time out waiting for actionability.

**Fix:** Omit `times` unless you are certain the overlay appears exactly once per test. For session-persistent banners (only dismissed once per domain), use `{ times: 1 }` with `context`-level scope; for SPAs with per-route banners, omit `times` or set it higher.

```typescript
// ❌ Handler exhausted after first dismiss — subsequent SPA route changes re-open banner
await page.addLocatorHandler(
  page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
  async () => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Accept' }).click(); },
  { times: 1 },
);

// ✅ No times limit — handler fires every time the overlay appears
await page.addLocatorHandler(
  page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
  async () => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Accept' }).click(); },
);
```

---

### 100. `locator.pressSequentially()` without `delay` may not trigger `input` events on controlled React/Vue inputs [community]

**What:** Components listening on the `input` DOM event (React controlled inputs, Vue `v-model`) may not update their internal state when `pressSequentially()` is used without the `{ delay }` option. The displayed value appears correct but the framework's state is stale — form submission sends an empty or old value.

**WHY:** Without `delay`, Playwright dispatches keystroke events at machine speed. React's synthetic event system relies on the `input` event being dispatched between keystrokes to update controlled component state. At zero delay, the browser may batch or coalesce `input` events, causing React to only process the final value or miss updates entirely.

**Fix:** Always provide `{ delay: 30 }` when using `pressSequentially()` on controlled inputs in React or Vue. If still unreliable, use `locator.fill()` for pure state updates and reserve `pressSequentially` only when keystroke-level event business logic is explicitly required.

```typescript
// ❌ React controlled input state may not update — submit sends empty value
await cardInput.pressSequentially('4111111111111111');

// ✅ delay gives React time to process input events between keystrokes
await cardInput.pressSequentially('4111111111111111', { delay: 30 });
```

---

### 101. `expect(locator).toHaveRole()` checks the computed ARIA role — not the HTML `role` attribute value [community]

**What:** `toHaveRole('button')` passes for `<button>` (implicit role) and `<div role="button">` (explicit attribute). But it also passes for `<input type="submit">` since the browser computes role `button` for that element. Meanwhile, `<a>` without `href` has computed role `generic`, NOT `link` — causing false failures when asserting `toHaveRole('link')` on anchor tags missing their `href`.

**WHY:** `toHaveRole()` uses the browser's accessibility tree computation, which maps implicit roles from HTML element semantics according to the ARIA in HTML specification. The computed role often differs from intuition — especially for `<a>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, and `<header>` elements where role depends on context and attributes.

**Fix:** Use `ariaSnapshot()` to verify what computed role Playwright actually observes for ambiguous elements before writing `toHaveRole()` assertions.

```typescript
// Debug: capture the computed ARIA role before asserting
const snapshot = await page.getByTestId('back-button').ariaSnapshot();
console.log(snapshot); // reveals computed role and name

// ❌ Fails if the <a> tag is missing href — computed role becomes 'generic'
await expect(page.getByText('Back')).toHaveRole('link');

// ✅ Use getByRole() locator which handles implicit role resolution correctly
await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Back' })).toBeVisible();
await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Back' })).toHaveRole('link');
```

---

### 102. Per-worker auth files can corrupt on worker restart — `parallelIndex` is reused [community]

**What:** When a Playwright worker crashes mid-run and restarts, the new worker receives the same `workerInfo.parallelIndex` as the dead worker. If the previous worker's auth file was partially written when the worker was killed (e.g., during `storageState({ path })`), the new worker reads a broken JSON file and all its tests fail with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`.

**WHY:** `parallelIndex` is deterministic for a given shard configuration and is reused on restart by design. File writes to `storageState` are not atomic — if the worker process dies mid-write, the file contains a partial JSON string. Node.js `fs.writeFileSync` on the internal path Playwright uses is not atomic across all platforms.

**Fix:** Write auth files atomically: write to a `.tmp` file first, then rename. Add a `try/catch` around the JSON read in fixture setup to re-authenticate on parse failure.

```typescript
import * as fs from 'fs';

// Atomic write prevents partial-file corruption on worker crash
const tmpPath = `${authFile}.tmp`;
await page.context().storageState({ path: tmpPath });
fs.renameSync(tmpPath, authFile); // atomic on POSIX; near-atomic on Windows NTFS
```

---

### 103. `mergeTests()` silently overwrites fixtures with the same name — last module wins [community]

**What:** If two fixture modules both define a fixture with the same name (including re-exporting or overriding the built-in `page` fixture), `mergeTests(moduleA, moduleB)` uses only the last module's version. The earlier module's customization is silently discarded. TypeScript types may still compile without errors.

**WHY:** `mergeTests()` merges fixture registries by name using object spread semantics — later entries overwrite earlier ones. There is no warning or error for conflicting fixture names. The silent overwrite is particularly dangerous when two modules both override the built-in `page` fixture (e.g., one for auth cookie injection, one for session storage restoration).

**Fix:** Give all custom overrides unique names (`authedPage`, `sessionPage`) instead of shadowing built-in fixture names. Only one fixture module in a merge set should override a built-in, and document that constraint explicitly in the fixture module.

```typescript
// ❌ Both modules define 'page' — authModule's version is silently discarded
export const test = mergeTests(authModule, sessionModule);
// authModule.page: injects cookies
// sessionModule.page: restores sessionStorage ← wins silently

// ✅ Each module exposes a uniquely named fixture
// authModule exports:    authedPage    (injects cookies)
// sessionModule exports: sessionPage   (restores sessionStorage)
// Tests explicitly request what they need — no hidden overwrite
test('checkout flow', async ({ authedPage, sessionPage }) => { /* ... */ });
```

---

### 104. `test.abort()` skips `afterEach` hooks — only fixture teardown is guaranteed to run [community]

**What:** When `test.abort()` is called inside a test body, Playwright marks the test as failed and halts further execution. `afterEach` hooks registered in the test file or describe block do NOT run after `test.abort()`. However, fixture teardown (the code after `await use()` inside a fixture definition) IS still executed.

**WHY:** `test.abort()` is an emergency exit designed to skip all remaining test scaffolding including hooks. It is distinct from throwing an error — a thrown error triggers retries AND `afterEach`; `test.abort()` does neither. Fixture teardown runs because the Playwright fixture lifecycle is implemented as a finally block at the runner level, not as a hook.

**Fix:** Move all critical cleanup (deleting database records, resetting shared state, closing external connections) into fixture teardown, not `afterEach` hooks, so it is guaranteed to run regardless of how the test terminates.

```typescript
// ❌ afterEach does NOT run if test.abort() is called — records leak
afterEach(async ({ request }) => {
  await request.delete(`/api/test-data/${seedId}`); // skipped on test.abort()!
});

// ✅ Fixture teardown always executes — even after test.abort()
export const test = base.extend<{ seedRecord: { id: string } }>({
  seedRecord: async ({ request }, use) => {
    const res    = await request.post('/api/test-data', { data: { label: 'cycle29-test' } });
    const record = await res.json();
    await use(record); // test body runs here
    // Teardown: runs unconditionally — even when test.abort() was called
    await request.delete(`/api/test-data/${record.id}`);
  },
});
```

---

## Key APIs Added / Updated — Cycle 29 Summary

| API | Version | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `page.addLocatorHandler(locator, fn, { times })` | v1.42+ | Auto-dismisses overlays before any blocked action | Cookie banners, chat widgets, promotional modals |
| `page.consoleMessages()` / `page.clearConsoleMessages()` | v1.56+ / v1.59+ | Post-hoc console log access scoped to last navigation | Assert no errors on page load; isolate log output per interaction |
| `page.pageErrors()` / `page.clearPageErrors()` | v1.56+ / v1.59+ | Uncaught JS exception collection | Smoke tests asserting zero runtime JS errors |
| `page.requests()` | v1.56+ | Last 100 network requests without event listeners | Retrospective analytics / tracking audit |
| `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleName(name)` | v1.44+ | Assert computed ARIA accessible name | Form label regression, icon button audits |
| `expect(locator).toHaveRole(role)` | v1.44+ | Assert computed ARIA role | Widget role regression, `<div>` button pattern |
| `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleDescription(desc)` | v1.44+ | Assert aria-describedby content | Help text, error hint association |
| `locator.pressSequentially(text, { delay })` | v1.29+ | Dispatch individual key events with delay | Masked inputs, autocomplete, controlled React inputs |
| `expect.configure({ soft, timeout })` | v1.39+ | Pre-configure assertion mode and timeout | Health-check tests, slow async assertions |
| `test.abort(reason)` | v1.50+ | Fail test immediately without triggering retries | Unrecoverable env conditions, broken prerequisites |
| `mergeTests(...modules)` | v1.39+ | Compose independent fixture modules | Multi-domain fixture sets without extend chains |
| `context.setGeolocation({ latitude, longitude })` | v1.0+ | Set GPS coordinates for the browser context | Delivery zones, geo-gated content, locale testing |
| `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` | v1.0+ | Set `prefers-color-scheme` media query | Dark mode visual regression, theme testing |

## Cycle 31 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 16: `locator.filter({ visible: true })` — Restrict Locators to Visible Elements Only (v1.51+) [official]

`locator.filter()` gained a `visible` boolean option in v1.51, allowing tests to scope assertions and interactions exclusively to elements that are in the DOM and not hidden. This solves the classic "multiple matching elements" error that arises when React or Vue conditionally renders and hides elements simultaneously.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('only visible product cards are interactable', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Without filter: matches BOTH rendered and CSS-hidden cards (multiple matches → error)
  // const allCards = page.getByRole('article', { name: /product/i });

  // With visible filter: only truly visible cards
  const visibleCards = page.getByRole('article').filter({ visible: true });

  // Assert expected count of visible products
  await expect(visibleCards).toHaveCount(12);

  // Interact safely — no "strict mode violation" from hidden duplicates
  await visibleCards.first().getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: /cart/i })).toContainText('1');

  // Compose with text filter for even narrower scope
  const inStockCards = page
    .getByRole('article')
    .filter({ visible: true })
    .filter({ hasText: 'In stock' });
  await expect(inStockCards).toHaveCount(9);
});

test('skeleton loaders are not visible after data loads', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Skeleton elements present in DOM but CSS-hidden once data loads
  const skeletons = page.getByTestId('skeleton-row').filter({ visible: true });
  await expect(skeletons).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.getByRole('row')).toHaveCount(10);
});
```

**When to use:** Any component that toggles visibility via `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` while keeping the element in the DOM (e.g., skeleton loaders, tabbed panels, virtual scrollers). Eliminates strict mode violations on shared component names.

**When NOT to use:** Do not rely on `visible: true` as a substitute for proper ARIA states — if an element is interactive but visually positioned off-screen (e.g., a skip-to-content link), it reports as not visible. Also, `visible: true` does not filter out elements clipped by `overflow: hidden` that are still technically visible per CSS — use `locator.boundingBox()` for spatial checks.

**Alternatives:** `locator.first()` (fragile — picks an arbitrary item); `page.getByRole('article', { name: 'X' })` with an exact name (only works if the name is known); `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` on a single locator. [official]

### Pattern 17: `testConfig.captureGitInfo` — Embed Git Metadata in Test Reports (v1.51+) [official]

Enabling `captureGitInfo` causes Playwright to embed the current branch name, commit hash, and author information into the HTML report and blob reporter metadata. This gives CI dashboards and flake-tracking systems the context to correlate failures with specific commits and authors without custom scripting.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Capture git context into report metadata
  captureGitInfo: { git: true },

  reporter: [
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['blob', { outputFile: `blob-report-${process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? '0'}.zip` }],
  ],

  use: {
    baseURL:    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace:      'on-first-retry',
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Access git info programmatically in a custom reporter
import type { Reporter, Suite, TestCase } from '@playwright/test/reporter';

class GitAwareReporter implements Reporter {
  onBegin(config: import('@playwright/test').FullConfig, suite: Suite) {
    const git = (config.metadata as any)?.git;
    if (git) {
      console.log(`[CI] Branch: ${git.branch}  Commit: ${String(git.sha).slice(0, 7)}`);
      console.log(`[CI] Author: ${git.authorName} <${git.authorEmail}>`);
      console.log(`[CI] Message: ${git.commitMessage}`);
    }
  }

  onTestEnd(test: TestCase, result: import('@playwright/test').TestResult) {
    if (result.status === 'failed') {
      const sha = (test as any)._test?.config?.metadata?.git?.sha ?? 'unknown';
      console.error(`FAILED ${test.title} @ ${sha}`);
    }
  }
}

export default GitAwareReporter;
```

**When to use:** Any project running tests in CI that needs failure-to-commit traceability. Particularly valuable for flake dashboards, blame workflows, and merge-queue integrations where knowing the offending commit is essential.

**When NOT to use:** In developer-local runs where git state may be dirty or the test run predates the commit. The `git` metadata is captured at test start — if you rebase mid-run, the captured SHA reflects the original HEAD.

**Alternatives:** Manually set `process.env.GIT_COMMIT` and read it in `globalSetup`; use the `--metadata` CLI flag to inject arbitrary key/value pairs. [official]

### Pattern 18: `--only-changed` CLI Flag — Run Tests for Modified Files Only (v1.46+) [official]

The `--only-changed` flag restricts the test run to files that have changed relative to a git ref (default: uncommitted changes against `HEAD`). This is a first-class Playwright feature, not a shell script filter, meaning it understands project configuration, glob patterns, and shard assignments.

```bash
# Run tests only in files changed since HEAD (uncommitted changes)
npx playwright test --only-changed

# Run tests changed since the last merge base with main
npx playwright test --only-changed=main

# Combine with project filter — only changed tests in the chromium project
npx playwright test --only-changed=origin/main --project=chromium

# Typical PR-gate pipeline entry (GitHub Actions)
# Only runs tests for files touched in the PR
npx playwright test --only-changed=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
```

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — recommended config that pairs with --only-changed
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir:        './e2e',
  fullyParallel:  true,
  retries:        process.env.CI ? 1 : 0,
  workers:        process.env.CI ? '50%' : undefined,
  captureGitInfo: { git: true }, // pairs well — report shows which commit changed
  reporter:       process.env.CI
    ? [['github'], ['html', { open: 'never' }]]
    : [['html', { open: 'on-failure' }]],
});
```

**When to use:** Feature-branch PR pipelines where running the full suite is too slow. Works best when tests are co-located with source files (e.g., `src/components/Button.spec.ts`). Also useful for local pre-commit hooks where you want to only run affected tests.

**When NOT to use:** Do not rely on `--only-changed` for full-suite gate checks on `main`. It only detects file-level changes — a shared fixture or POM that is not itself edited will not trigger re-runs of dependent tests. Always run the full suite on merge to `main`.

**Alternatives:** `--last-failed` (reruns previously failing tests); manual `--grep` filtering; test sharding to parallelize the full suite. [official]
