### Pattern 31: `toContainClass()` — Ergonomic CSS Class Assertion (v1.52+) [official]

`expect(locator).toContainClass(className)` asserts that an element has a specific CSS class without requiring knowledge of all other classes on the element. Unlike `toHaveClass()`, it does not force an exact match of the full class string — it passes as long as the expected class name is present. This is the idiomatic replacement for the fragile pattern of checking `className.includes('my-class')` via `evaluate()`.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('active nav item receives "active" class', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const dashboardLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Dashboard' });

  // ✅ Passes even if element also has 'nav-item', 'text-blue-600', etc.
  await expect(dashboardLink).toContainClass('active');

  // Navigate away and assert the class is removed
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
  await expect(dashboardLink).not.toContainClass('active');

  // Also works with multiple classes in one assertion
  const settingsLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' });
  await expect(settingsLink).toContainClass('active');
});

test('disabled button has correct visual state classes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  const submitBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit order/i });

  // Assert both a layout class and a state class independently
  await expect(submitBtn).toContainClass('btn-primary');
  await expect(submitBtn).not.toContainClass('disabled');

  // After emptying cart, button becomes disabled
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /clear cart/i }).click();
  await expect(submitBtn).toContainClass('disabled');
});
```

**When to use:** Verifying that state-driven CSS classes are applied correctly — active nav items, loading spinners, error borders, disabled states. Any time you care about one class among many.

**When NOT to use:** When you want to assert the complete set of classes on an element (use `toHaveClass()` with exact matching instead). Also avoid for non-class-driven state; prefer `toBeDisabled()`, `toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')`, and similar semantic assertions.

**Alternative:** `toHaveClass(/active/)` with a regex works but requires escaping and is less readable. `evaluate(el => el.classList.contains('active'))` bypasses auto-waiting and should be avoided. [official]

---

### Pattern 32: `locator.filter({ visible: true })` — Precise Filtering in Tabbed UIs (v1.51+) [official]

`locator.filter({ visible: true })` narrows a locator to only CSS-visible elements. In tabbed interfaces, skeleton loaders, or components with `display: none` / `visibility: hidden` toggling, multiple DOM elements may share the same role and name — only one panel being active at a time. Without the `visible` filter, `getByRole()` returns all matching elements including hidden ones, causing "strict mode violation" errors.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('only visible tab panel is queried', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  // Click the second tab
  await page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Notifications' }).click();

  // Without { visible: true }, both tab panels match — strict mode fails
  // With { visible: true }, only the active panel is returned
  const activePanel = page
    .getByRole('tabpanel')
    .filter({ visible: true });

  await expect(activePanel).toContainText('Email notifications');
  await expect(activePanel.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /weekly digest/i })).toBeChecked();
});

test('skeleton loader is hidden before filtering visible content', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Multiple card skeletons and real cards share the same structure
  const visibleCards = page
    .getByTestId('product-card')
    .filter({ visible: true });

  // Wait until actual cards are visible (skeletons use display:none on load)
  await expect(visibleCards).toHaveCount(12);
  const firstCardTitle = visibleCards.first().getByRole('heading');
  await expect(firstCardTitle).not.toBeEmpty();
});
```

**When to use:** Tabbed UIs, wizard steps, collapsible panels, and pages with skeleton loaders where hidden elements share the same role/name as visible counterparts.

**When NOT to use:** When you specifically need to assert on hidden elements (e.g., checking that a panel IS hidden). `filter({ visible: true })` will find zero elements in that case and the assertion will incorrectly pass or hang. Use `toBeHidden()` directly on the locator without the visible filter.

**Alternative:** `.nth(0)` after tab click (fragile — depends on DOM order), or scoping locator to a parent container that is unique per tab. [official]

---

### Pattern 33: `testProject.workers` — Per-Project Parallelism with Global Pool Awareness (v1.52+) [official]

Playwright v1.52 introduced `testProject.workers` to control how many workers a specific project may use from the shared global pool. This enables mixed-parallelism suites: fast API tests can claim many workers while slow database integration tests run serially, without separate CI jobs.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Global pool — all projects share this total
  workers: process.env.CI ? 8 : 4,

  projects: [
    {
      name: 'api',
      testDir: './e2e/api',
      workers: 8, // claim up to 8 workers for stateless API tests
    },
    {
      name: 'integration',
      testDir: './e2e/integration',
      workers: 1, // run integration tests serially (shared DB state)
    },
    {
      name: 'visual',
      testDir: './e2e/visual',
      workers: 2, // limit screenshot tests to avoid GPU contention
    },
    {
      name: 'e2e',
      testDir: './e2e/browser',
      // No workers override — uses whatever the pool has available
    },
  ],
});
```

```typescript
// In a test that needs serial execution within its project
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// No code changes needed — parallelism is controlled in config
test('create user', async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/users', {
    data: { email: 'test@example.com', role: 'admin' },
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(201);
});

test('list users includes created user', async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.get('/api/users');
  const users = await res.json();
  expect(users.some((u: { email: string }) => u.email === 'test@example.com')).toBe(true);
});
```

**When to use:** Large multi-project suites where different test types have very different parallelism requirements (stateless API tests vs. stateful DB tests vs. GPU-bound visual tests).

**When NOT to use:** When all your tests have the same parallelism characteristics — the per-project overhead is unnecessary. Also note: project `workers` cannot exceed the global `workers` value (see gotcha 110).

**Alternative:** Separate `playwright.config.ts` per project type (more isolation, more CI complexity). `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` for file-level serialization within a single project. [official]

---

### Pattern 34: `testConfig.failOnFlakyTests` — Zero-Flake-Tolerance CI Gate (v1.52+) [official]

Setting `failOnFlakyTests: true` causes Playwright to exit with code 1 when any test passes only on a retry — flagging it as flaky even though it ultimately "passed." Combined with `retries: 2`, this is the recommended pattern for merge-queue CI where every green run must be genuinely stable.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  retries:            process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
  failOnFlakyTests:   !!process.env.CI,   // v1.52+ — exit 1 if any test needed a retry
  reporter: [
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['github'],
  ],
  use: {
    trace: 'retain-on-first-failure',
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Example: a flaky test that uses random data and sometimes passes
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('search returns results', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('playwright');

  // If this assertion flaps due to a race condition, failOnFlakyTests will
  // report it as flaky even though retry eventually passed
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(5);
});
```

**When to use:** Merge-queue CI gates, release pipelines, and teams enforcing a zero-flake contract. Use alongside `retries: 2` so real environment issues still get a chance to pass.

**When NOT to use:** In development branches where exploratory test failures are expected. Setting this globally during active feature development will cause CI noise. Use an environment variable (`process.env.CI`) to enable only on the main branch pipeline.

**Alternative:** `--fail-on-flaky-tests` CLI flag for one-off enforcement without changing the config. External flake-tracking dashboards (Currents, BuildPulse) for monitoring without blocking. [official]

---

### Pattern 35: `locator.ariaSnapshot()` + External YAML Files — Aria Snapshot Management (v1.49+) [official]

`toMatchAriaSnapshot()` compares the accessibility tree of a locator or page against a YAML template. Storing snapshots in separate `.aria.yml` files (via the `name` option, v1.50+) keeps spec files readable and enables snapshot updates with `--update-snapshots` without touching spec code.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('navigation has correct ARIA structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' });

  // Inline snapshot — good for small, stable components
  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main":
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Home"
        - listitem:
          - link "Products"
        - listitem:
          - link "About"
  `);
});

test('product card structure matches baseline', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  const firstCard = page.getByTestId('product-card').first();

  // External YAML file — updated with: npx playwright test --update-snapshots
  await expect(firstCard).toMatchAriaSnapshot({
    name: 'product-card.aria.yml',
  });
});

test('search results list contains expected count', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search?q=laptop');

  const results = page.getByRole('list', { name: /results/i });

  // Regex matching for dynamic numeric content
  await expect(results).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - list:
      - listitem /Laptop .*/
      - listitem /Laptop .*/
  `);
});
```

**When to use:** Accessibility regression testing, broad structural validation of complex components, and CI gates that catch unintentional ARIA tree changes. Use external YAML files for components shared across multiple tests.

**When NOT to use:** For highly dynamic content where the tree changes every render. Also avoid asserting on the full page tree — scope to a meaningful container locator. The full-page ARIA snapshot includes off-viewport content (see gotcha 68).

**Alternative:** `expect(locator).toHaveAccessibleName()`, `toHaveRole()`, `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` for targeted single-property assertions without snapshot overhead. [official]

---

### Pattern 36: `page.emulateMedia()` — Dynamic Media Emulation Mid-Test [official]

`page.emulateMedia()` changes the active CSS media features (color scheme, print mode, reduced motion) at any point during a test without creating a new context. This enables testing responsive design variants and accessibility preferences within a single test, and is composable with `test.use()` for suite-wide defaults.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dark mode theme applies correct colors', async ({ page }) => {
  // Start in light mode (default)
  await page.goto('/settings');
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(255, 255, 255)');

  // Switch to dark mode mid-test
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(18, 18, 18)');

  // Verify chart component adapts without page reload
  const chart = page.getByTestId('revenue-chart');
  await expect(chart).toContainClass('theme-dark');
});

test('reduced motion disables CSS animations', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/onboarding');

  // Confirm animation duration is overridden by the app's prefers-reduced-motion rule
  const banner = page.getByRole('banner');
  const animDuration = await banner.evaluate(el =>
    getComputedStyle(el).animationDuration,
  );
  expect(animDuration).toBe('0.001s'); // app sets 0.001s under reduce preference
});

test('print layout hides navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/invoice/123');
  await page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' });

  // Nav should be hidden in print stylesheet
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeHidden();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-header')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Testing dark mode, high-contrast, reduced-motion, and print layout variants without spawning separate browser contexts. Ideal for component visual regression suites.

**When NOT to use:** When the media feature must be set before any JavaScript runs on first page load (some frameworks read `window.matchMedia` only at init time). In those cases, set the preference at the context level via `contextOptions: { colorScheme: 'dark' }` in `test.use()`.

**Alternative:** `test.use({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` for suite-wide defaults. `page.evaluate(() => window.matchMedia(...))` for reading (not setting) media state. [official]

---

### Pattern 37: `test.use()` — Fixture Overrides for Scoped Test Configuration [official]

`test.use()` inside a `test.describe()` block overrides built-in or custom fixture values for all tests in that scope without creating a separate config file. This enables locale, viewport, time zone, and credential variations at the describe-block granularity — the smallest practical scope.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/auth'; // extended test with auth fixtures

// Override viewport and locale for a "mobile DE" suite within the same spec file
test.describe('mobile DE locale smoke tests', () => {
  test.use({
    viewport:   { width: 375, height: 812 },
    locale:     'de-DE',
    timezoneId: 'Europe/Berlin',
    userAgent:  'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_0 like Mac OS X)',
  });

  test('price is formatted in German locale', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/1');
    // German: 1.299,00 € (period thousands, comma decimal)
    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-price')).toContainText('1.299,00');
  });

  test('mobile navigation hamburger is visible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /menu/i })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeHidden(); // collapsed by default
  });
});

test.describe('desktop EN locale tests', () => {
  test.use({
    viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    locale:   'en-US',
  });

  test('navigation is always visible on desktop', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Testing the same features at multiple viewport breakpoints, locales, or authentication roles within a single spec file. Avoids creating N separate test files for N configuration variants.

**When NOT to use:** When the configuration divergence is large enough to deserve separate project configurations in `playwright.config.ts`. `test.use()` overrides are invisible in the test list and can be confusing for contributors unfamiliar with the file.

**Alternative:** Playwright `projects` configuration for large multi-locale/multi-device matrices. Parameterized tests via `test.for()` (Playwright v1.57+) for configuration-as-data patterns. [official]

---

### Pattern 38: `mergeTests()` + `mergeExpects()` — Composing Multi-Domain Test Utilities [official]

`mergeTests()` combines fixture definitions from multiple modules into a single `test` object, and `mergeExpects()` combines custom matchers. Both were stabilised in v1.40+. This enables a clean "domain modules" architecture where auth, database, and UI fixtures live independently but are composed at the spec level with a single import.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts — auth-domain fixtures
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ authedPage: import('@playwright/test').Page }>({
  authedPage: async ({ page, context }, use) => {
    await context.addCookies([{ name: 'session', value: process.env.TEST_TOKEN!, url: '/' }]);
    await use(page);
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/db.ts — database fixtures
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ resetDb: () => Promise<void> }>({
  resetDb: async ({}, use) => {
    const reset = async () => { /* call DB reset endpoint */ };
    await use(reset);
    await reset(); // teardown
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/index.ts — merge all domains
import { mergeTests, mergeExpects } from '@playwright/test';
import { test as authTest }         from './auth';
import { test as dbTest }           from './db';
import { expect as customExpect }   from './matchers';

export const test   = mergeTests(authTest, dbTest);
export const expect = mergeExpects(customExpect);

// e2e/specs/orders.spec.ts — single import, all fixtures available
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures';

test('admin can create order', async ({ authedPage, resetDb }) => {
  await resetDb();
  await authedPage.goto('/admin/orders/new');
  await authedPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create order' }).click();
  await expect(authedPage.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Order created');
});
```

**When to use:** Large projects with multiple cross-cutting fixture concerns (auth, DB seeding, feature flags, mock servers). Keeps each fixture module small, independently testable, and easy to add or remove.

**When NOT to use:** For small suites with one or two fixtures — `base.extend()` directly is simpler. Also avoid if two modules define fixtures with the same name: the last module in the merge wins silently (see gotcha 103).

**Alternative:** Manual fixture composition with sequential `base.extend(extend1).extend(extend2)` — verbose but explicit about precedence. [official]

---

### Pattern 39: `page.requestGC()` — Memory Leak Detection in Long-Running Tests (v1.48+) [official]

`page.requestGC()` triggers a garbage collection hint in the browser. After GC, heap snapshots or `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` give more accurate retained-size numbers. Used in tests that verify components are cleaned up after unmount or that event listener counts don't grow across interactions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('detached nodes are GC-eligible after modal close', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Open and close the modal 5 times
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open modal/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeHidden();
  }

  // Request GC to evict unreachable detached modal nodes
  await page.requestGC(); // v1.48+

  // Use evaluate to count detached nodes via the performance API
  const retainedBytes = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    if ('measureUserAgentSpecificMemory' in performance) {
      const result = await (performance as any).measureUserAgentSpecificMemory();
      return result.bytes;
    }
    return null;
  });

  if (retainedBytes !== null) {
    // Retained memory should not grow unboundedly with repeated open/close
    expect(retainedBytes).toBeLessThan(50 * 1024 * 1024); // 50 MB ceiling
  }
});
```

**When to use:** Memory regression testing for single-page apps that open and close complex components repeatedly. Useful when you suspect event listener leaks or retained DOM subtrees.

**When NOT to use:** In standard functional tests — GC hints have no deterministic effect and add latency. Also note that GC is a *hint*, not a guarantee; the browser may ignore it. Do not write tests that will fail if GC did not actually run.

**Alternative:** Chrome DevTools `Memory` panel for interactive investigation. Heap snapshot diffing via CDP (`Target.activateTarget` + `HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot`) for deterministic profiling outside Playwright. [official]

---

### Pattern 40: `page.clock.setSystemTime()` vs `page.clock.setFixedTime()` — Choosing the Right Time Control API (v1.45+) [official]

Playwright's clock API offers two superficially similar methods with very different semantics. `setFixedTime()` only spoofs `Date.now()` / `new Date()` — timers (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`) still run on real time. `setSystemTime()` (after `clock.install()`) spoofs date AND controls all browser timers. Choosing the wrong one is the most common clock-related bug.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ✅ setFixedTime — for simple date display tests (no timer control needed)
test('dashboard shows correct date header', async ({ page }) => {
  // Does NOT install a fake timer engine — setInterval still runs normally
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-01-01T09:00:00Z'));
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('date-header')).toContainText('January 1, 2026');
});

// ✅ clock.install() + setSystemTime — for timer-driven UI tests
test('session timeout banner appears after 15 minutes of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install fake clock BEFORE goto so module-level timers are intercepted
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T09:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/app');

  // Advance 14 minutes — no banner yet
  await page.clock.runFor('14m');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeHidden();

  // Advance 1 more minute — banner appears at exactly 15m
  await page.clock.runFor('1m');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();
});

// Decision table:
// | Need                             | Use                               |
// | Only Date.now() / new Date()     | setFixedTime()                    |
// | Control setTimeout/setInterval   | clock.install() + runFor          |
// | Pause and inspect state          | clock.install() + pauseAt         |
// | Advance without timer dispatch   | clock.install() + setSystemTime   |
```

**When to use:** `setFixedTime()` for date-display-only components; `clock.install()` + `runFor()` / `pauseAt()` for any test involving timers, polling, debounce, or session expiry logic.

**When NOT to use:** Do not call `setFixedTime()` when the component under test uses `setTimeout` or `setInterval` for any state transitions — the timers will fire at real-world time, making the test flaky. Do not call `clock.install()` after `page.goto()` for the same reason (see gotcha 106).

**Alternative:** `vi.useFakeTimers()` / `jest.useFakeTimers()` for unit tests. For Playwright component tests, `page.clock` is the correct surface. [official]

---

### Pattern 41: `browserContext.clearCookies({ name, domain, path })` — Selective Cookie Removal (v1.43+) [official]

`browserContext.clearCookies()` accepts filter options to remove only specific cookies rather than wiping the entire cookie jar. This is essential in multi-tenant tests where a test needs to expire one auth cookie while preserving CSRF tokens or analytics cookies.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('expired session redirects to login without clearing CSRF token', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.goto('/app');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  // Selectively remove only the session cookie — keep CSRF and analytics cookies
  await context.clearCookies({ name: 'session_id' }); // v1.43+

  await page.reload();

  // Should redirect to login, not show an error about missing CSRF token
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toBeHidden(); // no "invalid request" error

  // Confirm CSRF cookie survived
  const cookies = await context.cookies();
  expect(cookies.some(c => c.name === 'csrf_token')).toBe(true);
});

test('clear only cookies from third-party domain', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Remove only analytics cookies from a specific domain
  await context.clearCookies({ domain: '.analytics.example.com' }); // v1.43+

  const remainingCookies = await context.cookies();
  const analyticsRemaining = remainingCookies.filter(
    c => c.domain.includes('analytics.example.com'),
  );
  expect(analyticsRemaining).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**When to use:** Auth expiry scenarios, multi-tenant login switching, testing partial cookie corruption, and verifying that CSRF protection survives auth cookie rotation.

**When NOT to use:** When you need a completely clean slate — `clearCookies()` with no args (clear all) or a fresh `context` from `browser.newContext()` is simpler and more reliable.

**Alternative:** `context.addCookies()` with an `expires: -1` value to mark a cookie as expired. `context.storageState()` save/restore pattern for full session snapshots. [official]

---

### Pattern 42: `page.addLocatorHandler()` with `times` — One-Shot Overlay Dismissal (v1.44+) [official]

`page.addLocatorHandler()` registers a callback to automatically dismiss overlays (cookie banners, GDPR popups, soft paywalls) when they appear and block interactions. The `times` option limits how many times the handler fires, preventing infinite loops when the overlay can reappear. `page.removeLocatorHandler()` cleans up after the scenario that needs it.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cookie banner auto-dismissed before checkout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register handler BEFORE goto — fires whenever the overlay locator becomes visible
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
    async (overlay) => {
      await overlay.getByRole('button', { name: /accept all/i }).click();
    },
    { times: 1 }, // dismiss at most once — prevents infinite loop if dialog re-opens
  );

  await page.goto('/');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Shop now' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();

  // Handler auto-dismissed the cookie dialog if it appeared during navigation
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout/);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /checkout/i })).toBeVisible();
});

test('subscription nag suppressed during content reading', async ({ page }) => {
  const nagDialog = page.getByTestId('subscription-nag');

  await page.addLocatorHandler(nagDialog, async () => {
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  });

  await page.goto('/article/long-form-content');
  // Read the full article without the nag blocking assertions
  const headings = page.getByRole('heading');
  await expect(headings).toHaveCount(7);

  // Explicit teardown — important if other tests in the same worker should NOT dismiss the nag
  await page.removeLocatorHandler(nagDialog);
});
```

**When to use:** Third-party overlays, GDPR consent banners, soft paywalls, and app-level promotional modals that appear unpredictably during navigation. Centralise in a fixture for reuse.

**When NOT to use:** When the overlay is part of the feature under test — the handler would mask actual behavior. Also avoid relying on `times: 1` for banners that reappear on every navigation (see gotcha 99 — `times: 1` still fires if the overlay re-opens after first dismissal).

**Alternative:** `context.addCookies()` to pre-set the "consent accepted" cookie before the test runs. `page.route()` to intercept the analytics request that triggers the consent banner. [official]

---

### Pattern 43: TLS Client Certificate Testing with `clientCertificates` (v1.46+) [official]

Playwright v1.46 added `clientCertificates` to `browserType.launchPersistentContext()` and `browser.newContext()`. This allows tests against mTLS-protected APIs and admin panels without a proxy. The certificate is sent automatically on connection — no manual header manipulation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

// playwright.config.ts — configure cert at context level for all tests in a project
// projects: [{ name: 'mtls', use: { clientCertificates: [...] } }]

test('admin panel accessible with valid client certificate', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Provide cert inline for one-off tests
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    clientCertificates: [
      {
        origin:     'https://admin.example.com',
        certPath:   path.resolve('certs/client.crt'),
        keyPath:    path.resolve('certs/client.key'),
        passphrase: process.env.CERT_PASSPHRASE,
      },
    ],
  });

  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('https://admin.example.com/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /admin dashboard/i })).toBeVisible();
  await context.close();
});

test('request without cert is rejected with 401', async ({ request }) => {
  // Default request context has no client cert — server should reject
  const res = await request.get('https://admin.example.com/api/users');
  expect(res.status()).toBe(401);
});

test('API request with client cert via APIRequestContext', async ({ playwright }) => {
  const apiContext = await playwright.request.newContext({
    clientCertificates: [
      {
        origin:   'https://admin.example.com',
        certPath: path.resolve('certs/client.crt'),
        keyPath:  path.resolve('certs/client.key'),
      },
    ],
  });
  const res = await apiContext.get('https://admin.example.com/api/health');
  expect(res.ok()).toBe(true);
  await apiContext.dispose();
});
```

**When to use:** Testing mTLS-protected internal services, admin endpoints, or B2B API integrations where the server requires a client-presented X.509 certificate for authentication.

**When NOT to use:** For standard bearer-token or cookie auth — `clientCertificates` adds cert management overhead that is not justified. Also avoid checking actual cert files into the repository; load them from secrets management.

**Alternative:** A reverse proxy that injects the client cert header (`X-Client-Cert-Subject`) before the test server. `page.route()` to inject auth headers for non-mTLS scenarios. [official]

---

### Pattern 44: `locator.filter({ hasText, hasNotText })` — Negative Text Filtering for Dynamic Lists [official]

`locator.filter()` accepts both `hasText` and `hasNotText` options, and `has` / `hasNot` with locator arguments. This enables precise element selection in dynamic lists where multiple items share the same role but differ by content — without resorting to `.nth()` (position-dependent) or CSS selectors (brittle).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('out-of-stock items cannot be added to cart', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Find all product cards that contain "Out of stock" text
  const outOfStockCards = page
    .getByRole('article')
    .filter({ hasText: /out of stock/i });

  const count = await outOfStockCards.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const card = outOfStockCards.nth(i);
    // The "Add to cart" button should be disabled on these cards
    await expect(card.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i })).toBeDisabled();
  }
});

test('filter removes item — remaining rows do not contain deleted email', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/admin/users');

  // Delete a specific user
  await page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasText: 'jane@example.com' })
    .getByRole('button', { name: /delete/i })
    .click();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /confirm/i }).click();

  // Assert deleted user is gone — all remaining rows must NOT contain that email
  const rowsWithDeleted = page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasText: 'jane@example.com' });
  await expect(rowsWithDeleted).toHaveCount(0);
});
```

**When to use:** Dynamic tables, product listings, and any list where you need to scope actions or assertions to items matching (or not matching) a text condition. Vastly more resilient than positional `.nth()` or XPath predicates.

**When NOT to use:** When the filtering logic is complex enough to require JavaScript (e.g., filtering by computed price range). In that case, `page.evaluate()` with DOM API filtering is cleaner.

**Alternative:** `page.getByText()` with exact match for single known values. `locator.filter({ has: page.getByRole('img', { name: 'sale' }) })` to filter by presence of a child locator rather than text. [official]

---

### Pattern 45: `test.fail.only()` — Focus-Run on Known Failing Tests (v1.49+) [official]

`test.fail.only()` marks a test as expected-to-fail AND focuses it for exclusive execution. It is the correct way to investigate a known regression in isolation without temporarily commenting out other tests or misusing `test.only()` on a failing test (which would make the suite report an unexpected pass if the test actually passes).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ✅ Focused failing test — runs only this test, expects failure
// Remove .fail.only() once the bug is fixed and replace with test.only() or plain test()
test.fail.only('cart total does not update after quantity change — regression #4821', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');

  const qtyInput = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: /quantity/i });
  await qtyInput.fill('3');
  await qtyInput.press('Tab'); // trigger onBlur update

  // BUG: total still shows price for qty=1 — this assertion will fail until fix is merged
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-total')).toContainText('$89.97'); // 3 × $29.99
});

test('checkout proceeds with valid cart', async ({ page }) => {
  // This test will NOT run when test.fail.only() is active above
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout/);
});
```

**When to use:** Investigating a specific known regression during development. The `fail` marker documents the expectation that this test should fail, and `.only` scopes execution to it. The test suite reports correctly — a `fail.only` test that fails is a PASS from the runner's perspective.

**When NOT to use:** Do not commit `test.fail.only()` to CI. It should be a local investigation tool only. Also do not use `test.fail()` (without `.only`) to permanently suppress a flaky test in CI — fix the underlying bug or use `test.fixme()` with a tracking link.

**Alternative:** `test.fixme('tracking issue #4821')` for deferring a known broken test in CI with a documented reason. `test.only()` when you want to focus on a passing test for debugging without the "expected failure" semantics. [official]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 32

### 112. `toContainClass()` does not auto-wait for the class to appear — it retries on assertion timeout, not on DOM settle [community]

**What:** `expect(locator).toContainClass('active')` retries up to the assertion timeout (default 5 s) if the class is not present. However, if the class is applied via a JavaScript animation library with a staggered delay longer than the assertion timeout, the assertion fails even though the class will eventually appear.

**WHY:** `toContainClass()` is an auto-retrying assertion that polls the current DOM state at each retry interval until the configured `expect.timeout` is reached. It does not wait "as long as needed" like `toBeVisible()` waits for visibility — it only waits up to the assertion timeout. If your animation library applies classes 6–8 seconds after triggering a transition, and your assertion timeout is 5 seconds, you get a spurious failure. Increase `expect.timeout` per-assertion or await the transition explicitly.

**Fix:** Either increase timeout inline (`await expect(el).toContainClass('active', { timeout: 10_000 })`) or wait for the transition to complete before asserting the class.

```typescript
// ❌ Fails if animation completes after the 5s assertion timeout
await page.getByRole('button').click();
await expect(page.getByTestId('drawer')).toContainClass('active');

// ✅ Wait for transitionend before asserting class state
await page.getByRole('button').click();
await page.getByTestId('drawer').evaluate(el =>
  new Promise(resolve => el.addEventListener('transitionend', resolve, { once: true })),
);
await expect(page.getByTestId('drawer')).toContainClass('active');
```

---

### 113. `mergeTests()` does not merge worker-scoped fixtures — worker fixtures from later modules silently shadow earlier ones [community]

**What:** When you `mergeTests(moduleA, moduleB)` and both modules define a worker-scoped fixture with the same name, the resulting merged test uses only the definition from `moduleB` with no error or warning. This is distinct from gotcha 103 (test-scoped fixture shadowing) and is more dangerous because worker fixtures are shared across all tests in a worker process.

**WHY:** `mergeTests()` resolves fixture name collisions by last-module-wins for both test-scoped and worker-scoped fixtures. A silently wrong worker fixture can corrupt test results across an entire worker's run, not just a single test. The Playwright team considers named collisions a programmer error and expects callers to avoid same-name fixtures across merged modules.

**Fix:** Namespace worker-scoped fixtures with a module prefix (e.g., `authWorker`, `dbWorker`) to make collisions structurally impossible. Audit merged modules for name conflicts before shipping.

```typescript
// ❌ Both modules export a worker-scoped 'db' fixture — moduleB silently wins
const merged = mergeTests(moduleA, moduleB); // moduleA's 'db' is dropped silently

// ✅ Prefix worker fixtures to avoid collision
// moduleA exports: dbAuth  (worker-scoped auth DB connection)
// moduleB exports: dbAnalytics  (worker-scoped analytics DB connection)
const merged = mergeTests(moduleA, moduleB); // no collision — both fixtures coexist
```

---

### 114. `page.addLocatorHandler()` fires during `expect()` retry polling — it can dismiss an overlay that should have been asserted [community]

**What:** `page.addLocatorHandler()` fires its callback any time Playwright detects the registered locator is blocking an action or assertion — including the retry-polling phase of `expect()` calls. If a test asserts that a certain dialog IS visible, but a locator handler is registered to dismiss that same dialog, the handler may dismiss it between assertion retries.

**WHY:** The locator handler mechanism intercepts at the low-level action layer, which includes the DOM-check phase of auto-retrying assertions. The handler does not distinguish between an action (click, fill) and an assertion retry — its job is to ensure overlays never block Playwright's interactions. This makes it impossible to assert on the very element the handler is configured to dismiss without first removing the handler.

**Fix:** Remove the locator handler before asserting that the overlay IS present. Use `page.removeLocatorHandler()` before the assertion and re-register afterward.

```typescript
// ❌ Handler dismisses the dialog during toBeVisible() retry polling
await page.addLocatorHandler(page.getByRole('dialog'), async (d) => {
  await d.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }).click();
});
await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible(); // may fail — handler dismissed it

// ✅ Remove handler before asserting the overlay is present
const dialogLocator = page.getByRole('dialog');
await page.removeLocatorHandler(dialogLocator);
await expect(dialogLocator).toBeVisible(); // safe — no handler interfering
// Re-register for subsequent navigation steps if needed
await page.addLocatorHandler(dialogLocator, async (d) => {
  await d.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }).click();
});
```

---

### 115. `test.use({ storageState })` in a `describe` block loads the state file at test-start — mid-run file mutations affect later tests [community]

**What:** When you call `test.use({ storageState: './auth.json' })` inside a `test.describe()` block, Playwright reads the JSON file from disk at the start of each test. If a parallel worker or global setup job rewrites `auth.json` during the suite run, later tests in the describe block receive the updated file content rather than the original snapshot.

**WHY:** `storageState` in `test.use()` is a context fixture option resolved at test startup, not a pre-loaded value frozen at suite parse time. The file path is evaluated lazily — each test context reads the file when the context is created. In parallel suites where multiple workers share a single auth file path, a worker that refreshes the token and writes back to the same path will cause a race condition that silently mutates state for other workers' subsequent tests.

**Fix:** Use per-worker auth file paths indexed by `testInfo.workerIndex` to prevent cross-worker file collisions, or pass a deep-copied state object instead of a file path.

```typescript
// ❌ All workers read/write the same path — race condition in parallel runs
await page.context().storageState({ path: './auth.json' });

// ✅ Per-worker file path — no cross-worker collision
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend({
  storageState: async ({ }, use, testInfo) =>
    use(`./auth-worker-${testInfo.workerIndex}.json`),
});
```

---

### 116. `expect(locator).toHaveCount(0)` resolves immediately before async content renders — it is not a safe "never appeared" assertion [community]

**What:** `expect(locator).toHaveCount(0)` satisfies on the first polling cycle when no elements match, because zero elements are found immediately on an async page before content renders. Developers use it to assert "this element was never present," but it passes before the page has finished loading and the elements may appear 100–500 ms later.

**WHY:** `toHaveCount()` is an auto-retrying assertion that resolves as soon as the count matches. For `n=0`, the condition is true on every polling cycle until elements appear — so on a page that renders asynchronously, the assertion passes in the first cycle (before render) even if elements would appear shortly after. The assertion does not "wait and confirm nothing appeared for 5 seconds"; it "passes at the first instant the count is zero." This is the correct behavior for asserting element removal after an action, but incorrect for asserting elements were never present on first load.

**Fix:** Wait for a stable DOM landmark that confirms the async render is complete before asserting a count of zero.

```typescript
// ❌ toHaveCount(0) resolves instantly before async content renders
await page.goto('/dashboard');
await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveCount(0); // passes at t=0ms — NOT safe

// ✅ Wait for page render to stabilise, then assert no errors
await page.goto('/dashboard');
await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible(); // confirms page rendered
await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveCount(0); // now safe
```

---

| API | Version | What it does | When to use it |
|-----|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `expect(locator).toContainClass(name)` | v1.52+ | Assert one CSS class without requiring exact full-class match | State-driven CSS classes, active nav, disabled states |
| `locator.filter({ visible: true })` | v1.51+ | Narrow locator to CSS-visible elements only | Tabbed UIs, skeleton loaders, dynamic show/hide |
| `testProject.workers` | v1.52+ | Per-project worker cap within the global pool | Mixed-parallelism suites (API + DB + visual) |
| `testConfig.failOnFlakyTests` | v1.52+ | Exit code 1 when any test needs a retry to pass | Zero-flake merge-queue gates |
| `expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name })` | v1.50+ | Compare accessibility tree against external YAML snapshot file | Accessibility regression, shared component baselines |
| `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme, reducedMotion })` | any | Change media features mid-test without new context | Dark mode, print, reduced-motion visual variants |
| `test.use({ locale, viewport, timezoneId })` | any | Scoped fixture overrides within a describe block | Multi-locale, multi-breakpoint tests in one spec file |
| `mergeTests()` + `mergeExpects()` | v1.40+ | Compose fixtures and matchers from multiple modules | Domain-split fixture architecture |
| `page.requestGC()` | v1.48+ | Hint browser to run garbage collection | Memory leak regression tests |

| `page.addLocatorHandler(locator, fn, { times })` | v1.44+ | Auto-dismiss overlays, limited by `times` count | Cookie banners, soft paywalls, subscription nags |
| `clientCertificates` in `browser.newContext()` | v1.46+ | mTLS client certificate for context/request | Admin panels, B2B APIs requiring client cert auth |
| `locator.filter({ hasNotText })` | v1.33+ | Negative text filter on a locator set | Assert deletion, filter out-of-stock items |
| `test.fail.only()` | v1.49+ | Focus-run a test that is expected to fail | Isolated regression investigation |
