### Pattern 170: Playwright Test Agents — Planner/Generator/Healer Pipeline (v1.56+) [official]

Playwright v1.56 introduced three built-in AI test agents that form a sequential pipeline: the **Planner** explores the application and produces structured Markdown test plans; the **Generator** converts plans into executable `.spec.ts` files with live selector verification; and the **Healer** executes failing tests and automatically repairs locator or assertion failures. Initialize agent definitions with `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude` (or `--loop=vscode` for VS Code). A **seed test** (`tests/seed.spec.ts`) bootstraps the environment — the agents use it to understand fixture setup, auth state, and navigation conventions before writing or healing any spec. Re-run `init-agents` after every Playwright upgrade to receive updated agent tooling.

```typescript
// tests/seed.spec.ts — environment bootstrap for agents
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('seed: authenticated dashboard', async ({ page }) => {
  // Agents use this test to learn your auth pattern and navigation baseline
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  // Signal to agents that the dashboard heading is the auth success indicator
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
});

// specs/checkout.md — plan file (produced by Planner agent)
// ## Add item to cart
// 1. Navigate to /products
// 2. Click "Add to cart" on any visible product card
// 3. Expect cart count badge to show "1"
//
// ## Proceed to checkout
// 1. Click "View cart" button
// 2. Expect /cart URL
// 3. Click "Checkout" button
// 4. Expect /checkout URL

// tests/create/checkout.spec.ts — generated by Generator agent from the plan
test('add item to cart', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.getByRole('article').first()
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: /cart/i })).toContainText('1');
});

test('proceed to checkout', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout/);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Agents require a running application to verify selectors during generation — they cannot produce tests from static analysis alone. Healer agent repair is best-effort: it skips tests when it determines the feature is genuinely broken rather than the selector being stale. Always review generated and healed tests before committing. Re-generating definitions after a Playwright upgrade (with `init-agents`) is mandatory — stale agent definitions lack access to new tools and produce inferior output. [official]

---

### Pattern 171: `page.screencast` — Annotated Video Recording for CI Evidence (v1.59+) [official]

`page.screencast` is a Chromium-only API that records tests as WebM video with optional visual annotations. Unlike `recordVideo` (which records silently), the screencast API lets tests inject chapter titles, highlighted element overlays, and custom HTML overlays into the video stream. This is the correct tool for producing AI agent "video receipts" and step-by-step walkthrough recordings for QA sign-off workflows.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout flow with annotated screencast', async ({ page, browserName }) => {
  test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'Screencast API is Chromium-only');

  // Start recording with 1280x720 output
  await page.screencast.start({
    path:    'test-results/checkout-flow.webm',
    size:    { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    quality: 80,
  });

  // Enable visual click/fill annotations (element highlight + action label)
  await page.screencast.showActions({
    duration: 800,    // ms each annotation persists
    fontSize:  20,
    position: 'bottom-right',
  });

  // Chapter title injected as centered overlay for video segmentation
  await page.screencast.showChapter('Step 1 — Add Product to Cart', {
    description: 'Navigate to products and add a widget',
    duration:    2000,
  });

  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: /cart/i })).toContainText('1');

  await page.screencast.showChapter('Step 2 — Proceed to Checkout');

  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout/);

  // Custom HTML overlay for environment annotation
  await page.screencast.showOverlay(
    '<div style="background:rgba(0,0,0,0.6);color:white;padding:4px 8px;font-size:14px">' +
    `ENV: ${process.env.APP_ENV ?? 'staging'}` +
    '</div>',
    { duration: 3000 }
  );

  await page.screencast.stop();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `page.screencast` is **Chromium-only** — it depends on CDP's `Page.startScreencast` command which is unavailable in Firefox and WebKit. Always guard with `test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', ...)`. The `onFrame` callback mode (streaming JPEG frames) enables live preview thumbnails and AI vision pipelines but adds CPU overhead; the `path` mode (file output) is lower overhead and suitable for CI. Do not confuse with `recordVideo` in `use:` config — `screencast` is test-body controlled and supports annotations; `recordVideo` runs passively for the entire test with no annotation support. [official]

---

### Pattern 172: `browser.bind()` / `browser.unbind()` — AI Agent Browser Session Sharing (v1.59+) [official]

`browser.bind(sessionName, options)` makes a launched browser available for connection by external clients (AI agents, CLI tools, other test processes) via a WebSocket endpoint. The returned `endpoint` URL can be passed to `chromium.connectOverCDP(endpoint)` or to `playwright-cli attach sessionName` for interactive inspection. `browser.unbind(sessionName)` stops accepting new connections. Use a worker-scoped fixture to manage the session lifecycle — the endpoint URL is tied to the OS process and becomes stale on worker restart.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/agent-session.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { chromium }     from '@playwright/test';

type AgentFixtures = { agentEndpoint: string };

export const test = base.extend<AgentFixtures>({
  agentEndpoint: [
    async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
      const sessionName = `worker-${workerInfo.workerIndex}`;
      const browser     = await chromium.launch();

      // Bind browser for external inspection — agents connect here
      const { endpoint } = await browser.bind(sessionName, {
        host: 'localhost',
        port: 0,  // OS-assigned ephemeral port
      });

      console.log(`[worker ${workerInfo.workerIndex}] agent endpoint: ${endpoint}`);
      // → ws://localhost:52341/playwright/session/worker-0

      await use(endpoint);

      await browser.unbind(sessionName);
      await browser.close();
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },  // bind once per worker, not per test
  ],
});

// In a test: pass endpoint to an AI agent or CLI tool for inspection
test('agent can inspect live checkout page', async ({ agentEndpoint, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Log for the AI agent's context
  console.log(`Connect to live browser: ${agentEndpoint}`);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /checkout/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```

```bash
# List all bound sessions from CLI in a separate terminal
npx playwright-cli show
# → worker-0  ws://localhost:52341/playwright/session/worker-0
```

**Tradeoff:** The endpoint URL is process-scoped — if the worker restarts (crash, `maxFailures` threshold hit), the new browser gets a different port. Never cache the endpoint at module level; always retrieve it from the worker-scoped fixture. Multiple clients can connect simultaneously, but concurrent mutations from two clients produce undefined ordering. Use `browser.bind()` for read-only agent inspection and `connectOverCDP()` mutations only from test code. [official]

---

### Pattern 173: `locator.normalize()` — Agent-Driven Locator Healing Review Loop (v1.59+) [official]

`locator.normalize()` converts any brittle CSS selector or XPath into a best-practice Playwright locator by querying the live DOM and choosing the most stable equivalent (role-based, label-based, or test-id-based). Use it in a review loop: call `normalize()` on every locator produced by legacy codegen, inspect the result, then upgrade if the suggested locator is semantically better. The method operates on the live page — it requires a running browser context.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('normalize and compare locator quality', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  // --- Brittle CSS locator from legacy test ---
  const brittle = page.locator('div.auth-panel > form > input:first-child');

  // normalize() consults the live DOM and suggests the best-practice equivalent
  const normalized = brittle.normalize();

  // Log both for human/agent review
  console.log('Original :', brittle.toString());
  // Original : locator('div.auth-panel > form > input:first-child')
  console.log('Normalized:', normalized.toString());
  // Normalized: locator('input[name="email"]')  — or getByLabel/getByRole if ARIA present

  // Verify the normalized locator points to the same element before replacing
  await expect(normalized).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(normalized).toBeVisible();

  // Use the normalized locator in actual assertions
  await normalized.fill('user@example.com');
  await expect(normalized).toHaveValue('user@example.com');
});

// Batch normalization utility — useful in healing loops
async function auditLocators(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  locators: Record<string, string>
): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  const results: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, selector] of Object.entries(locators)) {
    const original   = page.locator(selector);
    const normalized = original.normalize();
    results[name] = normalized.toString();
  }
  return results;
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `normalize()` prefers `getByTestId()` over `getByRole()` when an element has both `data-testid` and a semantic ARIA role. Automation cannot determine your project's selector hierarchy preferences — always review the output rather than replacing blindly. `normalize()` operates on the current DOM snapshot; if the page structure changes between page loads, the normalized locator may differ between runs. [official]

---

### Pattern 174: `page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' })` with Agent Repair Prompts [official]

The `mode: 'ai'` option produces a condensed ARIA tree optimized for LLM token efficiency — it removes redundant nesting, condenses repetitive structures, and omits ARIA-invisible elements. Combine with `depth` to further limit traversal for focused element regions. This is the primary mechanism for feeding page context into AI-driven test repair prompts, as passing a full ARIA tree to an LLM often exceeds context limits or produces noisy reasoning.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('capture AI-optimized snapshot for agent repair context', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Narrow to the form section (reduce token count, improve LLM focus)
  const formSnap = await page.locator('form[data-testid="checkout-form"]')
    .ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai', depth: 3 });

  // Attach to test report for agent consumption
  await test.info().attach('form-aria-ai.yaml', {
    body:        formSnap,
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });

  // Sample agent repair prompt template
  const repairPrompt = `
    The following Playwright test step failed:
      await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242424242424242');
    Error: Locator not found within 30000ms

    Current page accessibility tree (checkout form, depth 3):
    ${formSnap}

    Suggest a corrected Playwright locator for the card number input.
    Prefer getByRole > getByLabel > getByTestId.
  `.trim();

  // Log for the agent process to consume
  console.log('[AGENT_REPAIR_PROMPT]', repairPrompt);

  // Also capture full snapshot for WCAG compliance assertion
  await expect(page.locator('form[data-testid="checkout-form"]'))
    .toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - group "Payment Details":
        - textbox "Card number"
        - textbox "Expiry date"
        - textbox "CVC"
    `);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mode: 'ai'` omits `aria-hidden` elements, decorative SVGs, and role=presentation containers — visually present elements may be absent from the snapshot. Never use `mode: 'ai'` for WCAG compliance assertions where completeness matters; use the standard (no mode option) snapshot instead. Combine with `locator.ariaSnapshot()` scoped to specific page regions rather than `page.ariaSnapshot()` (whole page) to minimize token cost for large SPA pages. [official]

---

### Pattern 175: `page.screencast.showChapter()` + `showOverlay()` — Video Receipt Workflow for Agentic QA [community]

Teams using AI agents for autonomous QA need reproducible video evidence of test execution. The screencast chapter and overlay methods transform raw video into structured walkthroughs with segment markers, environment metadata, and failure context annotations. A `showChapter()` call marks the start of a logical section (analogous to `test.step()`), while `showOverlay()` injects arbitrary HTML for contextual metadata (branch name, feature flag state, environment).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test.describe('agent QA video receipt', () => {
  test('registration flow @video-receipt', async ({ page, browserName }) => {
    test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'Screencast is Chromium-only');

    const videoPath = path.join(test.info().outputDir, 'registration-receipt.webm');

    await page.screencast.start({ path: videoPath, size: { width: 1280, height: 720 } });
    await page.screencast.showActions({ duration: 700, position: 'bottom-left' });

    // Inject environment metadata visible in every frame
    await page.screencast.showOverlay(
      `<div style="position:fixed;bottom:4px;right:4px;` +
      `background:rgba(0,0,0,.55);color:#fff;font-size:11px;padding:2px 6px;` +
      `border-radius:3px;font-family:monospace">` +
      `${process.env.APP_ENV ?? 'staging'} | ${process.env.GITHUB_SHA?.slice(0, 7) ?? 'local'}` +
      `</div>`,
    );

    await page.screencast.showChapter('1. Navigate to Registration');
    await page.goto('/register');

    await page.screencast.showChapter('2. Fill Registration Form');
    await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Alice Example');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('alice@example.com');
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Secure!Pass99');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /create account/i }).click();

    await page.screencast.showChapter('3. Verify Welcome Screen', {
      description: 'Asserts that the dashboard loads post-registration',
    });
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /welcome/i })).toBeVisible();

    await page.screencast.stop();

    // Attach video to test report for agentic review
    await test.info().attach('registration-receipt.webm', {
      path:        videoPath,
      contentType: 'video/webm',
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Each `showChapter()` call briefly blocks frame rendering (the overlay is composited synchronously). For performance-sensitive test flows, call `showChapter()` before navigations, not mid-interaction. `showOverlay()` without a `duration` persists indefinitely — always provide a `duration` or call `hideOverlays()` before the next chapter to avoid stale metadata text in the video. The video attachment in the HTML report is accessible under the test's "Attachments" tab but is not automatically played inline — engineers must download and view it. [community]

---

### Pattern 176: `npx playwright test --debug=cli` — Agentic Test Debugging Session (v1.59+) [official]

`--debug=cli` starts a headless debugging session where Playwright exposes a step-by-step CLI interface. Unlike `--debug` (which opens Playwright Inspector GUI), `--debug=cli` is designed for automated agents: it outputs a session ID and structured command prompts to stdout, allowing an AI agent to drive test execution via shell commands. Pair with `browser.bind()` to let the agent observe the page state in real time while stepping through test actions.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — dedicated debug project for agentic debugging
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name:      'agent-debug',
      use:       { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], headless: false },
      testMatch: /debug\.spec\.ts/,
    },
  ],
});
```

```bash
# Start agentic debug session — outputs session ID and step prompts
npx playwright test --project=agent-debug --debug=cli tests/create/checkout.spec.ts

# Agent receives:
# SESSION: pw-debug-abc123
# STEP 1/5: page.goto('/products')
# [continue/skip/abort]:

# Attach to the running browser from a second agent process
npx playwright-cli attach pw-debug-abc123
```

```typescript
// When --debug=cli is active, page.pause() waits for agent resume signal
test('debug-mode checkout', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.pause();  // ← CLI debug session waits here for agent command
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `--debug=cli` is optimized for non-interactive agent workflows — it does not open any GUI and writes structured output to stdout for programmatic parsing. Running with `headless: false` is recommended so the agent can also use `browser.bind()` to connect a vision model. This mode is not suitable for CI pipelines — use it only in development or agent-controlled repair loops. [official]

---

### Pattern 177: `tracing.startHar()` with `urlFilter` — Scoped HAR Capture for Offline Replay (v1.60+) [official]

`context.tracing.startHar(path, options)` starts recording an HTTP Archive (HAR) scoped to the current tracing session. The `urlFilter` option (string glob or RegExp) limits capture to relevant API endpoints, preventing HAR files from bloating with CDN assets. Pair with `page.routeFromHAR()` to replay the captured traffic in subsequent tests for deterministic offline execution. Use `await using` syntax (TypeScript 5.2+ / Node 20+) for automatic finalization even when tests throw.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

// ── Recording: capture HAR during a live test run ──────────────────────────────
test('record checkout API traffic as HAR', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const harPath = path.join(test.info().outputDir, 'checkout-api.har');

  // Only capture /api/ requests — skip static assets, CDN, analytics
  await using _har = await context.tracing.startHar(harPath, {
    content:   'embed',   // embed response bodies (larger but self-contained)
    mode:      'full',    // capture all request/response metadata
    urlFilter: /\/api\//,
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
  // HAR finalizes automatically when `_har` goes out of scope (await using)
});

// ── Replay: use captured HAR for deterministic offline test ────────────────────
test('replay checkout flow from HAR', async ({ page }) => {
  // Route all /api/ traffic from the previously recorded HAR
  await page.routeFromHAR('./test-results/checkout-api.har', {
    url:    /\/api\//,
    update: !!process.env.UPDATE_HAR,  // set to re-record when API changes
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `content: 'embed'` produces self-contained HAR files suitable for offline replay but can be large (10–100 MB for API-heavy pages). Use `content: 'omit'` when you only need request/response metadata (headers, status codes) without bodies. `await using` requires TypeScript 5.2+ and Node 20+ — for older environments use `try/finally` with `tracing.stopHar()`. The `urlFilter` regex in `startHar` uses the same glob engine as `page.route()` — the v1.52 breaking change removed `?` wildcard support; use regex for query-string patterns. [official]

---

### Pattern 178: `consoleMessage.timestamp()` — Time-Window Console Log Assertions (v1.59+) [official]

`consoleMessage.timestamp()` returns the Unix millisecond timestamp when each message was emitted. Use it to perform time-window filtering on `page.consoleMessages()` without clearing the ring buffer between interactions — essential in tests that need to attribute console output to a specific user action without disturbing the accumulated history from earlier steps.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('export button produces no console errors', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  // Baseline: record timestamp before the action under test
  const beforeExport = Date.now();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /export csv/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/export complete/i);

  // Filter: only messages emitted after the export click
  const postExportMessages = (await page.consoleMessages())
    .filter(m => m.timestamp() >= beforeExport);

  const errors = postExportMessages.filter(m => m.type() === 'error');
  expect(errors, 'Console errors during export').toHaveLength(0);

  const warnings = postExportMessages.filter(m => m.type() === 'warning');
  // Tolerate at most 1 warning (third-party chart library noisy during export)
  expect(warnings.length, 'Unexpected warnings during export').toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
});

test('rapid navigation does not generate overlapping JS errors', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const navStart = Date.now();
  // Rapidly navigate between three routes
  for (const route of ['/products', '/cart', '/account']) {
    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  }

  const postNavErrors = (await page.pageErrors())
    .filter(e => e.timestamp >= navStart);

  expect(postNavErrors, 'JS errors during rapid navigation').toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `consoleMessage.timestamp()` is available for messages collected via `page.consoleMessages()` (v1.56+ ring buffer) — not for messages captured through `page.on('console', handler)` event listeners, which receive `ConsoleMessage` objects that also expose `.timestamp()`. The ring buffer holds only the last ~100 messages per navigation; for high-frequency logging pages, use `page.on('console', ...)` with a manually managed array. [official]

---

### Pattern 179: `response.httpVersion()` — Protocol Regression Assertions (v1.59+) [official]

`response.httpVersion()` returns the HTTP protocol version string (`'HTTP/1.1'`, `'HTTP/2.0'`, `'HTTP/3.0'`) for any intercepted response. Use it in smoke tests that guard against infrastructure regressions — CDN reconfiguration, load balancer rollbacks, or TLS certificate changes can silently downgrade your APIs from HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1, introducing head-of-line blocking that increases latency without changing functional behavior.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('critical API endpoints use HTTP/2', async ({ page }) => {
  const versionMap = new Map<string, string>();

  // Capture HTTP version for every /api/ response
  page.on('response', response => {
    if (response.url().includes('/api/')) {
      versionMap.set(response.url(), response.httpVersion());
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Assert all API calls used HTTP/2 or HTTP/3
  for (const [url, version] of versionMap) {
    expect(
      version,
      `Expected HTTP/2+ for ${url} but got ${version}`,
    ).toMatch(/^HTTP\/[23]/);
  }
});

test('static asset CDN uses HTTP/3 (QUIC)', async ({ page }) => {
  let cdnVersion: string | null = null;

  page.on('response', response => {
    if (response.url().includes('cdn.example.com')) {
      cdnVersion ??= response.httpVersion();
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Alert if CDN was downgraded from HTTP/3 to HTTP/2 (infra regression)
  expect(cdnVersion, 'CDN should use HTTP/3').toBe('HTTP/3.0');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** HTTP version is negotiated at the TLS/connection level — testing it requires that the test environment uses a real network stack (no `page.routeFromHAR()` or `route.fulfill()` for the target request). Replayed HAR responses always report the version from the HAR metadata, not the live protocol. This assertion is meaningful only in staging/production smoke tests with real backend connections. In local dev (HTTP/1.1 only), wrap with `test.skip(!process.env.CI)` to avoid always-failing assertions. [official]

---

### Pattern 180: `browserContext.clearCookies({ name, domain, path })` — Surgical Cookie Teardown (v1.54+) [official]

`browserContext.clearCookies()` accepts filter criteria (`name`, `domain`, `path`) to remove only matching cookies rather than wiping the entire cookie jar. This enables per-scenario auth teardown without destroying unrelated session state — for example, clearing only the auth token cookie between role-switch scenarios while preserving device fingerprint cookies and CSRF tokens that took multiple navigations to acquire.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('role-switch preserves session fingerprint cookie', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('admin@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/admin/);

  // Log out by clearing only the auth session cookie
  // Preserves: csrf_token, device_id, pref_* cookies
  await context.clearCookies({ name: 'session_token' });

  // Navigate as guest — device fingerprint cookie still present
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('viewer@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.VIEWER_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);

  // Verify the device fingerprint cookie survived the role switch
  const cookies = await context.cookies();
  expect(cookies.some(c => c.name === 'device_id')).toBe(true);
});

test('clear all cookies for a specific domain only', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Clear cookies set by the auth subdomain without touching analytics cookies
  await context.clearCookies({ domain: 'auth.example.com' });

  const remaining = await context.cookies();
  const authCookies = remaining.filter(c => c.domain.includes('auth.example.com'));
  expect(authCookies).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `clearCookies()` filter options are AND-ed — specifying both `name` and `domain` removes only cookies matching both criteria. If you need OR logic (remove cookie A OR all cookies from domain B), make two separate `clearCookies()` calls. The filter `domain` field uses exact domain matching — subdomain wildcards are not supported; to clear `auth.example.com` cookies you must specify `'auth.example.com'` exactly, not `'*.example.com'`. [official]

---

### Pattern 181: `testConfig.captureGitInfo` — Commit Traceability in HTML Reports (v1.51+) [official]

`captureGitInfo: true` embeds the current git commit SHA, branch name, author, commit message, and diff statistics into the HTML report metadata. This creates a direct link between a failing test in the report and the code change that caused it — engineers no longer need to cross-reference CI build numbers with git logs to identify the responsible commit. The property is safe to enable unconditionally; on non-git directories or environments without a git binary, it silently emits an empty object rather than failing the run.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — enable git traceability in all environments
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  captureGitInfo: {
    commit: true,   // SHA, message, author, date
    diff:   true,   // files changed (omit in large monorepos for performance)
  },

  reporter: process.env.CI
    ? [
        ['html', { open: 'never', outputFolder: 'playwright-report' }],
        ['blob'],   // for merge-reports in sharded pipelines
        ['github'], // GitHub Actions annotations
      ]
    : [['html', { open: 'on-failure' }]],
});
```

```bash
# After a CI run, the HTML report "Run Info" panel shows:
# Commit: 3f2a1b4 — fix: correct checkout tax calculation
# Branch: feature/checkout-tax-fix
# Author: Alice Example <alice@example.com>
# Files changed: 3 (+42 / -17)
```

**Tradeoff:** `diff: true` captures the list of changed files — in large monorepos with hundreds of changed files this can add noticeable overhead to report generation. Set `diff: false` for monorepos and rely on the commit SHA alone for cross-referencing with the version control system. `captureGitInfo` reads from the git working directory at test runner startup — it captures the HEAD commit, not in-flight staged changes. [official]

---

### Pattern 182: `page.clock.install()` + `clock.runFor()` — Deterministic Timer Sequence Testing (v1.45+) [official]

The Clock API (`page.clock.install()`) replaces `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, `clearInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, and `performance.now()` with deterministic fakes. `runFor(ms)` advances the fake clock by exactly `ms` milliseconds, firing all timers (including interval ticks) that fall within the range. This is the correct API for testing polling loops, debounce behavior, and session expiry — eliminates real-time waits and `waitForTimeout()` anti-patterns in timer-heavy tests.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session expiry warning appears at 29 minutes', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install clock BEFORE goto to intercept Date from the first script execution
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-15T10:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/app');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

  // Advance to T+29min (just before the 30-min session expiry)
  await page.clock.runFor(29 * 60 * 1000);

  // Warning should appear at the 29-minute mark
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Continue for 1 more minute — session should expire
  await page.clock.runFor(60_000);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
});

test('debounced search fires once after 300ms of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  const requests: string[] = [];
  page.on('request', req => {
    if (req.url().includes('/api/search')) requests.push(req.url());
  });

  await page.clock.install();
  await page.goto('/search');

  const searchInput = page.getByRole('searchbox');

  // Type rapidly — each keystroke resets the debounce timer
  await searchInput.pressSequentially('pla', { delay: 0 });
  await page.clock.runFor(150);  // still within debounce window — no request yet
  expect(requests).toHaveLength(0);

  await searchInput.pressSequentially('ywright', { delay: 0 });
  await page.clock.runFor(300);  // debounce fires after 300ms

  expect(requests).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(requests[0]).toContain('playwright');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Call `page.clock.install()` BEFORE `page.goto()` — the fake clock must be in place before any page scripts execute, otherwise `Date.now()` called during module initialization captures real time. After installing the clock, `page.waitForTimeout()` still waits real wall-clock time (it's a Playwright API, not a browser timer); use `page.clock.runFor()` to advance time instead of any timeout-based waits. Use `pauseAt()` for snapshot-in-time assertions and `runFor()` for interval-sequence assertions — they are not interchangeable. [official]

---

### Pattern 183: Multi-File `globalSetup` Array — Ordered Setup Projects (v1.49+) [official]

Since v1.49, `globalSetup` and `globalTeardown` accept arrays of module paths in addition to a single string. Each module runs in order. Combined with project `dependencies`, this replaces complex single-file global setup scripts with small focused setup modules that are easier to maintain and can be independently skipped. For full fixture access (traces, `page` object), use project `dependencies` instead of `globalSetup` — they run as ordinary test files with access to all Playwright APIs.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — array globalSetup with ordered initialization
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Array: runs in sequence — db-seed must complete before auth-setup
  globalSetup: [
    require.resolve('./tests/global-setup/db-seed.ts'),
    require.resolve('./tests/global-setup/auth-setup.ts'),
    require.resolve('./tests/global-setup/feature-flags.ts'),
  ],

  globalTeardown: [
    require.resolve('./tests/global-setup/cleanup.ts'),
  ],

  // Alternative: project dependencies (preferred — gets full fixture access)
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'db-seed',
      testMatch: /tests\/setup\/db-seed\.ts/,
    },
    {
      name: 'auth-setup',
      testMatch: /tests\/setup\/auth-setup\.ts/,
      dependencies: ['db-seed'],  // waits for db-seed project to complete
    },
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { storageState: 'playwright/.auth/user.json' },
      dependencies: ['auth-setup'],
    },
  ],
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Array `globalSetup` runs modules in order but does NOT run them in parallel — use project dependencies if setup stages are independent and you want parallel execution. `globalSetup` modules cannot use Playwright fixtures or record traces; project `dependencies` tests can. For most new projects, project `dependencies` is the recommended pattern over `globalSetup` entirely. [official]

---

### Pattern 184: `expect.soft()` — Non-Blocking Assertion Accumulation [official]

`expect.soft()` records an assertion failure without stopping test execution. The test continues running all remaining assertions, then fails at the end with a summary of all soft failures. This is the correct pattern for health-check tests that validate multiple independent properties of a page and need a complete diagnostic report rather than failing at the first missing element. Combine with `test.info().errors` to count soft failures in `afterEach` cleanup hooks.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('homepage health check — all sections present', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Soft assertions — all run regardless of individual failures
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('banner')).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('contentinfo')).toBeVisible();  // footer

  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('link', { name: /about/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('link', { name: /pricing/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('link', { name: /contact/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Hard assertion — if CTA is missing the test should stop here
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /get started/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Soft assertion count in afterEach (see pattern 9 for retry-safe cleanup)
  if (test.info().errors.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`${test.info().errors.length} soft assertion(s) failed`);
  }
});

// Pre-configure expect for all assertions in a scope
test('login form accessibility audit', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  const softExpect = expect.configure({ soft: true });

  // Every assertion in this scope is soft
  await softExpect(page.getByLabel('Email')).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'email');
  await softExpect(page.getByLabel('Password')).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'current-password');
  await softExpect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i })).toHaveAttribute('type', 'submit');
  await softExpect(page.locator('form')).toHaveAttribute('novalidate');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Soft assertion failures do not trigger `retries` — if a test uses `retries: 2` and fails with only soft failures, the test IS retried. Use `expect.soft()` only for assertions that represent independent, observable properties (presence of page regions, ARIA attributes); do NOT use for sequential-dependency assertions where a later assertion depends on the earlier one succeeding (use hard assertions for those). [official]

---

### Pattern 185: `page.route()` with `route.fetch()` + Selective Modification — Thin Proxy Pattern [official]

`route.fetch()` performs the original HTTP request and returns the real response, allowing the test to modify specific fields (headers, status, body) while passing everything else through unchanged. This "thin proxy" pattern is ideal for simulating error conditions in specific API fields without fully mocking the response — the rest of the real API response structure remains intact, reducing maintenance when the API schema changes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dashboard degrades gracefully when /api/metrics returns empty data', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/api/metrics', async route => {
    const real = await route.fetch();
    const body = await real.json();

    // Modify only the metrics array — preserve all other response fields
    await route.fulfill({
      response: real,
      json: { ...body, metrics: [], totalCount: 0 },
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByText(/no metrics available/i)).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).not.toBeAttached();
});

test('API 429 retry banner appears after rate-limit response', async ({ page }) => {
  let callCount = 0;

  await page.route('**/api/data', async route => {
    callCount++;
    if (callCount === 1) {
      // First call: return 429 with Retry-After header
      await route.fulfill({
        status:  429,
        headers: { 'retry-after': '2', 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        body:    JSON.stringify({ error: 'Rate limit exceeded' }),
      });
    } else {
      // Subsequent calls: pass through to real server
      await route.continue();
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/data');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /rate limit/i })).toBeVisible();
  // App should retry after delay — wait for real data to load
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `route.fetch()` makes a real HTTP request — tests using it are not fully offline and depend on backend availability. In CI without a running server, use `route.fulfill()` with fully mocked responses instead. When chaining multiple `route.fetch()` + `route.fulfill()` calls for the same URL in a test, ensure the `context.isClosed()` guard is in place to avoid "Target closed" errors on test timeout. [official]

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 37

---

### 154. `page.screencast.start()` called after `page.goto()` misses the initial page load in the recording [community]

**What:** If `page.screencast.start()` is called after `page.goto()`, the recording begins on the already-loaded page — the navigation itself (including any loading spinner, redirect chain, or initial paint) is absent from the video. Teams using screencasts for QA sign-off videos find that the recording starts on a fully-loaded page with no evidence of how the app transitioned to that state.

**WHY:** `page.screencast.start()` begins capturing frames from the browser's current rendering buffer at the moment it is called. Navigation events that completed before the call are not retroactively included. The Chromium CDP `Page.startScreencast` command captures the live compositor output only — it has no access to historical frames.

**Fix:** Call `page.screencast.start()` BEFORE `page.goto()`.

```typescript
// ❌ Misses the page load — recording starts on already-loaded page
await page.goto('/checkout');
await page.screencast.start({ path: 'checkout.webm' });

// ✅ Recording captures the full navigation including page load
await page.screencast.start({ path: 'checkout.webm' });
await page.goto('/checkout');
```

---

### 155. `browser.bind()` endpoint is valid only for the current browser process — `connectOverCDP()` fails after `browser.close()` [community]

**What:** The WebSocket endpoint returned by `browser.bind()` becomes unreachable immediately after `browser.close()` is called. Any external client holding the old endpoint URL receives `ECONNREFUSED`. This is obvious in serial code but becomes a subtle issue in fixtures that close the browser in teardown while an external agent is still mid-inspection.

**WHY:** The WebSocket server that exposes the `browser.bind()` endpoint runs inside the browser process. When the process exits, the OS closes all its sockets. There is no graceful reconnection mechanism — clients must re-acquire the endpoint from a new `browser.bind()` call on the restarted process.

**Fix:** Coordinate browser lifecycle with any external agent before calling `browser.close()`. In fixtures, call `browser.unbind(name)` first (which signals clients to disconnect), wait for client confirmation if applicable, then close.

```typescript
// ✅ Unbind before close — gives agents a chance to disconnect cleanly
await browser.unbind(sessionName);
// Optional: wait for agent acknowledgment via a shared signal (file, env var, socket)
await browser.close();
```

---

### 156. `page.clock.install()` after `page.goto()` does not retroactively fix `Date` calls in already-executed module code [community]

**What:** If your application stores `Date.now()` in a module-level variable during import (e.g., `const startTime = Date.now()` at the top of a module), calling `page.clock.install()` after `page.goto()` does not affect that value — the module already ran with real time and `startTime` captured the real timestamp.

**WHY:** `page.clock.install()` replaces `window.Date` and browser timer globals **at the moment it is called**. JavaScript module code that ran during `page.goto()` before the install already captured real `Date` references. The fake clock applies only to code that executes after the install call.

**Fix:** Call `page.clock.install()` before `page.goto()` to intercept all `Date` usage from the first script execution.

```typescript
// ❌ Module-level Date.now() already ran — fake clock has no effect on it
await page.goto('/app');
await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') });

// ✅ Install before goto — all page scripts see the fake clock from the start
await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') });
await page.goto('/app');
```

---

### 157. `locator.normalize()` returns the same locator unchanged when the element has no ARIA role and no `data-testid` [community]

**What:** `locator.normalize()` has no viable upgrade path for elements that are semantically anonymous — `<div>`, `<span>`, `<td>` without roles, ARIA labels, or `data-testid` attributes. In these cases `normalize()` returns a locator equivalent to the original (often CSS-based) rather than upgrading it. Teams running `normalize()` as a batch locator migration tool are surprised when 30–40% of their locators are unchanged.

**WHY:** `normalize()` upgrades to `getByRole()`, `getByLabel()`, `getByTestId()`, or `getByText()` by inspecting the live DOM. If none of those strategies produce a unique, unambiguous locator, it falls back to returning the original form. The method cannot invent ARIA attributes or test IDs that don't exist.

**Fix:** Treat unchanged `normalize()` output as a signal to improve the element's markup — add `data-testid`, `aria-label`, or a semantic HTML role. Use `normalize()` as a markup quality audit tool, not a magic locator fixer.

```typescript
// Audit helper: identify elements that normalize() cannot improve
async function findUnnormalizableLocators(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  selectors: string[]
): Promise<string[]> {
  const unchanged: string[] = [];
  for (const selector of selectors) {
    const original   = page.locator(selector);
    const normalized = original.normalize();
    if (original.toString() === normalized.toString()) {
      unchanged.push(selector);
    }
  }
  return unchanged;
}
```

---

### 158. `init-agents` definitions become stale after Playwright upgrades — agents silently use outdated tools [community]

**What:** After upgrading `@playwright/test`, running `npx playwright init-agents` regenerates agent definitions for the new version's tooling. Teams that skip this step continue using agent definitions from the previous version — the agents still execute but lack access to new tools, producing suboptimal selectors, missing new assertion APIs, and occasionally generating tests incompatible with the upgraded version.

**WHY:** Agent definitions are `.md` or config files that describe the tools (capabilities) available to each agent. Playwright adds new tools with each version (e.g., `locator.normalize()` in v1.59, `test.abort()` in v1.60). The agent definitions must be regenerated to include these new tool descriptions.

**Fix:** Make `init-agents` part of the Playwright upgrade checklist. Add a CI lint step that compares the Playwright version in `package.json` against the version embedded in the agent definition files.

```bash
# After every Playwright version bump:
npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude   # or --loop=vscode / --loop=opencode

# Verify definitions were updated by checking the version comment in the generated file
head -3 .github/playwright-agents.md
# Should show the current Playwright version
```
