### Pattern 186: `locator.filter({ hasNot, hasNotText })` — Exclusion-Based Row Narrowing [official]

`locator.filter()` accepts `hasNot` (a locator) and `hasNotText` (a string or regex) to exclude matching elements from a set. This complements the existing `has` / `hasText` options, enabling precise row selection in tables or lists without overly complex CSS selectors. The filters compose: you can chain `.filter({ hasText: 'Active' }).filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }) })` to narrow from both directions simultaneously. This removes the need to enumerate indices when only positional reasoning is otherwise available.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('archive all non-locked rows in the user table', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/admin/users');

  // Select every row that does NOT contain a "Lock" badge
  const unlockableRows = page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasNot: page.getByTestId('lock-badge') });

  const count = await unlockableRows.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Archive each row sequentially (DOM mutates after each click)
  for (const row of await unlockableRows.all()) {
    await row.getByRole('button', { name: 'Archive' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('dialog').getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm' }).click();
  }

  // Verify the table now contains only locked rows
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasNot: page.getByTestId('lock-badge') })
  ).toHaveCount(0);
});

test('skip rows with "Archived" text when collecting emails', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/crm/contacts');

  const activeRows = page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasNotText: /archived/i });

  const emails = await activeRows.getByRole('cell', { name: /@/ }).allInnerTexts();
  expect(emails.every(e => e.includes('@'))).toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** When the DOM mutates after each action (rows are removed), calling `.all()` once captures a snapshot — locators in that snapshot may become stale. Re-query the filter after each mutation or use a `while (await locator.count() > 0)` loop for mutation-safe iteration. [official]

---

### Pattern 187: `getByRole()` with `description` Option — Disambiguating Identical Role Names (v1.60+) [official]

When a page contains multiple elements with the same accessible role and name (e.g., two "Edit" buttons), `getByRole()` with the `description` option uses the element's `aria-describedby` or `title` attribute to pick the correct target. This avoids brittle `.nth(0)` index selectors that break when render order changes. The `description` option was added in v1.60 and maps directly to the ARIA accessible description — matching by the text of the referenced element, not its ID.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('edit the correct row when multiple Edit buttons share the same name', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/invoices');

  // Each "Edit" button has aria-describedby pointing to the invoice ID cell
  // <button aria-describedby="invoice-42">Edit</button>
  // <button aria-describedby="invoice-99">Edit</button>

  // ✅ Disambiguate by description — survives render-order changes
  await page.getByRole('button', {
    name:        'Edit',
    description: 'Invoice #42',
  }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toContainText('Invoice #42');
  await page.getByLabel('Amount').fill('500.00');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();

  // Confirm the correct row was updated
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasText: 'Invoice #42' })
  ).toContainText('500.00');
});

test('submit button described by a help tooltip is unambiguous', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  await page.getByRole('button', {
    name:        'Submit',
    description: 'Place your order and charge the card on file',
  }).click();

  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/order-confirmation/);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `description` matching requires the markup to use `aria-describedby` or a `title` attribute pointing to the descriptive text. If the app uses custom tooltip libraries that render tooltips outside the DOM element (e.g., absolutely positioned `<div>` without ARIA wiring), this option will not match. Audit the ARIA tree via `page.accessibility.snapshot()` to verify accessible descriptions are present before relying on this option. [official]

---

### Pattern 188: `tracing.group()` / `tracing.groupEnd()` — Logical Trace Sections for Multi-Step Workflows [official]

`context.tracing.group(name)` and `context.tracing.groupEnd()` wrap a block of trace events under a named section in the Trace Viewer timeline. This makes complex test flows readable at a glance — instead of scrolling through 50 raw network and DOM events, reviewers see collapsible headers such as "Login", "Add to Cart", and "Checkout". Groups nest arbitrarily and compose with `test.step()`: use `test.step` for assertion checkpoints and `tracing.group` for low-level implementation grouping.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('full purchase flow produces confirmation', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });

  // --- Group 1: Authentication ---
  context.tracing.group('Login');
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('buyer@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('s3cr3t');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);
  context.tracing.groupEnd();

  // --- Group 2: Shopping ---
  context.tracing.group('Add item to cart');
  await page.goto('/products/widget-pro');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to Cart' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText('1 item');
  context.tracing.groupEnd();

  // --- Group 3: Checkout ---
  context.tracing.group('Checkout');
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to Checkout' }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Card Number').fill('4242424242424242');
  await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel('CVC').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/order\/\d+\/confirmation/);
  context.tracing.groupEnd();

  await context.tracing.stop({ path: 'purchase-trace.zip' });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `tracing.group()` is synchronous — it emits a marker immediately without waiting for async operations inside the block. If an error is thrown inside the group, `groupEnd()` is never called, leaving an unclosed group in the trace. Wrap groups in try/finally to guarantee `groupEnd()` fires even on test failure. [official]

---

### Pattern 189: Worker-Scoped Fixtures for Expensive One-Time Setup — Shared DB Seed Pattern [official]

Worker-scoped fixtures run setup once per Playwright worker process rather than once per test. This is the right level for database seeding, auth-token acquisition, or schema migrations that are expensive but safe to share across tests in the same worker. The fixture receives `workerInfo.workerIndex` to create per-worker namespaced resources (e.g., `testdb_worker_0`, `testdb_worker_1`) so parallel workers do not collide.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/db.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

interface WorkerDB {
  baseUrl:   string;
  schemaName: string;
  teardown:  () => Promise<void>;
}

export const test = base.extend<{}, { workerDb: WorkerDB }>({
  workerDb: [
    async ({ browser }, use, workerInfo) => {
      const schema = `testdb_w${workerInfo.workerIndex}`;

      // Seed once for this worker — all tests in the worker share this schema
      await runMigrations(schema);
      await seedFixtureData(schema);

      const page = await browser.newPage();
      await page.goto(`/api/admin/activate-schema?name=${schema}`);
      await page.close();

      await use({
        baseUrl:    `http://localhost:3000?schema=${schema}`,
        schemaName: schema,
        teardown:   () => dropSchema(schema),
      });

      // Teardown runs once after ALL tests in this worker finish
      await dropSchema(schema);
    },
    { scope: 'worker', timeout: 60_000 },
  ],
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';

// e2e/specs/products.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/db';

test('product catalog loads seed data', async ({ page, workerDb }) => {
  await page.goto(workerDb.baseUrl + '/products');
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(10);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Worker-scoped fixtures cannot depend on test-scoped fixtures (like `page`) — they receive `browser` instead. Tests sharing a worker-scoped database must not mutate shared state; any test that inserts or deletes rows must clean up in its own teardown or use per-test transaction rollbacks. If a worker crashes, its teardown may not run — add cleanup in `globalTeardown` as a safety net. [official]

---

### Pattern 190: `auto: true` Fixture — Zero-Boilerplate Cross-Cutting Concerns [official]

Auto-fixtures execute for every test in a suite without the test explicitly requesting them. This pattern is ideal for cross-cutting concerns: log capture on failure, performance budget enforcement, accessibility audits, or request-count assertions. Auto-fixtures compose cleanly with the `testInfo.status` check to run cleanup only on failure, avoiding noise in passing runs.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auto-audit.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

export const test = base.extend<{
  autoA11yAudit:       void;
  captureConsoleErrors: void;
}>({
  // Attach accessibility violations to every failed test automatically
  autoA11yAudit: [
    async ({ page }, use, testInfo) => {
      await use();                         // test body runs here

      if (testInfo.status !== 'passed') {
        const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
          .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
          .analyze();

        if (results.violations.length > 0) {
          await testInfo.attach('a11y-violations', {
            body:        JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
            contentType: 'application/json',
          });
        }
      }
    },
    { auto: true },
  ],

  // Fail any test that produces console errors — no per-test assertions needed
  captureConsoleErrors: [
    async ({ page }, use, testInfo) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on('console', msg => {
        if (msg.type() === 'error') errors.push(msg.text());
      });

      await use();

      if (errors.length > 0) {
        await testInfo.attach('console-errors', {
          body:        errors.join('\n'),
          contentType: 'text/plain',
        });
        if (testInfo.status === 'passed') {
          throw new Error(`Console errors detected:\n${errors.join('\n')}`);
        }
      }
    },
    { auto: true },
  ],
});

export { expect };
```

**Tradeoff:** Auto-fixtures add execution overhead to every test, including ones that don't need the audit. For large suites, scope the fixture to a specific describe file (create a separate `test` export used only in audit-critical specs) rather than registering it globally. Auto-fixtures that trigger network calls (like `AxeBuilder.analyze()`) must guard against `context.isClosed()` to avoid errors during forced teardown on timeout. [official]

---

### Pattern 191: `locator.and()` — Intersection Locators for Multi-Attribute Matching [official]

`locator.and(other)` returns a new locator matching elements that satisfy BOTH the original locator and the `other` locator simultaneously. This is the "AND" counterpart to `locator.or()`. It composes cleanly with role, test-ID, label, and text locators for complex element targeting without resorting to CSS attribute chains. The key use case is finding an element that must match two independent semantic constraints, such as a button that has a specific accessible name AND is also inside a specific landmark region.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('submit inside checkout form, not newsletter form', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Two forms on the page both have a "Submit" button
  // Intersect: button named "Submit" AND inside the checkout form landmark
  const checkoutSubmit = page
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })
    .and(
      page.getByRole('form', { name: 'Checkout' }).getByRole('button')
    );

  await expect(checkoutSubmit).toBeVisible();
  await checkoutSubmit.click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/order-confirmation/);
});

test('locate highlighted revenue cells in table', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/quarterly');

  // Cells in the "Revenue" column AND marked as highlighted
  const highlightedRevenue = page
    .locator('[data-col="revenue"]')
    .and(page.locator('[data-highlight="true"]'));

  const count = await highlightedRevenue.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  const values = await highlightedRevenue.allInnerTexts();
  expect(values.every(v => parseFloat(v.replace(/[$,]/g, '')) > 0)).toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `locator.and()` evaluates both locator expressions on every retry — if either resolves to zero elements, the intersection is empty. When combining locators from different DOM subtrees, ensure the intersection is logically possible; `locator.and()` does not warn when the intersection is structurally impossible (e.g., combining a table cell locator with a button locator will always be empty). [official]

---

### Pattern 192: `page.addLocatorHandler()` with `times` Option — Bounded Overlay Dismissal [official]

`page.addLocatorHandler(locator, handler, { times })` registers a handler that fires up to `times` occurrences when the locator becomes visible during an action's auto-wait loop. Without `times`, the handler fires indefinitely. Use `times: 1` for one-shot overlays like cookie consent banners that appear only on first visit; use `times: N` for retry dialogs that may appear multiple times during a long test flow. The handler is removed automatically after `times` invocations, preventing ghost interceptions in later tests that share the same browser context.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cookie banner dismissed once — not intercepted on later clicks', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register handler BEFORE goto — fires at most once
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /accept|ok/i }).click();
    },
    { times: 1 }
  );

  await page.goto('/');

  // These clicks proceed normally after the one-time dismissal
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Products' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/products/);

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to Cart' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText('1 item');
});

test('conflict dialog dismissed up to 3 times during batch migration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: /conflict detected/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }).click();
    },
    { times: 3, noWaitAfter: false }
  );

  await page.goto('/bulk-operations');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Run Migration' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: 'Migration complete' })).toBeVisible({
    timeout: 30_000,
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Handlers registered with `times: 1` are not removed until after the first invocation — they do still fire during the test if the element appears. If the overlay never appears (e.g., dismissed via storage state), the unused handler quietly expires without error. Handlers run inside the auto-wait retry loop, so expensive async operations inside the handler can push the outer action past its timeout — keep handlers fast and focused. [official]

---

### Pattern 193: `context.tracing.startHar()` + `routeFromHAR()` — Record-Then-Replay Offline Test Strategy (v1.60+) [official]

`tracing.startHar()` records all network traffic for a context into a HAR file during a live run. That file can then be replayed offline via `page.routeFromHAR()` or `context.routeFromHAR()`, turning flaky integration tests into deterministic unit-style tests. The `urlFilter` option limits recording to only the endpoints you care about, keeping HAR files small. Combined with `{ update: 'changed' }` snapshot mode, teams can refresh HAR fixtures only when the API contract changes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

const HAR_FILE = path.join(__dirname, '../fixtures/api-responses.har');

// ─── Record mode: run once to generate the HAR fixture ───────────────────────
test.skip(process.env.RECORD_HAR !== 'true', 'Set RECORD_HAR=true to regenerate');

test('record HAR fixture for dashboard API', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await using _har = await context.tracing.startHar(HAR_FILE, {
    mode:      'minimal',
    content:   'attach',
    urlFilter: /\/api\/(metrics|users|reports)/,
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
  // tracing.stopHar() called automatically via `await using`
});

// ─── Replay mode: deterministic offline tests using saved HAR ─────────────────
test('dashboard loads correctly in offline mode', async ({ page }) => {
  // Route all matching requests through the HAR file — no real network needed
  await page.routeFromHAR(HAR_FILE, {
    url:      /\/api\//,
    update:   false,       // strict replay — fail if request not in HAR
    notFound: 'abort',     // abort unmatched requests rather than passing through
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Overview' })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText(/total revenue/i)).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** HAR files capture one point-in-time server response. If the backend returns dynamic data (timestamps, IDs, CSRF tokens), replay may break unless the frontend is resilient to stale tokens or the test masks dynamic fields. Use `mode: 'minimal'` to omit response bodies for requests you only need status codes from, reducing file size. A single HAR file covers one test scenario — do not share HAR fixtures between tests with different API call sequences. [official]

---

### Pattern 194: `box: true` Fixture — Collapsing Infrastructure Noise in Reports [official]

Fixtures declared with `{ box: true }` appear as a single collapsed step in the HTML reporter and Trace Viewer rather than exposing every internal action. This is the fixture-level counterpart to `test.step({ box: true })`. Use it for infrastructure helpers — database seeders, auth token refreshers, test-data factories — where showing internal implementation steps would obscure the test narrative. Boxed fixtures still run normally; only their reporting is compressed.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts
import { test as base, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';

export type AuthFixtures = {
  authenticatedContext: BrowserContext;
  adminContext:         BrowserContext;
};

export const test = base.extend<AuthFixtures>({
  authenticatedContext: [
    async ({ browser }, use) => {
      // All steps inside are hidden in reports when box: true
      const context = await browser.newContext();
      const page    = await context.newPage();
      await page.goto('/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_EMAIL!);
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD!);
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In' }).click();
      await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);
      await page.close();
      await use(context);
      await context.close();
    },
    { scope: 'test', box: true },
  ],

  adminContext: [
    async ({ browser }, use) => {
      const context = await browser.newContext();
      const page    = await context.newPage();
      await page.goto('/admin/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Admin Key').fill(process.env.ADMIN_KEY!);
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Enter Admin' }).click();
      await page.waitForURL(/admin\/dashboard/);
      await page.close();
      await use(context);
      await context.close();
    },
    { scope: 'test', box: true },
  ],
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';
```

**Tradeoff:** Boxed fixtures hide all internal steps from the HTML report and Trace Viewer, which makes debugging fixture failures harder. When a boxed fixture fails, the error message surfaces normally, but the step context is collapsed — add descriptive `console.error` output inside boxed fixtures so failures are traceable without unboxing them. [official]

---

### Pattern 195: `testProject.workers` — Project-Level Worker Parallelism Caps (v1.52+) [official]

`testProject.workers` overrides the global `workers` setting for a specific project. This allows critical slow projects (e.g., Safari/WebKit, mobile emulation) to be serialized (`workers: 1`) while fast projects (Chromium desktop) run with maximum parallelism. It also prevents I/O-intensive projects (e.g., screenshot comparison with heavy disk writes) from competing with lightweight API-only projects for the same worker pool.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  workers: process.env.CI ? 4 : '50%',   // global default

  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use:  { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      // Inherits global workers: 4 on CI
    },
    {
      name:    'webkit',
      use:     { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] },
      workers: 1,   // Safari flakes under parallelism — serialize it
    },
    {
      name:    'mobile-chrome',
      use:     { ...devices['Pixel 7'] },
      workers: 2,   // Limit mobile emulation — GPU emulation is expensive
    },
    {
      name:    'api-smoke',
      use:     {},   // No browser — pure API tests
      workers: 8,    // Cheap — max parallelism for fast feedback
    },
    {
      name:    'visual-regression',
      use:     { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      workers: 1,   // Screenshot diff writes must be serial to avoid FS conflicts
      testMatch: '**/*.visual.spec.ts',
    },
  ],
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `testProject.workers` controls concurrency per project but Playwright still schedules all projects together in the global runner pool. Setting one project to `workers: 1` does not prevent other projects from running in parallel alongside it. For true resource isolation (e.g., preventing any other test from running while a DB migration setup project runs), use project `dependencies` with setup projects instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 196: `expect(locator).toContainClass()` — Precise CSS State Assertions (v1.52+) [official]

`toContainClass(className)` asserts that a locator's element has the specified CSS class in its `classList` without requiring an exact full-class-string match. This replaces fragile `.toHaveClass(/regex/)` patterns for asserting presence of a single state class alongside dynamically generated class names (e.g., CSS Modules hashes, utility-first class stacks). Pass an array to assert multiple classes simultaneously — all must be present.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('active nav item has the active class after navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Products' }).click();

  // Doesn't matter what other classes Tailwind or CSS Modules add
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Products' })
  ).toContainClass('active');
});

test('submit button is disabled AND loading during submission', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Message').fill('Hello');

  // Keep loading state alive during assertion
  await page.route('**/api/contact', route =>
    new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => route.continue().then(r), 2000))
  );

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send Message' }).click();

  // Assert two state classes simultaneously
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send Message' })
  ).toContainClass(['disabled', 'loading']);
});

test('error inputs have validation class after empty submit', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/signup');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Register' }).click();

  await expect(page.getByLabel('Username')).toContainClass('field-error');
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Email')).toContainClass(['field-error', 'required']);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `toContainClass()` performs substring matching on class tokens — it will match `active` inside both `active` and `inactive` if the latter is used as a single class token. Use semantically unambiguous class names. For an array argument, the assertion requires ALL classes — it is not an OR check. [official]

---

### Pattern 197: `page.requestGC()` — Memory Leak Detection in Long-Running SPA Tests [official]

`page.requestGC()` triggers a browser garbage collection cycle and returns when it completes. This allows tests to measure heap size before and after an operation using `page.evaluate(() => performance.memory?.usedJSHeapSize)`, catching memory leaks in SPAs where components fail to unmount cleanly or event listeners are never removed. The pattern is most useful in endurance tests that simulate a user session of N page-navigations and assert that heap size does not grow unboundedly.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('navigating between 20 routes does not leak memory', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Warm up — let the app reach steady state
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Dashboard' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Reports' }).click();
  }

  await page.requestGC();
  const baselineHeap: number = await page.evaluate(
    () => (performance as any).memory?.usedJSHeapSize ?? 0
  );

  // Perform 20 navigation cycles
  for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Dashboard' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Reports' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
  }

  await page.requestGC();
  const finalHeap: number = await page.evaluate(
    () => (performance as any).memory?.usedJSHeapSize ?? 0
  );

  // Allow up to 20% heap growth; more indicates a leak
  const growthRatio = finalHeap / baselineHeap;
  expect(
    growthRatio,
    `Heap grew by ${((growthRatio - 1) * 100).toFixed(1)}% — possible memory leak`
  ).toBeLessThan(1.2);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `performance.memory` is a Chromium-only, non-standard API — this pattern does not work on Firefox or WebKit. `requestGC()` itself is supported cross-browser but the heap measurement is Chromium-specific. Memory measurements in headless mode may differ from headed mode due to GPU process differences. Use this as a smoke test for obvious leaks, not as a precise memory profiling tool. [official]

---

### Pattern 198: Component Test `hooksConfig` — Per-Test Provider Injection Without Remounting [official]

The `hooksConfig` object passed to `mount()` is forwarded to `beforeMount`/`afterMount` lifecycle hooks defined in `playwright/index.tsx`. This lets individual tests control which providers (Router, Theme, i18n, Redux Store) wrap the component — without changing mount call signatures or creating multiple fixture variants. The pattern replaces wrapper variations with a single mount call plus a config flag, keeping test files lean.

```typescript
// playwright/index.tsx  (component test entry point)
import { beforeMount } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react/hooks';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { ThemeProvider }  from './theme';
import { createTestStore } from '../test-utils/store';
import { Provider }        from 'react-redux';

export type HooksConfig = {
  withRouter?:   boolean;
  theme?:        'light' | 'dark';
  storePreload?: Record<string, unknown>;
};

beforeMount<HooksConfig>(async ({ App, hooksConfig }) => {
  const { withRouter = false, theme = 'light', storePreload = {} } = hooksConfig ?? {};
  const store = createTestStore(storePreload);

  const Wrapper = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
    <Provider store={store}>
      <ThemeProvider theme={theme}>
        {withRouter ? <BrowserRouter>{children}</BrowserRouter> : children}
      </ThemeProvider>
    </Provider>
  );
  return <Wrapper><App /></Wrapper>;
});

// ─── Component spec ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react';
import { UserProfile }   from './UserProfile';

test('renders user avatar in dark theme', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount<HooksConfig>(<UserProfile userId="42" />, {
    hooksConfig: { theme: 'dark', storePreload: { auth: { userId: '42' } } },
  });
  await expect(component.getByAltText(/avatar/i)).toBeVisible();
  await expect(component).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(18, 18, 18)');
});

test('navigation link works with router', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount<HooksConfig>(<UserProfile userId="42" />, {
    hooksConfig: { withRouter: true },
  });
  await component.getByRole('link', { name: 'Edit Profile' }).click();
  await expect(component).toContainText('/profile/42/edit');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `hooksConfig` values must be JSON-serializable — they are passed from the Node.js test process to the browser via a structured-clone boundary. Do not pass functions, class instances, or Symbols. If you need to inject a mock function (e.g., `onNavigate: jest.fn()`), use the component's callback props instead of `hooksConfig`. [official]

---

### Pattern 199: `mergeTests()` + `mergeExpects()` — Composing Multi-Module Fixture Sets [official]

`mergeTests()` combines `test` objects from multiple fixture modules into a single exported `test` that exposes all their fixtures without naming conflicts. `mergeExpects()` does the same for custom `expect` matchers. This pattern enables "fixture composition" — a database fixture module, an auth fixture module, and a UI helper module are developed independently and merged at the spec level, following the Single Responsibility Principle for fixture design.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/db.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ dbClient: DBClient }>({
  dbClient: async ({}, use) => {
    const client = await createTestDbClient();
    await use(client);
    await client.close();
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/auth.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
export const test = base.extend<{ authToken: string }>({
  authToken: async ({ request }, use) => {
    const res = await request.post('/api/auth/token', {
      data: { client_id: process.env.TEST_CLIENT_ID },
    });
    await use((await res.json()).token);
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/ui.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { DashboardPage } from '../pages/DashboardPage';
export const test = base.extend<{ dashboardPage: DashboardPage }>({
  dashboardPage: async ({ page }, use) => use(new DashboardPage(page)),
});

// e2e/fixtures/index.ts — merge all three
import { mergeTests } from '@playwright/test';
import { test as dbTest }   from './db';
import { test as authTest } from './auth';
import { test as uiTest }   from './ui';

export const test = mergeTests(dbTest, authTest, uiTest);
export { expect } from '@playwright/test';

// e2e/specs/reports.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures';

test('report reflects live DB data', async ({ dbClient, authToken, dashboardPage, page }) => {
  await dbClient.seed('reports', [{ id: 1, value: 9999 }]);
  await page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({ Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}` });
  await dashboardPage.goto();
  await expect(dashboardPage.revenueCell).toContainText('9999');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `mergeTests()` requires all fixture names across modules to be unique — a collision causes a runtime error at test startup (not at type-check time). Use TypeScript intersection types on the fixture interface to catch naming conflicts at compile time. When merging more than three modules, document the merged fixture set in a comment block to prevent contributors from introducing collisions. [official]

---

### Pattern 200: `page.clock.setSystemTime()` vs `page.clock.setFixedTime()` — Choosing the Right Time-Freeze Primitive [official]

`page.clock.setFixedTime(time)` freezes `Date.now()` and `new Date()` to a specific instant without installing the full fake clock — `setTimeout` and `setInterval` continue to fire on real time. `page.clock.setSystemTime(time)` (available after `page.clock.install()`) updates the clock's current time while preserving all pending timers, which will fire at their correct offsets relative to the new system time. Use `setFixedTime` for read-only date rendering assertions; use `setSystemTime` when advancing time while timers must continue running.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ─── setFixedTime: freeze Date without touching timers ───────────────────────
test('invoice footer shows correct fiscal year in December', async ({ page }) => {
  // Only Date.now() is affected — timers, setInterval, animations still run
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2025-12-31T23:59:59Z'));
  await page.goto('/invoices/new');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('fiscal-year')).toHaveText('FY 2025');
});

// ─── setSystemTime: advance time while timers fire normally ──────────────────
test('session expiry warning appears 5 minutes before token expires', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T09:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/app');

  // Jump to 09:54 — warning should NOT appear yet
  await page.clock.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-01-01T09:54:00Z'));
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).not.toBeVisible();

  // Jump to 09:55 and tick 1 second to trigger the setInterval check
  await page.clock.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-01-01T09:55:00Z'));
  await page.clock.runFor(1_000);

  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText(/5 minutes/i)).toBeVisible();
});

// ─── Decision table ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// | Goal                                  | API                         |
// |---------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
// | Freeze Date.now() for rendering tests | setFixedTime()              |
// | Advance clock while timers run        | install() + setSystemTime() |
// | Skip past waiting periods instantly   | install() + fastForward()   |
// | Tick forward in precise steps         | install() + runFor()        |
```

**Tradeoff:** `setFixedTime` is lightweight — no fake clock installation, no timer interception overhead. But it cannot advance time; every `new Date()` returns the same frozen instant for the lifetime of the test. `setSystemTime` requires `page.clock.install()` first, which replaces all timer globals (`setTimeout`, `Date`, `performance.now`). After `install()`, real-time timers no longer fire unless you explicitly call `runFor()` or `tick()`. [official]

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 38

### 159. `locator.all()` captures a DOM snapshot — it does NOT lazily re-query after mutations [community]

**What:** `await locator.all()` resolves the locator immediately and returns an array of frozen `Locator` instances pointing to the elements matched at call time. If the DOM mutates after the call (rows added, removed, reordered), iterating the returned array operates on stale references. Teams that iterate `await locator.all()` inside a `for...of` loop and perform mutating actions (delete, archive, reorder) within the loop find that later iterations throw "strict mode violation" or "element detached" errors because the element count or identities changed.

**WHY:** `locator.all()` is equivalent to calling `locator.nth(0)`, `locator.nth(1)`, ... up to the count at resolution time. Each returned `Locator` is bound to its positional index at that moment. After a DOM mutation, `nth(3)` may now point to a completely different element, or the element at that index may no longer exist.

**Fix:** For mutation-safe iteration, use a `while (await locator.count() > 0)` loop re-querying the first element each iteration — or collect all stable identifiers (text, test IDs) with `allInnerTexts()` or `allTextContents()` first, then act on each by identity rather than index.

```typescript
// ❌ Stale — DOM changes after each .click() but array is fixed at call time
for (const row of await page.getByRole('row').all()) {
  await row.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }).click();
}

// ✅ Safe — always re-queries the first remaining deletable row
while (await page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasText: /pending/i }).count() > 0) {
  await page.getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasText: /pending/i })
    .first()
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' })
    .click();
}
```

---

### 160. `page.addLocatorHandler()` does NOT fire during `page.waitForURL()` or `page.waitForLoadState()` wait loops [community]

**What:** `addLocatorHandler` fires during the auto-wait retry loop of action methods (`click`, `fill`, `check`, `hover`). It does NOT intercept overlays that appear while `page.waitForURL()`, `page.waitForLoadState()`, or `page.waitForSelector()` are waiting. If a cookie banner appears during a navigation wait, the locator handler will not dismiss it — the banner persists until the next action method begins.

**WHY:** `addLocatorHandler` is integrated into Playwright's actionability check loop, which only runs during performable action methods. Pure wait methods (`waitForURL`, `waitForLoadState`) do not cycle through the actionability check, so the handler is never evaluated during those waits.

**Fix:** Dismiss overlays that appear during navigation by hooking into `page.on('load')` or by adding an explicit dismiss step immediately after `goto()`. Alternatively, prevent the overlay entirely by injecting the dismissed state into storage before navigation via `addInitScript`.

```typescript
// ❌ Handler won't fire during waitForURL — banner may remain visible
await page.addLocatorHandler(banner, async () => banner.getByRole('button').click());
await page.goto('/checkout');  // banner may appear here and NOT be dismissed

// ✅ Pre-dismiss via storage injection — banner never appears at all
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  localStorage.setItem('cookie-consent', 'accepted');
});
await page.goto('/checkout');
```

---

### 161. `tracing.group()` left unclosed on test failure corrupts the Trace Viewer timeline [community]

**What:** If a test throws before `context.tracing.groupEnd()` is reached, the trace file is saved with an unclosed group. The Trace Viewer renders this as a group that spans to the end of the trace, visually obscuring all subsequent events as if they belong to the unclosed group. The events are present in the underlying ZIP, but the timeline display is misleading enough that triage teams frequently misidentify which step failed.

**WHY:** `tracing.group()` emits a "group start" marker to the trace buffer synchronously. `tracing.groupEnd()` emits the matching "group end" marker. If `groupEnd()` is never emitted, the Trace Viewer renderer has no boundary and extends the group to EOF.

**Fix:** Always wrap `tracing.group()` / `tracing.groupEnd()` pairs in a try/finally block, or extract them into a helper that guarantees `groupEnd()` fires even on failure.

```typescript
async function traceGroup(
  tracing: import('@playwright/test').Tracing,
  name: string,
  fn: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  tracing.group(name);
  try {
    await fn();
  } finally {
    tracing.groupEnd();
  }
}

// Usage
await traceGroup(context.tracing, 'Login', async () => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In' }).click();
});
```

---

### 162. `routeFromHAR()` with `notFound: 'abort'` silently aborts requests not in the HAR — no test error is thrown [community]

**What:** When `page.routeFromHAR(file, { update: false, notFound: 'abort' })` is used, any request whose URL does not match an entry in the HAR is network-aborted with `net::ERR_FAILED`. Tests see cryptic console errors and UI degradation that looks like backend failures but is actually a HAR coverage gap. Teams forget that a new API call added to the frontend after the HAR was recorded will be silently aborted rather than raising a clear test error.

**WHY:** `notFound: 'abort'` is the strictest mode: unmatched requests are network-aborted without throwing a JavaScript or Playwright test error. There is no built-in warning; you must observe the console error or a resulting UI regression.

**Fix:** During HAR development, use `notFound: 'fallback'` to pass unmatched requests to the real network. Once all requests are captured, switch to `notFound: 'abort'` and add a `page.on('requestfailed')` listener that fails the test explicitly when a request is aborted.

```typescript
// Add before routeFromHAR to catch coverage gaps explicitly
page.on('requestfailed', request => {
  throw new Error(
    `HAR missing entry for: ${request.url()} [${request.failure()?.errorText}]`
  );
});

await page.routeFromHAR(HAR_FILE, { url: /\/api\//, update: false, notFound: 'abort' });
```

---

### 163. `page.clock.install()` + `fastForward()` does NOT advance `performance.now()` in all browser builds [community]

**What:** `page.clock.fastForward(ms)` advances `Date`, `setTimeout`, and `setInterval` by the specified milliseconds. However, on some Chromium builds and all WebKit/Firefox builds, `performance.now()` is NOT advanced by `fastForward()` — it continues returning real elapsed time. Code that computes animation frame deltas or rate-limits using `performance.now()` rather than `Date.now()` will not be controlled by the fake clock, producing inconsistent test results across browsers.

**WHY:** `page.clock.install()` replaces `window.Date`, `window.setTimeout`, `window.setInterval`, `window.clearTimeout`, and `window.clearInterval`. `performance.now()` is part of the `Performance` interface, not the `Window` timer interface, and is not universally intercepted by Playwright's clock implementation across all browser engine versions.

**Fix:** For code that depends on `performance.now()`, either: (1) inject a `performance.now` stub via `page.addInitScript` before navigation, or (2) refactor the application code to use `Date.now()` for testability. Document this limitation in your clock fixture.

```typescript
// Polyfill performance.now() to track fake clock advances via a custom event
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  const _realNow = performance.now.bind(performance);
  let _offset = 0;
  window.addEventListener('__fakeClockAdvance', (e: any) => {
    _offset += e.detail.ms;
  });
  performance.now = () => _realNow() + _offset;
});
```

### Pattern 201: `TestStepInfo.skip()` + `TestStepInfo.attach()` — Conditional Steps with Inline Evidence (v1.55+) [official]

`test.step()` now passes a `TestStepInfo` object as its callback argument in Playwright v1.55+. This object exposes `.skip(condition, reason)` to conditionally skip the step body and `.attach(name, options)` to pin evidence directly to the step in the HTML report — without navigating up to the test-level `testInfo.attach()`. This keeps the attachment co-located with the step that produced it, making Trace Viewer navigation far more readable.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('responsive checkout flow', async ({ page, isMobile }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  await test.step('fill billing address', async (step) => {
    // Skip the desktop-only address autocomplete step on mobile viewports
    step.skip(isMobile, 'Address autocomplete is desktop-only');
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Address lookup' }).fill('123 Main');
    await page.getByRole('option').first().click();
  });

  await test.step('verify cart total', async (step) => {
    await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-total')).toBeVisible();

    // Attach a screenshot directly to this step (not to the test root)
    const screenshotBuffer = await page.screenshot({
      clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 400, height: 200 },
    });
    await step.attach('cart-total-screenshot', {
      body: screenshotBuffer,
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });
  });

  await test.step('submit order', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/confirmation/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `step.attach()` creates attachments scoped to the step's timing window. If a step is retried via `test.step`-level error recovery, previous attachments from the failed attempt remain in the report alongside the successful retry — potentially duplicating screenshots. For retried steps, name attachments with a suffix like `attempt-${retryIndex}` to disambiguate.

### Pattern 202: `testStepInfo.titlePath` — Structured Step Path in Custom Reporters (v1.55+) [official]

`TestStepInfo.titlePath` returns the full hierarchy of titles from the test file down through nested steps to the current step. Custom reporters can use this to group failures by feature area without string-parsing the flat title string.

```typescript
// e2e/reporters/step-reporter.ts
import type { Reporter, TestCase, TestResult, TestStep } from '@playwright/test/reporter';

interface StepRecord {
  path:     string[];
  duration: number;
  error:    string | null;
}

class StepPathReporter implements Reporter {
  private stepLog: StepRecord[] = [];

  onStepEnd(test: TestCase, result: TestResult, step: TestStep): void {
    // titlePath gives: ['checkout.spec.ts', 'guest checkout', 'fill billing address']
    const path = (step as any).titlePath as string[];

    if (step.error) {
      this.stepLog.push({
        path,
        duration: step.duration,
        error:    step.error.message ?? 'unknown',
      });
    }
  }

  async onEnd(): Promise<void> {
    // Group failures by feature (first two path segments)
    const byFeature: Record<string, StepRecord[]> = {};
    for (const record of this.stepLog) {
      const key = record.path.slice(0, 2).join(' > ');
      (byFeature[key] ??= []).push(record);
    }
    console.log('Step failures by feature:', JSON.stringify(byFeature, null, 2));
  }
}

export default StepPathReporter;
```

**Tradeoff:** `titlePath` is available on the `TestStep` object inside reporter callbacks, but its TypeScript type in older `@playwright/test/reporter` type definitions may not include it — requiring a cast. Pin `@playwright/test` to `>= 1.55` and regenerate your TypeScript types to get full type safety without casts.

### Pattern 203: `browserContext.clearCookies({ name, domain, path })` — Surgical Cookie Teardown (v1.54+) [official]

`browserContext.clearCookies()` now accepts filter options to remove only matching cookies rather than wiping all cookies in the context. Use this to reset a single auth cookie between role-switch scenarios without destroying session storage or other cookies needed by the test.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('admin sees audit log; viewer does not', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'e2e/.auth/admin.json' });
  const page    = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('/admin/audit');
  await expect(page.getByRole('table', { name: 'Audit log' })).toBeVisible();

  // Remove only the session token cookie — preserve locale and preference cookies
  await context.clearCookies({ name: 'session_token' });

  // Load viewer auth state into the existing context (v1.59 setStorageState)
  await context.setStorageState({ path: 'e2e/.auth/viewer.json' });

  await page.reload();
  await page.goto('/admin/audit');

  // Viewer should be redirected away from the admin route
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard|forbidden/);
  await context.close();
});

// Cleaning up only a specific domain's cookies (useful in multi-origin setups)
test('clears only third-party analytics cookies', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  // Remove cookies from the analytics subdomain only
  await context.clearCookies({ domain: 'analytics.example.com' });

  const remaining             = await context.cookies();
  const analyticsStillPresent = remaining.some(c => c.domain === 'analytics.example.com');
  expect(analyticsStillPresent).toBe(false);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `clearCookies({ name })` matches cookies by exact name, not a regex. If your app uses session tokens with environment-prefixed names (e.g., `session_token_dev`, `session_token_staging`), you must call `clearCookies()` once per variant. Consider normalizing cookie names across environments, or using `clearCookies({ domain })` as the less-fragile filter.

### Pattern 204: `cookie.partitionKey` — CHIPS Partitioned Cookie Testing (v1.54+) [official]

Chrome's CHIPS (Cookies Having Independent Partitioned State) specification introduces cookies scoped to a top-level site partition. Playwright v1.54 adds `partitionKey` to the cookie object returned by `context.cookies()` and accepted by `context.addCookies()`, enabling tests to set and assert partitioned third-party cookies correctly.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('embedded widget sets CHIPS-compliant partitioned cookie', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('https://host-site.example');

  // Navigate into the embedded third-party iframe
  const widgetFrame = page.frameLocator('iframe[src*="widget.example"]');
  await widgetFrame.getByRole('button', { name: 'Accept preferences' }).click();

  // Read all cookies and find the partitioned one
  const allCookies  = await context.cookies();
  const partitioned = allCookies.filter(c => c.partitionKey !== undefined);

  expect(partitioned.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(partitioned[0].name).toBe('widget_prefs');
  expect(partitioned[0].partitionKey).toMatchObject({ sourceScheme: 'https' });
});

// Pre-seed a partitioned cookie so the widget loads in the expected theme
test('widget reads pre-seeded partitioned preference', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await context.addCookies([{
    name:         'widget_prefs',
    value:        'theme=dark&lang=en',
    domain:       'widget.example',
    path:         '/',
    partitionKey: { topLevelSite: 'https://host-site.example', hasCrossSiteAncestor: true },
    sameSite:     'None',
    secure:       true,
  }]);

  await page.goto('https://host-site.example');
  const frame = page.frameLocator('iframe[src*="widget.example"]');
  await expect(frame.getByTestId('theme-indicator')).toHaveText('dark');
});
```

**Tradeoff:** CHIPS behavior is Chromium-only in the current Playwright browser matrix. Firefox and WebKit bundled with Playwright ≤ v1.61 do not implement cookie partitioning. Guard these tests with `test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'CHIPS partitioned cookies are Chromium-only')` to avoid false failures in cross-browser CI matrices.

### Pattern 205: `test.info().annotations` — Runtime Annotation Enrichment for Dynamic Failures (v1.52+) [official]

`testInfo.annotations` is a mutable array that tests and fixtures can push to at runtime. Unlike static `@tag` annotations in `test()` declarations, runtime annotations capture dynamic context — API response codes, feature flag states, or detected environment versions — that only become available during test execution.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout completes for active users', async ({ page, request }, testInfo) => {
  // Check feature flag state at runtime
  const flagRes              = await request.get('/api/feature-flags/checkout-v2');
  const { enabled, variant } = await flagRes.json();

  // Annotate the test result with the flag state — visible in HTML report
  testInfo.annotations.push({
    type:        'feature-flag',
    description: `checkout-v2: ${variant ?? 'off'}`,
  });

  if (!enabled) {
    testInfo.annotations.push({
      type:        'skip-reason',
      description: 'checkout-v2 flag disabled in this environment',
    });
    test.skip();
  }

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/confirmation/);
});

// Auto fixture: attach build metadata to every test in the suite
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend({
  buildAnnotations: [async ({}, use, testInfo) => {
    const buildId   = process.env.CI_BUILD_ID   ?? 'local';
    const commitSha = process.env.CI_COMMIT_SHA ?? 'dev';
    testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'build-id',   description: buildId });
    testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'commit-sha', description: commitSha });
    await use(undefined);
  }, { auto: true }],
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Runtime annotations are written to the result JSON and HTML report but are NOT filterable by `--grep` at the command line — `--grep` only matches static `test()` title/tag annotations. If you need to filter by runtime annotation in CI, parse `test-results.json` in a post-run script and apply filtering there.

### Pattern 206: `testConfig.captureGitInfo` — Commit Traceability in HTML Reports (v1.51+) [official]

When `captureGitInfo: { commit: true }` is set in `playwright.config.ts`, Playwright captures the current git commit hash, branch name, and commit message at run-start and embeds them in the HTML and JSON reports. This lets teams trace any historical failure directly back to the commit that introduced it without correlating CI job IDs manually.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Embed git context in all report artifacts
  captureGitInfo: { commit: true, diff: false },

  reporter: [
    ['html', { open: 'never', outputFolder: 'playwright-report' }],
    ['json', { outputFile:   'test-results/report.json' }],
  ],

  use: {
    baseURL:    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace:      'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
});
```

```typescript
// e2e/scripts/verify-git-metadata.ts — post-run check for CI
import fs   from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

const reportPath = path.resolve('test-results/report.json');

if (fs.existsSync(reportPath)) {
  const report   = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf-8'));
  const commitId = report?.gitInfo?.commit?.id ?? null;

  if (!commitId) {
    console.warn('WARNING: git metadata missing from report — is git installed in CI?');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`Report captured commit: ${commitId}`);
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `captureGitInfo` reads git state from the working directory at run-start. In ephemeral CI containers using shallow clones (`--depth=1`), the commit message may be truncated and the branch name may be absent. Prefer `{ diff: false }` (the default) to avoid the expensive `git diff` operation; rely on `commit.id` for traceability. Also note: `git` must be installed in the container — see Gotcha #72.

### Pattern 207: `chromium.launchPersistentContext()` — Persistent Profile for Extension and Complex Auth Testing [official]

`browserType.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir, options)` launches a browser with a persistent user data directory, preserving extensions, cookies, and service worker registrations across sessions. Unlike `storageState` (which saves a JSON snapshot), this reuses the actual Chromium profile — required for testing browser extensions or multi-step auth flows that cannot be reconstructed from JSON.

```typescript
import { chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import path         from 'path';

const PROFILE_DIR = path.resolve('./test-profiles/admin-session');

// One-time setup: warm a persistent profile with a real login
async function warmAdminProfile(): Promise<void> {
  const browser = await chromium.launchPersistentContext(PROFILE_DIR, {
    headless: false,   // must be headed for real MFA flows
    channel:  'chrome',
  });

  const page = await browser.newPage();
  await page.goto('https://app.example.com/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  // Complete real MFA interactively — session saved to profile
  await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);

  await browser.close();
  console.log(`Profile saved to ${PROFILE_DIR}`);
}

// Test reuse: re-open the profile — auth is already present
async function runTestWithProfile(): Promise<void> {
  const browser = await chromium.launchPersistentContext(PROFILE_DIR, {
    headless: true,   // headless reuse after profile is warmed
  });

  const page = await browser.newPage();
  await page.goto('https://app.example.com/dashboard');
  // Session cookie is loaded from the profile — no login needed
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="user-menu"]');
  console.log('Dashboard loaded with persisted session');

  await browser.close();
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Persistent user data directories are not portable across Playwright Chromium versions — a profile built with Chromium 124 may silently fail to load session data in Chromium 126 due to internal IndexedDB format changes. Always re-warm persistent profiles after a Playwright version bump that updates the bundled Chromium (visible in the release notes). CI pipelines should prefer `storageState` JSON files for portability; use `launchPersistentContext` only for local developer workflows or extension testing.

---

### Pattern 208: `page.consoleMessages()` / `page.pageErrors()` — Post-Hoc Observability Without Eager Listeners (v1.57+) [official]

`page.consoleMessages()` returns all console messages emitted since the page was created. `page.pageErrors()` returns all uncaught JavaScript errors. Both methods eliminate the need to register `page.on('console')` / `page.on('pageerror')` listeners ahead of time — you can inspect what happened after the fact in `afterEach` hooks or assertion helpers.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Global afterEach: retroactively fail any test that produced uncaught JS errors
test.afterEach(async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  if (testInfo.status === 'passed') {
    const errors = page.pageErrors();
    if (errors.length > 0) {
      testInfo.annotations.push({
        type:        'uncaught-error',
        description: errors.map(e => e.message).join('; '),
      });
      testInfo.status = 'failed';
      testInfo.error  = { message: `Uncaught JS errors: ${errors[0].message}` };
    }
  }
});

// Retroactive console assertion in a specific test
test('dashboard emits no console errors on load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Load analytics' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('analytics-chart')).toBeVisible();

  // Check after the interaction — no upfront listener required
  const consoleErrors = page
    .consoleMessages()
    .filter(m => m.type() === 'error');

  expect(
    consoleErrors,
    'Console errors detected:\n' + consoleErrors.map(m => m.text()).join('\n'),
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` buffer messages for the lifetime of the `Page` object. In long-running tests that navigate many times (20+ pages), the buffer may grow large. There is no `.clear()` method — if you need only messages from a specific navigation, filter by `consoleMessage.timestamp()` (v1.59+) relative to a timestamp captured before the navigation.

---

### Pattern 209: `page.requests()` — Retroactive Network Assertion After Navigation (v1.57+) [official]

`page.requests()` returns all HTTP requests made by the page since it was created, as an array of `Request` objects. Paired with `page.consoleMessages()`, this gives full retroactive observability without upfront `page.on('request')` listener wiring.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout page makes exactly one payment API call', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/confirmation/);

  // Retroactively inspect all requests made during the test
  const allRequests  = page.requests();
  const paymentCalls = allRequests.filter(
    r => r.url().includes('/api/payment') && r.method() === 'POST',
  );

  // Assert idempotency: exactly one payment POST should have been made
  expect(paymentCalls, 'Expected exactly one payment POST — possible double-submit').toHaveLength(1);
});

// Detect unexpected cross-origin analytics beacons
test('product page makes no analytics beacons', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/123');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const baseOrigin = new URL(process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000').origin;
  const beacons    = page.requests().filter(r => {
    try {
      const reqOrigin = new URL(r.url()).origin;
      return reqOrigin !== baseOrigin && /analytics|tracking|beacon|pixel/.test(r.url());
    } catch { return false; }
  });

  expect(beacons, `Unexpected beacons: ${beacons.map(r => r.url()).join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `page.requests()` includes every request including prefetches, service worker fetches, and favicon requests. Unfiltered, the array can be hundreds of entries on asset-heavy pages. Always filter by URL pattern and HTTP method before asserting length. For request/response pairing, combine with `request.existingResponse()` (v1.59+) or use `page.waitForResponse()` for the synchronous pattern.

---

### Pattern 210: `test.slow()` — Tripling Timeouts for Known-Slow Test Scenarios [official]

`test.slow()` multiplies all timeouts for the current test by 3 (the default factor). Call it inside a test body or `test.beforeEach` based on a runtime condition — it adjusts timeouts without hardcoding specific millisecond values that may drift as the app grows.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Mark a single test as slow — triples its timeout
test('generates and downloads a 10MB PDF report', async ({ page }) => {
  test.slow();   // default 30 s → 90 s for this test only

  await page.goto('/reports');
  await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Date range' }).selectOption('last-year');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Generate full report' }).click();

  // Generating a full-year PDF may take 45+ seconds in CI
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText(/ready|complete/i, { timeout: 80_000 });

  const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Download PDF' }).click();
  const download = await downloadPromise;
  expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/report-\d{4}\.pdf$/);
});

// Conditional slow mark — only in CI where I/O is slower
test('syncs 1000 records', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  if (process.env.CI) {
    test.slow();   // triple the timeout in CI environments only
  }

  await page.goto('/sync');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start sync' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('sync-progress')).toHaveText('100%', { timeout: 60_000 });
  await expect(page.getByTestId('sync-status')).toHaveText('Done');
});

// Fixture approach: triple timeout for tests tagged @slow
export const test = test.extend({
  page: async ({ page }, use, testInfo) => {
    if (testInfo.tags.includes('@slow')) test.slow();
    await use(page);
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `test.slow()` is a timeout multiplier — it does NOT affect `globalTimeout`. A test marked slow that exceeds `globalTimeout` will still be killed. Avoid combining `test.slow()` with per-assertion `{ timeout }` overrides — when both are present, the smaller timeout wins and the slow multiplier may appear ineffective. Prefer `test.slow()` for globally slow tests rather than patching individual assertions.

---

### Pattern 211: `expect.configure({ timeout, message, soft })` — Named Assertion Presets [official]

`expect.configure()` returns a custom `expect` instance with preset timeout, failure message, and soft-assertion behavior. Create named presets — `networkExpect`, `softExpect`, `syncExpect` — to apply consistent assertion semantics across related tests without scattering timeout values throughout spec files.

```typescript
import { expect as baseExpect, test } from '@playwright/test';

// Long timeout for network-heavy assertions
const networkExpect = baseExpect.configure({ timeout: 15_000 });

// Soft assertion accumulator for form validation checks
const softExpect = baseExpect.configure({ soft: true });

// Zero timeout for already-loaded synchronous state
const syncExpect = baseExpect.configure({ timeout: 0 });

test('checkout form validation accumulates all errors', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();

  // Soft assertions — collect ALL failures, don't stop at first
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('name-error')).toHaveText('Name is required');
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('card-error')).toHaveText('Card number is required');
  await softExpect(page.getByTestId('cvv-error')).toHaveText('CVV is required');

  // Force hard failure if any soft assertion failed
  expect(testInfo.errors).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('API data loads before user interaction', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Network assertion: 15 s to let the API call resolve
  await networkExpect(page.getByRole('grid', { name: 'Sales data' })).toBeVisible();

  // Sync assertion: grid is already visible — row count is an immediate DOM read
  await syncExpect(
    page.getByRole('row').filter({ has: page.locator('td') }),
  ).not.toHaveCount(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Custom matchers added via `expect.extend()` on the base `expect` are NOT automatically inherited by a configured instance in Playwright < v1.56. If you use `mergeExpects()` to compose matchers, create configured presets from the merged instance (not from `@playwright/test`'s raw `expect`) to avoid losing custom matchers.

---

### Pattern 212: `page.clock.setFixedTime()` vs `page.clock.setSystemTime()` — Choosing the Right Date-Freeze Primitive (v1.45+) [official]

`setFixedTime()` patches only `Date.now()` and related date constructors — timers (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`) continue on their real schedule. `setSystemTime()` requires `clock.install()` first and freezes both Date AND all timer callbacks. Choosing the wrong one produces correct-looking but logically flawed tests.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// ── setFixedTime: patch Date only — timers still run ───────────────────────────
test('membership renewal badge shows "expires in 30 days"', async ({ page }) => {
  // No clock.install() needed — setFixedTime patches Date only
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-06-01T12:00:00Z'));

  await page.goto('/account');
  // Component reads Date.now() to compute days-until-expiry
  // Timers for polling or animations still fire on real schedule
  await expect(page.getByTestId('expiry-badge')).toHaveText('Expires in 30 days');
});

// ── setSystemTime: install full fake clock — timers suspended ──────────────────
test('session timeout warning appears after 25 min of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install();
  await page.goto('/app');
  await page.clock.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00Z'));

  // Advance 25 minutes — fires each timer callback in sequence
  await page.clock.fastForward('25:00');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: 'Session expiring' })).toBeVisible();
});

// Decision table
// | Need                                              | API                       |
// |---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
// | Freeze Date.now() only; let timers run normally   | setFixedTime()            |
// | Control Date AND timer callbacks together         | install() + setSystemTime() |
// | Advance clock step-by-step, firing each callback  | runFor() / tick()         |
// | Jump clock to endpoint, skipping intermediate     | fastForward()             |
```

**Tradeoff:** `setFixedTime()` is lighter and safer for date-display tests because it does not intercept `requestAnimationFrame` or `setInterval`. If your component chains timers (e.g., a `setInterval` that reads `Date.now()` and schedules a `setTimeout` based on the delta), `setFixedTime()` will produce inconsistent results because the timer fires with the real clock but reads the fake date. Use `install()` + `setSystemTime()` to keep date and timer semantics in sync for such components.

---

### Pattern 213: `testConfig.snapshotPathTemplate` with `{testFileBaseName}` — Flat Snapshot Organization (v1.55+) [official]

The `{testFileBaseName}` token resolves to the test filename without its extension, enabling flat snapshot directories named after spec files rather than deeply nested folder hierarchies that mirror the full directory tree.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Flat snapshot dirs: __snapshots__/checkout-snapshots/order-summary-chromium.png
  snapshotPathTemplate:
    '{snapshotDir}/{testFileBaseName}-snapshots/{arg}{-projectName}{ext}',

  expect: {
    toMatchSnapshot: {
      maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01,  // 1% pixel tolerance
      threshold:          0.2,  // per-pixel color distance
    },
  },

  use: {
    baseURL:    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
});

// e2e/specs/checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('order summary matches baseline', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/review');
  const summary = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Order summary' });
  await expect(summary).toMatchSnapshot('order-summary.png');
  // Saved to: __snapshots__/checkout-snapshots/order-summary-chromium.png
});

// Custom snapshot path via testInfo.snapshotPath() with kind option (v1.53+)
test('product card visual regression', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  const card           = page.getByTestId('product-card').first();
  const screenshotPath = testInfo.snapshotPath('product-card', { kind: 'visual' });
  const screenshot     = await card.screenshot();
  expect(screenshot).toMatchSnapshot(screenshotPath);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `{testFileBaseName}` shortens paths but loses directory context. Two spec files with the same base name in different directories (e.g., `auth/login.spec.ts` and `admin/login.spec.ts`) write snapshots to the same `login-snapshots/` folder, causing collisions. Add a `{projectName}` suffix or enforce unique spec file base names across the project as a CI lint rule.

---

### Pattern 214: `npx playwright install --list` — Installed Browser Inventory in CI Pre-Flight Checks (v1.53+) [official]

`npx playwright install --list` prints a tab-separated table of every Playwright-managed browser: its name, version, and executable path. Use this in CI setup scripts to verify the correct browsers are installed before the run — eliminating cryptic "browser not found" failures that hide the real cause.

```typescript
// e2e/scripts/verify-browsers.ts
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

interface BrowserEntry {
  name:    string;
  version: string;
  path:    string;
}

function getInstalledBrowsers(): BrowserEntry[] {
  const output = execSync('npx playwright install --list', { encoding: 'utf-8' });
  return output
    .split('\n')
    .filter(line => line.trim().length > 0 && !line.startsWith('Browser'))
    .map(line => {
      const [name, version, ...rest] = line.split('\t');
      return { name: name.trim(), version: version.trim(), path: rest.join('\t').trim() };
    });
}

const installed = getInstalledBrowsers();
const required  = ['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit'];

for (const req of required) {
  const found = installed.find(b => b.name.toLowerCase().includes(req));
  if (!found) {
    console.error(`FATAL: Required browser "${req}" not installed. Run: npx playwright install`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`OK  ${req} v${found.version} → ${found.path}`);
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/playwright.yml
- name: Verify Playwright browsers
  run: npx ts-node e2e/scripts/verify-browsers.ts
- name: Install missing browsers
  run: npx playwright install --with-deps
```

**Tradeoff:** The `--list` output format is not a stable public API — column order or separator characters may change between Playwright minor versions. Do not use the parsing script above in long-lived production code. Pin the Playwright version in `package.json` so the format matches the parser, and treat this as a diagnostic pre-flight check rather than a durable integration.

---

### Pattern 215: `locator.filter({ hasNot, hasNotText })` + Exclusion Chaining — Narrowing Rows by Absent State [official]

`filter({ hasNot: locator })` excludes elements containing a matching descendant; `filter({ hasNotText: pattern })` excludes elements whose `textContent` includes the pattern. Chain multiple `filter()` calls to build a declarative, readable exclusion query that reads like natural language.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('all pending tasks have no completion badge', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/tasks');

  const doneIcon   = page.locator('[data-icon="check-circle"]');
  const pendingRows = page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasNotText: /done|completed/i })
    .filter({ hasNot: doneIcon });

  // Assert at least some pending rows exist
  await expect(pendingRows).not.toHaveCount(0);
  // Assert NO pending row has a done icon
  const pendingWithIcon = pendingRows.filter({ has: doneIcon });
  await expect(pendingWithIcon).toHaveCount(0);
});

// Asserting a data table has zero error rows
test('import results contain no error rows', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/import/results');

  const errorBadge = page.getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: /error/i });
  const dataRows   = page.getByRole('row').filter({ has: page.locator('td') });
  const errorRows  = dataRows.filter({ has: errorBadge });

  await expect(
    errorRows,
    `Expected 0 error rows — found ${await errorRows.count()}`,
  ).toHaveCount(0);
});

// Chaining hasNot + hasNotText for compound exclusion
test('inbox shows unread messages only', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/inbox');
  const readIcon = page.locator('[aria-label="Read"]');
  const unread   = page
    .getByRole('listitem')
    .filter({ hasNotText: /read/i })
    .filter({ hasNot: readIcon });

  await expect(unread).not.toHaveCount(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `filter({ hasNotText })` uses the full DOM `textContent`, which includes text from visually hidden elements (sr-only spans, aria-label fallbacks, hidden badges). A row that looks blank may still be excluded if it contains a hidden `aria-label` matching the pattern. When exclusion must be based on visible text only, use `filter({ hasNot: locator.filter({ hasText, visible: true }) })` to combine visibility with the text check.
