## Cycle 55 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 411: `locator.or()` + `.filter({ visible: true })` for hydration-safe conditional UI** [official]
When a page has two possible CTAs (e.g., logged-in vs. guest), `locator.or()` can throw a strict-mode violation if both elements are momentarily present in the DOM during React hydration or an A/B test flip. Appending `.filter({ visible: true })` resolves ambiguity by selecting the only currently visible variant.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout CTA works regardless of auth state', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/product/123');

  const guestCta  = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in to buy' });
  const memberCta = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' });

  // Hydration can transiently attach both; filter to the visible one only
  const activeCta = guestCta.or(memberCta).filter({ visible: true });

  await expect(activeCta).toBeVisible();
  await activeCta.click();

  // Assert correct post-click destination depending on which was shown
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/(login|cart)/);
});
```
Tradeoff: If the component deliberately shows two visible buttons for different viewport breakpoints (e.g., mobile sticky + desktop inline), `.filter({ visible: true })` may still match two elements. In that case, add `.first()` or further narrow with `.and(page.getByRole(..., { name: 'exact' }))`.

---

**Pattern 412: `page.getByRole()` with `description` option for accessible description matching** [official]
Since v1.60, `page.getByRole()` accepts a `description` option that matches the element's accessible description (the `aria-describedby` or `aria-description` attribute). This allows you to distinguish between multiple elements with the same role and name but different descriptions — without resorting to `nth()` or brittle CSS selectors.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form fields with shared label but unique descriptions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  // Two password fields share the role "textbox" + similar name but have unique descriptions
  const newPassword = page.getByRole('textbox', {
    name:        'Password',
    description: 'Must be at least 12 characters',
  });
  const confirmPassword = page.getByRole('textbox', {
    name:        'Password',
    description: 'Re-enter your new password',
  });

  await newPassword.fill('SecurePass!2026');
  await confirmPassword.fill('SecurePass!2026');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save changes' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveText(/Password updated/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `description` matching requires the app to emit `aria-describedby` or `aria-description` correctly. If those attributes are absent or inconsistently set, this locator silently matches nothing and the test hangs until timeout rather than emitting a useful error. Always audit `aria-describedby` wiring in your component library before relying on this option at scale.

---

**Pattern 413: `locator.highlight({ style })` + `page.hideHighlight()` for visual debugging sessions** [official]
`locator.highlight()` draws a colored overlay on matched elements in the live browser window, and since v1.60 the `style` option lets you customize the overlay CSS (e.g., red border for errors, green for valid). Call `page.hideHighlight()` before assertions to avoid the overlay influencing screenshot comparisons.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('highlight validation errors before screenshot assertion', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();

  const errorFields = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /required/i });

  // Visually mark error fields during interactive debug; style is arbitrary CSS text
  await errorFields.highlight({ style: 'outline: 3px solid red; background: rgba(255,0,0,0.1)' });

  // Pause for manual inspection in headed mode; no-op in CI because headed is false
  if (process.env.PWDEBUG) await page.pause();

  // Clear highlight before visual snapshot so the overlay does not pollute the diff
  await page.hideHighlight();

  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('checkout-errors.png');
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.highlight()` is a debugging aid, not an assertion. It has no effect on test pass/fail status and does not verify the element is visible. Forgetting to call `page.hideHighlight()` before `toHaveScreenshot()` will cause every subsequent visual regression run to produce diffs due to the persistent overlay.

---

**Pattern 414: `tracing.startHar()` / `tracing.stopHar()` for network-level HAR capture** [official]
Introduced in v1.60, `tracing.startHar()` captures a HAR file covering all requests made within a tracing scope. Unlike `page.routeFromHAR()` (which replays), this API records live traffic for post-mortem analysis or seeding future mocks.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test('record checkout network traffic to HAR', async ({ page, context }) => {
  const harPath = path.join(test.info().outputDir, 'checkout.har');

  await context.tracing.startHar({ path: harPath, updateContent: 'attach' });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/30');
  await page.getByLabel('CVC').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay now' }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order confirmed' })).toBeVisible();

  await context.tracing.stopHar();

  // Attach HAR to the test report for post-mortem network inspection
  await test.info().attach('checkout.har', { path: harPath, contentType: 'application/json' });
});
```
Tradeoff: `updateContent: 'attach'` embeds response bodies in the HAR file, which can produce very large files for APIs returning large payloads (images, binary blobs). Use `updateContent: 'discard'` when you only need request/response metadata (timings, status codes) and not body content. HAR files are written on `stopHar()` — if the test crashes before that call, the file may be incomplete or absent.

---

**Pattern 415: `test.abort()` for unrecoverable fixture precondition failures** [official]
Since v1.60, `test.abort()` lets fixtures and hooks terminate a test with a descriptive message when a precondition is unrecoverably broken — rather than letting the test limp through with misleading assertion failures downstream. This is distinct from `test.skip()` (test intentionally skipped) and `test.fail()` (expected failure).
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Fixture that aborts the test if the seed user cannot be found
const seedUserTest = test.extend<{ seedUser: { id: string; email: string } }>({
  seedUser: async ({ request }, use, testInfo) => {
    const resp = await request.get('/api/test/seed-user');

    if (!resp.ok()) {
      // Abort rather than proceeding — downstream assertions would all be misleading
      test.abort(`Seed user endpoint returned ${resp.status()} — environment not ready`);
      return; // unreachable but satisfies TypeScript control-flow
    }

    const user = await resp.json();
    await use(user);

    // Teardown: clean up the seed user after the test
    await request.delete(`/api/test/seed-user/${user.id}`);
  },
});

seedUserTest('order history shows seed user orders', async ({ page, seedUser }) => {
  await page.goto(`/admin/users/${seedUser.id}/orders`);
  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('row')).toHaveCount({ min: 1 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `test.abort()` marks the test as failed (not skipped), so it counts against CI pass rates. Use it only for infrastructure failures (missing seed data, unreachable services) that are not expected conditions. For intentional skips (feature flags, platform exclusions), use `test.skip()`. `test.abort()` does not stop the entire suite — other tests continue running normally.

---

**Pattern 416: `locator.drop()` for external drag-and-drop file upload zones** [official]
`locator.drop()` (v1.60) dispatches synthetic `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` events on a target element, simulating a file or item being dragged from outside the browser. This is the correct approach for testing upload dropzones that are not `<input type="file">` elements.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test('CSV file can be dropped onto the import zone', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/data/import');

  const dropZone = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Drop files here' });
  await expect(dropZone).toBeVisible();

  // Use setInputFiles on the hidden input that the dropzone delegates to
  const filePath = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'sample-import.csv');
  await page.getByTestId('file-upload-input').setInputFiles(filePath);

  // Alternatively, locator.drop() dispatches drag events on the drop target element
  const dragSource = page.getByTestId('draggable-file-item');
  await dragSource.drop(dropZone);

  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText(/Importing/);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveText(/Import complete/, { timeout: 15_000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.drop()` moves an element already in the DOM onto a target — it does not simulate an OS-level file drag from outside the browser. For true external file drop simulation (files dragged from the OS file manager), dispatch a `DragEvent` manually with a `DataTransfer` containing files, or use `<input type="file">` interaction if the app exposes one as an accessibility-friendly alternative. `locator.drop()` is most reliable in Chromium; WebKit and Firefox handling of synthetic drag events can differ.

---

**Pattern 417: `expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for full-page accessibility tree regression** [official]
`toMatchAriaSnapshot()` captures the full ARIA tree of the page (or a subtree via a locator) and compares it against a stored snapshot. The `boxes` option (v1.60) appends bounding box coordinates to each node, enabling spatial assertions for AI agents and layout verification.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dashboard ARIA tree matches snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Basic ARIA snapshot — checks structure and accessible names
  await expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main":
      - link "Home"
      - link "Reports"
      - link "Settings"
    - main:
      - heading "Dashboard" [level=1]
      - region "Summary metrics":
        - text: /\\d+ active users/
  `);
});

test('dashboard ARIA snapshot with bounding boxes for spatial layout check', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // boxes: true appends [box=x,y,width,height] to each node for spatial assertions
  const snapshot = await page.locator('main').ariaSnapshot({ boxes: true });
  expect(snapshot).toContain('[box=');
  // Persist for AI agent consumption or spatial regression
  await test.info().attach('aria-boxes.txt', { body: snapshot, contentType: 'text/plain' });
});
```
Tradeoff: ARIA snapshots are highly sensitive to copy changes — any text update in a heading or link label will break the snapshot even if the structural behavior is unchanged. Use regex patterns (`/text/`) in ARIA snapshot templates for volatile content. The `boxes` option produces verbose output that is impractical for human review; reserve it for automated spatial validation pipelines rather than standard regression tests.

---

**Pattern 418: `expect.configure()` for per-suite timeout and message defaults** [official]
`expect.configure()` creates a scoped `expect` instance with custom `timeout`, `message`, or `soft` defaults. This is useful in fixtures or helpers that perform a series of assertions with domain-specific timeout requirements — avoiding the need to repeat `{ timeout: N }` on every assertion.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Fixture providing a slow-expect configured for async-heavy pages
const slowTest = test.extend<{ slowExpect: typeof expect }>({
  slowExpect: async ({}, use) => {
    // 30-second timeout for assertions in data-processing pages
    const slow = expect.configure({ timeout: 30_000 });
    await use(slow);
  },
});

slowTest('report generation completes and data table populates', async ({ page, slowExpect }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/generate');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Run report' }).click();

  // All assertions use the 30-second timeout without repeating { timeout: 30_000 }
  await slowExpect(page.getByRole('progressbar')).toBeHidden();
  await slowExpect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();
  await slowExpect(page.getByRole('row')).toHaveCount({ min: 10 });

  // Override back to fast for UI interaction assertions
  const fastExpect = expect.configure({ timeout: 2_000 });
  await fastExpect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export CSV' })).toBeEnabled();
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect.configure()` returns a new `expect` function — it does not mutate the global `expect`. Sharing a `slowExpect` instance across fixtures leaks the timeout into tests that do not need it unless the fixture properly scopes the instance. Prefer fixture-injected configured expects over module-level constants, which silently affect all tests in the file.

---

**Pattern 419: `locator.and()` for compound attribute + role guards** [official]
`locator.and()` narrows a locator by adding an additional filter without creating a new query. It is the correct way to require two independent locator conditions on the same element — for example, a tab that must have a specific role AND a `aria-selected="true"` attribute.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('only the active tab panel is interactable', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  // Find tab triggers that are both buttons AND currently selected
  const activeTab = page.getByRole('tab').and(
    page.locator('[aria-selected="true"]')
  );

  await expect(activeTab).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(activeTab).toHaveText('General');

  // Navigate to the next tab and confirm the active indicator moves
  await page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Security' }).click();

  const newActiveTab = page.getByRole('tab').and(
    page.locator('[aria-selected="true"]')
  );
  await expect(newActiveTab).toHaveText('Security');

  // Assert the General panel is no longer visible
  await expect(page.getByRole('tabpanel', { name: 'General' })).toBeHidden();
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.and()` applies both conditions simultaneously at evaluation time, inheriting the strictness of both constituent locators. If either locator matches multiple elements before the intersection, the strict check fires on the narrowed set. When tabs transiently show `aria-selected="true"` during animation, add `.filter({ visible: true })` to resolve the transient multi-match.

---

**Pattern 420: `page.addLocatorHandler()` with `times` option for one-shot overlay dismissal** [official]
`page.addLocatorHandler()` registers a handler that fires whenever a locator becomes visible, automatically dismissing overlays that interrupt test actions. The `times` option limits invocation count — useful for one-shot prompts (cookie consent, onboarding modals) that should never reappear once dismissed.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('onboarding modal dismissed once does not block navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register handler before navigation so it catches the modal on first appearance
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Welcome to the app' }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: 'Get started' }).click();
    },
    { times: 1, noWaitAfter: true } // fire once; don't wait for network after dismiss
  );

  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Navigate through several pages — modal should not reappear
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Reports' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/reports/);

  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/settings/);

  // Confirm the handler was fully consumed (modal never re-triggered)
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Welcome to the app' })).toBeHidden();
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `times: 1` means the handler fires exactly once. If the modal can legitimately re-appear (e.g., after a session reset mid-test), a second appearance will block subsequent actions without any handler to dismiss it, causing a timeout. Omit `times` (default unlimited) for modals that can reappear, and use `times: 1` exclusively for prompts that the app contract guarantees appear at most once per session.

---

**Pattern 421: `page.routeFromHAR()` for deterministic third-party API mocking** [official]
`page.routeFromHAR()` replays a pre-recorded HAR file, serving matching requests from the recording without hitting live servers. This eliminates flakiness caused by rate limits, network latency, or upstream API changes in tests that exercise third-party integrations.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test('payment flow completes with mocked Stripe API', async ({ page }) => {
  const harPath = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'stripe-checkout.har');

  // Route all Stripe requests through the HAR; unmatched requests fall through to real network
  await page.routeFromHAR(harPath, {
    url:    /stripe\.com/,
    update: false, // never update the HAR during this test run
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242424242424242');
  await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/30');
  await page.getByLabel('CVC').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay $49.99' }).click();

  // Response is served from HAR — no live Stripe call made
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Payment successful' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: HAR files must be kept up to date as third-party APIs evolve. A stale HAR silently serves outdated response shapes, causing tests to pass against production-incompatible mocks. Schedule periodic HAR refreshes by running with `update: 'missing'` (adds new requests only) or `update: true` (re-records all) in a dedicated CI job, and commit the refreshed HAR alongside any code change that triggered the API contract update.

---

**Pattern 422: `toHaveCSS()` with pseudo-element selectors for design-system token validation** [official]
Since v1.60, `toHaveCSS()` supports a `pseudo` option for `::before` and `::after`, allowing assertions against computed styles of generated content — a common source of visual regressions that pixel-diff screenshots would catch but unit tests miss entirely.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('required field indicator uses correct color token', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form/contact');

  const requiredLabel = page.getByText('Email address').and(
    page.locator('[data-required="true"]')
  );

  // Assert the label color matches the brand token
  await expect(requiredLabel).toHaveCSS('color', 'rgb(220, 38, 38)');

  // Assert the ::after pseudo-element renders the asterisk via generated content
  await expect(requiredLabel).toHaveCSS('content', '"*"', { pseudo: '::after' });

  // Assert focus ring uses the design-system focus token
  const emailInput = page.getByLabel('Email address');
  await emailInput.focus();
  await expect(emailInput).toHaveCSS('outline-color', 'rgb(59, 130, 246)');
  await expect(emailInput).toHaveCSS('outline-width', '2px');
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveCSS()` reads computed styles, which depend on the page's stylesheet being fully loaded and applied. In tests that check styles immediately after navigation (before fonts or stylesheets resolve), computed values may be browser defaults rather than design-system values. Always assert CSS styles after `waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` at minimum. Pseudo-element `{ pseudo: '::after' }` support is most reliable in Chromium; Firefox and WebKit handle generated-content computed style access inconsistently.

---

**Pattern 423: `page.clock.pauseAt()` + manual `tick()` for timer-driven UI testing** [official]
`page.clock.pauseAt()` freezes the browser clock at a specific point and lets you advance time manually with `clock.tick()`. This is the right tool for testing components that poll on intervals, countdown timers, or session-timeout warnings — making time-dependent behavior deterministic without `waitForTimeout()`.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session timeout warning appears at 5 minutes of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  // Freeze time at a known reference point before navigation
  await page.clock.pauseAt(new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00Z'));

  await page.goto('/app');
  await page.getByLabel('Username').fill('alice@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Dashboard' })).toBeVisible();

  // Advance 4 minutes 59 seconds — warning should NOT yet appear
  await page.clock.tick(4 * 60 * 1000 + 59_000);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: 'Session expiring' })).toBeHidden();

  // Advance one more second — warning should now appear
  await page.clock.tick(1_000);
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: 'Session expiring' })).toBeVisible();

  // Dismiss and confirm the warning clears
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Stay logged in' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog', { name: 'Session expiring' })).toBeHidden();
});
```
Tradeoff: `clock.pauseAt()` fires each pending timer exactly once when the tick passes its scheduled time — it does not repeatedly re-fire repeating timers the way real time does. Components using `setInterval` will fire each interval tick once per `clock.tick()` call that crosses the interval boundary. If a component relies on multiple consecutive interval firings (e.g., a progress bar that increments 10% per second), call `clock.tick(1_000)` repeatedly or use `clock.runFor(10_000)` to fire all intermediate ticks.

---

**Pattern 424: `page.request` vs. `request` fixture — choosing the right API context** [official]
Playwright provides two ways to make HTTP requests in tests: `page.request` (shares the browser context including cookies and storage) and the `request` fixture (an isolated `APIRequestContext` with its own cookie jar). Choosing wrong causes subtle auth failures or cross-test state leakage.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('API call authenticated via browser session uses page.request', async ({ page }) => {
  // Log in via UI — sets session cookie in the browser context
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('admin@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('password');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');

  // page.request shares the browser's cookie jar — the session cookie is included
  const resp = await page.request.get('/api/admin/users');
  expect(resp.status()).toBe(200);
  const users = await resp.json();
  expect(users).toHaveLength(5);
});

test('isolated API test uses request fixture to avoid cookie bleed', async ({ request }) => {
  // request fixture has its own cookie jar — no browser session contamination
  const loginResp = await request.post('/api/auth/token', {
    data: { email: 'api-user@example.com', password: 'secret' },
  });
  expect(loginResp.status()).toBe(200);
  const { token } = await loginResp.json();

  const profileResp = await request.get('/api/user/profile', {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  });
  expect(profileResp.status()).toBe(200);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.request` is convenient for testing endpoints that require a browser session, but it couples API assertions to UI login flows. If the login flow changes, both the UI test and the API assertion break simultaneously. Prefer the `request` fixture with explicit auth headers for pure API tests to keep them decoupled from browser navigation. In parallel test runs, both `page.request` and the `request` fixture contexts are isolated per worker by default.

---

**Pattern 425: `locator.contentFrame()` + `frameLocator.owner()` for round-trip iframe navigation** [official]
`locator.contentFrame()` converts a locator pointing at an `<iframe>` element into a `FrameLocator` scoped to that frame's content. The reverse — `frameLocator.owner()` — returns the `Locator` for the `<iframe>` element itself. Together they enable assertions on both the host page's iframe container and the frame's internal content.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('embedded payment iframe loads and submits correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');

  // Locate the iframe element on the host page
  const iframeEl = page.getByTitle('Secure payment form');
  await expect(iframeEl).toBeVisible();

  // Convert to FrameLocator to interact with iframe content
  const paymentFrame = iframeEl.contentFrame();

  // Wait for frame content to be ready before interacting
  await paymentFrame.getByRole('main').waitFor();

  await paymentFrame.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242424242424242');
  await paymentFrame.getByLabel('Expiry date').fill('12/30');
  await paymentFrame.getByLabel('Security code').fill('123');

  // Round-trip: get the iframe element back from the frame locator for attribute assertion
  const iframeOwner = paymentFrame.owner();
  await expect(iframeOwner).toHaveAttribute('data-ready', 'true');

  // Submit from within the frame
  await paymentFrame.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).click();

  // Assert on the host page after frame submit
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order confirmed' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.contentFrame()` returns a `FrameLocator` — it does not wait for the iframe to load or for the frame's document to be ready. If the iframe URL is slow to resolve (e.g., a third-party payment SDK), assertions inside `paymentFrame` will fail until the frame is fully loaded. Use `paymentFrame.getByRole('main').waitFor()` or a known stable inner element assertion to confirm the frame is ready before interacting with its contents.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G140: `locator.all()` returns a DOM snapshot — dynamic additions after the call are invisible**
Calling `locator.all()` immediately returns whatever elements are currently in the DOM without waiting for any dynamic content. If the list is populated by an async operation (API fetch, virtual scroll load), calling `.all()` before the fetch resolves returns an empty array or a partial list, and the test passes vacuously rather than asserting against the real data.
WHY: `locator.all()` is deliberately non-retrying — the docs explicitly warn "does not wait for elements to match the locator, and instead immediately returns whatever is present in the page." It is designed for cases where you already know the list is stable and just want to iterate. Using it on async-populated lists violates the auto-waiting contract that every other locator method provides.
Fix: Wait for the list to reach a known stable state before calling `.all()`. Use `await expect(locator).toHaveCount(expectedN)` first to let auto-waiting confirm the correct number of elements, then call `.all()` to iterate.

---

**Gotcha G141: `page.waitForSelector()` is a legacy ElementHandle API — handles go stale across React reconciliation**
`page.waitForSelector()` is a legacy API that returns an `ElementHandle`, bypassing Playwright's locator-based auto-waiting and retry mechanism. Tests that use it alongside locator assertions can produce flaky results because the element handle snapshot may become stale between `waitForSelector()` and a subsequent locator action.
WHY: `ElementHandle` is a snapshot of a DOM node at a point in time. If the node is removed and re-added by React reconciliation between the `waitForSelector()` call and a subsequent `.click()`, the handle points to a detached node. Locator-based methods re-query the DOM on every retry, making them immune to this staleness. The docs now mark `waitForSelector()` as legacy.
Fix: Replace `page.waitForSelector('selector')` with `await expect(page.locator('selector')).toBeAttached()` (or `toBeVisible()`), then use a locator for subsequent interactions. Never store an `ElementHandle` across `await` boundaries in modern Playwright tests.

---

**Gotcha G142: Soft assertion failures in `beforeEach` do not prevent the test from running**
`expect.soft()` marks the test as failed but does not throw. When soft assertions are used inside a `beforeEach` hook to validate setup preconditions, the test body runs regardless of the accumulated soft failures — often producing confusing cascading errors because the setup was incomplete.
WHY: `expect.soft()` is designed to continue execution within a test to collect all failures at once. It uses the same "accumulate errors" mechanism in hooks as in tests — meaning a soft failure in `beforeEach` adds to `testInfo.errors` but does not abort the hook or prevent the test from starting. This is by design but surprises teams who use soft assertions as lightweight precondition guards.
Fix: Use regular (non-soft) `expect()` in `beforeEach` hooks for setup preconditions. Soft assertions are appropriate inside the test body for multi-field form validation or multi-step UI flows, but preconditions that would invalidate the entire test must use hard assertions so the test is skipped or failed cleanly before any test-body code runs.

---

**Gotcha G143: `page.route()` glob patterns silently skip query strings containing `?` or `[` since v1.52**
A route registered with `page.route('**/api/search?query=*', ...)` no longer matches after v1.52 — the `?` is treated as a literal character and the route silently fails to intercept requests, causing tests to hit the real server without any error or warning.
WHY: Playwright aligned its glob engine with the `minimatch` v3 → v5 upgrade, which dropped support for `?` as a single-character wildcard and `[...]` as character ranges in URL globs to avoid security ambiguity. Tests written before v1.52 that relied on `?` in route patterns continue to compile and run without errors — they simply never match, creating a silent regression that only surfaces when the route handler is expected to have been called.
Fix: Use a regex for URL patterns that include query strings: `page.route(/\/api\/search/, ...)`. For path-only matching (no query string), glob patterns remain fully supported.

---

**Gotcha G144: `expect().not.toBeVisible()` passes for elements that are `display:none` but still attached**
`expect(locator).not.toBeVisible()` asserts the element is not visible, but it passes both for elements that are hidden (`display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, `opacity:0`) AND for elements that do not exist in the DOM at all. This means a test that expects an element to have been removed from the DOM entirely can pass vacuously when the element is merely hidden.
WHY: Playwright's visibility check uses a composite rule: an element is visible if it has a non-zero bounding box and is not hidden by CSS. `not.toBeVisible()` negates this — it passes for both the "absent from DOM" and "hidden by CSS" cases. If the product requirement is that an element must be fully removed (e.g., a dialog closed with `remove()` vs. `display:none`), a stricter assertion is needed.
Fix: Use `expect(locator).not.toBeAttached()` to assert the element is fully removed from the DOM. Use `expect(locator).toBeHidden()` to assert the element exists but is not visible. Use `toHaveCount(0)` for lists that should be fully empty. Match the assertion to the exact product requirement: "not rendered" vs. "rendered but hidden."

### New Patterns

**Pattern 426: Worker-scoped fixture for expensive server initialization** [official]
Worker fixtures initialize once per worker process and are shared across all tests running in that worker. This is the correct scope for expensive operations like starting a local server, provisioning a database schema, or creating a test user account that can be reused across the test file.
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/server.fixture.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { createServer, type Server } from 'node:http';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';

type WorkerFixtures = {
  localServer: { baseUrl: string; server: Server };
};

export const test = base.extend<Record<string, never>, WorkerFixtures>({
  localServer: [
    async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
      const port = 3100 + workerInfo.workerIndex;  // unique port per worker
      const server = createServer((req, res) => {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
        res.end(JSON.stringify({ worker: workerInfo.workerIndex }));
      });

      await promisify(server.listen.bind(server))(port);
      console.log(`[worker ${workerInfo.workerIndex}] server on :${port}`);

      await use({ baseUrl: `http://localhost:${port}`, server });

      // Teardown — runs once after ALL tests in the worker complete
      await promisify(server.close.bind(server))();
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';
```
```typescript
// e2e/specs/server.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/server.fixture';

test('worker server returns correct worker index', async ({ page, localServer }) => {
  await page.goto(`${localServer.baseUrl}/status`);
  await expect(page.getByText(/"worker":\d/)).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Worker-scoped fixtures share state across all tests that run in the same worker. If any test mutates the fixture's state (e.g., writes to the database, changes server config), subsequent tests in the same worker inherit that mutation. Worker fixtures are appropriate for read-only or reset-on-test resources. For truly isolated state, use `test`-scoped fixtures even if initialization is slower.

---

**Pattern 427: `locator.filter({ hasNot })` — negative descendant filtering** [official]
`filter({ hasNot: locator })` excludes elements that contain a matching descendant. It is the complement of `filter({ has: locator })` and enables expressing "give me all rows that do NOT have a delete button" — patterns that `filter({ has })` cannot express alone.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/data-grid.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('pending rows do not show a delete button', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/orders');

  const pendingRows = page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ hasText: 'Pending' })
    .filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }) });

  // Every visible pending row should be free of a delete action
  const count = await pendingRows.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (const row of await pendingRows.all()) {
    await expect(row.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' })).not.toBeAttached();
  }
});

test('rows with errors show retry but not approve', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/orders');

  // Get error rows: have Retry, do NOT have Approve
  const errorRows = page
    .getByRole('row')
    .filter({ has: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }) })
    .filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Approve' }) });

  await expect(errorRows).not.toHaveCount(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `filter({ hasNot })` re-evaluates the predicate on every auto-retry. For tables with hundreds of rows, each retry scans all rows for the absent descendant, which can be slower than asserting on a known stable count. Prefer `toHaveCount(0)` on the inner locator for simple "none present" checks — use `hasNot` only when you need the filtered parent rows for further assertions.

---

**Pattern 428: `page.addInitScript()` for environment stub injection** [official]
`page.addInitScript()` runs a script in the page context before any other scripts execute, including framework bootstrapping and first render. This makes it the correct place to stub `window.matchMedia`, override `Date`, inject feature flag globals, or mock third-party SDKs that apps read on initialization.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/feature-flags.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows beta badge when beta flag is enabled', async ({ page }) => {
  // Inject flag before page scripts run
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (window as any).__FLAGS__ = { betaDashboard: true, darkMode: false };
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'beta' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('hides beta badge when flag is disabled', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (window as any).__FLAGS__ = { betaDashboard: false, darkMode: false };
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'beta' })).not.toBeAttached();
});

test('app uses fixed date for snapshot testing', async ({ page }) => {
  // Freeze Date to 2026-01-15T09:00:00Z so date-dependent UI is deterministic
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const FIXED = new Date('2026-01-15T09:00:00Z').getTime();
    const OrigDate = Date;
    (window as any).Date = class extends OrigDate {
      constructor(...args: ConstructorParameters<typeof OrigDate>) {
        super(args.length ? args[0] : FIXED);
      }
      static now() { return FIXED; }
    };
  });

  await page.goto('/reports/today');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading')).toContainText('January 15');
});
```
Tradeoff: `addInitScript()` runs in every navigation of the page — including redirects after login. If the stub is navigation-sensitive (e.g., the flag endpoint responds differently on the settings page), a single blanket `addInitScript` override may be too broad. Scope injection with `if (window.location.pathname.startsWith('/dashboard'))` guards inside the script, or use `page.route()` to intercept the flag-serving API instead.

---

**Pattern 429: `workerStorageState` — parallel role-based auth with unique accounts per worker** [official]
Each worker index gets a distinct authenticated session file, enabling multiple parallel test workers to run with fully isolated identities. This prevents one worker's session-modifying tests from invalidating another worker's session.
```typescript
// e2e/auth/worker-setup.ts
import { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

// Run with: --workers=4, generates .auth/worker-0.json … worker-3.json
setup('authenticate worker session', async ({ page }, workerInfo) => {
  const email    = `ci-worker-${workerInfo.workerIndex}@example.com`;
  const authFile = path.join(__dirname, `../.auth/worker-${workerInfo.workerIndex}.json`);

  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(email);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.CI_WORKER_PASS!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');

  await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
});
```
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  globalSetup: './e2e/auth/worker-setup.ts',
  use: {
    // Each worker picks its own storage state file
    storageState: ({ workerIndex }: { workerIndex: number }) =>
      `e2e/.auth/worker-${workerIndex}.json`,
  },
});
```
```typescript
// e2e/specs/profile.spec.ts — no login code needed, session loaded from file
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('worker can view its own profile', async ({ page }, workerInfo) => {
  const expectedEmail = `ci-worker-${workerInfo.workerIndex}@example.com`;
  await page.goto('/profile');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('profile-email')).toHaveText(expectedEmail);
});
```
Tradeoff: `workerStorageState` requires pre-provisioning one test account per worker in your test environment. In ephemeral CI environments, the provisioning step (global setup) must be idempotent — re-running `globalSetup` should not fail if the accounts already exist. Consider API-based account creation in `globalSetup` with `PUT /api/users/ensure` (upsert semantics) rather than `POST /api/users` (fails if exists).

---

**Pattern 430: `expect.extend()` — custom assertion for domain-specific invariants** [official]
`expect.extend()` registers a custom matcher that surfaces domain language in assertion failures. Instead of a generic "expected X to equal Y", a custom matcher reports "expected price '$1,299.99' to be a valid formatted USD price" — much faster to triage.
```typescript
// e2e/matchers/price.matcher.ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

expect.extend({
  async toDisplayValidUsdPrice(locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator) {
    const text = await locator.innerText();
    const priceRegex = /^\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*(\.\d{2})?$/;
    const pass = priceRegex.test(text.trim());

    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        pass
          ? `Expected locator NOT to display a valid USD price, but got "${text}"`
          : `Expected locator to display a valid USD price (e.g. $1,299.99), but got "${text}"`,
    };
  },

  async toBeWithinRange(
    locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator,
    min: number,
    max: number
  ) {
    const text  = await locator.innerText();
    const value = parseFloat(text.replace(/[$,]/g, ''));
    const pass  = value >= min && value <= max;
    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        `Expected ${value} to be between ${min} and ${max}`,
    };
  },
});

// Augment TypeScript types
declare module '@playwright/test' {
  interface Matchers<R> {
    toDisplayValidUsdPrice(): R;
    toBeWithinRange(min: number, max: number): R;
  }
}
```
```typescript
// e2e/specs/pricing.spec.ts
import '../matchers/price.matcher';
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('product price is valid USD', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/widget');
  const price = page.getByTestId('product-price');
  await expect(price).toDisplayValidUsdPrice();
  await expect(price).toBeWithinRange(10, 5000);
});
```
Tradeoff: Custom matchers are not retrying by default — if you need auto-waiting, call `expect.poll()` inside the matcher body or use `locator.waitFor()` before the assertion. Matchers added via `expect.extend()` are global for the process; import the matcher file in every spec that needs it (or in a global `setup` file listed in `require` config) to ensure TypeScript types resolve correctly.

---

**Pattern 431: `page.waitForResponse()` with predicate for selective response gating** [official]
`page.waitForResponse(predicate)` returns a promise that resolves when a matching response is received, letting you gate subsequent assertions on a specific API response rather than polling for UI changes. The predicate form is more precise than URL globs alone — it can inspect status, headers, and body.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/save-draft.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('draft is saved automatically after 2 seconds of idle', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/editor/new');

  // Start waiting for the auto-save response BEFORE triggering the action
  const autosaveResponse = page.waitForResponse(
    resp => resp.url().includes('/api/drafts') && resp.request().method() === 'POST'
  );

  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Title' }).fill('My Draft');
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Content' }).fill('Draft content here');

  // Wait up to 5s for the debounced auto-save to fire
  const response = await autosaveResponse;
  expect(response.status()).toBe(201);

  const body = await response.json();
  expect(body).toMatchObject({ id: expect.any(String), status: 'draft' });

  // UI should now reflect saved state
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Saved');
});

test('confirms image upload succeeds before asserting gallery', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/gallery/upload');

  const [uploadResponse] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/api/uploads') && r.status() === 200),
    page.setInputFiles('input[type="file"]', 'e2e/fixtures/test-image.png'),
  ]);

  const { url } = await uploadResponse.json();
  expect(url).toMatch(/^https:\/\/cdn\.example\.com\//);

  await expect(page.getByRole('img', { name: 'test-image.png' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `waitForResponse()` must be called BEFORE the action that triggers the request — if you `await` the action first, the response may have already arrived and the `waitForResponse` promise never resolves. Always set up the response waiter before triggering the interaction, using `Promise.all` to start both concurrently if needed. For multi-response flows, collect all waiters before initiating any action.

---

**Pattern 432: `context.grantPermissions()` for geolocation, notifications, and clipboard access** [official]
`browserContext.grantPermissions()` pre-grants browser permissions so the test page never shows a permission dialog during test execution. This is essential for geolocation-dependent features, push notification flows, and clipboard read/write tests.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/location.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('store locator shows nearby stores using geolocation', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Grant permission and set a fixed geolocation before the page loads
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    permissions: ['geolocation'],
    geolocation: { latitude: 37.7749, longitude: -122.4194 },  // San Francisco
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('/stores/nearby');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Find stores near me' }).click();

  // Stores within 10 miles of SF should appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem').first()).toContainText('San Francisco');
  await context.close();
});

test('notification prompt is pre-granted and subscription dialog appears', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ permissions: ['notifications'] });
  const page    = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('/notifications/subscribe');
  // No permission dialog interrupts the test
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Enable notifications' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Notifications enabled');
  await context.close();
});

test('clipboard paste populates the invite code field', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ permissions: ['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write'] });
  const page    = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('/invite');
  // Write to clipboard and paste into the input
  await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('INVITE-XYZ-789'));
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Invite code' }).focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Invite code' })).toHaveValue('INVITE-XYZ-789');
  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Geolocation and notification permissions are reset to the default ("ask") for each new `BrowserContext`. If your test fixture creates a new context via `browser.newContext()`, always grant permissions before navigating. Using `use: { permissions: [...] }` in `playwright.config.ts` applies permissions to contexts created from the default `page` fixture — but NOT to contexts you create manually inside a test via `browser.newContext()`.

---

**Pattern 433: `page.evaluate()` with argument passing for DOM inspection and state extraction** [official]
`page.evaluate()` runs a function in the browser context and returns a serializable result. Pass structured arguments as the second parameter to inject test-specific values into the browser function — avoiding string concatenation in the serialized code which is error-prone and breaks on special characters.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/cart.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cart total is computed correctly after adding items', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');

  // Extract structured data from the DOM in one evaluate call
  const cartData = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="cart-row"]'));
    return rows.map(row => ({
      name:     (row.querySelector('[data-testid="item-name"]') as HTMLElement)?.innerText,
      quantity: parseInt((row.querySelector('[data-testid="item-qty"]') as HTMLInputElement)?.value ?? '0', 10),
      price:    parseFloat((row.querySelector('[data-testid="item-price"]') as HTMLElement)?.innerText.replace('$', '') ?? '0'),
    }));
  });

  const expectedTotal = cartData.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity * item.price, 0);
  const displayedTotal = await page.getByTestId('cart-total').innerText();
  expect(parseFloat(displayedTotal.replace('$', ''))).toBeCloseTo(expectedTotal, 2);
});

test('item visibility filter correctly hides out-of-stock products', async ({ page }) => {
  const threshold = 5;  // Pass from test scope — no string interpolation needed

  await page.goto('/inventory');

  const hiddenCount = await page.evaluate((minStock: number) => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-stock]'))
      .filter(el => parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-stock') ?? '0', 10) < minStock)
      .length;
  }, threshold);

  await page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Hide low-stock items' }).click();
  const remainingCount = await page.locator('[data-stock]').count();
  expect(remainingCount).toBe((await page.locator('[data-stock]').count()) - hiddenCount);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.evaluate()` serializes arguments and return values with `JSON.stringify` — class instances, functions, DOM nodes, and `undefined` values are silently dropped or converted. If you need to pass a DOM element to `evaluate()`, use `locator.evaluate(fn, arg)` which passes the element handle directly. For complex return types, prefer `toMatchObject()` over `toEqual()` since non-serializable fields may be absent.

---

**Pattern 434: `testInfo.attach()` — structured artifact capture for debugging** [official]
`testInfo.attach()` adds named artifacts to the test report — JSON data, screenshots, logs, or raw buffers — that appear in the HTML report alongside the test. Use it for API response bodies, accessibility scan results, or performance timings that are too verbose to assert on but essential for debugging failures.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/search.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('search returns relevant results', async ({ page, request }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('playwright testing');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  // Capture the raw API response for offline debugging
  const apiResp = await request.get('/api/search?q=playwright+testing');
  const apiBody = await apiResp.json();

  await testInfo.attach('search-api-response', {
    body:        JSON.stringify(apiBody, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Capture a screenshot of the results page
  const screenshot = await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true });
  await testInfo.attach('search-results-screenshot', {
    body:        screenshot,
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Assert only on count — full response is in the attachment for review
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(apiBody.results.length);
  expect(apiBody.results.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});

test('captures performance metrics on checkout completion', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Complete order' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/confirmation');

  const metrics = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const nav = performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0] as PerformanceNavigationTiming;
    return {
      domContentLoaded: nav.domContentLoadedEventEnd - nav.startTime,
      loadTime:         nav.loadEventEnd - nav.startTime,
      ttfb:             nav.responseStart - nav.requestStart,
    };
  });

  await testInfo.attach('perf-metrics', {
    body:        JSON.stringify(metrics, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Soft assert on performance budget — failures surface but do not block ship
  expect.soft(metrics.ttfb).toBeLessThan(200);
  expect.soft(metrics.loadTime).toBeLessThan(3000);
});
```
Tradeoff: Attachments are stored in `test-results/` and embedded in the HTML report. Large attachments (full-page screenshots, verbose JSON) significantly increase report file size — especially in CI where hundreds of tests run. Use `testInfo.attach()` for failure artifacts and in targeted performance/accessibility tests. Combine with `video: 'retain-on-failure'` and `trace: 'on-first-retry'` so attachments complement rather than duplicate the existing trace.

---

**Pattern 435: `locator.pressSequentially()` for realistic character-by-character typing** [official]
`locator.pressSequentially(text)` dispatches individual `keydown`, `keypress`, `input`, and `keyup` events for each character, simulating realistic keyboard input. Use it for inputs that react to each keystroke — autocomplete dropdowns, live search, character counters, and masked inputs that need individual character events.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/search-autocomplete.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('autocomplete appears after typing three characters', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const searchInput = page.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Search products' });

  // Type character-by-character — triggers debounced autocomplete on each keystroke
  await searchInput.pressSequentially('wid', { delay: 80 });

  // Dropdown should appear after 3 chars
  const dropdown = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: 'Suggestions' });
  await expect(dropdown).toBeVisible();
  await expect(dropdown.getByRole('option')).toHaveCount(5);

  // Continue typing to narrow results
  await searchInput.pressSequentially('get', { delay: 80 });
  await expect(dropdown.getByRole('option')).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(dropdown.getByRole('option').first()).toContainText('Widget');
});

test('masked phone input formats as user types', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/contact');

  const phoneInput = page.getByLabel('Phone number');

  // Masked inputs transform on each keypress — use pressSequentially
  await phoneInput.pressSequentially('2125550199', { delay: 50 });

  // Masked input should reformat to (212) 555-0199
  await expect(phoneInput).toHaveValue('(212) 555-0199');
});
```
Tradeoff: `pressSequentially()` is substantially slower than `fill()` because it fires multiple events per character. For inputs that do not listen to individual keystrokes (standard text inputs, non-masked fields), always prefer `fill()` — it is 10–50× faster. Reserve `pressSequentially()` for inputs with live-validation, masking, autocomplete, or character-limit counters that inspect each `input` event. The `delay` option adds artificial inter-keystroke pauses; omit it in headless CI where timing is not under test.

---

**Pattern 436: `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders()` for persistent auth and custom header injection** [official]
`page.setExtraHTTPHeaders()` appends headers to every subsequent request from the page, including navigation requests, API calls, and static asset fetches. It is the correct mechanism for injecting Bearer tokens, API version headers, or test-environment flags that must be present on every request.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/api-version-header.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('API version header is sent with every request', async ({ page }) => {
  // Inject the API version on every request from this page
  await page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({
    'X-API-Version':  '2026-01',
    'X-Test-Session': `pw-${Date.now()}`,
  });

  // Capture headers from the first API call
  const [request] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForRequest(r => r.url().includes('/api/')),
    page.goto('/dashboard'),
  ]);

  expect(request.headers()['x-api-version']).toBe('2026-01');
  expect(request.headers()['x-test-session']).toMatch(/^pw-\d+$/);
});

test('bypass CDN cache for test isolation using custom header', async ({ page }) => {
  const cacheKey = `test-${process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_INDEX ?? '0'}-${Date.now()}`;

  await page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({ 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Bypass-Cache': cacheKey });
  await page.goto('/products');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('data-freshness')).not.toContainText('cached');
});

test('impersonate user role using internal test header', async ({ page }) => {
  // Test environments may support role impersonation via X-Test-Role header
  await page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({ 'X-Test-Role': 'super-admin' });
  await page.goto('/admin/settings');

  // Super-admin controls should be visible
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Purge all caches' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `setExtraHTTPHeaders()` applies to all requests from the page — including third-party analytics, CDN assets, and cross-origin API calls. Custom headers sent to third-party domains may trigger CORS preflight errors or leak internal test markers to external services. Scope extra headers to first-party requests using `page.route()` with a condition instead of `setExtraHTTPHeaders()` if you need header injection for specific routes only.

---

**Pattern 437: `context.setOffline()` for network failure and offline state testing** [official]
`browserContext.setOffline(true)` simulates a complete loss of network connectivity for the entire browser context. Use it to test offline banners, service worker caching, and error states that only appear when the network is unavailable.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/offline.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows offline banner when network is lost mid-session', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Assert we start online
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'connection' })).toHaveText('Online');

  // Cut the network
  await context.setOffline(true);

  // Trigger an action that requires the network
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh data' }).click();

  // App should detect the failure and show an offline indicator
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: 'No internet connection' })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'connection' })).toHaveText('Offline');

  // Restore network
  await context.setOffline(false);

  // App should recover automatically
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'connection' })).toHaveText('Online');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: 'No internet connection' })).not.toBeVisible();
});

test('PWA serves cached content while offline', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  // Warm the service worker cache
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Go offline and navigate to a cached route
  await context.setOffline(true);
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Service worker should serve from cache
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Products' })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /offline/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.setOffline(true)` blocks ALL network access for the context — including service worker fetch events and `fetch()` calls inside Web Workers. If your offline test depends on the service worker itself serving cached content, the service worker's own outbound network requests (for background sync, push, etc.) are also blocked. For fine-grained network failure simulation (timeout on one endpoint, error on another), use `page.route()` with `route.abort('failed')` instead of `setOffline()`.

---

**Pattern 438: `page.getByRole()` with `exact: false` for flexible accessible name matching** [official]
By default, `getByRole()` with a `name` option matches the full accessible name exactly (case-insensitively). Setting `exact: false` enables substring matching — useful for elements whose accessible names include dynamic data like counts, badges, or dates that change between test runs.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/notifications.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('notification bell is accessible and shows unread badge', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/inbox');

  // ❌ Fragile: exact count baked into locator — breaks when count changes
  // page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Notifications 3 unread' })

  // ✅ Flexible: substring match — works regardless of unread count
  const notifBell = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Notifications', exact: false });
  await expect(notifBell).toBeVisible();
  await notifBell.click();

  // Assert the exact badge count once we control the data
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'unread count' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('date-stamped export button is clickable regardless of today\'s date', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  // Button label is "Export report for May 14, 2026" — date changes every day
  const exportBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export report for', exact: false });
  await expect(exportBtn).toBeVisible();
  await exportBtn.click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Export options', exact: false })).toBeVisible();
});

test('shopping cart button reflects current item count', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();

  // Cart button may say "Cart (1)" or "Shopping cart — 1 item"
  const cartBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'cart', exact: false });
  await expect(cartBtn).toBeVisible();
  await expect(cartBtn).toContainText('1');
});
```
Tradeoff: `exact: false` can create inadvertently broad locators that match multiple elements — e.g., searching for `name: 'Save'` with `exact: false` might match "Save as draft", "Save and publish", and "Auto-save enabled". Always verify the match count with `await expect(locator).toHaveCount(1)` or use `.filter({ has: ... })` to narrow after an `exact: false` role query. For stable UI text, prefer exact matching to keep tests self-documenting.

---

**Pattern 439: `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` for ordered test groups** [official]
`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` forces all tests in the `describe` block to run in order on the same worker, sharing browser state. Use it for multi-step flows that build on each other — wizard forms, checkout sequences, or setup/operate/teardown workflows — where each step must see the state left by the previous step.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/checkout-flow.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// All tests share browser state — run in sequence on the same worker
test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' });

test.describe('end-to-end checkout flow', () => {
  test('step 1: browse catalog and add item to cart', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/shop');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart', exact: true }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: 'cart' })).toContainText('1');
  });

  test('step 2: proceed to checkout from cart', async ({ page }) => {
    // Browser state carries the cart from step 1
    await page.goto('/cart');
    await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(1);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Proceed to checkout' }).click();
    await page.waitForURL('/checkout');
  });

  test('step 3: complete shipping details', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Test User');
    await page.getByLabel('Address').fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Testville');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to payment' }).click();
    await page.waitForURL('/checkout/payment');
  });

  test('step 4: confirm order placement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242424242424242');
    await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/30');
    await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
    await page.waitForURL('/confirmation');
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order confirmed' })).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Serial mode eliminates test isolation within the describe block — a failure in step 2 causes all subsequent steps to be skipped, and the test results show only step 2 as the root cause. Never use `serial` mode for tests that should be independently runnable. Use it exclusively for intentional stateful flows where step N is meaningless without the state left by step N-1. Always add a teardown `afterAll` to clean up the shared state, even in serial mode.

---

**Pattern 440: `locator.selectOption()` with value, label, and index overloads** [official]
`locator.selectOption()` selects one or more `<option>` elements by value string, visible label text, element index, or `<option>` `ElementHandle`. Mixing overload forms within one call enables selecting by whichever attribute is most stable for your component.
```typescript
// e2e/specs/forms.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('country selector supports value, label, and index forms', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/locale');

  const countrySelect = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Country' });

  // Select by value attribute (most stable — not affected by display text changes)
  await countrySelect.selectOption({ value: 'US' });
  await expect(countrySelect).toHaveValue('US');

  // Select by visible label text
  await countrySelect.selectOption({ label: 'Canada' });
  await expect(countrySelect).toHaveValue('CA');

  // Select by index (0-based) — use only when value/label are dynamic
  await countrySelect.selectOption({ index: 0 });
  await expect(countrySelect).not.toHaveValue('');
});

test('multi-select locale filter accepts mixed overloads', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/filter');

  const regionSelect = page.locator('select[name="regions"]');

  // Select multiple options simultaneously
  await regionSelect.selectOption([
    { value: 'NA' },          // North America by value
    { label: 'Europe' },      // Europe by label
    { value: 'APAC' },        // Asia-Pacific by value
  ]);

  await expect(regionSelect).toHaveValues(['NA', 'EU', 'APAC']);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('selected-regions-count')).toHaveText('3 regions selected');
});

test('priority select uses value to avoid locale display text differences', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/tasks/new');

  // In localized UIs, label text changes by locale but value is stable
  await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /priority/i }).selectOption({ value: 'high' });
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /create task/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('task-priority-badge')).toHaveText(/high/i);
});
```
Tradeoff: Selecting by `{ label: '...' }` is the most readable form but is fragile when label text is translated, truncated, or dynamically generated. Selecting by `{ value: '...' }` is the most stable form — option values are typically API contract keys that change less often than display text. Avoid `{ index: N }` except in tests that explicitly verify option order; index-based selection produces unreadable test failures ("expected index 2 to be selected" tells you nothing about the user intent).

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G145: Worker-scoped fixtures accumulate mutable state across tests in the same worker**
Tests that share a worker-scoped fixture can inadvertently see mutations left by previous tests. If a worker fixture exposes a mutable object (a database pool, an in-memory store, a cache), and test A writes to it, test B in the same worker reads the mutated value — creating an order-dependent test failure.
WHY: Worker fixtures are designed for resource sharing across tests in the same worker process. Playwright does not reset or reinitialize a worker fixture between tests — the same instance is handed to every test that requests it. This is the correct behavior for read-only resources (a started server, a compiled asset) but is a footgun for mutable shared state.
Fix: Worker fixtures should expose only read-only or reset-safe resources. If the fixture manages mutable state (a mock server's recorded calls, a database seed state), add a `beforeEach` that resets the mutable portion: `test.beforeEach(async ({ myWorkerFixture }) => { myWorkerFixture.clearRecordedCalls(); })`. Alternatively, move the mutable resource to a `test`-scoped fixture so it is re-created for each test.

---

**Gotcha G146: `page.addInitScript()` does not run on popup pages opened from within the test**
Scripts registered with `page.addInitScript()` are bound to the specific `Page` instance. When the test opens a popup (via `window.open()`, a clicked link with `target="_blank"`, or a form with `target="_blank"`), the popup is a new `Page` object and does not inherit any init scripts from the opener.
WHY: `addInitScript()` registers a script on a `Page` object's script injection queue. The browser models a popup as a fully independent browsing context (or shares a context but creates a new document). Neither mechanism propagates page-level init scripts. The popup starts with a clean script environment.
Fix: Capture the popup using `page.waitForEvent('popup')` or `context.waitForEvent('page')`, then call `popup.addInitScript(...)` before the popup navigates: `const [popup] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('popup'), triggerPopupAction()]); await popup.addInitScript(() => { /* stub */ }); await popup.waitForLoadState();`. For context-wide script injection, use `context.addInitScript()` instead of `page.addInitScript()` — context-level init scripts apply to every page and popup within the context.

---

**Gotcha G147: `context.grantPermissions()` only affects the current BrowserContext — new contexts do not inherit permissions**
Calling `context.grantPermissions(['geolocation'])` grants permission for the context created by the test fixture. If the test code also calls `browser.newContext()` to create an additional context for a second role or a popup scenario, that new context starts with default (prompt) permissions — it does not inherit the granted permissions from the first context.
WHY: Browser permissions are scoped to the `BrowserContext` level — this is a Chromium/WebKit/Firefox security model, not a Playwright limitation. Each context maintains its own permission store. `context.grantPermissions()` modifies only the calling context's store.
Fix: Call `grantPermissions()` on every context that needs the permission, or configure permissions via `browser.newContext({ permissions: [...] })` at creation time. If you manage contexts in fixtures, pass the desired permissions through the fixture configuration rather than calling `grantPermissions()` ad-hoc in tests.

---

**Gotcha G148: `locator.pressSequentially()` triggers browser autofill and extension interference in headed mode**
Tests that use `pressSequentially()` for email or password fields in headed (non-headless) Chrome can fail intermittently because Chrome's autofill manager and password manager intercept keypress events and populate the field with saved credentials — overriding the test input mid-sequence.
WHY: `pressSequentially()` fires real keyboard events, which Chrome's autofill heuristics treat as genuine user input. When an email-like value is typed keystroke by keystroke into an `<input type="email">`, Chrome may override the field contents with a saved credential after the `@` symbol is typed. This only happens in headed mode (autofill is disabled in headless) and in tests running on a developer machine with saved passwords.
Fix: Use `page.getByLabel(...).fill(value)` for credentials — `fill()` bypasses keyboard event dispatch and sets the value directly, avoiding autofill triggers. If you genuinely need keystroke-by-keystroke behavior for the email field (live validation test), add `autocomplete="off"` to the test fixture's HTML, or run the test in headless mode only. Never test autocomplete behavior with real browser credential managers.

---

**Gotcha G149: `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` retry runs only the failing test body — preceding state-building steps are absent on retry**
With `mode: 'serial'`, if test N fails or becomes flaky, tests N+1 through the end of the describe block are all marked as skipped — they are not retried. If Playwright retries the failed test (due to `retries: 2`), it retries only that specific test in isolation, not the preceding steps that built the shared state. The subsequent tests then run on a page that lacks the state from steps 1 through N-1.
WHY: Serial mode shares a single browser context across all tests in the block by not recreating the page between tests. When a test fails, Playwright's retry mechanism re-runs just that test body — it does not re-run the whole describe block from the beginning. The retry sees the same empty-state page as a fresh test, not the accumulated state from the prior steps.
Fix: Add `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial', retries: 0 })` to disable retries for serial blocks — a retry on a shared-state test is almost always misleading. Instead, fix serial suite flakiness by adding explicit state restoration in `beforeEach` for each step, or restructure the flow as a single `test` with `test.step()` calls, which retries the entire flow on failure.

### Patterns

**Pattern 441: `page.exposeFunction()` for Node.js crypto and fs utilities in browser context** [official]
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as crypto from 'crypto';

test.beforeEach(async ({ context }) => {
  // Expose at context level so every page including popups has access
  await context.exposeFunction('sha256', (text: string) =>
    crypto.createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex')
  );
  await context.exposeFunction('nowMs', () => Date.now());
});

test('upload form signs payload before submission', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/upload');
  await page.getByLabel('File name').fill('report.pdf');

  // Compute signature using the exposed Node.js function
  const filename = 'report.pdf';
  const sig: string = await page.evaluate(
    async (name) => (window as any).sha256(name),
    filename
  );

  await page.getByTestId('signature-input').fill(sig);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText(/upload accepted/i);
});
```
Tradeoff: `exposeFunction` serializes arguments and return values across the Node↔browser boundary — primitives and plain objects work, but class instances, `Buffer`, `Uint8Array`, and `undefined` are dropped or coerced. Prefer registering at the `context` level rather than `page` level so popups and redirects inherit the binding without re-registration; page-level exposure must be re-applied to each new `Page` object.

---

**Pattern 442: `context.exposeBinding()` for page-aware Node.js callbacks** [official]
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('analytics module receives correct page URL on each navigation', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const urls: string[] = [];

  // exposeBinding passes {page, frame, browserContext} as first arg
  await context.exposeBinding('recordNavigation', ({ page: pg }, url: string) => {
    urls.push(`${pg.url()} -> ${url}`);
  });

  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    // Called by the app analytics module on each route change
    (window as any).__analyticsCallback = (url: string) =>
      (window as any).recordNavigation(url);
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /reports/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /settings/i }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /settings/i })).toBeVisible();
  expect(urls).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(urls[0]).toMatch(/dashboard.*reports/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `exposeBinding` provides the `{ page, frame, browserContext }` source metadata that `exposeFunction` lacks — use it when the Node.js callback needs to correlate the call with the originating page (e.g., multi-tab audit logging). The binding callback executes in the Node.js event loop synchronously before the browser resolves the awaited call; avoid blocking I/O inside it or the browser page will hang until the callback returns.

---

**Pattern 443: `page.addLocatorHandler()` for predictable overlay dismissal** [official]
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout completes even when cookie consent banner appears mid-flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register handler BEFORE navigation; fires automatically whenever the
  // locator becomes visible during any subsequent action
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie consent/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /accept all/i }).click();
      // Wait for dialog to leave DOM before Playwright retries the blocked action
      await dialog.waitFor({ state: 'detached' });
    },
    { noWaitAfter: false, times: 3 }
  );

  await page.goto('/shop');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).first().click();
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
  // Verify banner was dismissed (handler ran at least once)
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie consent/i })).not.toBeAttached();
});
```
Tradeoff: `addLocatorHandler` is designed for overlays that appear at unpredictable points in the test flow (cookie banners, newsletter modals, chat widgets). Do not use it to replace explicit state setup — if the banner should never appear in unit or integration environments, suppress it via feature flag or cookie seed instead of masking it with a handler. The `times` option prevents infinite loops when the dismissal action itself triggers a re-render of the overlay; omitting it risks an infinite dismiss cycle.
