**Pattern 615** — `locator.filter({ has })` with `locator.count()` for Conditional Test Branch
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('promotional banner is dismissed and does not reappear', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const promoBanner = page.getByRole('banner').filter({
    has: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Dismiss' }),
  });

  const bannerCount = await promoBanner.count();

  if (bannerCount > 0) {
    // Banner is present — dismiss it and assert it disappears
    await promoBanner.getByRole('button', { name: 'Dismiss' }).click();
    await expect(promoBanner).not.toBeAttached();

    // Navigate away and back — banner should not return in the same session
    await page.goto('/products');
    await page.goto('/');
    await expect(promoBanner).not.toBeAttached();
  } else {
    // Banner was already dismissed in this session (e.g., by a shared storageState)
    testInfo.annotations.push({
      type: 'info',
      description: 'Promotional banner was not present — may have been dismissed by auth fixture',
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `locator.count()` to branch test logic based on whether a UI element is present allows the test to handle optional or session-dependent UI elements gracefully — making the test robust against shared auth fixtures that might have already dismissed the banner — but conditional test branches mean the test has two execution paths, and only one is exercised per run; if the banner is never present in CI (because the shared `storageState` always pre-dismisses it), the primary test path never runs and regressions in the dismissal flow go undetected; ensure the banner is testable by using a fixture that provides a fresh, unauthenticated context for this specific test.

**Pattern 616** — `locator.pressSequentially()` for Character-by-Character Input with Live Validation
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('OTP input accepts digits one at a time and auto-advances focus', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/verify');

  // OTP fields react per-character — pressSequentially simulates real user typing
  const otpField = page.getByLabel('One-time passcode');
  await otpField.pressSequentially('123456', { delay: 50 });

  // After the last digit, the form should auto-submit
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Verification successful' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('search autocomplete shows suggestions after second character', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const searchBox = page.getByRole('searchbox');

  // Type 'wi' one character at a time — 'w' alone should not trigger suggestions
  await searchBox.pressSequentially('w', { delay: 30 });
  await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).not.toBeVisible();

  await searchBox.pressSequentially('i', { delay: 30 });
  await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('option')).toHaveCount(5);
});

test('credit card number field formats input with spaces on each group', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');
  const cardField = page.getByLabel('Card number');

  await cardField.pressSequentially('4242424242424242', { delay: 10 });

  // Masked input field should show formatted value with spaces
  await expect(cardField).toHaveValue('4242 4242 4242 4242');
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.pressSequentially(text, { delay })` fires individual key events per character at a configurable rate, which is required for inputs that respond to keystroke events for masking, validation, or autocomplete triggering — but it is significantly slower than `locator.fill(text)` which writes the entire value atomically without key events; only use `pressSequentially` when character-level event handling is the specific behavior under test and use `fill` for all other text inputs to keep the test suite fast.

**Pattern 617** — `expect(locator).toHaveCount()` Guarded by Loading-State Assertion
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('search results list shows exactly 10 items after full load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search?q=playwright');

  // Wait for the loading skeleton to detach before asserting result count
  // Prevents toHaveCount() from resolving during the transient empty state
  await expect(page.getByTestId('results-skeleton')).not.toBeAttached({ timeout: 10_000 });

  // Now assert the stable, final count
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(10);
});

test('filtered product list updates count correctly after filter change', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(20); // initial unfiltered count

  await page.getByLabel('Category').selectOption('Electronics');

  // Spinner appears during re-fetch — wait for it to disappear before counting
  await expect(page.getByTestId('filter-loading-spinner')).not.toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(7); // electronics only
});

test('paginated list shows correct count per page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/invoices?page=2');

  // Wait for the page-number indicator to confirm we are on page 2
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation').getByText('Page 2 of 5')).toBeVisible();

  // Now assert exactly 10 items per page
  await expect(page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('columnheader') }))
    .toHaveCount(10);
});
```
Tradeoff: Waiting for a loading indicator to disappear before asserting `toHaveCount()` ensures the assertion runs against the stable final state rather than a transient render state — but it requires every list component to expose a consistent loading signal (`data-testid="skeleton"`, `aria-busy`, or a spinner) that tests can wait on; if the component renders loading state inconsistently across different query types (some show a spinner, others show a skeleton, some show nothing), each test must know which signal to wait for, increasing coupling between tests and component implementation details.

**Pattern 618** — `page.evaluate()` with Explicit JSON-Serializable Arguments
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('slider value is within specified bounds after drag', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/range-picker');

  const slider = page.getByRole('slider');
  await slider.dragTo(page.getByTestId('range-midpoint'));

  // Pass min/max as explicit args — never capture from outer TS scope in a closure
  const { min, max } = { min: 0, max: 100 };
  const isInRange = await page.evaluate(
    ({ min, max }) => {
      const slider = document.querySelector('[role="slider"]') as HTMLInputElement;
      const value = parseFloat(slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0');
      return value >= min && value <= max;
    },
    { min, max } // serializable plain object — no Map, Set, Date, or class instances
  );

  expect(isInRange).toBe(true);
});

test('reading multiple DOM properties atomically avoids race conditions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');

  // Read badge count and total simultaneously in one evaluate call
  const { badgeCount, totalText } = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    badgeCount: parseInt(
      document.querySelector('[data-testid="cart-badge"]')?.textContent ?? '0',
      10
    ),
    totalText: document.querySelector('[data-testid="cart-total"]')?.textContent ?? '$0.00',
  }));

  expect(badgeCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  expect(totalText).toMatch(/^\$\d+\.\d{2}$/);
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing values as explicit arguments to `page.evaluate()` correctly serializes primitives, plain objects, and arrays — but `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, `RegExp`, and class instances are silently converted to `{}` or lose their prototype; when you need to pass a `Date`, serialize it to `date.toISOString()` before passing and reconstruct with `new Date(iso)` inside the evaluate body; add a TypeScript utility type `type Jsonable = ...` that rejects non-serializable types at the call site to enforce this contract statically across the codebase.

**Pattern 619** — `test.afterAll()` with `try/catch` and `testInfo.annotations` for JUnit-Safe Teardown
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

let createdResourceIds: string[] = [];

test.afterAll(async ({ request }, testInfo) => {
  // Clean up all resources created during the describe block
  for (const id of createdResourceIds) {
    try {
      const res = await request.delete(`/api/test/resources/${id}`);
      if (!res.ok()) {
        // Surface as annotation — not as a throw — to keep JUnit report clean
        testInfo.annotations.push({
          type: 'warning',
          description: `Cleanup failed for resource ${id}: HTTP ${res.status()}`,
        });
      }
    } catch (err) {
      testInfo.annotations.push({
        type: 'warning',
        description: `Cleanup exception for resource ${id}: ${(err as Error).message}`,
      });
    }
  }
  createdResourceIds = []; // reset for next run
});

test('creating a resource adds it to the list', async ({ page, request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/test/resources', { data: { name: 'Test Item' } });
  expect(res.ok()).toBeTruthy();
  const { id } = await res.json();
  createdResourceIds.push(id); // track for cleanup

  await page.goto('/resources');
  await expect(page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasText: 'Test Item' })).toHaveCount(1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping `afterAll` cleanup in `try/catch` with annotation reporting prevents teardown exceptions from marking an entire JUnit describe block as failed — which is the correct behavior for cleanup failures that do not invalidate test assertions — but it also means cleanup failures are easy to miss if engineers do not review test annotations; set up a CI step that scans for `type: 'warning'` annotations in the test results XML and sends a Slack alert when cleanup warnings accumulate across multiple runs, indicating a systemic teardown reliability issue.

**Pattern 620** — Scoped `page.route()` Patterns Using Regex to Prevent Accidental CDP Interception
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('all API requests are intercepted by scoped route handler', async ({ page }) => {
  const interceptedUrls: string[] = [];

  // CORRECT: scoped regex targets only /api/ paths — never catches CDP or extension URLs
  await page.route(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+\/api\//, async (route) => {
    interceptedUrls.push(route.request().url());
    await route.continue(); // forward to real server; replace with fulfill() to mock
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Dashboard' })).toBeVisible();

  // Verify we only intercepted application API calls, not browser internals
  expect(interceptedUrls.every(url => url.includes('/api/'))).toBe(true);
  expect(interceptedUrls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});

test('blocking third-party trackers does not affect application routes', async ({ page }) => {
  const blockedDomains = ['google-analytics.com', 'doubleclick.net', 'hotjar.com'];

  // Block each tracker domain explicitly — not with a catch-all
  for (const domain of blockedDomains) {
    await page.route(new RegExp(`https?://.*${domain.replace('.', '\\.')}/`), route =>
      route.abort('blockedbyclient')
    );
  }

  // Application routes should load normally
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Using a regex anchored to `^https?://[^/]+/api/` ensures the route handler only matches URLs where `/api/` appears as the first path segment — preventing accidental matches against third-party CDN URLs like `cdn.example.com/assets/api-docs/` — but regex patterns in `page.route()` are evaluated against the full URL string (not just the path), so a pattern that works for `http://localhost:3000/api/` may not match `https://api.myapp.com/users/` if the API is hosted on a subdomain; test route patterns against your actual application URL shapes using a temporary `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.url()))` listener before writing the pattern.

### Community Gotchas

**G205** — `locator.type()` is deprecated; calling it on Playwright >= 1.38 produces warning noise in CI logs
Why this matters: `locator.type(text)` was deprecated in Playwright 1.38 in favor of `locator.pressSequentially(text)`. The method still works but emits a deprecation warning to `process.stderr` on every call. In CI environments that treat any stderr output as an error (some GitHub Actions configurations and bash scripts with `set -e pipefail`), this warning can cause otherwise-passing tests to trigger CI job failures. Teams that have hundreds of `type()` calls across a large test suite discover the problem only after upgrading Playwright, when their CI pipeline suddenly shows dozens of new "failures" that are actually just deprecation warnings.
Fix: Replace all `await locator.type(text)` calls with `await locator.pressSequentially(text)` — the behavior is identical (character-by-character keydown/keypress/keyup/input events). Run a project-wide find-replace: search for `\.type\(` and replace with `.pressSequentially(`. Add an ESLint rule from `eslint-plugin-playwright` to ban the `type` method to prevent reintroduction. Confirm zero warnings appear in CI log output after migration.

---

**G206** — `expect(locator).toHaveCount(n)` passes during a transient render state before the final count is reached
Why this matters: When a search results list loads incrementally — rendering the first batch of 5 items while the next batch of 5 is still in-flight — `expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(5)` can resolve as soon as the first batch renders, before the second batch arrives. The test passes with 5 items even though the correct final count is 10. This is most common with virtual-scroll implementations, paginated API calls that resolve in parallel, or React Suspense boundaries that render partial data. The failure is silent: the count assertion passes but subsequent assertions (e.g., `toHaveText` on the 8th item) fail with an index-out-of-range error.
Fix: Wait for a terminal loading signal before asserting count: `await expect(page.getByTestId('loading-more-indicator')).not.toBeAttached()` or `await expect(page.getByTestId('results-count-label')).toHaveText('10 results')`. If no explicit loading signal exists, assert a specific item from the second batch by content: `await expect(page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Item 10' })).toBeVisible()` — which will retry until the second batch renders.

---

**G207** — `page.evaluate()` with class instances silently receives empty objects `{}` instead of the original value
Why this matters: `page.evaluate((map) => map.size, new Map([['key', 'val']]))` passes a `Map` as the argument, which Playwright serializes using the structured-clone algorithm. `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, `RegExp`, and class instances are not supported by structured clone in Playwright's Node.js-to-browser serialization path — `Map` arrives as `{}` in the browser, and `{}.size` is `undefined` rather than `1`. TypeScript does not catch this because the closure signature accepts `any`. The test may pass vacuously (the predicate returns a falsy value that happens to match), or fail with a confusing `undefined is not a number` error in the browser evaluation context.
Fix: Convert non-serializable types to their JSON-equivalent before passing: `await page.evaluate((arr) => arr.length, Array.from(myMap.entries()))`. For `Date`, pass `date.toISOString()` and reconstruct with `new Date(iso)` inside the browser. For class instances, pass a plain object of the relevant properties. Add a utility type `Serializable<T>` to enforce that `page.evaluate()` arguments are JSON-safe at the TypeScript type level using conditional types.

---

**G208** — `test.afterAll()` failures in a describe block cause JUnit test reports to mark the entire block failed
Why this matters: Playwright's JUnit reporter marks a `describe` block as failed when `test.afterAll()` throws — even if every individual test inside the block passed all assertions. Jenkins, GitHub Actions test summaries, and similar CI platforms that parse JUnit XML interpret the describe-block failure as test failures, causing the build to turn red. The failure message in the JUnit XML is the teardown error (e.g., "database connection timeout") rather than a test assertion, making it appear that the tests failed for an unrelated reason. Teams spend hours debugging "failing tests" that are actually passing — the teardown is the only broken part.
Fix: Wrap `test.afterAll()` teardown in `try/catch` and report failures as annotations rather than thrown exceptions: `catch (err) { testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'warning', description: String(err) }) }`. Reserve uncaught throws from `test.afterAll()` only for corrupting-state failures where subsequent test runs would be invalid (e.g., a test schema left in a broken migration state). Prefer using `{ scope: 'worker' }` fixtures with proper teardown blocks for cleanup — fixture teardown failures are attributed per-test rather than per-describe-block.

---

**G209** — `page.route('**', handler)` accidentally intercepts Playwright's internal browser protocol requests
Why this matters: The glob `'**'` in `page.route('**', handler)` matches every URL including Playwright's internal Chrome DevTools Protocol extension URLs (`chrome-extension://...`), service worker scope URLs, and DevTools-injected scripts. When the handler calls `route.fulfill()` for all matched requests, Playwright's internal bookkeeping receives incorrect responses, causing coverage collection to fail silently, trace files to be incomplete, and in some Chromium versions, an unhandled WebSocket disconnect that crashes the test with a non-descriptive `Target closed` error.
Fix: Never use `'**'` as a catch-all route pattern. Always scope patterns to your application's URL space: `'*/**/api/**'` for API routes or `new RegExp(process.env.APP_URL + '/api/')` for environment-aware matching. For passive request observation (logging, asserting request presence), use `page.on('request', handler)` which does not intercept the request and cannot corrupt Playwright internals. If you need to block all external domains, enumerate them explicitly: `page.route(/.*\.(analytics|tracking)\.(com|io)/, r => r.abort())`.

### Patterns

**Pattern 621** — `locator.filter({ visible: true })` for Strict Visible-Element Count Assertions
```typescript
// e2e/specs/active-items.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('only active (visible) list items are counted after filter is applied', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/todos');

  // Create 3 todos, mark one complete
  for (const t of ['Task A', 'Task B', 'Task C']) {
    await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'New todo' }).fill(t);
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  }
  await page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Task A' })
    .getByRole('checkbox').check();

  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Active' }).click();

  // Without filter({ visible: true }) getByRole('listitem') would still match
  // all 3 items including the completed one hidden by display:none —
  // causing strict-mode violation or wrong toHaveCount result
  const visibleTodos = page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ visible: true });

  await expect(visibleTodos).toHaveCount(2);
  await expect(visibleTodos.nth(0)).toHaveText('Task B');
  await expect(visibleTodos.nth(1)).toHaveText('Task C');
});
```
Tradeoff: `filter({ visible: true })` (v1.51) excludes elements hidden by `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or `opacity: 0`, and elements with zero bounding boxes — but elements placed off-screen with `position: absolute; left: -9999px` and a non-zero height still pass the visibility check because `isVisible()` does not test viewport intersection; use `clip-path: inset(50%)` with `width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden` instead of off-screen positioning for accessible-hide patterns so `isVisible()` correctly returns false.

**Pattern 622** — `storageState({ indexedDB: true })` for Firebase Authentication Snapshot
```typescript
// e2e/setup/firebase-auth.ts
import { chromium, type FullConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import { mkdirSync } from 'fs';
import { join }      from 'path';

export default async function setup(_config: FullConfig): Promise<void> {
  const authDir = join('playwright', '.auth');
  mkdirSync(authDir, { recursive: true });

  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page    = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto(process.env.APP_URL + '/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.QA_EMAIL!);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.QA_PASSWORD!);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();

  // Firebase Auth v9 + Google Identity Platform store the session token under
  // 'firebase:authUser:...' in IndexedDB — NOT in localStorage or cookies.
  // Without indexedDB: true the saved state looks valid but restores to an
  // unauthenticated context because the IDB token is absent.
  await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard', { timeout: 15_000 });
  await context.storageState({
    path:      join(authDir, 'firebase-user.json'),
    indexedDB: true,
  });

  await browser.close();
}
```
Tradeoff: `indexedDB: true` (v1.51) serializes every IDB database and object store for the origin — apps that pre-populate a large data cache (product catalogue, offline documents) into IDB before the login page is done will produce a 20–100 MB snapshot that adds seconds to context creation for every test; block data-fetching routes with `context.route('**/api/**', r => r.fulfill({ body: '[]' }))` during setup to prevent IDB data stores from being populated, keeping the snapshot to auth-token stores only.

---

**Pattern 623** — `test.step.skip()` for Browser-Engine-Conditional Step Suppression
```typescript
// e2e/specs/share-feature.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('share button flow — Web Share API available on Chromium only', async ({
  page, browserName,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/articles/first-post');

  await test.step('article is displayed', async () => {
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })
    ).toBeVisible();
  });

  await test.step('native share sheet via Web Share API', async (step) => {
    // Web Share API is only available in Chromium-based browsers
    step.skip(
      browserName !== 'chromium',
      'Web Share API unavailable in this browser — skipping step'
    );

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /share/i }).click();
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /share/i })
    ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  });

  await test.step('copy-link fallback is always present', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /copy link/i }).click();
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('status')
    ).toContainText(/copied/i);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `step.skip()` (v1.50 `TestStepInfo`) marks only that step as skipped while the test continues and ultimately reports "passed" — correct when a single browser-specific API is absent — but the step-level skip is invisible at the test-level in HTML summary rows, JUnit XML, and GitHub Actions annotations; to surface the skip to monitoring pipelines, add `testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'skip', description: reason })` inside the skipped step body.

---

**Pattern 624** — `expect(locator).toContainClass()` for Class-List Order-Independent State Testing
```typescript
// e2e/specs/accordion.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('accordion panels toggle the correct expanded/collapsed CSS classes', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/components/accordion');

  const firstPanel = page.getByRole('region').first();
  const firstTrigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Section 1' });

  // toHaveClass() requires exact full class string — breaks when animation
  // frameworks inject transient classes like 'is-animating'.
  // toContainClass() checks one class at a time, order-independent.
  await expect(firstPanel).toContainClass('accordion__panel');
  await expect(firstPanel).toContainClass('accordion__panel--collapsed');
  await expect(firstPanel).not.toContainClass('accordion__panel--expanded');

  await firstTrigger.click();

  await expect(firstPanel).toContainClass('accordion__panel--expanded');
  await expect(firstPanel).not.toContainClass('accordion__panel--collapsed');

  // Structural base class persists across both states
  await expect(firstPanel).toContainClass('accordion__panel');
});
```
Tradeoff: `toContainClass()` (v1.52) checks a single class name independent of the full class list — resilient to ordering and additive animation classes — but cannot detect the mutual-exclusion bug where `accordion__panel--expanded` and `accordion__panel--collapsed` both exist simultaneously; add `expect(firstPanel).not.toHaveClass(/accordion__panel--expanded.*accordion__panel--collapsed/)` to explicitly guard against the coexistence case.

---

**Pattern 625** — Aria Snapshot `/children deep-equal` for Release-Gate Navigation Integrity
```typescript
// e2e/specs/navigation-integrity.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('application header contains exactly the approved navigation links', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // /children deep-equal fails if any link is added, removed, or reordered —
  // use on release branch to prevent undisclosed navigation changes shipping
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Primary' })
  ).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Primary":
      - /children deep-equal:
        - link "Dashboard"
        - link "Projects"
        - link "Reports"
        - link "Settings"
  `);
});

test('footer legal links resolve to correct destinations', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // /url asserts the accessible href alongside the link name (v1.52)
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('contentinfo')
  ).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - contentinfo:
      - link "Privacy Policy" [url="/legal/privacy"]
      - link "Terms of Service" [url="/legal/terms"]
      - link "Cookie Settings" [url="/legal/cookies"]
  `);
});
```
Tradeoff: `/children deep-equal` rejects any addition, removal, or reorder — ideal for security audits asserting no unauthorized links are present in production navigation — but it blocks every PR during active feature development when nav items are frequently added; keep `deep-equal` confined to a `navigation-release-gate.spec.ts` that runs only in the release pipeline, and use `/children contain` mode in development-branch tests.

**Pattern 626** — Worker-Indexed Auth Accounts to Eliminate Cross-Worker State Collisions
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/isolated-auth.fixture.ts
import { test as base, chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import { join }                   from 'path';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync }  from 'fs';

type IsolatedAuthFixtures = { isolatedUser: { email: string; index: number } };

export const test = base.extend<{}, IsolatedAuthFixtures>({
  isolatedUser: [
    async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
      const idx      = workerInfo.workerIndex;
      const email    = `qa-worker-${idx}@example.com`;
      const authDir  = join('playwright', '.auth');
      const authFile = join(authDir, `isolated-${idx}.json`);

      mkdirSync(authDir, { recursive: true });

      if (!existsSync(authFile)) {
        const browser  = await chromium.launch();
        const context  = await browser.newContext();
        const page     = await context.newPage();
        await page.goto(process.env.APP_URL + '/login');
        await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(email);
        await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.TEST_PASS!);
        await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
        await page.waitForURL('**/app');
        await context.storageState({ path: authFile });
        await browser.close();
      }

      await use({ email, index: idx });
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

test('profile update is scoped to the worker\'s isolated account', async ({
  page, isolatedUser,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/profile');
  const newBio = `Worker ${isolatedUser.index} bio — ${Date.now()}`;
  await page.getByLabel('Bio').fill(newBio);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText(newBio)).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Worker-indexed accounts guarantee zero cross-worker data collisions at the cost of provisioning N test accounts (where N equals `--workers`) — this is handled by a seed script for self-hosted databases but is costly on per-seat SaaS platforms; use a distributed lock (e.g., a Postgres advisory lock or Redis SETNX) to allocate accounts dynamically from a smaller shared pool if per-seat licensing makes N accounts impractical.

**Pattern 627** — `mergeTests()` Combining Database and Accessibility Fixture Modules
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/db.fixture.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const dbTest = base.extend<{ dbProduct: { id: string; name: string } }>({
  // Module-prefixed name eliminates mergeTests() collision risk
  dbProduct: async ({}, use) => {
    const product = { id: 'prod-001', name: 'Widget Pro' };
    await use(product);
    // teardown: DELETE product from test database
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/a11y.fixture.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder              from '@axe-core/playwright';

export const a11yTest = base.extend<{
  a11yScan: (scope?: string) => Promise<void>;
}>({
  a11yScan: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(async (scope = 'html') => {
      const res = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .include(scope)
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
        .analyze();
      expect(res.violations, 'axe violations').toHaveLength(0);
    });
  },
});

// e2e/fixtures/combined.ts
import { mergeTests } from '@playwright/test';
import { dbTest }     from './db.fixture';
import { a11yTest }   from './a11y.fixture';

export const test = mergeTests(dbTest, a11yTest);

// e2e/specs/product.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/combined';

test('product detail page is accessible with real seeded data', async ({
  page, dbProduct, a11yScan,
}) => {
  await page.goto(`/products/${dbProduct.id}`);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: dbProduct.name })).toBeVisible();
  await a11yScan('main');
});
```
Tradeoff: `mergeTests()` composes orthogonal fixture sets without boilerplate re-exports — but silently adopts the last-argument fixture when two modules share a name; enforce a module-prefix naming convention (`dbProduct`, `a11yScan`, `mailMessages`) to make accidental collisions structurally impossible without a deliberate naming-convention violation.

**Pattern 628** — `{ box: true }` Fixture for Collapsing Auth Flow in Trace Viewer
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/boxed-login.fixture.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

export const test = base.extend<{ signedIn: void }>({
  // box: true collapses all internal auth steps into one "signedIn" entry
  // in the trace viewer — keeps the trace timeline focused on test-specific
  // interactions rather than 5 login sub-steps on every single test
  signedIn: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      await page.goto('/auth/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('qa@example.com');
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Passw0rd!');
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
      await page.waitForURL('**/app/home');
      await use();
      await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.clear());
    },
    { box: true },
  ],
});

// Test traces show one atomic "signedIn" step, not 5 auth sub-steps
test('home feed renders the welcome message', async ({ page, signedIn }) => {
  await page.goto('/app/home');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /welcome/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `{ box: true }` makes the auth fixture appear as one collapsed entry in traces — excellent for readability when every test uses the same auth flow — but hides internal step details when the fixture itself has a bug; remove `{ box: true }` temporarily when debugging fixture-level failures so the step tree becomes visible, then restore it before merging.

**Pattern 629** — Option Fixtures for Per-Project Feature-Flag and Locale Matrix
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/project-config.fixture.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type ConfigOptions  = { appLocale: string; betaFeatures: boolean };
type ConfigFixtures = { configPage: (path: string) => Promise<void> };

export const test = base.extend<ConfigOptions & ConfigFixtures>({
  appLocale:    ['en-US', { option: true }],
  betaFeatures: [false,   { option: true }],

  configPage: async ({ page, appLocale, betaFeatures }, use) => {
    await use(async (path: string) => {
      await page.goto(path);
      await page.evaluate(
        ([locale, beta]) => {
          localStorage.setItem('locale', locale);
          localStorage.setItem('beta',   String(beta));
        },
        [appLocale, String(betaFeatures)] as [string, string]
      );
      await page.reload();
      await expect(page.locator('[data-app-ready]')).toBeAttached();
    });
  },
});

// playwright.config.ts:
// projects: [
//   { name: 'en-stable', use: { appLocale: 'en-US', betaFeatures: false } },
//   { name: 'en-beta',   use: { appLocale: 'en-US', betaFeatures: true  } },
//   { name: 'de-stable', use: { appLocale: 'de-DE', betaFeatures: false } },
// ]

import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/project-config.fixture';

test('beta feature badge is shown only when beta mode is active', async ({
  configPage, page, betaFeatures,
}) => {
  await configPage('/dashboard');
  const badge = page.getByTestId('beta-badge');
  if (betaFeatures) {
    await expect(badge).toBeVisible();
  } else {
    await expect(badge).not.toBeVisible();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Option fixtures drive an N-environment matrix from a single spec file via `playwright.config.ts` project definitions — eliminating duplicated spec files — but option values are frozen at worker startup and cannot change mid-test; tests that verify the feature-flag toggle UI interaction must use a separate non-option fixture that writes to `localStorage` dynamically rather than relying on the option value.

---

**Pattern 630** — `AxeBuilder.withTags()` Route-Scoped WCAG 2.1 AA Audit With `testInfo.attach()`
```typescript
// e2e/specs/wcag-audit.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder       from '@axe-core/playwright';

const CRITICAL_ROUTES = ['/login', '/checkout', '/dashboard', '/settings'];

for (const route of CRITICAL_ROUTES) {
  test(`${route} satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA`, async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto(route);
    await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
      .exclude('[data-a11y-pending]')
      .analyze();

    await testInfo.attach(`violations-${route.replaceAll('/', '_')}.json`, {
      body:        Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2)),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });

    expect(
      results.violations.filter(v => ['critical', 'serious'].includes(v.impact ?? '')),
      `Critical/serious WCAG violations on ${route}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: `withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])` satisfies WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 A/AA compliance requirements — but WCAG 2.2 criteria (focus appearance, target minimum size, dragging motions) require adding `'wcag22a'` and `'wcag22aa'`; pin `@axe-core/playwright` to a release that documents 2.2 rule support and validate coverage by running `axe.getRules(['wcag22aa']).length > 0` in a smoke test before declaring 2.2 conformance.

**Pattern 631** — `test.step()` Per-Step `timeout` to Isolate Slow Server-Side Operations
```typescript
// e2e/specs/bulk-export.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('bulk PDF export completes within 90-second SLA', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/export');

  await test.step('configure export', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Scope' }).selectOption('all-time');
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Format' }).selectOption('PDF');
  });

  const dlReady = page.waitForEvent('download');

  // Export job runs server-side and can take up to 80 seconds for large datasets.
  // Step-level timeout isolates this budget — other steps retain the global 30s.
  await test.step(
    'start export and await file download',
    async () => {
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export' }).click();
      const dl = await dlReady;
      expect(dl.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.pdf$/i);
    },
    { timeout: 90_000 }
  );

  await test.step('verify success notification', async () => {
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('status', { name: /export complete/i })
    ).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Per-step `timeout` (v1.50) gives the slow export its own time budget without inflating the global `testTimeout` for the whole spec file — preventing the long step from masking unrelated timeout regressions — but the timeout does not cascade into nested sub-`test.step()` calls; inner steps inherit the global `testTimeout`, so flatten deeply nested slow operations to a single `test.step()` level when the budget must cover the composed operation.

---

**Pattern 632** — `TestStepInfo.attach()` for Inline PDF and Screenshot Evidence
```typescript
// e2e/specs/invoice-audit.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('invoice PDF download attaches evidence to the HTML report', async ({
  page, request,
}) => {
  const flags = await (await request.get('/api/flags')).json() as {
    pdfInvoices: boolean;
  };

  await page.goto('/invoices/INV-00042');

  await test.step('download invoice PDF', async (stepInfo) => {
    stepInfo.skip(!flags.pdfInvoices, 'PDF invoices not enabled in this environment');

    const dlPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Download PDF' }).click();
    const dl = await dlPromise;

    const savedPath = await dl.path();
    if (savedPath) {
      // Attach PDF inline — visible as a link in the HTML report step detail
      await stepInfo.attach('INV-00042.pdf', {
        path:        savedPath,
        contentType: 'application/pdf',
      });
    }

    expect(dl.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/INV-00042.*\.pdf$/);
  });

  await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-status')).toHaveText('Paid');
});
```
Tradeoff: `stepInfo.attach()` (v1.51) embeds files inline in the HTML report as base64 data URIs for one-click inspection — but large binary attachments (multi-page PDFs, videos) inflate the HTML file itself; configure the HTML reporter with `doNotInlineAssets: true` and `attachmentsBaseURL` pointing to S3 or Azure Blob Storage so the report file stays small while each attachment is accessible via an external URL.

---

**Pattern 633** — `captureGitInfo` to Embed Commit SHA and Message in HTML Reports
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // captureGitInfo (v1.51): runs `git log` at startup and embeds the commit
  // SHA, author, and subject line in the HTML report header so that engineers
  // inspecting a report published hours after its generating push can
  // immediately trace back to the specific code change that introduced a failure.
  captureGitInfo: {
    commit: true,
    diff:   false,   // skip full diff — prevents large patches bloating the report
  },

  reporter: [
    ['html', {
      open:        'never',
      outputFolder: 'playwright-report',
    }],
    ['github'],
  ],

  use: {
    baseURL:    process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace:      'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },

  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,

  projects: [
    { name: 'chrome',  use: { channel: 'chrome' } },
    { name: 'firefox'                              },
    { name: 'webkit'                               },
  ],
});
```
Tradeoff: `captureGitInfo` adds ~50 ms cold-start overhead from the `git log` subprocess and silently produces blank git metadata when `.git` is absent from the Docker image layer — common when `.dockerignore` excludes `.git` to reduce image size; validate by checking `git rev-parse HEAD` succeeds inside the CI container before running tests, and mount `.git` as a read-only volume if the image layer excludes it.

---

**Pattern 634** — `failOnFlakyTests` Paired With `retries: 2` as a Hard CI Flake Gate
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // failOnFlakyTests is a no-op without retries > 0.
  // "Flaky" means: failed on attempt N, passed on attempt N+1 (within the same run).
  // With retries: 0 there are no subsequent attempts — "flaky" is impossible.
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,

  // Exit code 1 when any test is classified flaky (passed only after a retry).
  // Prevents teams from merging code that introduces intermittent failures.
  failOnFlakyTests: !!process.env.CI,

  reporter: [
    ['github'],
    ['html', { open: 'never' }],
    ['json', { outputFile: 'results.json' }],
  ],

  use: {
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
    video: 'retain-on-failure',
  },

  // Quarantine: tag known-flaky tests with @flaky and run CI as:
  // npx playwright test --grep-invert @flaky
  // This preserves the gate for new regressions while excluding tracked flakes.
});
```
Tradeoff: `failOnFlakyTests: true` blocks PR merges the moment any test requires a retry, making flakiness a first-class defect — but it misfires during CI infrastructure degradation (slow runners, network brownouts) where tests are correct but the environment is unreliable; use `@flaky` tagging with `--grep-invert @flaky` to quarantine environment-flaky tests while keeping the gate active for newly introduced test regressions.

---

**Pattern 635** — Per-Project `workers` Count for Engine-Specific Parallelism Optimization
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  workers: 4,  // global default, overridden per project below

  projects: [
    {
      name:    'chrome-smoke',
      use:     { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      grep:    /@smoke/,
      workers: 8,    // Smoke tests are fast and independent — maximize throughput
    },
    {
      name:    'firefox-full',
      use:     { ...devices['Desktop Firefox'] },
      workers: 2,    // Firefox renderer is heavier — cap to avoid OOM on 4-core CI
    },
    {
      name:    'webkit-e2e',
      use:     { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] },
      workers: 1,    // WebKit has socket-contention flakiness at > 1 on Linux CI
    },
    {
      name:    'mobile',
      use:     { ...devices['Pixel 5'] },
      workers: 4,
    },
  ],
});
```
Tradeoff: Per-project `workers` (v1.52) enables fine-grained parallelism tuning per browser — smoke tests run at 8x parallelism while serial-safe WebKit tests use 1 worker — reducing total CI wall time without OOM failures — but this setting does not interact with sharding: `--shard=2/4` partitions tests before per-project `workers` applies, so a `workers: 1` project creates a serial bottleneck inside its shard while other projects in the same shard run at full concurrency, producing uneven shard completion times that inflate total CI duration.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G210** — `storageState({ indexedDB: true })` Captures All IDB Stores — Data Caches Inflate Snapshot Size
Why this matters: `browserContext.storageState({ path: 'auth.json', indexedDB: true })` serializes every IndexedDB database and object store registered under the origin. Applications that pre-populate large datasets (product catalogues, document lists, offline assets) into IDB before the login flow completes will produce auth snapshots of 20–100 MB. Every test that loads `storageState: 'auth.json'` pays the full deserialization cost at context creation time. Teams migrating from cookie-based auth to Firebase IDB auth discover this only when CI wall time triples and artifact storage costs spike, with no code changes to the test setup explaining the sudden bloat.
Fix: During global setup, intercept all data-fetching routes before navigating to the login page: `await context.route('**/api/**', r => r.fulfill({ status: 200, body: '[]', contentType: 'application/json' }))`. This prevents the app from populating IDB data stores during auth capture so only the auth token stores are serialized. Add a CI assertion on file size: `const size = fs.statSync('playwright/.auth/user.json').size; if (size > 512_000) throw new Error(`auth snapshot too large: ${size}`)` to catch future data-cache regressions early.

---

**G211** — `stepInfo.skip()` Is Invisible at the Test Level — HTML Summary Rows Always Show "Passed"
Why this matters: When `stepInfo.skip(condition, reason)` is called inside a `test.step()` body, Playwright marks the step as skipped in the trace and in the expanded step-detail view of the HTML report. The test continues executing remaining steps and ultimately reports "passed" at the test level. The test-level pass/fail/skip counters, JUnit XML `<skipped>` elements, and GitHub Actions inline annotations all remain unchanged — the skip is invisible in every monitoring pipeline that reads test-level outcomes. Teams using skip counts to track "tests that could not verify a feature in this environment" discover that `stepInfo.skip()` is systematically excluded from their metrics, producing over-reported environment coverage.
Fix: Push an explicit test-level annotation from inside the step body: `testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'skip', description: `Step '${stepName}' skipped: ${reason}` })`. This annotation surfaces in the HTML report test-row detail panel, in the JSON reporter output, and in JUnit XML `<properties>` so it is visible to all downstream consumers. For systematic per-environment skips affecting multiple tests, prefer structuring tests into separate `test.describe` blocks gated by `test.skip(featureDisabled, reason)` in `beforeEach` so the entire test is classifiably skipped.

---

**G212** — `mergeTests(a, b)` Silent Last-Arg-Wins Collision on Identically Named Fixtures
Why this matters: `mergeTests(authTest, dbTest)` merges fixture registrations from both modules. When both define a fixture with the same identifier — for example both export a `setup` fixture — `mergeTests` silently adopts `dbTest`'s definition and discards `authTest`'s. There is no TypeScript compile error (the type system sees only the merged export), no runtime warning, and no log message. The first symptom is test failures where auth setup steps are missing or produce unexpected state. Because the collision is invisible in the type system and produces no diagnostic, engineers typically spend hours debugging test logic before discovering the fixture shadowing.
Fix: Enforce a module-prefix naming convention across all fixture files: `authSetup`, `dbSeedUser`, `mailMessages` — never the generic `setup`, `user`, or `data`. Add a CI lint script that reads all `test.extend()` calls and fails the build if any fixture name appears in more than one module without an explicit override annotation. If a collision is intentional, document it with a comment at the `mergeTests()` call site: `// intentional: dbTest.setup supersedes authTest.setup for this integration suite`.

---

**G213** — `captureGitInfo` Silently Produces Empty Report Metadata When `.git` Is Not on Disk
Why this matters: `captureGitInfo: { commit: true }` runs `git log -1 --format=...` at Playwright runner startup. Docker images built with `.dockerignore` entries that exclude `.git` — a common practice to reduce image size — have no git repository on disk. The `git` command exits non-zero, Playwright catches the error without logging a warning, and the HTML report is generated with blank commit SHA, author, and message fields. Engineers reviewing the report assume the empty fields indicate a configuration bug and file CI infra tickets for a non-issue that will never reproduce outside Docker.
Fix: Add a pre-test CI step: `git rev-parse HEAD || { echo "ERROR: .git absent — captureGitInfo will produce blank report metadata"; exit 1; }`. In Docker-based CI, mount `.git` as a read-only volume: `-v $(pwd)/.git:/workspace/.git:ro`. If mounting `.git` is not feasible, disable `captureGitInfo` and inject commit metadata via environment variables read by a custom `onBegin()` reporter hook that writes to the HTML report title via the `title` option.

---

**G214** — `failOnFlakyTests: true` With `retries: 0` Has Zero Observable Effect
Why this matters: Playwright classifies a test as "flaky" only when it fails on one or more attempts and passes on a later retry within the same invocation. With `retries: 0` (the framework default), every test has exactly one attempt — "flaky" is structurally impossible — and every outcome is either "passed" or "failed". Setting `failOnFlakyTests: true` without a corresponding `retries: 2` produces a configuration that loads and runs silently without errors but never triggers the non-zero exit code. Teams add `failOnFlakyTests: true` expecting immediate protection against intermittent failures, observe zero change in CI behavior, and incorrectly conclude the feature is broken — when in fact `retries` was simply not configured.
Fix: Always co-locate `failOnFlakyTests` and `retries` as a single logical block: `retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0, failOnFlakyTests: !!process.env.CI`. Write a CI pre-flight check that evaluates the exported Playwright config and exits non-zero when `failOnFlakyTests === true && retries === 0`: `node -e "const cfg = require('./playwright.config'); const c = cfg.default; if (c.failOnFlakyTests && !c.retries) process.exit(1)"`. Validate end-to-end by inserting a `Math.random() < 0.5`-gated throw in one test, running with `CI=true`, and verifying exit code 1 with "flaky" in the output.

**Pattern 636** — `video: { show: { actions, test } }` Annotated Video Recording (v1.60+)
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  use: {
    // v1.60+: video sub-options embed visual action and test-name overlays
    video: {
      mode:    'retain-on-failure',   // record but only keep on failure
      size:    { width: 1280, height: 720 },
      show:    {
        actions: true,   // overlay bright highlight boxes on every interacted element
        test:    true,   // show a test-name banner at the start of each test segment
      },
    },
  },
});
```
```typescript
// Use in CI alongside page.screencast for step-level annotations:
// page.screencast (v1.59) lets you start/stop recording per test.step()
// while the config-level `video` option gives full-test coverage with
// the new v1.60 show.* overlays automatically applied.
//
// Comparison:
//   config video                   page.screencast (v1.59)
//   --------------------------     --------------------------------
//   Always on per config          Controlled per test.step()
//   show.actions auto overlay     showActions() manual call
//   show.test banner auto         showChapter() manual narration
//   Chromium + Firefox + WebKit   Chromium ONLY
//
// Recommendation: use config video + show.* for CI failure videos;
// use page.screencast for demo recordings and complex step-level narration.
```
Tradeoff: `show.actions` and `show.test` (v1.60) embed interaction highlights and test-name banners directly into the video stream without any test-code changes — making failure videos immediately readable without manually correlating timestamps to reporter output — but enabling both sub-options increases video encoding overhead by approximately 5–15% on large suites with many small interactions; use `mode: 'retain-on-failure'` rather than `'on'` to limit encoding to only the tests that actually fail, keeping the overhead acceptable.

**Pattern 637** — `testInfoError.cause()` Chain-of-Cause Failure Reporting (v1.49+)
```typescript
// Custom reporter: propagate Error.cause chain into JUnit XML
import type { Reporter, TestCase, TestResult } from '@playwright/test/reporter';

class CauseChainReporter implements Reporter {
  onTestEnd(test: TestCase, result: TestResult): void {
    if (result.status !== 'failed') return;

    for (const error of result.errors) {
      const message = error.message ?? '(no message)';
      console.error(`FAIL: ${test.title}`);
      console.error(`  Message: ${message}`);

      // v1.49+: error.cause mirrors JavaScript Error.cause chain
      let cause: typeof error.cause = error.cause;
      let depth = 1;
      while (cause) {
        console.error(`  ${'  '.repeat(depth)}Caused by: ${cause.message ?? '(no message)'}`);
        cause = (cause as typeof error).cause;
        depth++;
        if (depth > 10) { console.error('  ...(truncated)'); break; }
      }
    }
  }

  // Surface cause in a fixture for test-code use:
  // if (testInfo.errors.length > 0) {
  //   const rootCause = testInfo.errors[0].cause?.message;
  //   testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'root-cause', description: rootCause ?? '' });
  // }
}

export default CauseChainReporter;
```
```typescript
// Throwing errors with cause for upstream fixture failures:
import { test } from '@playwright/test';

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  try {
    await page.goto('/app');
    await page.waitForSelector('[data-app-ready]', { timeout: 5_000 });
  } catch (original) {
    // Wrap with cause so custom reporters can inspect the original
    throw Object.assign(
      new Error('App did not reach ready state in beforeEach'),
      { cause: original }
    );
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `error.cause` (v1.49) propagates the standard JavaScript `Error.cause` chain through Playwright's reporter API, enabling custom reporters to distinguish a root database-connection failure from the test-assertion failure it causes — but Playwright's built-in reporters (HTML, JUnit, GitHub Actions) currently display only the top-level error message, not the cause chain; `error.cause` provides value only when consumed by a custom reporter or when the root error is surfaced via `testInfo.annotations` for visibility in standard report outputs.

**Pattern 638** — `PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD=1` Browser Process Dashboard (v1.59+)
```bash
# Show all @playwright/test-managed browsers in the operating system's
# process list with labeled window titles (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
# Useful for debugging worker stalls and zombie browser processes in CI.
PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD=1 npx playwright test --workers=4

# Combine with --headed to visually observe browser windows alongside
# process metadata. Disable in production CI to avoid environment variable
# side effects leaking into the test process environment.
PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD=1 PWDEBUG=console npx playwright test --headed --grep @smoke
```
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts: suppress PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD in CI to avoid
// unintended behavior on headless agents that don't support windowed views.
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Never set PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD in config — it must remain a shell env var.
  // Add to CI secrets rotation documentation: PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD should be
  // 0 or unset in automated pipelines.
  reporter: process.env.CI
    ? [['github'], ['blob']]
    : [['html', { open: 'on-failure' }]],
});
```
Tradeoff: `PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD=1` labels launched browser processes with the worker index and browser type, making it trivial to identify which worker is stalled in a multi-worker local run using Activity Monitor or Task Manager — but the dashboard window titles are rendered by Playwright's internal browser launcher and do not appear in headless mode, making the flag a local debugging aid only; there is no programmatic API to query the dashboard state from within tests, so it cannot replace `context.tracing.start()` for automated diagnostics.

**Pattern 639** — `playwright-bdd` BDD/Cucumber Integration With Playwright Fixtures [community]
```typescript
// Install: npm install -D playwright-bdd
// Generates Playwright-native test files from .feature files — no custom runner needed.

// features/login.feature
// Feature: User login
//   Scenario: Successful login with valid credentials
//     Given I am on the login page
//     When I submit valid credentials
//     Then I should see the dashboard

// steps/login.steps.ts
import { createBdd } from 'playwright-bdd';
import { test }      from '../fixtures/auth.fixture';

const { Given, When, Then } = createBdd(test);

Given('I am on the login page', async ({ loginPage }) => {
  await loginPage.goto();
});

When('I submit valid credentials', async ({ loginPage }) => {
  await loginPage.login(
    process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL ?? 'admin@example.com',
    process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD ?? 'pw'
  );
});

Then('I should see the dashboard', async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
});
```
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts integration
import { defineConfig }     from '@playwright/test';
import { defineBddConfig }  from 'playwright-bdd';

const testDir = defineBddConfig({
  features: 'features/**/*.feature',
  steps:    'steps/**/*.steps.ts',
});

export default defineConfig({
  testDir,
  // All standard Playwright options work: tracing, video, reporters, sharding
  reporter: [['html', { open: 'never' }], ['junit', { outputFile: 'results.xml' }]],
});
// Run: npx bddgen && npx playwright test
// npx bddgen generates intermediate .spec.ts files; check these into VCS for
// IDE navigation and to avoid re-generation on each CI startup.
```
Tradeoff: `playwright-bdd` transforms `.feature` files into standard Playwright spec files using standard `test.extend()` fixtures — all Playwright features (sharding, retry, tracing, parallelism) work without wrapping — but `.feature` files must be kept in sync with step definitions; missing step definitions cause a generation error, not a test failure, which surfaces before CI runs and can block the pipeline on a simple typo. [community]

**Pattern 640** — `monocart-reporter` HTML Grid Reporter With Suite/Case/Step Visualization [community]
```typescript
// Install: npm install -D monocart-reporter
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig }      from '@playwright/test';
import MonocartReporter      from 'monocart-reporter';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    [
      'monocart-reporter',
      {
        name:       'E2E Test Report',
        outputFile: './test-results/report.html',

        // Column definitions: each key maps to a test.info() property
        columns: (defaultColumns: MonocartReporter.ColumnDef[]) => {
          const statusColumn = defaultColumns.find(c => c.id === 'status');
          if (statusColumn) statusColumn.width = 80;
          return [
            ...defaultColumns,
            // custom column: surfaces the @tag list from test annotations
            {
              id:      'tag',
              name:    'Tags',
              align:   'center',
              width:   100,
              formatter: (v: string[]) => v?.join(', ') ?? '',
            },
          ];
        },

        // Aggregate trends across CI runs via an external data store
        trend: './test-results/trend.json',

        // Show coverage summary alongside test results
        coverage: {
          entryFilter:   (entry: unknown) => true,
          sourceFilter:  (sourcePath: string) => sourcePath.startsWith('src/'),
        },
      },
    ],
  ],
});
```
```typescript
// Tagging pattern to populate the custom 'tag' column:
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout flow completes', {
  tag:        ['@checkout', '@smoke'],
  annotation: [{ type: 'issue', description: 'PROJ-1234' }],
}, async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Checkout' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `monocart-reporter` renders suites, cases, and steps in an HTML grid with built-in trend tracking and optional V8 coverage integration — making it the most information-dense built-in-replacement reporter in the ecosystem — but the `coverage` feature requires a separate V8 coverage collection step (`page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` in a `beforeEach` hook) and is Chromium-only; teams using Firefox or WebKit as the primary browser cannot get accurate JS coverage numbers and should combine `monocart-reporter` with the HTML grid features only, omitting the coverage section. [community]

**Pattern 641** — `@guidepup/playwright` VoiceOver and NVDA Screen Reader Integration [community]
```typescript
// Install: npm install -D @guidepup/playwright
// Requires macOS with VoiceOver or Windows with NVDA installed.

// e2e/specs/voiceover-login.spec.ts
import { voTest as test, expect } from '@guidepup/playwright';

test.use({
  voiceover: true,   // Enable VoiceOver on macOS; use nvda: true on Windows
});

test('login form is announced correctly by VoiceOver', async ({
  page, voiceover,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  // Focus the email field via keyboard
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).focus();

  // Confirm VoiceOver announces the field name and role
  const spokenPhrase = await voiceover.spokenPhrase();
  expect(spokenPhrase).toContain('Email');
  expect(spokenPhrase).toContain('text field');

  // Navigate to next field with Tab and assert the password field announcement
  await voiceover.next();
  const pwPhrase = await voiceover.spokenPhrase();
  expect(pwPhrase).toContain('Password');

  // Trigger a validation error and verify the error is announced
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await voiceover.next();
  const errorPhrase = await voiceover.spokenPhrase();
  expect(errorPhrase).toMatch(/required|error/i);
});
```
```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — isolate VoiceOver tests to a dedicated project
// because they cannot run in CI without the OS-level accessibility APIs.
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      name:      'voiceover',
      testMatch: /\.voiceover\.spec\.ts/,
      use:       { ...devices['Desktop Safari'] },   // VoiceOver requires Safari/WebKit
    },
    {
      name:      'chromium',
      testMatch: /(?<!voiceover)\.spec\.ts/,
      use:       { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
    },
  ],
});
// Run VoiceOver tests locally:
//   npx playwright test --project=voiceover
// Skip in CI (VoiceOver requires GUI):
//   npx playwright test --ignore-glob "**/*.voiceover.spec.ts"
```
Tradeoff: `@guidepup/playwright` drives the real operating system screen reader (VoiceOver on macOS, NVDA on Windows) against a live browser, producing the most accurate accessibility signal possible — it tests the actual announcements users with disabilities hear, not just ARIA attributes — but screen reader testing requires a GUI environment and cannot run headless, making it unsuitable for standard CI pipelines; run these tests on a dedicated macOS/Windows CI node or a locally triggered pre-release gate, and use `@axe-core/playwright` for automated WCAG scans in the standard CI pipeline. [community]

### Community Gotchas (continued)

**G215** — `video: { show: { actions: true } }` Has No Effect Without `mode` Set to a Recording-Active Value
Why this matters: `show.actions` and `show.test` are sub-options of the `video` config object (v1.60+). Setting them to `true` inside a config where `video: { mode: 'off' }` (the default for non-CI configurations) has zero effect — the overlays are never rendered because no recording takes place. Teams copy the `show.*` options from documentation into their config without confirming that `mode` is set to `'on'`, `'retain-on-failure'`, or `'on-first-failure'`, then wonder why failure videos lack the highlighted-action overlays they expected. The options parse and load without error regardless of `mode`.
Fix: Always set `mode` explicitly alongside `show.*`: `video: { mode: 'retain-on-failure', show: { actions: true, test: true } }`. Add a config validation comment above the `video` block: `// mode must not be 'off' for show.* options to have any effect`. To confirm overlays are working, run one test locally with `mode: 'on'` and open the resulting `.webm` file in a media player before deploying to CI.

---

**G216** — `playwright-bdd` `npx bddgen` Must Re-run After Every `.feature` File Change — Generated Specs Go Stale Silently
Why this matters: `playwright-bdd` works by generating intermediate `.spec.ts` files from `.feature` files via `npx bddgen`. If the `.feature` file is updated (new Scenario, changed step text) but `bddgen` is not re-run before `npx playwright test`, Playwright runs the stale generated spec from the previous generation. The stale spec passes or fails based on the old scenario, not the new one — producing a silent incorrect test run with no "file is outdated" warning. CI pipelines that cache generated files across runs are particularly vulnerable.
Fix: Add `bddgen` to the CI test command: `"test": "npx bddgen && npx playwright test"`. Add a `pre-commit` hook that runs `bddgen` when any `.feature` file is staged: `echo '#!/bin/sh\nnpx bddgen' > .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit`. Commit the generated `.spec.ts` files to VCS so diffs are reviewable in PRs and stale detection is possible by checking whether `git diff` shows unstaged changes after `bddgen`.

---

**G217** — `testInfoError.cause` Is Not Surfaced by Built-In Reporters — Only Visible in Custom Reporters
Why this matters: `testInfoError.cause` (v1.49) and `testError.cause` mirror the JavaScript `Error.cause` property, enabling chained error diagnostics in custom reporters. However, none of Playwright's built-in reporters (HTML, JUnit, GitHub Actions, Blob) render the cause chain — they show only the outermost error message and stack trace. Teams that expect the HTML report to show "caused by: database connection refused" below the "login failed" assertion error are disappointed to find that Playwright's reporter implementation ignores `.cause` entirely, and users who add `throw Object.assign(new Error('outer'), { cause: originalError })` in fixtures to annotate failures find no improvement in built-in report readability.
Fix: Access `error.cause` only in a custom reporter class implementing `Reporter.onTestEnd()`. To surface root causes in the HTML report without a custom reporter, push the cause message as a `testInfo.annotations` entry: `testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'root-cause', description: String(error.cause?.message) })` from within a `test.afterEach()` hook that reads `testInfo.errors`. This surfaces the cause in the HTML "Annotations" panel visible to all report consumers.

**Pattern 642** — `playwright-magic-steps` Auto-Transform Comments into Test Steps [community]
```typescript
// Install: npm install -D playwright-magic-steps
// Activate via NODE_OPTIONS in package.json:
// "test": "cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=\"-r playwright-magic-steps\" playwright test"

// VS Code extension support (.vscode/settings.json):
// { "playwright.env": { "NODE_OPTIONS": "-r playwright-magic-steps" } }

// e2e/specs/checkout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // step: Navigate to shop homepage
  await page.goto('/shop');

  // step: Add first product to cart
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText('1 item');

  // step: Proceed to checkout
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/\/checkout/);

  // step: Fill in shipping address
  await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Alice Smith');
  await page.getByLabel('Address').fill('123 Main St');
  await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Springfield');

  // step: Submit order
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```
```typescript
// Variable interpolation in step titles:
test('search for product', async ({ page }) => {
  const query = 'wireless headphones';

  // step: Search for "${query}"
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill(query);
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /results/i })).toBeVisible();
});

// Nested steps (indent controls nesting):
test('nested step example', async ({ page }) => {
  // step: Authenticate
  await page.goto('/login');
  if (true) {
    // step: Fill credentials
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');
    // stepend
  }
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  // step: Verify dashboard loaded
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Dashboard' })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `playwright-magic-steps` turns `// step: title` comments into `test.step()` wrappers at module load time via a Node.js `require` hook, requiring zero code changes to get structured steps in the Trace Viewer and HTML report — beneficial for teams adopting Playwright on an existing test suite without wanting to manually wrap every block. The hook performs string transformations that can conflict with template literals or multi-line arrow functions that span a step boundary; always test with `--workers=1` after adding the module to confirm no unexpected behavior. Because steps are injected by a require hook (not by the TypeScript compiler), they do not appear in `.d.ts` files and IDE refactoring tools do not know about step boundaries. The `stepend` comment is required to close a step opened inside a nested `if`/`try` block — forgetting it causes subsequent code to be grouped into the wrong step. [community]

**Pattern 643** — Fixture `{ title }` Option — Custom Display Name in Reports [official]
```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/database.ts
// By default, Playwright uses the fixture property name as the step label in the trace.
// The { title } option lets you override that with a human-readable label.

import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { DatabaseClient } from '../lib/db';

type DbFixtures = {
  db: DatabaseClient;
  seedData: { userId: string; email: string };
};

export const test = base.extend<DbFixtures>({
  // Without { title }: shows as "db" in traces — cryptic for reviewers
  // With  { title }: shows as "PostgreSQL test client" — immediately clear
  db: [
    async ({}, use) => {
      const client = await DatabaseClient.connect(process.env.TEST_DB_URL!);
      await use(client);
      await client.disconnect();
    },
    { title: 'PostgreSQL test client' },
  ],

  // Combining title + scope + timeout for a slow worker-scoped DB seeder
  seedData: [
    async ({ db }, use, workerInfo) => {
      const email = `worker${workerInfo.workerIndex}@example.com`;
      const { userId } = await db.createTestUser(email);
      await use({ userId, email });
      await db.deleteTestUser(userId);
    },
    {
      scope:   'worker',
      title:   'Seed test user for worker',
      timeout: 30_000,   // independent of the test timeout
    },
  ],
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';
```
```typescript
// e2e/specs/profile.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/database';

test('user profile shows email', async ({ page, seedData }) => {
  // Trace viewer shows:
  //   fixture: PostgreSQL test client     ← from { title }
  //   fixture: Seed test user for worker  ← from { title }
  //   (test body steps follow)
  await page.goto(`/users/${seedData.userId}`);
  await expect(page.getByText(seedData.email)).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Fixture option decision table:**

| Option | Type | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `title` | `string` | Human-readable label shown in Trace Viewer / HTML report instead of the property name |
| `scope` | `'test'` \| `'worker'` | Lifecycle — per-test (default) or per-worker |
| `timeout` | `number` (ms) | Time budget for fixture setup+teardown, independent of test timeout |
| `box` | `boolean` \| `'self'` | Collapse internal steps in traces; `'self'` keeps named sub-steps visible |
| `auto` | `boolean` | Run automatically without declaring in test parameters |
| `option` | `boolean` | Mark as a configurable option that can be overridden per-project |

Tradeoff: `{ title }` is a pure UX improvement — it has no effect on fixture behavior, timeout, or ordering. Its value is highest for internal platform fixtures (database clients, mock servers, auth helpers) whose property names (`db`, `srv`, `auth`) are opaque to test authors reading CI reports. Setting `{ title }` alongside `{ scope: 'worker', timeout: N }` is the recommended pattern for slow, expensive worker-level fixtures because all three options combine in a single object. Titles do not localize — hard-coded English strings are common in codebases that don't need multi-language test reports. [official]

**Pattern 644** — `Libretto` — Open-Source Playwright CLI Toolkit for Coding Agents [community]
```typescript
// Install: npm install -D libretto-playwright
// Libretto provides a CLI and SDK for AI coding agents to inspect pages,
// capture network traffic, and generate automation scripts — all built on Playwright.

// Use case 1: Interactive page inspection during agentic test generation
// npx libretto inspect https://myapp.localhost:5173
// → prints ARIA tree, page title, and visible links to stdout as JSON
// → an LLM agent feeds this JSON to its planning step before writing locators

// Use case 2: Network traffic capture for HAR generation
// npx libretto capture --url https://myapp.localhost:5173 --action "click:button[data-testid=checkout]"
// → records full request/response HAR; exports to ./libretto-output/capture.har

// Use case 3: Generate a Playwright spec scaffold from an inspection
// npx libretto generate --url https://myapp.localhost:5173 --goal "fill out registration form"
// → emits a draft spec to stdout; agent refines and saves

// SDK integration: embed Libretto inspection into fixture setup
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import { LibrettoClient } from 'libretto-playwright';

type LibrettoFixtures = { inspector: LibrettoClient };

export const test = base.extend<LibrettoFixtures>({
  inspector: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const client = new LibrettoClient(page);
    await use(client);
  },
});

// e2e/specs/agentic-discovery.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/libretto';

test('discover navigation structure', async ({ page, inspector }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  // Capture ARIA tree for agent review
  const ariaJson = await inspector.inspect();
  // ariaJson: { title, ariaTree, links, forms, buttons }
  expect(ariaJson.links.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Libretto is designed for the agentic test generation workflow — it wraps Playwright's `page.ariaSnapshot()`, network recording, and codegen capabilities into a CLI interface consumable by coding agents without requiring those agents to understand Playwright's full API surface. Teams using GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or Claude to write Playwright tests can point the agent at a Libretto inspection JSON rather than raw Playwright API calls, reducing hallucination of incorrect selectors. For human-authored tests, Libretto adds no value over native Playwright APIs; its overhead (an extra dependency, an extra CLI invocation) is unjustified unless you have an agentic test generation workflow. Libretto is early-stage; pin the version and audit each update before upgrading in CI. [community]

**Pattern 645** — `BrowserClaw` — AI Browser Automation via Accessibility Snapshots [community]
```typescript
// BrowserClaw is an AI browser automation framework built on Playwright that
// uses accessibility-snapshot-based element targeting (via ARIA ref tokens)
// rather than traditional CSS/XPath selectors or LLM-generated locators.

// How it works:
// 1. BrowserClaw calls page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true }) to get the ARIA tree
// 2. The AI agent selects elements by their ARIA ref token (e.g., ref=e23)
// 3. BrowserClaw translates ref tokens back to live Playwright locators
//    using locator(':aria-ref(e23)') or similar internal mechanisms
// 4. Actions (click, fill, assert) are executed via stable Playwright calls

// Contrast with direct Playwright + ariaSnapshot usage:
test('agent-driven checkout (native Playwright)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Capture ARIA tree with refs — the agent sees this and picks targets
  const snap = await page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true, mode: 'ai' });
  /*
    - heading "Checkout" [ref=e1]
    - textbox "Card number" [ref=e7]
    - textbox "Expiry" [ref=e8]
    - button "Pay now" [ref=e12]
  */

  // Agent extracts refs; test uses them directly via locator()
  // Note: ref tokens are ephemeral — re-snapshot after any DOM change
  await page.locator(':aria-ref(e7)').fill('4111 1111 1111 1111');
  await page.locator(':aria-ref(e8)').fill('12/28');
  await page.locator(':aria-ref(e12)').click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /payment confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```
```typescript
// Why ref-based targeting is more stable than CSS selectors for AI agents:
//
// ❌ AI hallucination risk: LLMs often generate CSS selectors from visual
//    descriptions (e.g. ".checkout-form .submit-btn") — these break on refactors.
//
// ✅ Ref-based: the ARIA tree is generated at runtime from the live DOM — no
//    hallucination possible. The ref token points to the actual DOM node.
//
// ✅ Combined pattern: use ariaSnapshot for discovery (AI agent reads structure),
//    then standard semantic locators for final assertions (resilient to re-snapshots).

test('best-practice hybrid', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');
  // Step 1 (AI discovery): snapshot the form to identify structure
  const snap = await page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' });
  // Step 2 (human/static assertion): use semantic locators for assertions
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /username/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i })).toBeEnabled();
});
```
Tradeoff: BrowserClaw's ref-based approach eliminates selector hallucination at the cost of snapshot staleness — refs change on every `ariaSnapshot()` call and become invalid after DOM mutations or page navigations. Any agentic workflow using BrowserClaw must re-snapshot after each significant action to obtain fresh refs. For non-agentic, human-authored tests, BrowserClaw adds complexity without benefit; stick with `getByRole()`, `getByLabel()`, and `getByText()`. BrowserClaw is community-maintained and early-stage — treat it as a pattern reference rather than a production dependency for high-criticality test suites. [community]

### Community Gotchas (continued)

**G218** — `playwright-magic-steps` Step Boundaries Break Inside Template Literals and Ternary Expressions
Why this matters: `playwright-magic-steps` injects `test.step()` wrappers by transforming source code at the module level — it looks for `// step: title` comments at statement level and treats the next statement start as the step body boundary. When a `// step:` comment appears inside a template literal assignment or an inline ternary expression, the transform misidentifies the step body and either wraps the wrong code or produces a JavaScript syntax error that only appears at runtime. Teams using complex multi-line arrow functions discover the error only when running the suite, not at TypeScript compile time.
Fix: Keep `// step:` comments at the top-level statement scope — never inside template literals, ternaries, or complex one-liner expressions. If you need to annotate code inside a conditional block, use a plain `test.step()` call instead: `await test.step('title', async () => { ... })`. Add a `// stepend` comment to close any step that opens inside an `if`/`try` block to ensure the transform knows where the step body ends.

---

**G219** — Fixture `{ title }` Shows in the Trace as Setup/Teardown — Not in the Test Step List
Why this matters: When a fixture has `{ title: 'My custom title' }`, the title appears in the Trace Viewer under the fixture setup/teardown sections (the collapsed panels before and after the test steps) — it does NOT appear as a named step inside the test's own step list. Teams expect the fixture title to add a labelled entry to the test timeline they can click on in the HTML report; instead, it only changes the fixture panel header. This confusion is most common when teams migrate from `test.step()` wrappers inside fixtures (which do appear in the step list) to `{ title }` declarations (which do not).
Fix: If you need fixture actions to appear as clickable steps in the test timeline, use `test.step('title', async () => { ... })` inside the fixture body. Use `{ title }` for human-readable fixture panel headers in Trace Viewer. Combine both: `{ title: 'Database setup' }` on the fixture declaration (for the panel header) plus `await test.step('Run migrations', ...)` inside the body (for timeline entries).

---

**G220** — BrowserClaw ARIA Ref Tokens Are Not Stable Across Navigation — Never Cache Refs Across `goto()` Calls
Why this matters: ARIA ref tokens produced by `page.ariaSnapshot({ ref: true })` are generated fresh each time `ariaSnapshot()` is called — they are ephemeral identifiers bound to the current DOM snapshot. If an AI agent collects refs from a snapshot taken before a `page.goto()` call and then uses those refs after the navigation, the locator `:aria-ref(e7)` will either resolve to the wrong element (if element order coincidentally matches) or throw a "no element" error. Teams building LLM-driven test scripts that collect all refs at the start of a test and use them throughout multiple navigations discover that refs from the first snapshot are meaningless on the second page.
Fix: Re-snapshot after every navigation, dynamic DOM update, or route change before issuing ref-based actions. Structure agentic test loops as: `(snapshot → decide → act → assert) × N` — never hoist a single snapshot to the top of a multi-step flow. If the test spans multiple pages, track refs per-navigation and discard prior refs after each `page.goto()`.
